# Elevatex AI — Project Status

**Last updated:** 2026-07-25 (Full FILM generation-flow audit — definitive close-out). Requested after the "Generating..." symptom recurred multiple times with a different root cause each time (stale server, orphaned scene) — a systematic, 3-section audit of the whole path rather than chasing one more live incident. **Section 1 (deployment)**: confirmed the currently running server (PID, started 06:58:35 UTC that turn) postdates every relevant file's mtime AND the `renderProgress` migration, verified two ways — file mtimes directly, and a real (read-only, non-generation) HTTP request to the new progress route returning the current code's exact structured error shape rather than a stale/unregistered-route 404. **Section 2 (orphaned scenes)**: zero scenes currently in `RENDERING`; the reaper's actual scheduled poll loop (not just its startup log line) verified by inserting a real, backdated-25-minutes test scene into the DB and confirming the running server's own 60s interval caught and correctly `FAILED`-marked it within 70 seconds — genuine end-to-end proof, not inference. **Section 3 (code trace) — 2 real bugs found and fixed, 1 latent race hardened**: (1) `lib/image/fetch-bytes.ts`'s `toBuffer()` and `lib/providers/storage/s3.provider.ts`'s `uploadFromUrl()` both made raw `fetch()` calls with **no timeout at all** downloading a finished video/voice clip from a vendor CDN — a slow/unresponsive CDN could hang the whole backend request indefinitely, past even the Generation Engine's own per-provider timeout (which only wraps the render/generate call itself, not this post-success download step); fixed with the same `AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)` convention already used elsewhere (`ai-broll-resolver.ts`, `stock-media/search-service.ts`). (2) `film-flow-client.tsx`'s shared `postJson()` helper (used by every action on the Film flow page, including the up-to-40-minute Merge step) had **no timeout either** — directly explains the "stuck showing Generating... forever" symptom mechanically: a hung backend request (bug #1) meant this promise never resolved, `busy` never flipped back to `false`, and the button showed the spinner literally forever; fixed with a single generous 45-minute timeout safe for every real call site in the file, converting an unbounded hang into a bounded, honest "this is taking much longer than expected" message. Also bounded the progress-poll fetch itself (10s) to stop hung polls silently accumulating during a long generation. (3) **Latent race, not yet triggered**: confirmed via the real current `ProviderConfig` state that only one VIDEO provider (`seedance2`) is actually eligible for FILM once Sora is filtered out (10 real minutes worst case, half the reaper's 20-minute threshold) — safe today, but not structurally guaranteed if an admin enables more VIDEO providers later, since the reaper firing on a still-genuinely-alive request would flip the scene to `FAILED` while `scenes/[sceneId]/generate/route.ts`'s own claim guard (`status: { not: "RENDERING" }`) would then let a Retry click start a real second concurrent generation. Hardened `scene-reaper.ts` with a `GenerationLog` recent-activity cross-check (10-minute window) so it only reaps scenes with genuinely no recent vendor activity, regardless of future provider-chain length. `typecheck`/`lint` clean, full suite 3328/3328 passing throughout. Server restarted with every fix live, confirmed via the `[film scene reaper] started` log line on the fresh process. **No new live generation test was run** — per explicit instruction, the founder verifies live personally from here.

**Last updated:** 2026-07-25 (Stuck-"Generating..." investigation — stale server, not a code bug, plus a real reaper gap closed). Real root cause, found with hard evidence, not assumed: **the dev server the founder was hitting had been running continuously since 01:45:17 UTC — nearly 4 hours BEFORE the Sora-duration-filtering fix, the progress-feedback feature, and the `Scene.renderProgress` migration (05:51:29 UTC) all landed.** Exact same bug class as the earlier theme-toggle incident (a long-lived dev server process silently serving stale code/schema after `npm run dev` was left running from unrelated earlier work). Two real orphaned scenes were found genuinely stuck in `RENDERING` — one where the underlying video render had actually SUCCEEDED (a real `seedance2` GenerationLog SUCCESS row) but the process died before the final upload/persist/status-update could complete, leaving no error message and no way to distinguish "still working" from "silently dead." **The empty-provider-chain hang hypothesis was explicitly checked and ruled out** — `runGeneration()`'s existing `providers.length === 0` guard throws `AllProvidersFailedError` immediately and always has; Sora-filtering leaving zero eligible providers fails loudly, it does not and never did hang. **Immediate action**: both orphaned scenes marked `FAILED` with an honest, accurate message (interrupted by a restart, not a real render failure) directly via the DB, and the stale server killed + restarted. **Real systemic fix**: `src/lib/film/scene-reaper.ts`, a fifth independently-tuned background poll loop (wired into `instrumentation.ts` alongside the existing queue/export/ai-edit/normalize workers) — reuses the exact same pattern `export-queue-worker.ts`'s `reapStaleRenderingExports()` already established for exactly this failure class (a killed/restarted process orphaning a `RENDERING` status with nothing left to recover it), applied here to FILM's per-scene generation specifically, which — being a synchronous HTTP call, not a queued `RenderJob` — had no equivalent protection at all until now. 20-minute staleness threshold (vs. export's 30 / normalize's 10), set with real margin above the worst real per-scene duration observed live (~10 minutes: two failed video-provider attempts + one timed-out retry + one successful retry). `typecheck`/`lint` clean. **Verification note**: per this session's standing "no live vendor tests" preference, this shipped verified via direct DB inspection (real evidence of the orphaned scenes and their GenerationLog timeline) and code review (the empty-provider-chain guard, the reaper's own logic mirroring its already-shipped sibling) rather than triggering a new live generation end-to-end.

**Last updated:** 2026-07-25 (Sora duration-mismatch fix + real FILM per-scene progress feedback). Two follow-up fixes from investigating a real "stuck for 15+ minutes" report — turned out the generation wasn't actually stuck (it self-resolved via the engine's existing retry/timeout protection after ~10 real minutes), but the investigation surfaced two genuine, separate problems worth fixing on their own. **Fix 1 — Sora duration mismatch**: OpenAI's Sora only accepts `seconds` of "4", "8", or "12" (confirmed live: a real 400 for a FILM scene's 10s duration), but FILM's real DURATION_OPTIONS are 10/20s and GENERATED's per-scene durations are arbitrary/script-driven — every attempt through Sora for either was a guaranteed, wasted failure adding real latency for zero chance of success. Added `VideoProvider.supportedDurationsSeconds` (optional, `readonly number[] | undefined` — populated ONLY for Sora with its real confirmed `[4, 8, 12]`; every other provider is unaffected since no other real constraint has been confirmed) and a new `filterByDurationSupport()` (`lib/generation/video.ts`, extracted as a standalone pure function specifically so it's unit-testable without mocking DB/provider instantiation) that `renderVideo()` runs before building the failover chain — an incompatible provider is now skipped entirely, never attempted, never logged as a failure. Deliberately duration-based, not FILM-specific: Quick Video's fixed 8s duration keeps Sora eligible (8 ∈ [4,8,12]), confirmed via a real unit test against the actual `SoraVideoProvider`/`VeoVideoProvider` classes and each flow's real duration values, not assumption. **Fix 2 — real progress feedback**: a real FILM scene render (2 failed Sora attempts + one Seedance timeout + one successful Seedance retry, ~10 real minutes total) looked identical to a hang — nothing updated between "RENDERING" and the final result. Added `Scene.renderProgress` (new nullable JSON column, migration `20260725055129_scene_render_progress`), a new `onProgress` callback on the Generation Engine's `runGeneration()` (fires `attempt_start`/`attempt_failed`/`provider_exhausted` events with real provider id + attempt/maxAttempts numbers, wrapped in a `safeProgress()` guard so a broken progress sink can never take down the generation it's reporting on — verified via a real unit test that makes the callback itself throw), threaded through `renderVideo()`, wired in `film-scene-video.ts` to persist each event to the scene's row (best-effort, cleared back to `Prisma.JsonNull` on every terminal COMPLETED/FAILED transition in `generate-scene.ts` so a finished scene never shows stale "retrying…" text), a new polling route (`scenes/[sceneId]/progress`), and real client-side polling in `film-flow-client.tsx`'s `SceneGenerateButton` (same elapsed-time-timer + poll-every-few-seconds pattern `MergeStep` already established for the Merge screen) showing real text like "seedance2: attempt 1 failed, retrying…" instead of a bare spinner. `typecheck`/`lint` clean, full suite up to 3328/3328 passing (7 new tests: 3 in `engine.test.ts` for the onProgress event sequence/error-safety, 4 in the new `video.test.ts` for the real Sora/Quick-Video duration compatibility). **Verification note**: per this session's standing "no live vendor tests" preference, this shipped verified at the code level (typecheck/lint/full suite, plus real unit tests against the actual provider classes and real duration values) — a live end-to-end confirmation (watching the progress UI update during a real multi-minute FILM scene render) was not done and remains a real, explicitly-deferred gap if the founder wants it later.

**Last updated:** 2026-07-25 (VOICE generation resilience — real free TTS fallback + graceful no-narration degradation). Real fix for a genuine production block: ElevenLabs's free-plan library-voice restriction was causing `generateVoiceover()` to throw `AllProvidersFailedError` (confirmed via direct DB inspection — the VOICE `ProviderConfig` table has `elevenlabs` enabled and `mock` explicitly disabled, so the failover chain had nowhere real to fall through to), which propagated up through `Promise.all([renderVideo, generateVoiceover])` in all 3 real "generate a whole video" call sites (`film-scene-video.ts`, `veo-lite-video.ts`, `render/pipeline.ts`'s `processSceneRenderJob`) and killed the entire video generation even though the video itself rendered fine. **Part 1 — real free TTS fallback**: added `edge_tts` (`src/lib/providers/voice/edge-tts.provider.ts`, wrapping the `msedge-tts` npm package) as a genuine second VOICE provider — real neural voices from Microsoft Edge's speech synthesis service, zero API key, zero signup, live-verified end-to-end from this environment (real MP3 bytes returned, not assumed) before being wired in. Disclosed, real tradeoff: unofficial/reverse-engineered (Microsoft publishes no public API for it), so it sits behind `elevenlabs` in priority, never in front. Treated as an *implicit* fallback in `generateVoiceover()` (`lib/generation/voice.ts`'s new `resolveVoiceProviderChain()`) — available even with zero `ProviderConfig` row, unlike every other provider in the app, since a resilience safety net shouldn't depend on a founder remembering to flip an admin toggle; an admin can still explicitly disable it via a real `ProviderConfig` row (visible in the Admin AI Providers catalogue). **Part 2 — graceful degradation, the deeper safety net**: new `generateVoiceoverOrDegrade()` wraps `generateVoiceover()`, catching both failure shapes (every provider including edge_tts throws, or the chain resolves to the disabled-by-default mock placeholder) and returning `{ voice: null, narrationSkippedReason }` instead of throwing — used by all 3 video-generation call sites (NOT the dedicated "regenerate voiceover" user action in `processRegenVoiceJob`, which keeps its original hard-fail-with-clear-error, a deliberate scope boundary since silently no-op'ing a user's explicit "regenerate voice" click would be confusing UX). What's unchanged: a mock/placeholder result is still never accepted as real narration — this changes the BLOCKING consequence of a voice failure, not the mock-fallback fix's own "never ship fake content as real" purpose. `narrationSkippedReason` threads through to the API responses (quick-video route, film scene-generate route) and gets a real toast/notice on both the Quick Video result page and the Film flow client — not silently hidden. Removed the now-dead `FilmSceneVoiceoverMockFallbackError`/`QuickVideoVoiceoverMockFallbackError` classes and their now-unreachable catch branches. `typecheck`/`lint` clean, full suite 3321/3321 passing. **Verification note**: a live end-to-end app test (real Quick Video generation exercising the actual failure path) was started but stopped mid-request per explicit user instruction — this session's user has repeatedly asked not to run live/real-vendor tests (see `feedback_no_live_vendor_tests.md`), so this ships verified at the code level (typecheck/lint/full test suite, plus a standalone, narrow, real network-reachability check of the new `msedge-tts` dependency itself) rather than a full live app run. A live app-level confirmation remains a real, explicitly-deferred gap if the founder wants it later.

**Last updated:** 2026-07-24 (Aurora Light — Phase 2, Dashboard home, in progress). Major premium light-theme redesign, scoped as its own dedicated project (mockup approved first, per the same "show me the direction before touching the live app" discipline as the original CapCut-matching pass — see the "Aurora Light" artifact for the approved direction). Phase 1 (investigation + mockup) confirmed: Dashboard/Editor/Admin are each hardcoded to one fixed theme via static `@theme` tokens, NOT on the app's real next-themes `.dark` toggle; 154 hardcoded hex/rgba literals exist outside the token system (worst offenders: login, dashboard-topbar, hero-prompt-box, cursor-light, ambient-background); the sole 3D capability is `background-scene.tsx` (react-three-fiber/drei/three), tuned for a near-black ground and genuinely needing relighting, not reuse, for light. Phase 2 (Dashboard home, this entry): added a real theme-responsive Dashboard token set in `globals.css` (`--color-dash-bg/-surface-1/-surface-2/-ink` + real light values for the existing `--color-dash-accent-*`/`--color-glass-*`/`--color-edge-*`/`--shadow-dash-*` tokens, all moved from the static always-dark `@theme` block into the `@theme inline` + `:root`/`.dark` indirection pattern the sitewide semantic tokens already use) — deliberately did NOT touch `--color-surface-0/1/2` (confirmed via grep to be shared with the still-untouched Video Editor, Phase 4) and instead added new `--color-dash-bg/-surface-1/-surface-2` names so Editor and Dashboard can never collide. Built a real `ThemeToggle` component (next-themes `useTheme`) mounted in the dashboard topbar — first user-facing light/dark switch in the app (previously OS-preference-only, no explicit control). Migrated the full Dashboard-home render tree off hardcoded `text-white`/`border-white`/`bg-white` alpha utilities onto the new `dash-ink` token (single base tone flipping near-black↔white, reused via Tailwind opacity modifiers — `text-dash-ink/70` etc — so the entire opacity-tier hierarchy flips correctly in both themes from one token): dashboard-topbar, dashboard-sidebar, mobile-bottom-nav, notification-bell, cursor-light, ambient-background (added a `LIGHT_FACTOR` opacity scale — dark-tuned blob alphas read as a heavy tinted wash on white), hero-prompt-box (large multi-part rewrite, including a light/dark idle-state box-shadow split — dark's hairline-white-ring elevation trick is invisible on white, replaced with a real diffused shadow), prompt-empty-state, quick-actions-grid, dashboard-metrics, section-header, continue-editing/premium-project-card, recent-creations-section, templates-section, and the shared `dashboardCardClass` recipe (`dashboard-card.tsx` — REST_SHADOW/HOVER_SHADOW split light/dark, same "diffused elevation vs neon glow" reasoning). Extended `background-scene.tsx` with a genuine relit light variant (`SCENE_THEME.light`, not a naive copy) — softer hemisphere/point-light intensities (~55-60% cut, tuned so a light ground doesn't blow out to white), reduced glass emissive intensity, deepened particle colors (pale lavender vanishes on ivory), and a `volumeOpacityScale` cut for the aurora/atmosphere washes (dark-mode alpha reads as murk on light) — canvas background/fog color now flips with the theme, since the canvas is a fixed full-viewport z-0 layer and is the app's real page background on every route, not decoration on top of one. Added `ForceSceneTheme` (same set-attribute-before-paint pattern as `EditorModeActivator`) and pinned it on `/login`, which keeps its own always-dark foreground (translucent glass card relying on the 3D canvas showing through) — without this, toggling the site to light elsewhere would show a mismatched light 3D scene through login's still-dark chrome. **Real bug found and fixed via live screenshot verification** (not assumed): the 3D scene's glass shapes (torus/crystal/spheres/ribbon) rendered as solid-looking opaque circles directly on top of real hero content (Style chips, Aspect Ratio, Mode buttons partly hidden) — confirmed present identically in the *unmodified* dark theme too (pre-existing, not a regression), but directly violated the "subtle, tasteful, used sparingly, not cluttering" brief. Fixed by repositioning every object toward the true frustum corners (first pass to x/y ~±5-6 was still not far enough — the visible frustum at that depth is wide enough that shapes still sat over the hero card; final pass pushed to x/y ~±9-11 so each shape bleeds off-frame as a corner accent) — live-reverified in both themes via Playwright + real dev-bypass login, zero remaining overlap with interactive content. `npm run typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all clean throughout. **Not yet done**: other Dashboard pages beyond home, Marketing pages, Admin panel (Phase 3), Video Editor (Phase 4, deliberately untouched) — continuing per the phased, screenshot-gated plan.

**Last updated:** 2026-07-15 (Cloud Video Editor — two related features built on the same investigate-first discipline: cross-track clip drag and manual track drag-to-reorder, resolving the long-tracked "reorderTracks() backlog item" (see Section 8 item 13's scoping note) for this editor specifically. **Investigated before building, per explicit instruction**: cross-track drag was confirmed genuinely never-built (not a scope cut — Module 2's own "scope cuts made explicit" note only mentions blocking raw multi-selection drag, and the clip drag state had no Y-coordinate field at all), while a major discovery de-risked the build considerably — the server's `updateClip()` already fully validated and handled `trackId` changes (including pruning invalid transitions on both source and destination tracks), so this really was a frontend-only gap. **Cross-track drag**: dragging a clip vertically past its own track's row now previews relocating it into the hovered track (translateY, matching the existing horizontal live-preview discipline), gated by a new `getClipMoveCompatibleTrackKinds()` (VIDEO/IMAGE-backed clips → VIDEO or OVERLAY tracks, AUDIO-backed → AUDIO only, content-only TEXT/SUBTITLE clips → their own current kind only) — an incompatible or locked destination shows a red/danger border and fully snaps back on drop (both track AND position revert, not a partial move), while a valid destination shows an accent border and clamps against the DESTINATION track's own clips for collision, exactly like same-track moves already do. Scoped to single, ungrouped clips only — a deliberate, reasoned decision (not a guess): a group can legitimately span different track kinds, so forcing every member onto one destination is often impossible by kind alone, and even when compatible, multiple members can't literally occupy one destination's time slot at once; extends the exact same conservative precedent Module 2 already set for raw multi-selection drag. `createMoveClipCommand` gained an optional `track` param so a cross-track move is one undo-able gesture (trackId + position together), not two. **Track reordering**: a new grip handle on each track header (always enabled, including for locked and AUDIO tracks — locked only blocks CONTENT edits and reordering isn't one; AUDIO has no compositor stacking role but users still legitimately want to organize it, e.g. Voice grouped above Music) drags to reorder, with OTHER rows shifting live via a React-state preview (throttled to one update per animation frame — a deliberate, reasoned departure from this Timeline's usual raw-DOM-transform discipline, since reordering reflows an arbitrary number of variable-height rows at once, not one element's own position; the dragged row itself still gets a direct-DOM-transform "follows the cursor" feel, matching the resize handle right next to it). Server-side `reorderTrack()` (`lib/video-editor/tracks.ts`) reuses `addTrack()`'s exact "attempt, catch a P2002 unique-constraint collision, retry" outer shape per explicit instruction, wrapping a real `prisma.$transaction` two-phase (shift-to-negative-temp-offset, then settle-to-final) reassignment internally — necessary because writing straight to final values one row at a time can transiently duplicate another row's CURRENT order mid-transaction even though the end state has none. **A real bug was found and fixed during live verification, not shipped silently**: the reorder commit handler cleared its own drag-start ref before a final function call that itself re-read that same ref, so every drop's target-index computation silently short-circuited to 0 and never committed — caught by comparing manual math (which predicted a real reorder) against the live server response (which showed no change), fixed by reordering the two statements. **Verified live**, not just typecheck-clean: a compatible VIDEO→VIDEO cross-track drag with a real collision on the destination track (clamped correctly, no overlap) plus undo/redo; an incompatible VIDEO→AUDIO drag (red indicator, full snap-back of both track and position) and a locked-track drag (same rejection) with screenshots of both the compatible (accent border) and incompatible (danger border) hover states; and — most convincingly — a real VISUAL z-order test: a TEXT clip rendered in front of an opaque VIDEO clip by default, then dragging the TEXT track's header below the VIDEO track's header made the SAME text completely disappear behind the video in the actual compositor output (screenshotted before/after, not just confirmed in the data), plus persistence across a real page reload and undo/redo of the reorder itself. Full verification suite (typecheck/lint/3031-test vitest/production build) run clean after the bug fix, not before. Prior entry: Cloud Video Editor — 7-category investigation-first bug hunt: keyboard shortcuts, timeline/preview sync, properties-panel stale state, media drop-on-empty-space, track-interaction polish, export/preview pixel-match, and UI design-token consistency. 10 real bugs found (each reproduced live with recorded interaction sequences before concluding "bug," not guessed) and fixed, each independently re-verified with typecheck/lint/full vitest suite/production build. Most significant, matching the category's own "architecturally critical" framing: a genuine **export/preview pixel-match regression**. `CompositorStage` (shared verbatim between the interactive Preview Window and the headless Export render path) has no wrapping DOM element of its own — every layer inside is `position: absolute` against whatever parent it's given. The Export stage (`render-workspace.tsx`) is pinned to the project's literal native resolution; the Preview stage was only CSS-fit (`aspect-ratio` + `height:100%`) to whatever size the window happened to give it. Since every TEXT-layer style (fontSize/strokeWidth/shadowBlur/glow) is a raw, unscaled CSS px value, the SAME 64px font wrapped to one line in the export but two lines in the live preview — confirmed by building a real project (keyframed transform, a CROSSFADE transition, animated/styled text, audio), exporting it, ffmpeg-extracting frames at 4 timestamps, and screenshotting the live preview at those exact same timestamps using the identical seek+video-settle discipline the export pipeline itself uses (SSIM 0.88-0.91 → 0.97 after the fix; the 2-line-vs-1-line difference was visually obvious, not compression noise). Fixed by rendering `CompositorStage` inside a `ResizeObserver`-driven wrapper pinned to native resolution, then CSS `transform: scale()`-ing it down to the on-screen stage size — preview and export now share the exact same rendering math for every absolute-px style, not just text. Also fixed: two keyboard duplicate-handler bugs (ArrowLeft/Right double-firing because `timeline-panel.tsx` and `preview-window.tsx` both registered a handler for the same shortcut; redo-after-undo-of-delete silently no-op'ing, the same "closure captures the original pre-undo id, but undo() recreates the resource under a NEW server id" class already fixed once for a sibling command, now fixed for both remaining instances); the Timeline ruler had no drag-to-scrub at all (only `onClick`, which only fires once at mouseup — a real mousedown→move→move→up sequence left the playhead completely frozen for the whole gesture, confirmed via real recorded mouse events, not single clicks); Transform/Audio properties-panel numeric fields had no local edit buffer, so typing a multi-digit value got corrupted mid-type by the controlled `value` snapping back to the stale pre-commit prop (typing "155" into Scale committed `1`; typing "175" into Volume committed `2`), plus a separate slider drag-release bug where releasing a drag flashed back to the old value for ~1-1.5s before showing the real committed one; dropping an asset directly onto an existing WRONG-KIND track (e.g. a VIDEO asset onto an AUDIO track's own row) skipped the smart track-kind-resolution check entirely and landed there uncorrected, now routed through the same reuse-or-create resolution empty-space drops already use; Mute/Solo/Hide/Lock track toggles had no optimistic update at all (measured live: 1.4-4.0s from click to any visual change; fixed to ~170-300ms via TanStack Query's onMutate/onError/onSettled triad), plus Mute/Hide were missing the active-state accent-color highlight Solo/Lock already had (icon-shape-only, a subtler signal at 14px); and two small design-token cleanups (a hand-picked `text-[11px] leading-[13px]` duplicating the existing `text-micro` token exactly; a leftover pre-migration `border-white/5` where `border-editor-line` was already the established replacement for that exact pattern elsewhere). Track resize-drag and Add-Track were also investigated: resize was already correct (smooth, live, rAF-driven, no bug); Add Track's slow round-trip (1.2-3.9s even warm) was judged too risky to fix via full optimistic insert (the server's `order` field has real prepend/append/collision-retry logic, itself the fix for a prior bug — guessing it client-side risked a worse flash-of-wrong-position glitch), so it got an immediate loading-spinner/disabled-button treatment instead (confirmed live: appears within 10ms of click). A few UI-consistency findings were deliberately left as reported-not-fixed (asset-card hover-border states using ad-hoc `white/20` instead of an established token that doesn't yet exist; `TrackHeader`'s 5 icon buttons being raw `<button>` elements instead of the shared `Button` component every comparable icon-only control elsewhere in the same file uses) since fixing them would mean inventing a new design decision or risking a spacing regression in a tightly-packed row, rather than a safe mechanical token swap — flagged for the founder to prioritize rather than guessed at. Prior entry: Cloud Video Editor — three fixes. (1) Export button clipping: TWO stacked bugs, not one — `editorPrimary`'s own baked-in `min-w-[120px]` survived alongside a call-site `w-20` (different tailwind-merge classGroups, both kept), AND `MotionPrimaryButton` (motion-primitives.tsx) applies its `className` prop to the outer `motion.div` wrapper only, hardcoding `"w-full"` on the actual `<button>` inside — so no size override passed to it EVER reached the real element, the same conflict already found and fixed for the Uploads "Import" button in an earlier pass. Fixed by switching Export to the plain `Button` component directly (losing the hover/tap micro-animation on this one instance, same trade-off already accepted for Import) with explicit `min-w-0` — confirmed via `boundingBox()` it now renders at exactly 80×30px and never overflows the header at 1920/1440/1366px widths. (2) Timeline clip corners: `rounded-editor-button` (14px, shared with real buttons) was giving clips the same rounded-pill look as a button; split into a new dedicated `--radius-editor-clip` token (4px) so future button-radius tuning can never accidentally drag clip corners along with it — registered in `src/lib/utils.ts` per the standing rule added earlier today. (3) **Resizable panel dividers, the biggest addition** — Left/Preview/Right column boundaries and the Preview-row/Timeline boundary are now real drag handles (`panel-resize-handle.tsx`), built with the exact same rAF-batched "direct DOM write during the drag, commit to the store only on release" discipline the Timeline's own clip-drag already established: dragging writes a CSS custom property straight onto `document.documentElement` via `style.setProperty()`, bypassing React entirely mid-gesture, and only pointerup commits the final clamped value into a new `store.tsx` state slice (`leftPanelWidth`/`rightPanelWidth`/`timelineHeight`) that persists to `localStorage` — this app's only existing UI-preference pattern (matching `theme-provider.tsx`'s own precedent; no `UserPreference` DB model exists yet). Verified live end-to-end: typecheck/lint (85 warnings, same baseline)/vitest (3014/3014)/build all clean. Playwright confirmed both new sizes render exactly as set (420px/420px) on a real populated 3-track project (TEXT/VIDEO/AUDIO clips with a real uploaded video+audio pair), and — given this immediately follows an urgent clip-drag regression investigation — explicitly re-checked that drag-move still works correctly after the resize (a real clip drag committed the expected startMs). One test-only flake surfaced during that specific re-check (an identical, already-logged-elsewhere pattern: a single isolated non-commit that did not reproduce on immediate retry, unrelated to this change since it touched only container CSS, nothing in the drag/coordinate code path) — not treated as a new regression. Prior entry: **URGENT regression fix: clip dragging (move + trim-left) was genuinely broken after repeated use, real bug, root-caused and fixed, not a false alarm.** Reported live as "dragging clips, text specifically, does not move at all" — contradicting extensive prior verification, so treated as a serious regression from the start, not dismissed. Investigation: killed all node processes (one orphaned beyond the dev server itself), cleared `.next`, restarted clean, then reproduced with real Playwright mouse-move sequences (not single clicks) against real VIDEO/TEXT/AUDIO clips. First attempt showed inconsistent results (a fresh clip's first drag worked, but immediately-repeated drags on the same clip sometimes showed zero visual movement mid-drag despite the API still committing an intended-looking value) — traced with `elementFromPoint`/computed-style/bounding-box diagnostics at each step, ruling out a pointer-events or z-index/stacking interception first (the most likely candidate given the timing right after several visual-polish passes touched overlay elements — confirmed NOT the cause; every layer at the clip's click point had `pointer-events: auto` and correctly resolved to the clip's own div). **Real root cause, confirmed via direct code read + a targeted before/after repro:** `ClipBlock`'s `onUp()` (move and trim-left only — the two drag modes that change `startMs`) holds the clip's visual position with `el.style.transform = translateX(...)` until the server-confirmed `clip.startMs` lands and the component re-renders with an updated `left`. `width` is inside the JSX-managed `style={{ left, width }}` object, so React itself overwrites it on every render — but `transform` never is (it's set imperatively, outside anything JSX declares), so nothing ever cleared the held offset once `left` genuinely caught up. Every subsequent move/trim-left on the same clip then stacked another uncleared transform on top of the last one: confirmed live via a real 2-drag repro where a clip's rendered position measured exactly 120px off from where its own freshly-committed `startMs` said it should be, after exactly one prior drag — and the live visual during that second drag was completely frozen (0px movement) even though the eventual commit was still numerically correct, an exact match for "I'm dragging it and it isn't moving." The identical pattern existed a second time in `keyframe-track.tsx` (the animatable-properties row under a selected clip), which receives the same live `style.transform` writes from `ClipBlock`'s `syncKeyframeTrack` for the same reason. Fixed both: a `React.useEffect` keyed on `clip.startMs` that resets `el.style.transform = ""` the instant the prop it's derived from (`left`) is already correct, in both `timeline-panel.tsx` (`ClipBlock`) and `keyframe-track.tsx` (added a local `rootElRef` there since it previously only had a callback ref into a shared registry, nothing to read the current node from). Resize-right was never affected (it only ever writes `width`, never `transform`). **Verified with real, recorded mouse-down/move-in-steps/mouse-up sequences, not single clicks, exactly as demanded:** a dedicated stress test ran 5 consecutive move-drags on a VIDEO clip, 5 on a TEXT clip, 3 on an AUDIO clip, and 3 trim-left resizes — all 16 attempts showed the pre-drag position exactly matching the prior commit (zero drift), the correct mid-drag visual delta every time (previously stuck at 0px by the second attempt), and the correct final committed value every time. A separate visual-evidence run captured real before/mid-drag/after-release screenshots of a VIDEO clip's Timeline row (including its keyframe-track row moving in sync) confirming the fix live, not just via API values. One isolated anomaly during that second, looser evidence-capture script (1 of 4 drags across 3 runs failed to commit, despite a correct mid-drag visual) did not reproduce on two immediate retries and doesn't match the reported failure signature (frozen/stuck visual) — logged here for visibility, not chased further, since the actual reported bug's root cause is identified, fixed, and independently confirmed via the much larger, cleaner 16/16 stress test. Verified end-to-end: typecheck/lint (85 warnings, same baseline)/vitest (3014/3014)/build all clean. Per the explicit instruction accompanying this report, no further visual/styling work proceeded until this was confirmed fixed with real evidence — this entry is that confirmation. Prior entry: global button/motion/empty-state pass, the largest single visual change this session. **One shared gradient button variant, not hand-styling.** New `variant="editorPrimary"` on the shared `buttonVariants` cva config (`components/ui/button.tsx`) — additive-only (a brand-new variant key no other call site opts into, so it can't regress the light-themed marketing/dashboard/admin consumers of the same component), gradient derived from `--color-editor-accent` (first stop is the literal token; second stop is that hue mixed ~30% toward black, computed by hand rather than `color-mix()` for reliable cross-browser Tailwind arbitrary-value parsing), `rounded-editor-button` (14px), `h-editor-button-height` (44px), a hover glow shadow. Paired with a new `size="none"` (emits zero sizing classes) so the variant's own baked-in height/padding never has to fight the `size` axis. Applied to the editor's actual primary CTAs — Export (top bar), Upload media (Uploads sidebar), Start Export (export panel — this specifically closes the "still shows the sitewide primary color" limitation flagged in the design-token-foundation entry above), and EmptyState's action-button slot. Deliberately NOT applied to ghost/icon utility buttons (Undo/Redo/History/split/delete/zoom/playback/etc.) — scoped to genuine "the one main thing to click" CTAs, matching the brief's own named examples (Export, Share, Upload media), not a blanket re-skin of every button in the editor. **Framer Motion micro-animations (already a dependency, newly used in the editor), via shared components not scattered props.** New `motion-primitives.tsx`: `MotionPrimaryButton` (wraps the editorPrimary variant in `whileHover{scale:1.03}`/`whileTap{scale:0.97}` at 200ms, mirrors the existing `components/dashboard/gradient-tool-card.tsx` wrap-the-interactive-element pattern already established elsewhere in this app), `MotionCard` (hover-only `scale:1.02` for media-library cards — no `whileTap`, and genuinely two separate DOM nodes rather than one: `motion.div`'s TypeScript types redefine `onDragStart`/`onDrag`/`onDragEnd` for Framer's own pan-gesture system, a real, confirmed compile-time conflict with the native HTML5 `DragEvent` these draggable cards need — the outer motion.div owns the hover animation and box styling, a plain inner `<div>` owns the real `draggable`/`onDragStart` attributes), `MotionPanelFade` (entrance-only opacity fade for panel switches — sidebar section swap and right-panel tab swap; deliberately no exit-fade/crossfade, since the sidebar's structurally-different panels would otherwise briefly coexist and jump the layout), `MotionRailLabel` (fills the one real gap in the rail's existing width transition — the label text itself had no reveal animation before, appearing/disappearing instantly). All respect `useReducedMotion()`, matching this app's own existing `components/shared/fade-in.tsx` convention. Every one of the drag/trim-critical rAF-driven interaction handlers in `timeline-panel.tsx` was left untouched — no Framer Motion anywhere near the pointer-move/pointer-up drag or resize-handle code paths. **New Timeline empty state** — the one genuinely missing empty state found in a full sweep of the editor (every sidebar section already had one): a project with zero clips used to render bare, message-less track lanes. Now shows the shared `EmptyState` (icon, "No clips yet", "Drop video, audio, or image files onto a track, or upload media to get started.", a real "Open media library" action reusing the same `activeSidebarSectionId` store action the Properties Panel's empty state already uses) as a `pointer-events-none` overlay so it never blocks dropping directly onto the real track lanes underneath. No "Generate with AI" anywhere. **Two real bugs found and fixed during live verification, both would have shipped broken without the live pass:** (1) the empty-state overlay's action button was initially unclickable — a track-lane `<div>` rendered later in the DOM sat at the same effective stacking level and covered it; fixed by raising the overlay to `z-20`. (2) after that fix, drag-to-timeline broke — tracing it down found the ENTIRE EmptyState block (icon, title, description, not just the button) had been wrapped in `pointer-events-auto`, silently blocking drops anywhere under that centered text block; fixed by scoping `pointer-events-auto` to just the button itself inside `EmptyState` (a no-op for every other existing EmptyState usage, which was never inside a pointer-events-none ancestor to begin with). **A third, more systemic bug found along the way, in the shared `cn()` utility**, not this pass's own new code: `editorPrimary`'s `rounded-editor-button` was silently losing to the base `buttonVariants` string's `rounded-md` — computed style showed 8px, not 14px. Root cause: `src/lib/utils.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge()` config only ever registered custom `font-size`/`text-color` token groups (its own comment already explains why this matters), never `rounded`/`shadow`, so tailwind-merge couldn't recognize `rounded-editor-button` and `rounded-md` as the same conflicting group — both classes survived into the DOM, and whichever's stylesheet rule Tailwind happened to generate later silently won. Fixed by registering `rounded-editor-button`/`rounded-editor-card` under `rounded` and `shadow-editor-card` under `shadow` in that same config — this was a latent, app-wide gap (not editor-scoped), only now surfaced because `editorPrimary` is the first place this session combined a custom radius token with the shared Button's own `cva` base classes in one string. **Standing engineering rules** (apply to every future milestone): never break existing APIs · never duplicate business logic · reuse existing services · every feature ships type-safe with validation, error handling, and unit tests where applicable · every milestone ends with build+lint+typecheck+verification · keep the provider abstraction intact and provider-agnostic · keep the credit engine generic · keep all pricing/credits/limits admin-configurable · **any properties-panel input bound to clip/track/project data must be a controlled input reflecting live store state — never `defaultValue`/uncontrolled** (Module 7 Bug #1: `defaultValue` inputs silently stuck on stale values after any external change — a caption-template apply, undo/redo — that didn't originate from typing into that same field; applies to Module 8's volume/pan/pitch/speed controls and every future properties-panel field) · **headless Chromium does not reliably reproduce native browser chrome (OS-style scrollbars/arrow buttons, native form controls, other OS-level UI) — a headless Playwright screenshot can look fixed while a real Chrome-on-Windows window still shows the old broken rendering** (2026-07-15: a "thin scrollbar" CSS fix looked correct in headless verification but still showed native arrow-button scrollbars in a real browser); any visual verification touching native browser chrome needs either a real non-headless browser check or a `getComputedStyle`/property-level assertion (e.g. asserting `scrollbar-width: none` is actually computed, not just that the class is present in markup) instead of trusting a headless screenshot alone, 12. **any NEW custom `@theme` token (font-size, color, radius, shadow, spacing, or any other Tailwind-mergeable property) added to `globals.css` must also be registered in `src/lib/utils.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge()` config the same day** — tailwind-merge can't infer a custom token's classGroup from its name alone, so an unregistered token combined with ANY other class sharing the same utility prefix (`text-`, `h-`, `rounded-`, etc.) gets silently treated as one conflicting group, with tailwind-merge keeping only whichever class came last and dropping the other from the DOM entirely — no error, no warning, it just renders at the wrong size/color with nothing to grep for (found 3 separate times in this codebase already: radius/shadow on 2026-07-13, font-size/color again on 2026-07-15 for the editor's own token scale, and height on 2026-07-15 for `editor-button-height`); `src/lib/utils.test.ts` now has regression tests for this exact pattern — treat this as a standing category to check for in every future visual pass, not a one-off · update this file after every milestone.

## 1. Completed Features

### Milestone 1 — Design system & landing page
- Tailwind v4 + shadcn (radix-nova preset) design tokens, full marketing site (`src/app/(marketing)`).

### Milestone 2 — Authentication
- NextAuth v5, two providers: phone OTP (Credentials) and Google OAuth.
- Dev-mode OTP (`devOtp` returned in response + logged) when `MSG91_AUTH_KEY` is unset; per-phone (3/hr) and per-IP (20/hr) rate limits — verified live, including the rate limit actually triggering.
- Onboarding flow gated by `Profile.onboardingCompletedAt`; edge middleware (`src/middleware.ts` → `lib/auth/config.ts`) redirects incomplete profiles, and now also gates `/admin/*` by `role === "ADMIN"`.
- 5 free signup credits granted through the Credit Engine (amount is admin-configurable, not hardcoded).

### Milestone 3 — AI video generation core
- Template library (10 verticals seeded), brief → AI script (LLM Provider) → user edits → render queue.
- Postgres-backed render queue (`lib/queue/queue.ts`) with atomic conditional-UPDATE claiming; in-process worker (dev) and a secret-gated internal cron route (production).

### Milestone 4 — Provider abstraction, monetization & admin panel
- **6 provider abstractions**, each with a vendor-agnostic interface + Mock adapter + one real adapter, selected at runtime via `getXProvider()` factories reading admin config:
  | Category | Real adapter | Vendor credential(s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | LLM | OpenAI (`gpt-4o-mini`, REST) | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
  | Image | OpenAI Images (`gpt-image-1`, REST) | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
  | Voice | ElevenLabs (REST) | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` |
  | Video | Replicate (REST, polling) | `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN`, `REPLICATE_MODEL_VERSION` |
  | Storage | AWS S3 / Cloudflare R2 / MinIO (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`) | `S3_*` |
  | Payment | Razorpay (`razorpay` SDK) | `RAZORPAY_*` |
- **Verified boundary:** zero vendor SDK/REST calls or vendor env var reads outside `src/lib/providers/*` (grepped repo-wide). The one unavoidable exception is `/api/billing/webhook` reading the `x-razorpay-signature` header name — see Known Issues.
- **Admin-configurable system** (`src/lib/admin/config.ts`): Zod-validated registry, `SystemConfig` DB table, 30s in-process cache, self-describing (`inputType`/`options`) so the admin UI renders generically with zero per-field code.
- **Credit Engine** (`src/lib/credits/engine.ts`): credits as discrete `CreditLot` rows (signup/purchased/subscription/promotional/referral), admin-configurable consumption order (`EXPIRING_FIRST`/`FREE_FIRST`/`PURCHASED_FIRST`), row-locked atomic multi-lot debit, `expireStaleLots()` maintenance job. **All 3 consumption orders + expiry + insufficient-credit rejection verified with a dedicated test harness — 14/14 assertions pass.**
- **Download Service** (`src/lib/downloads/download-service.ts`): the only path to the watermark-free master asset. Validates, in order: existing entitlement (free re-download) → daily rate limit → active subscription with remaining monthly downloads → credits. **Verified live:** free unlimited rendering, first download charges exactly 1 credit, re-download is free and re-signs the URL, subscription downloads bypass credits entirely, admin-tunable rate limit actually blocks the Nth download.
- **Monetization**: Pay Per Download (credit packages) and Monthly Subscription both implemented; `PaymentIntent` tracks every checkout from creation to vendor confirmation; `lib/billing/fulfillment.ts` is the single vendor-agnostic settlement function called by both the real (signature-verified) Razorpay webhook and the Mock-mode confirm endpoint — idempotent (verified: double-confirm correctly rejected with 409).
- **Admin panel** (`/admin/*`, role-gated both at the edge and server-side): provider selection, download/credit rules, pricing plans + credit packages CRUD. All API routes verified live (GET/PATCH/POST against a running server).
- Preview (free, unlimited, watermarked, 480p/720p, streaming only) vs. master (paid, full-HD, no watermark, signed-URL-only) asset split, both generated per render via two provider calls.

### Security hardening from the production audit
- **Fixed a signature-verification bug** in both `storage/sign.ts` and `razorpay.provider.ts`: `Buffer.from(str, "hex")` silently truncates at the first non-hex character instead of throwing, so a signature string with valid-prefix + garbage-suffix decoded to the same bytes as a correct signature and passed `timingSafeEqual`. Both now reject any signature whose string length doesn't exactly match the expected hex length before ever constructing a Buffer. Confirmed exploitable via direct HTTP test before the fix (403 → was previously 307/success); confirmed closed after.
  - Practical impact was low (forging a *new* signature still requires the secret), but it was a real verification-logic flaw, not just a style issue.

### Milestone 5 — Payment loop closed (2026-06-27)
- **`POST /api/videos/[id]/purchase`**: opens a `ONE_TIME_DOWNLOAD` PaymentIntent + vendor order for a single video's master download — no credit package or subscription required. Reuses the already-seeded "Pay Per Download" `PricingPlan` row as its price source (admin-configurable from `/admin/pricing`, no new config key added) and the existing `getReadyProject`/`findExistingDownload` checks from `download-service.ts` rather than duplicating them. Rejects with `ERR_NOT_CONFIGURED` (409) while the plan's price is still ₹0, and `ERR_INVALID_STATE` (409) if the user already owns the download.
- **`GET /api/billing/payment-intents/[id]`**: read-only status poll for the client after a real vendor's checkout widget reports success. Fulfilment itself still only ever happens through the signature-verified webhook or the mock-confirm endpoint — this route never settles anything.
- **Real Razorpay `checkout.js` widget** (`src/lib/payments/checkout-client.ts`): the one client-side file allowed to know about a specific vendor's widget, mirroring `razorpay.provider.ts` being the one server-side file allowed to import the SDK. `billing-actions.tsx` (credits page) and `video-detail-client.tsx` (one-time purchase) both branch on `checkoutConfig.provider`: `mock` keeps the existing instant-confirm path, `razorpay` opens the widget and polls the new payment-intent route until it leaves `PENDING`.
- **Subscription cancellation**: `POST /api/billing/subscriptions/cancel` sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd` (cancel-at-period-end, the standard SaaS default — no proration needed) and calls the configured Payment Provider's new `cancelSubscription()` method so a real vendor's recurring billing actually stops (Mock is a no-op). Surfaced as a "Cancel" button on the credits page next to the active plan.
- **Provider abstraction extended, not bypassed**: added `cancelSubscription(input: CancelSubscriptionInput): Promise<void>` to the `PaymentProvider` interface with both Mock and Razorpay implementations — no provider-specific branching anywhere outside `lib/providers/payment/*`.
- **Bug fix found and closed before it could bite production**: `fulfillment.ts` was storing the *payment* id in `Subscription.providerRef` instead of the vendor's *subscription* id, which would have silently broken cancellation against a real vendor (Mock mode masked it since cancellation there is a no-op regardless). Fixed and verified live — `providerRef` now correctly holds the vendor subscription id end-to-end.
- **Unit tests added** (`vitest`, new dev dependency, `npm test`): `pay-per-download.test.ts` (price-guard), `mock.provider.test.ts` (no-op cancel), `razorpay.provider.test.ts` (webhook signature verify — including a regression test for the hex-truncation bypass fixed in the audit), `checkout-client.test.ts` (unsupported-provider rejection, payment-intent polling). 12/12 pass.
- **Verified live end-to-end** against a real Postgres-backed dev server in mock-provider mode: purchase → poll (PENDING) → mock-confirm → poll (PAID) → re-purchase correctly blocked (already owns it) → download succeeds with zero credit deduction (`method: "ONE_TIME_PURCHASE"`); subscribe → `providerRef` correctly populated → cancel → `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true` persisted → re-cancel correctly blocked (409).

### Milestone 6 — AI Generation Engine (2026-06-27)
A unified, provider-agnostic orchestration layer (`src/lib/generation/`) now sits in front of all 4 generation categories (LLM/Image/Voice/Video), adding failover, retry, timeout, cost tracking, health monitoring, and usage analytics **once**, generically — none of that is duplicated per category or per provider.
- **Common provider interface**: `GenerationProvider` (`id`, `category`) is now the base every category-specific interface (`LLMProvider`, `ImageProvider`, `VoiceProvider`, `VideoProvider`) extends, and every adapter (Mock and real) implements it. The category-specific method (`generate`/`render`) is unchanged — existing call shapes weren't broken, the common surface was added underneath them.
- **The Generation Engine** (`lib/generation/engine.ts`, `runGeneration()`): the single function every category's request goes through.
  - **Failover**: providers are tried in the admin-configured priority order; on exhausted retries it moves to the next one.
  - **Retry**: configurable max attempts per provider with linear backoff (`GENERATION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`/`_BACKOFF_MS`).
  - **Timeout**: per-category timeout races every attempt (`GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS_LLM`/`_IMAGE`/`_VOICE`/`_VIDEO`).
  - **Health monitoring**: a `ProviderHealth` row per (category, provider) — a circuit breaker that marks a provider DOWN after N consecutive failures (`GENERATION_HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`) and skips it for a cooldown window (`GENERATION_HEALTH_COOLDOWN_MS`), but never lets the chain go fully empty (a total-outage blip still gets one attempt).
  - **Cost tracking**: vendor cost (USD) is computed per successful call from admin-configurable per-provider rate cards (`GENERATION_COST_RATES` — unit is one of `PER_CALL`/`PER_1K_TOKENS`/`PER_1K_CHARS`/`PER_SECOND`/`PER_IMAGE`). This is internal vendor-cost analytics, deliberately separate from user-facing pricing (`PricingPlan`/`CreditPackage`) — it does not change what a user is charged.
  - **Usage analytics**: one `GenerationLog` row per provider *attempt* (not per logical request), so a request that retries then fails over produces multiple rows attributing latency/cost/outcome to the vendor that actually ran.
  - All of the above (retry/timeout/health-check/cost/log functions) are dependency-injected with real DB-backed defaults — unit-tested by substituting fakes, no Postgres required for the orchestration logic itself.
- **Provider priority is admin-configurable**, not a single-select: `PROVIDER_LLM_PRIORITY`/`PROVIDER_IMAGE_PRIORITY`/`PROVIDER_VOICE_PRIORITY`/`PROVIDER_VIDEO_PRIORITY` replace the old single-enum `PROVIDER_LLM`-style keys with ordered arrays, edited from `/admin/providers` as a comma-separated list (new generic `string_list` admin-form input type) — a single-element array behaves exactly like the old config. The valid ids for each list come from one shared constant per category (`LLM_PROVIDER_IDS` etc. in each `lib/providers/*/index.ts`) consumed by both the factory's switch statement and the config schema, so there's one source of truth, not two.
- **New provider adapters** (all credentials env-var-only, never admin/DB-stored):
  | Category | New adapter | Vendor credential(s) |
  |---|---|---|
  | LLM | Gemini (`gemini-1.5-flash`, REST) | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, optional `GEMINI_MODEL` |
  | LLM | Self-hosted (generic REST contract — Ollama/vLLM/custom) | `SELF_HOSTED_LLM_URL`, optional `SELF_HOSTED_LLM_API_KEY` |
  | Image | Flux (Black Forest Labs, via Replicate predictions) | `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` (shared with Video), `FLUX_MODEL_VERSION` |

  "ChatGPT Images" from the milestone brief is the existing `OpenAIImagesProvider` (`gpt-image-1`) — not duplicated under a new name, just folded into the Image priority list.
- **Self-hosted models are a first-class seam, not an afterthought**: `SelfHostedLLMProvider` demonstrates the pattern (env-var base URL + optional bearer token, minimal JSON contract) a future self-hosted Image/Voice/Video adapter would follow — same shape, different category.
- **Wired into the existing pipeline, not bolted alongside it**: `/api/videos` (script generation) and the queue processor (`lib/queue/processor.ts`, preview render / master render / thumbnail / voiceover — superseded in Milestone 7 by the per-scene processor in `lib/render/pipeline.ts`) now call `lib/generation/{llm,image,voice,video}.ts` instead of a provider factory directly. Storage upload and credit charging are completely unchanged — rendering is still free, credits are still spent only at download time; the engine only changes *how* a generation call is made, not the business rules around it.
- **Admin UI**: new `/admin/generation` page — retry/timeout/health/cost-rate policy (generic `AdminConfigForm` against the new `generation_policy` config category, including a new `json` input type for the cost-rate table), a live provider-health table, a 24h usage-analytics table, and a recent-failures feed. Backed by `GET /api/admin/generation/health` and `GET /api/admin/generation/analytics`.
- **Unit tests** (24 new, `vitest`): `engine.test.ts` (9 cases — success, failover, per-provider retry, all-providers-failed, empty-chain, health-skip, all-unavailable-fallback, timeout-triggers-failover, cost-computed-from-usage), `health.test.ts` (the circuit-breaker state machine — HEALTHY→DEGRADED→DOWN, cooldown expiry, re-trip-on-cooldown-failure), `cost.test.ts` (all 5 rate units + zero-rate/no-usage edge cases). All against pure, DB-free functions via the engine's dependency-injection seams.
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server: script generation through the engine (mock chain) logs a `SUCCESS` row and a `HEALTHY` health row; setting `PROVIDER_LLM_PRIORITY` to `["openai","mock"]` with no `OPENAI_API_KEY` configured produces exactly the expected failover — 2 failed attempts against `openai` (recorded `DEGRADED`, consecutive failures 2 of threshold 3) logged with the real configuration error message, then a successful fallback to `mock`; a full render (video preview+master, thumbnail) through the engine completes normally and logs `VIDEO`/`IMAGE` usage rows correctly attributed.

### Milestone 7 — Production Video Generation Pipeline (2026-06-27)
A `VideoProject` no longer renders as one opaque job — it's decomposed into independently-rendered `Scene`s that render in parallel, retry individually, cache individually, and merge only once every scene succeeds.

- **Scene Engine** (`src/lib/scenes/engine.ts`): deterministically splits the AI-generated script into scenes by its existing `[HOOK]/[BODY]/[CTA]` section markers (falling back to paragraph breaks, then to a single scene for unstructured text — never zero scenes for a non-empty script), and allocates each scene a duration proportional to its text length out of the template's total duration (with a floor per scene, last scene absorbing the rounding remainder). Each `Scene` has `prompt`, `negativePrompt`, `durationSeconds`, `imageKey`/`videoKey`/`voiceKey`/`subtitleKey` (separate storage keys, never commingled), `subtitleText`, `backgroundMusicUrl`, `transition` (`CUT`/`FADE`/`DISSOLVE`/`SLIDE`), and `status` (`PENDING`/`RENDERING`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`). Subtitles are a deterministic WebVTT formatter (`lib/scenes/subtitle.ts`) over the scene's own script line — no speech-to-text provider needed. Background music is a static, admin-configurable default track URL applied at scene-creation time — not an AI-generated artifact, no new provider category.
- **Render Queue, reused not duplicated**: `RenderJob` gained a nullable `sceneId` — a scene-render job (`sceneId` set) and the final merge job (`sceneId` null) flow through the exact same `claimNextJob()`/`completeJob()`/`failJob()` atomic-claim functions, distinguished only by a dispatch check in `lib/render/pipeline.ts`. No second job table, no second claim mechanism.
- **Real parallel rendering**: `claimNextJob()`'s atomic conditional `UPDATE...WHERE status='PENDING'` was always safe for concurrent callers — Milestone 7 is the first time that's exploited. `drainQueue(concurrency)` (`lib/render/pipeline.ts`) runs N concurrent claim-and-process loops (`RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY`, admin-configurable, default 3); both the in-process dev worker and the `/api/internal/queue/process` cron route call it instead of draining sequentially.
- **Each scene renders once, at final quality** — the merge step (not the scene step) is what produces both the watermarked preview and the clean master from the same already-rendered scene clips, so a scene is never generated twice and vendor cost is paid once per scene, not twice (an efficiency win over the pre-Milestone-7 design, which rendered the whole project twice).
- **Automatic merge-after-all-succeed, race-safe**: `VideoProject.mergeQueued` is an atomic guard (`updateMany({mergeQueued: false} -> {mergeQueued: true})`) so when several scenes complete within milliseconds of each other under parallel rendering, only one of them wins the right to enqueue the merge job — the same atomic-conditional-update pattern already established elsewhere in this codebase, reused rather than reinvented.
- **Merge is provider-routed, not bolted on**: `VideoProvider` gained `mergeScenes(req): Promise<VideoRenderResult>`; `lib/generation/video.ts`'s new `mergeSceneVideos()` wrapper routes it through the exact same `runGeneration()` engine as `renderVideo()` — merge gets failover/retry/timeout/cost/health/analytics for free, zero new orchestration code. `MockVideoProvider.mergeScenes()` fakes a real concatenation (proportional simulated latency, canned output) so the full pipeline is exercisable end-to-end without ffmpeg; `ReplicateVideoProvider.mergeScenes()` honestly throws (Replicate's text-to-video API has no generic clip-concatenation capability) rather than faking support.
- **Failed scenes retry automatically, then surface individually**: a scene render failure resets the scene to `PENDING` and retries (up to admin-configurable `RENDER_MAX_ATTEMPTS`) before the job is marked terminal; once a scene is terminally `FAILED` and no scene is still in flight, the whole project flips to `FAILED` — but the other scenes stay `COMPLETED` (cached), so `POST /api/videos/[id]/scenes/rerender-failed` only re-renders what actually failed, then lets the same finalize logic re-queue the merge once everything succeeds. Verified live: editing a failed scene's prompt (`PATCH .../scenes/[sceneId]`, allowed only while `FAILED`) then calling rerender-failed re-rendered only that one scene and the project re-completed with the other two scenes' timestamps untouched.
- **Pause/Resume/Cancel**: pausing bulk-flips a project's not-yet-claimed (`PENDING`) `RenderJob`s to `PAUSED` (`claimNextJob()`'s `WHERE status='PENDING'` already excludes them — no claim-query changes needed); resuming flips them back. Cancelling extends the existing `POST /api/videos/[id]/cancel` route (still handles `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` exactly as before) to also cover `QUEUED`/`RENDERING`/`PAUSED`, cancelling not-yet-claimed jobs and `PENDING` scenes. None of this preempts a job already `PROCESSING` — that job finishes naturally, a documented limitation rather than a silent gap. Verified live: a project paused mid-render stayed frozen across two full worker poll cycles (6+s), then progressed to completion immediately on resume; a cancelled project's scenes stayed `CANCELLED` with zero further worker activity afterward.
- **Live progress**: `GET /api/videos/[id]/scenes` (one-shot list + computed progress) and `GET /api/videos/[id]/scenes/stream` (Server-Sent Events — pushes diffs to the client instead of the client polling). Honest about the trade-off: the SSE endpoint still polls the DB server-side every 1.5s under the hood, it's not true pub/sub push — same kind of documented simplicity-over-infrastructure call as `lib/admin/config.ts`'s in-process-only cache.
- **Storage**: every scene artifact (image/video/voice/subtitle) gets its own key under `scenes/{sceneId}/...`, the merged outputs stay under `videos/{projectId}/...` exactly as before — zero changes to the `StorageProvider` interface, pure reuse. (Mock-mode's `uploadFromUrl` passes external mock URLs through as-is rather than re-hosting at the requested key — a pre-existing mock simplification, not new this milestone; `S3StorageProvider` genuinely fetches and re-uploads to the exact requested key.)
- **Signed downloads need no changes**: the merge step still produces a `masterVideoUrl` *key* (never a fetchable URL) exactly as the pre-Milestone-7 pipeline did, so the existing Download Service / `getSignedDownloadUrl()` path works unmodified. Verified live end-to-end against a real signed URL.
- **Rendering analytics, history, and an admin dashboard**: `lib/render/analytics.ts` (`getQueueSnapshot()`, `getSceneRenderStats()`, `getRenderHistory()`) backs two new admin routes (`GET /api/admin/render/queue`, `GET /api/admin/render/history`) and a new `/admin/render` page — queue depth/in-flight counts, a 24h scene-render stats panel, a render-history table covering both scene and merge jobs, plus the render-policy config (`RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY`, `RENDER_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `DEFAULT_NEGATIVE_PROMPT`, `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_MUSIC_URL`) editable via the existing generic `AdminConfigForm` — same pattern as `/admin/generation`, no new UI primitives. `GenerationLog` gained a nullable `sceneId` so per-scene generation cost/latency is attributable, not just per-project.
- **Frontend**: `video-detail-client.tsx` now mounts a `SceneProgressPanel` (SSE-driven) while a project is `QUEUED`/`RENDERING`/`PAUSED`/`FAILED` — per-scene status badges, a progress bar, and the Pause/Resume/Cancel/Re-render-failed buttons, each gated to the project states where they're valid. `VideoStatusBadge` gained a `PAUSED` entry.
- **Unit tests added** (16 new, `vitest`): `lib/scenes/engine.test.ts` (script splitting — markers/paragraphs/single-scene/empty/maxScenes cap; duration allocation — proportional, single-scene, floor-respecting; progress computation), `lib/scenes/subtitle.test.ts` (WebVTT formatting — timestamps, hours/minutes rollover, trimming, zero-duration floor). 52/52 total tests pass.
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server, full pipeline end-to-end: project created → script generated → 3 scenes decomposed (proportional durations) → all 3 rendered in parallel by the worker (each with its own image/video/voice/subtitle artifact and a real voiceover-driven duration override when the template has `includeVoiceover`) → merge auto-queued exactly once (`mergeQueued` race-guard) → project `COMPLETED` → signed download URL minted successfully. Separately verified: pause freezes progress across 2+ worker poll cycles then resumes correctly; cancel stops a render and stays cancelled; a simulated scene failure + prompt edit + `rerender-failed` re-rendered only that scene and the project re-completed; the SSE stream emits an `update` then a terminal `done` event; the admin render queue/history/config endpoints and the `/admin/render` page all return correct live data; `GenerationLog` rows correctly attribute `scene_render`/`scene_image`/`voiceover`/`merge_preview`/`merge_master` operations to their scenes (30 logs with `sceneId` set, matching exactly 10 scenes × 3 generation calls each).

### Milestone 8 — AI Content Studio (2026-06-28)
The user-facing pre-render workspace: scenes are now created right after script generation (not at render-confirm time), so there's something editable before the user ever commits to rendering. Four architectural decisions were made up front (via direct user confirmation, all "recommended" options): scenes created at script-ready time, a dedicated `Asset` table, project-level version snapshots (not per-field diffs), and collaboration as schema-scaffolding only.

- **Scene lifecycle moved earlier**: `Scene` rows are now created immediately after AI script generation (`SceneStatus.DRAFT`, new first enum value) instead of at render-confirmation time — see `createScenesFromScript()` called from `POST /api/videos`. `POST /api/videos/[id]/render` no longer creates scenes; it now 409s with `ERR_INVALID_STATE` if a project somehow has zero scenes, and otherwise just claims the status transition and calls the unchanged `enqueueRenderableScenes()` (its existing `status: {not: "COMPLETED"}` query already covers flipping `DRAFT` → `PENDING`, no changes needed there).
- **Script Studio** (`lib/ai/script-studio.ts`): Rewrite/Expand/Shorten/Translate/Hook-generator/CTA-generator are all just different prompt strings over the *same* `generateScript()` call (requirement to keep using the existing Generation Engine, satisfied trivially — no new generation call sites). `POST /api/videos/[id]/script/transform` and `.../script/variants` are **generate-only**: they return the candidate text for the user to review, exactly like the original script generation already does — applying a result reuses the existing `PATCH /api/videos/[id]` script-edit route rather than adding a second save path. `MockLLMProvider` was extended (marker-based: an `"Original:\n"` tag plus keyword/phrasing detection) to simulate distinguishable rewrite/expand/shorten/translate/hook/cta output without a real LLM — real adapters need no changes since they already follow arbitrary prompt instructions.
- **Prompt Studio**: `Scene.imagePrompt`/`Scene.videoPrompt` (nullable, fall back to `Scene.prompt` when unset) let a user fine-tune the image/video prompt independently of the narration script per scene. `PromptRecord` logs every prompt a user explicitly edits or generates (script transforms, scene image/video/negative-prompt edits) — distinct from `GenerationLog`, which logs vendor-attempt telemetry, not user-authored text. `PromptTemplate` (user-owned) is a reusable saved prompt, full CRUD via `/api/prompt-templates`. **Scope cut, by design**: no standalone "live preview generation" in Prompt Studio — every generation call still flows exclusively through the existing render pipeline (Requirement 11, satisfied without a new generation call site).
- **Scene Editor**: drag-and-drop reorder (`@dnd-kit/core`+`/sortable`+`/utilities`, new dependency) via `POST /api/videos/[id]/scenes/reorder`; add/delete scene (`lib/scenes/engine.ts`'s new `appendScene()`/`deleteSceneAndRenormalize()`, the latter re-normalizing `order` to a contiguous `0..n-1` sequence so the `@@unique([videoProjectId, order])` constraint and the merge step's ordering both stay correct); duration/transition/voice/background-music/subtitle editing via a widened `PATCH /api/videos/[id]/scenes/[sceneId]` (now allowed on `DRAFT` scenes too, not just `FAILED` as in Milestone 7); thumbnail selection (`VideoProject.thumbnailSceneId`, a plain string field rather than a relation, to avoid dual-relation complexity) via `POST /api/videos/[id]/thumbnail`.
- **Voice selection**: new admin config `AVAILABLE_VOICES` (id/label/gender array) backs the picker; `Scene.voiceId` threads into a new optional `VoiceGenerateRequest.voiceId`; `ElevenLabsVoiceProvider` maps known studio voice ids to real ElevenLabs voice ids via `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID_BY_STUDIO_VOICE`, falling back to the existing per-language default when unset or unmapped — `MockVoiceProvider` needs no changes. **Background music**: new admin config `BACKGROUND_MUSIC_LIBRARY` (id/label/url array) backs the picker; `Scene.backgroundMusicUrl` (already existed from Milestone 7) becomes independently user-editable.
- **Asset Library**: new `Asset` table (one row per generated/uploaded file, linked to user + optionally project/scene), populated *additively* from the upload calls already in `lib/render/pipeline.ts` — never a second upload path. `lib/assets/service.ts`'s `recordAsset()`/`listAssets()` resolve a storage key to a public URL at read time via the Storage Provider, mirroring how `Scene`/`VideoProject` already store keys, not URLs. "Music" has no per-user rows — `GET /api/assets` always includes the admin-configured `BACKGROUND_MUSIC_LIBRARY` list alongside the user's own assets for a unified library UI.
- **Autosave / version history / undo-redo**: "autosave" needed no special backend code — the Studio's granular routes (scene `PATCH`, reorder, script `PATCH`) already persist every edit immediately; `recordProjectVersion()` is called at the end of each, storing a full JSON snapshot (`ProjectVersion`) and deduping against the most recent one (`JSON.stringify` comparison) so no-op saves don't grow the table. `restoreVersion()` only works pre-render (`DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY`) since it fully deletes-and-recreates `Scene` rows from the snapshot — enforced by an atomic conditional update, not a separate check-then-act. Undo/redo (`use-undo-redo.ts`) is explicitly a **client-side, in-memory command stack** — no backend endpoint — scoped to text-field edits only (script text; scene prompt/imagePrompt/videoPrompt/negativePrompt/subtitleText), deliberately not covering structural operations (add/delete/reorder scene) which already have their own explicit, visible actions.
- **Collaboration scaffolding**: `ProjectCollaborator` (`userId`, `videoProjectId`, `role` — `VIEWER`/`EDITOR`/`OWNER`) exists in the schema only, per the user's explicit choice — no invite UI, no API routes, no realtime sync. `VideoProject.userId` ownership remains the only real authority today; this table is groundwork for a future milestone, not yet enforced or exposed anywhere.
- **Frontend**: new `/videos/[id]/studio` page (server component fetches project/scenes/voice-config, redirects to `/videos/[id]` for any non-`DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` status — Studio is purely the pre-render workspace) with four tabs (Script Studio, Scene Editor, Asset Library, History) built on the existing design system (`Tabs`/`Button`/`Select`/`Textarea`/`Badge` from `components/ui`). The `/create` wizard was simplified from 4 steps to 2 (Template, Brief) — script review/edit and render confirmation moved entirely into the Studio; submitting the brief now redirects straight to `/videos/[id]/studio`. `/videos/[id]` (the post-render progress/result page) redirects to the Studio for any project still `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY`.
- **Unit tests added** (12 new, `vitest`): `lib/ai/script-studio.test.ts` — transform-prompt construction (tone clause, expand/shorten/translate, language defaulting), variants-prompt construction, and the numbered-list parser (numbered, parenthesis-numbered, unnumbered fallback, count cap). 64/64 total tests pass. (Scene Engine's new `appendScene()`/`deleteSceneAndRenormalize()`/`reorderScenes()` and the versioning module's snapshot/dedupe logic are DB-bound, not pure — consistent with this codebase's existing convention of unit-testing only DB-free logic, they're covered by the live verification pass below instead.)
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server, full Studio lifecycle end-to-end: project created → 3 scenes auto-created `DRAFT` + first `ProjectVersion` snapshot recorded → all 6 Script Studio operations (rewrite/expand/shorten/translate/hook/cta) returned distinguishable Mock output → applying a rewritten script via the existing `PATCH` route correctly grew version history → scene `PATCH` (imagePrompt/videoPrompt/voiceId/transition/duration) persisted and logged matching `PromptRecord` rows → add scene → drag-and-drop reorder (`POST .../scenes/reorder`) → delete scene with order renormalization confirmed → thumbnail set to a non-first scene → render confirmed and completed, with the merge step's thumbnail correctly preferring the chosen scene over `scenes[0]`, `Asset` rows recorded for every scene image/video/voice plus the project preview/master/thumbnail outputs, and (verified separately, by temporarily enabling `includeVoiceover` on a test template) `voiceId` correctly threaded into the voiceover generation call and a `VOICE`-kind `Asset` recorded. Also verified: version restore on a pre-render project correctly reverted the script to an earlier snapshot; scene edits, thumbnail changes, and re-render are all correctly rejected with `ERR_INVALID_STATE` (409) once a project reaches `COMPLETED`; prompt-template create/list/delete round-tripped correctly including a 404 on double-delete.

### Milestone 9 — Professional Video Editor (2026-06-28)
A full browser-based, multi-track video editor sits **additively** on top of the Scene Engine/render pipeline from Milestones 7-8 — every prior milestone's models, queue, and Generation Engine call sites are unchanged. Four architectural decisions were made up front (via direct user confirmation, all "recommended" options): a new Track/Clip layer rather than touching `Scene`, Export routed through an extended Mock compositor (a real compositor stays documented future work, not built this milestone), a new word-level Caption model additive alongside `subtitleText`/`subtitleKey`, and collaboration scope limited to schema/architecture only (still no realtime sync).

- **Timeline Engine** (`lib/timeline/engine.ts`): new `Track` (`kind`: `VIDEO`/`IMAGE`/`TEXT`/`CAPTION`/`STICKER`/`AUDIO`/`MUSIC`, `order`, `isMuted`, `isHidden`) and `Clip` (`startMs`/`durationMs`/`trimStartMs`, optional `sceneId`/`assetId`, `content` JSON for TEXT/STICKER/CAPTION payloads) models reference `Scene`/`Asset` by id — the Scene Engine and render pipeline never know the Timeline exists. `ensureTimeline()` idempotently seeds VIDEO/AUDIO/MUSIC/CAPTION tracks from a project's current scenes the first time the Editor is opened (AUDIO/MUSIC clips only where a scene actually has a voiceover/music). All clip math — `splitClipSpan`, `canMergeClips`, `mergeClipSpans`, `duplicateClipSpan` — is pure and unit-tested; `trimStartMs` is the offset into the *source* media a clip's visible window begins at, so Resize/Split never need to re-render anything. `replaceSceneSource()` (AI Editing's "Replace scene") repoints every clip referencing a scene at a different scene/asset in one DB-only pointer swap.
- **Captions Engine** (`lib/captions/engine.ts`): a genuinely new `CaptionBlock`/`CaptionWord` model, additive alongside the existing `Scene.subtitleText`/`subtitleKey`. `generateWordTimings()` is a deterministic, proportional-to-character-length auto-timing split (same pattern as Milestone 7's `allocateSceneDurations()`) — no speech-to-text provider needed. Editing or regenerating captions rebuilds the scene's *actual* rendered subtitle artifact via a new `buildWordLevelVtt()` (`lib/scenes/subtitle.ts`), so Caption Editor edits reach the render pipeline, not just bookkeeping.
- **Export System as a new Generation Engine operation, not a parallel pipeline**: `VideoProvider` gained `composeTimeline(req): Promise<VideoRenderResult>`; `lib/generation/video.ts`'s new `composeTimeline()` wrapper routes it through the exact same `runGeneration()` engine as `render()`/`mergeScenes()` — failover/retry/timeout/cost/health/analytics for free, zero new orchestration code. `MockVideoProvider.composeTimeline()` fakes a real multi-track composite (simulated latency proportional to clip count/duration, canned output); `ReplicateVideoProvider.composeTimeline()` honestly throws — the exact same "Mock fakes it, real adapter documents the gap" pattern already established for `mergeScenes()`. New `Export` model (`resolution` 720p/1080p/4K, `codec` H264/H265/VP9, `watermark`, `status`, `outputKey`) plus `lib/export/service.ts`'s `createExport()`.
