- **Background Rendering reuses the existing Render Queue, not a second one**: Export jobs and the new "Regenerate voice" AI-editing action are `RenderJob` rows tagged `payload: {kind: "export"|"regen_voice", ...}`, created via direct `tx.renderJob.create()` (the same bypass-`enqueueJob()`-for-custom-payloads pattern `rerenderFailedScenes()`/`enqueueRenderableScenes()` already used). `lib/render/pipeline.ts`'s `processNextJob()` now checks `payload.kind` *before* its original `sceneId`-truthy/merge fallback — existing scene/merge jobs have `payload: {}` (kind `undefined`), so this is purely additive and the original dispatch is byte-for-byte unchanged for them. New `processExportJob()` resolves every Clip's source URL (Scene artifact, Asset, or a raw `content.sourceUrl` for a Stock pick with no Asset row — the same "static URL reference, no Asset row" pattern `Scene.backgroundMusicUrl` already used) and calls `composeTimeline()`. New `processRegenVoiceJob()` redoes only the voiceover, deliberately leaving `durationSeconds` untouched (the scene's video/image were already rendered at the original length).
- **AI Editing decomposition**: "Change image/video prompt" is folded into "Regenerate scene" (`regenerateScene()` now accepts optional prompt overrides, applied in the *same* transaction that resets the scene to PENDING) — not routed through the Studio's `PATCH .../scenes/[sceneId]`, since that route deliberately rejects edits to a COMPLETED scene (would race the worker) and loosening that gate would be a real regression for Milestone 8's Studio. "Regenerate voice" is a new isolated RenderJob kind (`processRegenVoiceJob`). "Regenerate subtitles" is deterministic, so it's synchronous (no queue) — `regenerateCaptionWords()`. "Replace scene" is a synchronous DB-only pointer swap. None of `processSceneRenderJob`/`processMergeJob`/the Studio's PATCH route were modified.
- **Media Library**: new `AssetSource` enum (`AI_GENERATED`/`UPLOAD`/`STOCK`/`BRAND`) added to the *existing* `Asset` table (defaults to `AI_GENERATED`, so every existing pipeline call site that never passes it keeps working unchanged) plus a new `STICKER` `AssetKind`. New `POST /api/assets/upload` (multipart, fixed 100MB ceiling + per-kind MIME allowlist — a technical safety limit, not a business rule) goes through the *same* Storage Provider + `recordAsset()` every pipeline-generated asset already uses. "Stock" (`STOCK_ASSET_LIBRARY`) and "Music" both have no per-user rows — both are admin-configured content lists exposed alongside real `Asset` rows through the same `GET /api/assets`, matching the established `AVAILABLE_VOICES`/`BACKGROUND_MUSIC_LIBRARY` pattern.
- **Admin-configurable content, not business rules**: `STOCK_ASSET_LIBRARY`, `AVAILABLE_FONTS`, `TEXT_STYLE_PRESETS`, `CAPTION_STYLE_PRESETS` are new `CONFIG_REGISTRY` entries (`studio_content` category) — curated lists an admin edits, same as `AVAILABLE_VOICES`. `TEXT_ANIMATIONS` (`NONE`/`FADE_IN`/`SLIDE_UP`/`POP`/`TYPEWRITER`) is a fixed literal union instead, matching the precedent that creative/UX enums (`SCRIPT_TONES`, `VIDEO_OBJECTIVES`) are code constants while content *libraries* are admin-editable.
- **Versioning extended for safety, not (yet) reachable**: `lib/projects/versioning.ts`'s snapshot now also captures Tracks/Clips/CaptionBlocks (correlated by `order`, not raw id, since `restoreVersion()` deletes-and-recreates Scene rows with brand-new ids) and `restoreVersion()` rebuilds the whole timeline layer from the snapshot afterward — without this, a restore would silently orphan every Clip (`Clip.scene` is `onDelete: SetNull`) and drop every caption (`CaptionBlock.scene` is `onDelete: Cascade`). **Caveat, called out honestly**: `restoreVersion()` is still gated to `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` (Milestone 8's original, unmodified guard), and Tracks/Clips only ever exist once a project has left that range (the Editor page redirects `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` projects to the Studio) — so today this fix is pure defensive correctness for the moment those two states overlap in a future milestone, not something exercisable by the current page-routing. Left in deliberately: it's a real latent-corruption fix for two already-shipped features interacting, not speculative scope creep.
- **Collaboration groundwork**: `ProjectCollaborator` gained `lastActiveAt` (nullable) — schema-only, per the user's explicit choice. Still no invite UI, no realtime sync, no presence/cursor UI.
- **Frontend**: new `/videos/[id]/editor` page (server component, redirects `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` to the Studio — the Editor composites real scene artifacts, nothing to edit before scenes exist), linked from `/videos/[id]`'s "Open Editor" button. One `EditorContext` (`editor-types.tsx`) shared by six panels instead of prop-drilling: **Timeline** (multi-track, hand-rolled pointer-event drag-to-move/drag-edge-to-resize — dnd-kit's sortable strategy fits reorderable lists, not freeform pixel positioning + resize on a time axis; HTML5 drag-and-drop from the Media Library onto a track lane), **Layers** (add/remove/mute/hide tracks, `@dnd-kit`-free since Track has no reorder operation in this milestone), **Text Editor** (fonts/colors/stroke/shadow/animation/templates on a TEXT clip's `content`), **Caption Editor** (word-level text/timing grid, regenerate-timing, style presets), **Scene Preview** (a genuine in-browser composite — base VIDEO/IMAGE layer plus absolutely-positioned TEXT/STICKER overlays driven by one `playheadMs` clock via `requestAnimationFrame`, with seek/zoom — explicitly a *preview*, not the real compositor, which is still `composeTimeline()`), **Media Library** (Upload/AI-generated/Stock/Brand/Music tabs, drag-to-timeline), **AI Editing** (Replace/Regenerate scene/Regenerate voice/prompt changes, links to the Captions panel for subtitle regeneration rather than duplicating it), **Export** (resolution/codec/watermark + a polling history list). Keyboard shortcuts: Space (play/pause), ←/→ (seek, Shift for 1s steps), Delete (delete selected clip), S (split at playhead), Ctrl/Cmd+D (duplicate) — all ignored while a form field has focus. Responsive: stacks to a single column below `lg`.
- **Unit tests added** (20 new, `vitest`): `lib/timeline/engine.test.ts` (`splitClipSpan`, `canMergeClips`, `mergeClipSpans`, `duplicateClipSpan`, `buildSeedClipsFromScenes` — 13 cases), `lib/captions/engine.test.ts` (`generateWordTimings` — empty/single-word/multi-word-proportional/minimum-floor/whitespace-collapse, 7 cases). 84/84 total tests pass. (DB-touching functions in both engines, plus the export service and pipeline's new processors, are covered by the live verification pass below instead — consistent with this codebase's established convention of unit-testing only DB-free logic.)
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server, full Editor lifecycle end-to-end: project created → rendered to `COMPLETED` → `GET .../timeline` auto-seeded VIDEO/AUDIO/MUSIC/CAPTION tracks with one VIDEO clip per scene → split a clip at an offset → merged the two halves back into one (exact original span restored) → duplicated a clip → added a TEXT track + clip with `content` styling → updated that content → muted the MUSIC track → removed the TEXT track (clips cascade-deleted) → `GET .../captions/[sceneId]` auto-seeded word-level timings → `PATCH` saved manual word edits + a style preset → `POST .../regenerate` recomputed timings from the *edited* text and the scene's `subtitleText`/`subtitleKey` were confirmed updated to the new VTT → `POST .../scenes/[sceneId]/regenerate` with new image/video prompts correctly flipped the project to `RENDERING`, completed, and persisted the new prompts → `POST .../regenerate-voice` swapped only the voiceKey → `POST .../scenes/[sceneId]/replace` repointed exactly the targeted clip's `sceneId` and left every other clip untouched → `POST .../exports` created an `Export` + tagged `RenderJob`, picked up by the same in-process queue worker, composited by `MockVideoProvider.composeTimeline()`, and resolved to a downloadable URL — entirely through the existing Background Rendering queue → `POST /api/assets/upload` (multipart PNG) succeeded and the asset appeared in `GET /api/assets?source=UPLOAD`, alongside an unrelated `?source=` validation check. The `/videos/[id]/editor` page itself returned 200 with all six panel labels present in the server-rendered HTML and zero errors in the dev server log across the entire session.

### Milestone 10 — Production AI Integration, Provider Management & Zero-Code Installation (2026-06-28)
The single biggest architectural pivot since Milestone 6: provider **credentials** move from env-var-only to **DB-first with env-var fallback**, so a non-technical founder can configure every AI/storage/payment vendor from the Admin Panel after install, with zero code edits and zero redeploys. Every existing Generation Engine/Queue/Credits/Scene/Editor/Studio call site is unchanged — only how a provider's credentials/model/policy are *resolved* changed, not how generation is *orchestrated*.

- **Credential resolution, centralized**: new `lib/providers/credentials.ts` is the one module that knows about both the new `ProviderConfig` table and the old env vars. `resolveProviderCredentials(category, providerId)` checks the DB first (`ProviderConfig` row, secrets AES-256-GCM-decrypted) and falls back to the pre-Milestone-10 env var only when the DB value is absent — once an admin saves a provider once, the DB is authoritative for that field. `listEnabledProviderConfigs(category)` returns the admin-configured priority order, falling back to the old `PROVIDER_*_PRIORITY` SystemConfig keys only while the category has zero `ProviderConfig` rows at all (an empty/all-disabled result *after* the admin has saved something legitimately means "no providers," not "fall back to legacy"). All 8 existing real adapters (OpenAI LLM/Images, Gemini, ElevenLabs, Flux, Replicate, S3, Razorpay) were refactored to a `constructor(config: ProviderRuntimeConfig = {})` taking already-resolved credentials — none of them read `process.env` directly anymore. All 6 factory `index.ts` files became `async` to call `resolveProviderCredentials()` before constructing.
- **Encryption** (`lib/security/{encryption,master-key}.ts`): AES-256-GCM, `ivHex:authTagHex:ciphertextHex` single-column format. The one secret that can't itself live encrypted in the DB — the master key — comes from `CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (env, 64 hex chars) if set, otherwise is auto-generated on first use and persisted to a gitignored `.encryption-key` file at the project root (zero-setup default). `maskSecret()` (only the last 4 characters ever shown) is used everywhere a saved secret is echoed back to the Admin Panel — the plaintext is never returned once saved. 8 round-trip/tamper/masking unit tests, including a GCM-auth-failure-on-tampering regression test.
- **New `ProviderConfig`/`ProviderAuditLog` tables**: `ProviderConfig` (one row per (`category`, `providerId`)) holds `enabled`, encrypted `apiKeyEncrypted`/`apiSecretEncrypted`/`extraSecretEncrypted`, `model`, `defaultQuality`, `priority`, `monthlyBudgetUsd`/`dailyBudgetUsd`/`rateLimitPerMinute`, `timeoutMs`/`retryCount`, `extraConfig` (JSON, vendor-specific non-secret fields like an S3 bucket/region), `keyExpiresAt`, `lastTestedAt`/`lastTestResult`/`lastTestError`. `ProviderAuditLog` records every admin action (`update`/`test_connection`) with `fieldsChanged` (names only, never values) — Part 9's "audit every provider action," satisfied without a second place a credential could leak from.
- **Per-provider budget/rate-limit enforcement, as a new engine filter** (`lib/generation/budget.ts`): `evaluateBudget()` (pure) + `checkProviderBudget()` (DB-backed, queries `GenerationLog` for today's/this-month's spend and request count) plug into `runGeneration()` as a new filter applied *after* the existing health-check filter. Deliberately the opposite failure posture from health: health fails *open* (a transient blip across every provider gives the full chain one more shot rather than refusing outright); budget fails *closed* (an admin-set hard cap being exceeded by every provider throws `AllProvidersFailedError` with budget-reason summaries — a deliberate cap, not noise, must never be silently bypassed). Per-provider `timeoutMs`/`retryCount` overrides (`getProviderPolicyOverrides()`) also plug into the engine's existing per-provider loop, falling back to the category-wide policy when unset.
- **4 new best-effort Video adapters** (Veo, Kling, Hailuo, Runway) — real REST integrations against each vendor's documented API shape, but explicitly flagged in code comments as **not verified against a live account** (preview APIs whose field names have shifted), and all default `enabled: false` per Part 1's "feature flag expensive providers." A new shared `lib/providers/poll.ts` (`pollUntilSettled()`) generic long-running-operation poller backs all 4 (Replicate/Flux's existing polling loops were left as-is to limit blast radius).
- **`GenerationProvider.model`** (new optional field on the common provider interface): every real adapter with a model concept (LLM ×2, Image ×2, Voice ×1, Video ×6) now exposes the model it's actually using as a public readonly property, computed once in its constructor. The engine logs it on every `GenerationLog` row (`model` column, new) alongside three new usage-breakdown columns (`usageTokens`/`usageImages`/`usageSeconds`, populated from the same `GenerationUsage` the cost estimator already computed) — Part 8's "track Provider, Model, Tokens, Images, Voice/Video Seconds" with zero new tracking mechanism, just persisting numbers the engine already had in memory.
- **Admin → AI Providers** (`/admin/ai-providers`, replacing `/admin/providers` which now redirects there): one page covering all 12 admin-configurable (category, providerId) pairs across LLM/Image/Voice/Video/Storage/Payment — Enable/Disable, masked API Key/Secret inputs (PATCH-style: omitted = untouched, `""` = clear, non-empty = re-encrypt — this is what lets re-saving the rest of a form leave an already-saved key in place), Model, Default Quality, Priority, Monthly/Daily Budget, Rate Limit, Timeout, Retry Count, Key-expiry date, Test Connection, Save. `mock` is intentionally never listed (needs no credentials) and `self_hosted` LLM stays env-var-only (it's a URL, not an apiKey/apiSecret pair) — both documented exclusions from the catalogue, not oversights.
- **Real Test Connection** (`lib/providers/test-connection.ts`): a cheap, read-only, real network call per vendor (OpenAI `/v1/models`, ElevenLabs `/v1/user`, Replicate `/v1/account`, S3 `HeadBucketCommand`, Razorpay `orders.all({count:1})`), with a best-effort/shape-only fallback for the 4 unverified video vendors. Verified live against the real OpenAI API with a deliberately bogus key — got back a genuine 401, proving this isn't a fake check.
- **Provider Dashboard** (`lib/admin/provider-dashboard.ts`, `GET /api/admin/ai-providers/dashboard`): one row per catalogue entry — Status (`HEALTHY`/`DEGRADED`/`DOWN`/`NO_TRAFFIC`/`NOT_TRACKED` for Storage/Payment, which never go through the Generation Engine), Current Model, Avg Response, Success/Failure Rate, Today's Requests/Cost, Monthly Cost, Last Error, a derived Health Score (0-100, health status dominates — `DOWN` always scores 0), and (Video only) the shared render-queue depth. Joins `ProviderConfig`/`ProviderHealth`/`GenerationLog` — no new counters.
- **Installation Wizard** (`/install`, `lib/installation.ts`'s `isInstalled()`/`ensureInstalled()`/`ensureNotInstalled()` gated on a `SystemConfig` flag, `INSTALLATION_COMPLETED`, cached `true` forever in-process once confirmed): 7 steps — Create Super Admin (reuses the existing Phone-OTP `signIn`, since the app has no password field at all, then a narrowly-scoped `POST /api/install/promote-admin` flips the new account to `ADMIN` and a `useSession().update({role:"ADMIN"})` call refreshes the JWT immediately, extending the jwt callback's existing `trigger==="update"` handling — the exact same pattern already used for `onboardingCompleted`), Database test, Storage config+test, Payment config+test, AI Providers config+test (Steps 2-7 call the *same* `/admin/ai-providers` PATCH/test routes the Admin Panel uses post-install — no parallel install-time provider-config code), Seed (`lib/seed-defaults.ts`'s `seedDefaults()`, shared between `prisma/seed.ts`'s CLI path and the wizard's `/api/install/seed` route — templates/credit-packages/pricing-plans defined exactly once), Finish. The wizard is permanently inaccessible once installed (`ensureNotInstalled()` 404s/redirects `/install` itself).
- **Critical bug found and fixed via a real production build, not typecheck/lint/vitest**: adding `await ensureInstalled()` as the first line of `(marketing)/layout.tsx`, `(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, and `admin/layout.tsx` (each doing a conditional `redirect()` based on a DB check, *before* any `auth()`/cookie read) caused Next.js to **statically prerender these routes at build time with the redirect baked in forever** — Next's static-analysis only detects dynamism from recognized APIs (cookies/headers), not arbitrary async DB calls. Confirmed via the build output showing `○` (Static) instead of `ƒ` (Dynamic) for `/`, `/admin/*`, `/login`, `/onboarding`. Fixed with an explicit `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` on all 5 affected files (4 layouts + `install/page.tsx`) — this is specifically what protects the "wizard must never reappear after install" guarantee from being silently broken by static caching, the single most important fix this milestone.
- **Prompt Optimization** (`lib/prompts/optimizer.ts`, `POST /api/prompt-optimize`): routes through the *same* `generateScript()` call every other LLM operation uses (never a parallel "optimization model" pipeline) with a structured `OPTIMIZED:`/`NEGATIVE:` prompt format, parsed tolerantly (falls back to the raw response if a model doesn't follow the format). Records both the original and optimized text via the *existing* `recordPrompt()` mechanism — Prompt Studio's existing chronological per-(user,kind) history already IS prompt versioning, no second table needed. Negative-prompt suggestions are only requested for IMAGE/VIDEO kinds (a SCRIPT prompt has no visual negative-prompt counterpart). **Prompt Analytics** (`getPromptAnalytics()`, `GET /api/prompt-analytics`) is a pure derivation over `PromptRecord` — per-kind count/avg-length over a window, can never drift from what was actually recorded since it reads the same table `recordPrompt()` writes.
- **Cost Management dashboard** (`lib/admin/cost-management.ts`, `GET /api/admin/cost-management`, new `/admin/cost-management` page): breakdowns by Provider, Model, Project (top 20), User (top 20), and Subscription plan, plus rolled-up totals (requests, cost, tokens, images, voice seconds, video seconds) — all derived from `GenerationLog`, including the new `model`/usage columns. The subscription breakdown is a pure, unit-tested bucketing function (`bucketBySubscription()`) over every user with usage in the window (not just the displayed top 20), joined against each user's most recent `ACTIVE` `Subscription`'s plan name, with a "No active subscription" bucket for the rest — computed over the full set so the percentages stay meaningful even though the per-user table is capped for display.
- **Global expiring-key reminder**: `listExpiringProviderKeys()` (any enabled provider with `keyExpiresAt` within 7 days, including already-expired) backs a banner rendered in `admin/layout.tsx` itself — visible on *every* `/admin/*` page, not just the AI Providers card the founder happens to have open. Key **rotation** itself needed no new mechanism: the existing PATCH/Save flow already supports re-entering a new key (the masked-secret PATCH semantics already established in Phase B), and every change is already audit-logged via the existing `fieldsChanged` mechanism.
- **Architecture rules upheld**: zero hardcoded provider lists outside `PROVIDER_CATALOGUE`/each category's `*_IDS` constant; zero business logic duplicated (budget/rate-limit, prompt optimization, and cost reporting all reuse the existing Generation Engine, `recordPrompt()`, and `GenerationLog` rather than inventing parallel tracking); the Generation Engine, Queue, and Credit Engine were never bypassed — Milestone 10 only changed *where credentials/policy come from*, never *how generation is orchestrated*.
- **Unit tests added** (29 new, `vitest`): `lib/security/encryption.test.ts` (8 — round-trip, random-IV-different-ciphertext, malformed-payload, GCM-tamper-detection, masking), `lib/generation/budget.test.ts` (6 — pure `evaluateBudget()`), `lib/generation/engine.test.ts` (+4 — per-provider retry/timeout override, budget-skips-one-provider, budget-exhausts-all-throws), `lib/prompts/optimizer.test.ts` (8 — prompt-builder format-by-kind, response-parser well-formed/fallback/no-negative-section), `lib/admin/cost-management.test.ts` (3 — `bucketBySubscription()` grouping/no-subscription-bucket/cost-descending-sort). 113/113 total tests pass.
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server: full install-wizard walkthrough (OTP sign-in → promote-admin → session role refresh confirmed via the real NextAuth `/api/auth/session` POST body shape → DB test → Storage/Payment disable → AI Provider save with a bogus OpenAI key → Test Connection returning a genuine 401 from OpenAI's real API → masked-secret-preservation confirmed (re-saving without `apiKey` left the previously-saved key untouched) → Seed → Finish → confirmed `/install` now redirects away and `/admin` no longer redirects to `/install`); `/api/prompt-optimize`/`/api/prompt-analytics` exercised end-to-end through the real Generation Engine (temporarily enabling a `mock` LLM `ProviderConfig` row, since the only saved real LLM key in this dev DB was the deliberately-bogus test key from the install-wizard pass); `/api/admin/cost-management` confirmed correct provider/project/user/subscription aggregation including "(deleted user)"/"No active subscription" fallbacks; the global expiring-key banner confirmed rendering on `/admin` and the `/admin/cost-management` page's SSR shell confirmed rendering with zero dev-server errors. Also caught and fixed, mid-verification, a stale leftover dev-server process (from earlier in the same work session) silently serving pre-Milestone-10 compiled code on the test port, masking the new routes — restarted cleanly before re-testing.

### Milestone 11 — AI Talking Head Marketing Editor (2026-06-28)
A second, genuinely new input modality alongside the existing brief→script→render pipeline: a user uploads a finished talking-head video instead of writing a brief, and the platform transcribes/understands/edits it automatically. `VideoProject.sourceType` (`GENERATED` default | `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD`) is the one seam this hangs off — everything downstream of "turn raw input into Scenes" (Scene rendering, Timeline/Editor, render Queue, Credit Engine, Provider abstraction, Versioning, Prompt system) is **100% reused, unmodified**, exactly as `lib/scenes/engine.ts`'s Milestone 7 documentation predicted ("the one function an LLM-based scene planner would replace, with nothing downstream needing to change"). Four decisions were confirmed up front: Brand Kit is per-User (no Workspace model exists); OpenAI Whisper is the first real Transcription adapter; upload/transcription/analysis/planning are free, credits are charged only at actual AI image/video generation and at Export; "Premium AI Video Generation" is a new admin feature flag, independent of subscription plan.

- **Schema**: `VideoProject.sourceType`/`sourceAssetId`; `Transcript` (1:1, cascade-deleted with the project) + `TranscriptSegment` (`order`/`startMs`/`endMs`/`text`/`paragraphIndex`/`wordTimings` JSON/`analysis` JSON/`sceneId`); `Scene.visualType` (nullable `SceneVisualType` — `FACE_ONLY`/`B_ROLL`/`IMAGE`/`LOGO`/`SCREENSHOT`/`WEBSITE`/`GRAPH`/`CHART`/`ICON`/`ANIMATION`/`TEXT_OVERLAY`, null for every `GENERATED`-flow scene); `BrandKit` (1:1 per user — logo/intro/music/outro/watermark asset refs, primary/secondary color, font, watermark position). `ProviderCategory`/`GenerationCategory` both gained `TRANSCRIPTION`, getting failover/retry/health/cost-tracking for free through the existing Generation Engine.
- **Transcription provider category** (`lib/providers/transcription/{types,mock,openai-whisper,index}.ts`, `lib/generation/transcription.ts`) — cloned from the Voice category's exact shape. **TRANSCRIPTION is DB-only by design** (no legacy `SystemConfig` priority-list fallback, unlike LLM/Image/Voice/Video, which predate the Admin Panel and still default to `["mock"]`) — an admin must explicitly enable a Transcription provider via `/admin/ai-providers` before the feature works, exactly as the live e2e pass below had to simulate.
- **Large-file presigned upload**: `StorageProvider.createSignedUploadUrl()` (additive) + `POST /api/assets/upload-url` (mints a presigned PUT + pending `Asset` row) + `POST /api/assets/[id]/confirm-upload` — bypasses the existing 100MB multipart route entirely for multi-GB talking-head clips, same `Asset` table, same `recordAsset()` bookkeeping. New admin flag `TALKING_HEAD_AI_VIDEO_GENERATION_ENABLED` (default `false`) gates AI-video-generation asset decisions.
- **Speech Intelligence**: `POST /api/videos/talking-head` creates a `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD` project and enqueues a `payload.kind:"transcribe"` `RenderJob` — covered by pause/resume/cancel with zero changes since those operate purely on status, never `payload.kind`. `processTranscribeJob()` calls Whisper (or Mock), runs pure `detectSilenceGaps()`/`assignParagraphIndices()` (`lib/transcription/segmentation.ts`), writes `Transcript`/`TranscriptSegment` rows, and auto-enqueues a `"analyze"` job — both run automatically while the project is still `DRAFT`/free, before the user ever sees a bill.
- **AI Context Understanding + Visual Planner** (`lib/talking-head/{context-analysis,visual-planner}.ts`): batched LLM calls (same `generateScript()` every other operation uses, same numbered-list/regex-parse pattern as Script Studio) extract entities/tags/hook/CTA/emotion per transcript segment, then pick one `SceneVisualType` per segment. Pure `groupSegmentsIntoScenes()` merges contiguous same-type/same-paragraph segments into `Scene` rows — the literal LLM-planned replacement for `splitScriptIntoSceneTexts()` that Milestone 7 anticipated. Manual edits reuse the existing Scene `PATCH` route (just gained `visualType`).
- **Intelligent Asset Selection + automatic reuse-vs-generate branch**: pure `selectAssetForScene()` (`lib/talking-head/asset-selector.ts`) runs a waterfall — REUSE_EXISTING → REUSE_BRAND → REUSE_UPLOADED → STOCK → AI_IMAGE/AI_VIDEO (the last gated by the premium flag, downgrading to AI_IMAGE when off). `processSceneRenderJob()` gained one early branch: a talking-head scene with a resolved REUSE/STOCK decision copies the existing storage key directly (no provider call, no cost); only AI_IMAGE/AI_VIDEO decisions actually call `generateImage()`/`renderVideo()`. Same `RenderJob`, same per-scene retry, same `tryFinalizeProject()` shape.
- **One shared base video, many scenes**: each talking-head scene's "video" is the *same* uploaded source asset, sliced via `Clip.trimStartMs` — a field that existed in the schema since Milestone 9 but was never threaded into `TimelineClipInput`/`composeTimeline()` until now (a small, justified bug-fix-as-part-of-the-feature). `buildTalkingHeadSeedClips()` seeds one trimmed VIDEO clip per scene; `applyAutomaticEditingPlan()` (`lib/talking-head/timeline-plan.ts`) layers TEXT/IMAGE/VIDEO overlay clips on top from the visual plan + asset-selector decisions, idempotently. **Finalization bypasses the merge job entirely** — there's no per-scene video to concatenate, so `tryFinalizeProject()` branches talking-head projects straight to `finalizeTalkingHeadProject()`, setting `previewVideoUrl`/`masterVideoUrl` from the source asset directly and deferring all real overlay compositing to the Editor's *existing* `composeTimeline()` (Track/Clip-aware) at Export time — explicitly not a second compositing engine.
- **Smart Captions reuse real Whisper word timestamps**: `deriveSceneWordTimings()` (`lib/captions/engine.ts`) reads `TranscriptSegment.wordTimings` when present instead of the proportional-estimate fallback every `GENERATED`-flow scene still uses, and auto-applies bold emphasis + the Brand Kit's `primaryColor` highlight to hook/CTA-tagged words.
- **Brand Kit** (`GET/PATCH /api/brand-kit`, per-user): applied automatically wherever a project doesn't already override it — LOGO asset-selector tier, a default background-music clip seeded by `ensureTimeline()` — the same defaulting pattern `Scene.backgroundMusicUrl` already established, not a new mechanism.
- **AI Marketing Assistant**: deliberately scoped to 6 of the brief's 10 "Improve X" actions — Hook/CTA (new scene-scoped `POST .../scenes/[sceneId]/variants`, reusing `runScriptVariants()` against the scene's text), B-roll (existing `regenerateScene()`), Captions (existing `regenerateCaptionWords()`, now Whisper-timing-aware), Thumbnail (existing route), Music (new `swapBackgroundMusic()`). Storytelling/Engagement/Script/Voice rewrites were explicitly **left out**, documented in code: you cannot rewrite a talking head's spoken audio in place, and there's no TTS voice to swap on an uploaded video.
- **Cost Optimization + Credits**: pure `estimateProjectCost(scenes, creditRates, vendorRates)` (`lib/talking-head/cost-estimator.ts`) reuses the existing `computeCost()` rate-card logic to preview the bill *before* any paid generation runs (`GET /api/videos/[id]/cost-estimate`), shown live in the Visual Plan Review step. New `CreditTransactionType` values `AI_GENERATION`/`EXPORT` and admin config `TALKING_HEAD_CREDIT_COSTS` (`aiImageCredits`/`aiVideoCreditsPerSecond`/`exportCredits`) back atomic per-scene charging inside the same transaction as scene completion (with a pre-check via `getCreditBalance()` so a call that would be rejected anyway never spends vendor cost first) — a scene that resolves to reuse/stock is never charged. Export charging is scoped to `sourceType === "TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD"` only; the `GENERATED` flow's Export remains free/unchanged, per Known Issue #9.
- **Frontend**: `/create/talking-head` (2-step upload wizard, presigned-PUT-via-`XMLHttpRequest` for real progress events) plus a small "Upload a video instead" link from `/create`; `/videos/[id]/studio` now branches by `sourceType` to render either the existing `StudioClient` or the new `VisualPlanReviewClient` (polls while transcription/analysis run in the background, shows per-scene visual-type editor + live cost estimate + the same "Confirm & generate" action the `GENERATED` flow uses). Verified the Editor and AI Editing panel need zero changes — every place that reads `imagePrompt`/`videoPrompt`/`imageUrl` already null-guards correctly.
- **Unit tests added** (46 new, `vitest`): `lib/transcription/segmentation.test.ts`, `lib/talking-head/{context-analysis,visual-planner,asset-selector,cost-estimator}.test.ts`, plus `lib/timeline/engine.test.ts` gained a `buildTalkingHeadSeedClips` block. 159/159 total tests pass.
- **Live e2e bug found and fixed during verification, not by a test**: `POST /api/videos/[id]/render` had `if (!project.generatedScript) return apiError(...)`, which incorrectly 409'd *every* talking-head project (none have a `generatedScript` by design) — fixed to `if (project.sourceType === "GENERATED" && !project.generatedScript)`. Also added FAILED-status propagation for `"transcribe"`/`"analyze"` job failures (previously only the `RenderJob` failed, leaving the project silently stuck `DRAFT` with no visible error in the new polling UI).
- **Verified live** against a real Postgres-backed dev server, full pipeline end-to-end via a minted NextAuth JWT session cookie driving the real HTTP routes (not bypassing them): presigned upload → confirm → `POST /api/videos/talking-head` → automatic transcribe→analyze (7 segments, all analyzed, 7 scenes planned) → free cost estimate → manual `visualType` override (`PATCH .../scenes/[sceneId]`) → confirm/render → pause mid-`QUEUED` correctly parked the job, resume correctly un-parked it → scenes resolved (a forced `IMAGE` scene correctly fell through to `AI_IMAGE` generation and charged exactly 1 credit, matching `TALKING_HEAD_CREDIT_COSTS.aiImageCredits`; every `FACE_ONLY`/`TEXT_OVERLAY` scene charged nothing) → project finalized straight to `COMPLETED` with no merge job → `GET .../timeline` showed the base VIDEO track correctly trimmed per-scene plus IMAGE/CAPTION/TEXT/MUSIC overlay tracks → captions derived 12 real Whisper-timed words → AI Marketing Assistant's hook-variant generator, B-roll regenerate, caption regenerate, and music-clear all returned 200 → Brand Kit PATCH/GET round-tripped → Export created and correctly charged 2 credits, matching `exportCredits`. Also discovered and worked around (by seeding the expected `ProviderConfig` rows, simulating the one-time admin setup a real install would also need) a pre-existing environment gap: this dev DB's `ProviderConfig` table had a disabled real `LLM/openai` row, which blocks the legacy `["mock"]` fallback for *that* category specifically (the fallback only applies when zero rows exist) — not a Milestone 11 regression, but worth knowing before assuming Mock providers "just work" in every dev environment.

### Milestone 12 — Production Infrastructure, Launch Readiness & Founder Acceptance Test (2026-06-29)
Not a new feature milestone — the "can real paying customers use this in production" pass across 10 phases (A–J): infrastructure hardening, observability, the SaaS mechanics every paying product needs, a security review, performance work, public-facing pages, deployment tooling, and a full founder acceptance test before declaring launch-ready. Every phase reused existing systems (queue, credit engine, provider abstraction, audit log pattern) rather than rewriting them, per the standing engineering rules.

- **Phase A — Production Infrastructure**: `lib/cache/cache.ts` (`getOrSetCache`/`invalidateCache`) — Redis-backed when `REDIS_URL` is set, in-process `Map` fallback otherwise (same pattern Milestone 10 established for provider credentials); `lib/admin/config.ts` refactored onto this shared cache instead of its own bespoke Map. `lib/security/rate-limit.ts` (`checkRateLimit`) — Redis atomic `INCR`+`EXPIRE`, DB-row (`RateLimitHit`) fallback, admin-configurable thresholds via `RATE_LIMITS` config, fails open when no policy exists. Dead Letter visibility (`getDeadLetterJobs()`) + manual admin "Retry" action and Queue Metrics (`getQueueThroughput()`/`getJobLatencyPercentiles()`) added to `/admin/render`. New `/admin/storage` panel: `Asset` counts/sizes by kind/source/user + reachability check.
- **Phase B — Monitoring & Reliability**: structured logging via `pino` (`lib/observability/logger.ts`) replacing raw `console.*` in the queue worker/render pipeline/generation engine, threaded with the existing `meta.requestId` envelope (one trace id, not a second mechanism). Sentry wired in as fully optional/env-gated (`SENTRY_DSN`), no-op otherwise. OpenTelemetry deliberately *not* added as a second SDK — Sentry's own tracing is OTel-based, and a separate collector needs infra this generic-VPS deployment doesn't assume (documented in `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`). New `/admin/health` (DB ping, Redis ping if configured, S3 reachability, provider circuit breakers, queue depth — pure aggregation of already-existing functions) and a lightweight `ErrorLog` model + `logError()` for non-generation errors, Sentry-additive when configured.
- **Phase C — SaaS Features**: **Referral system** (`Profile.referralCode`/`referredByUserId`, lazily generated, one-time-only via a null-check, bidirectional `grantCredits()` with `type: REFERRAL`, admin-configurable `REFERRAL_BONUS_CREDITS`) surfaced on `/credits`. **Coupon codes** (`CouponCode`/`CouponRedemption`) — `CREDITS` type grants instantly via `grantCredits()`, `PERCENT`/`FIXED` discount a credit-package purchase at checkout; admin CRUD at `/admin/coupons` mirroring `/admin/pricing`. **Billing History** (`GET /api/billing/history`, joins `PaymentIntent`+`CreditTransaction`+`Download`) as a new tab on `/credits`. **GST-ready Invoices** (`Invoice` model, sequential `invoiceNumber`, frozen `businessDetailsSnapshot` JSON, lazy `pdf-lib` PDF generation uploaded through the Storage Provider, signed-URL download) auto-created inside the existing `fulfillPaymentIntent()` settlement path — one new call site, not a parallel settlement flow; new `BUSINESS_TAX_DETAILS` config (legal name/GSTIN/address), renders "GSTIN: not provided" gracefully when empty. **Usage Dashboard** (`/usage`, `getUserUsageSummary()`) — per-user videos/scenes/exports/credits-consumed, GENERATED-vs-TALKING_HEAD split. **Email provider category** (`lib/providers/email/{types,mock,resend,index}.ts`, identical shape to Payment/Storage/Transcription) backing `lib/notifications/email.ts`. **Notifications** (`Notification` model, `notifyUser()`/`broadcastNotification()`, dual-channel in-app+email, fire-and-forget so a notification failure never blocks a render) hooked into the existing `tryFinalizeProject()`/`finalizeTalkingHeadProject()`/Export-completion call sites; polling bell UI (30s) + `/admin/notifications` broadcast composer.
- **Phase D — Security**: full `Content-Security-Policy` + `Strict-Transport-Security` (production-only) added to `next.config.ts`'s existing `securityHeaders`. `checkRateLimit()` applied to video/talking-head creation, asset upload, AI Marketing Assistant actions, export creation, with OTP send migrated onto the same shared helper (behavior-preserving). **Abuse Detection** (`lib/admin/abuse-detection.ts`) — rule-based, flags excessive rate-limit hits (≥50/24h) or fast `AI_GENERATION` credit burn (≥100/1h), read-only `/admin/abuse` view; manual suspend/unsuspend now actually enforced via `requireSession()`'s fresh `accountStatus` check (the pre-existing `User.accountStatus` field was never wired up before this milestone). **CSRF**: an `Origin`-header check composed directly into `authConfig.callbacks.authorized` in `middleware.ts` (not a parallel middleware function, to avoid NextAuth `auth()` overload-resolution conflicts) — blocks cross-origin mutating `/api/*` requests, allows no-Origin requests (curl/webhooks). **Upload magic-byte validation** (`file-type` package) on the multipart upload path only — the presigned-URL path is a documented, accepted gap since those bytes never transit the server. **Audit Logging** generalized from `ProviderAuditLog` into `AuditLog` (`userId?`/`resource`/`action`/`detail` JSON, names/ids only — never secrets), written at credit grants, coupon redemptions, subscription cancellations, suspend/unsuspend, broadcast sends. `lib/env.ts`'s Zod schema extended to validate `SENTRY_DSN`/`RESEND_API_KEY`/`REDIS_URL` at boot.
- **Phase E — Performance**: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`-verified indexes added on real hot paths (`RenderJob` claim, `GenerationLog` aggregations, the new `Notification`/`AuditLog`/`Invoice` queries). Phase A's cache layer applied to the admin cost-management/provider-dashboard aggregations with short TTLs. Large-upload handling re-verified (still bypasses the Next.js server entirely via the Milestone 11 presigned path — no rebuild needed). Lighthouse pass against the landing page: caught and fixed a real sitewide dark-mode contrast bug (see Bugs Found below) — `color-contrast` audit went from 6 violations to 0, accessibility score to 100/100.
- **Phase F — Public Launch Pages**: `/pricing` (live `PricingPlan`/`CreditPackage` data, same source as `/api/billing/plans`), `/faq`, `/contact` (`POST /api/contact` storing a `ContactMessage` + admin email via the Email provider; confirmed XSS-safe — a `<script>` payload in the message field is stored and would render as plain text, never executed), `/privacy`/`/terms`/`/cookies` (real product-tailored content, flagged in documentation — not on the page — as AI-drafted pending actual legal review), `/help`, `/release-notes` (sourced from this file's milestone history).
- **Phase G — Deployment**: multi-stage `Dockerfile` (deps → builder → runner, `output: "standalone"`, non-root `nextjs` user — no Prisma binary-engine workaround needed since the `pg` driver adapter has no native query-engine binary); `docker-compose.yml` extended with `app` + optional `redis` alongside the existing `postgres` service; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (typecheck+lint+vitest+build on every push/PR, no deploy job); `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` with concrete VPS steps, full env var checklist, `pg_dump` backup/restore procedure, zero-downtime deploy notes, and multi-instance worker-scaling notes (the atomic-claim queue already makes this safe — documented, not rebuilt).
- **Phase H — Founder Acceptance Test**: a scripted HTTP-level + SSR-HTML pass (no browser-automation tool available in this environment) through every major flow using two live-minted NextAuth session cookies, run as one continuous stateful session (referral applied between the two test users, coupon redeemed, subscription purchased and cancelled, talking-head video uploaded/transcribed/rendered/exported/downloaded, GENERATED-flow video created/rendered/notified) rather than isolated per-feature checks — mirroring a real founder using their own product end-to-end. Covered: public pages, install-era auth, onboarding, referral codes, coupons (valid+double-redeem-rejected), credit-package purchase → invoice → PDF, subscription purchase → credit grant → cancel (`cancelAtPeriodEnd`), billing history, notifications (render-complete + broadcast), rate limiting (OTP 429, cross-origin CSRF 403), upload magic-byte rejection, admin Health/Render-queue/Dead-Letter/Cost-Management/Abuse/Storage/AI-Providers dashboards, user suspend/unsuspend (session invalidated immediately), the full GENERATED-flow regression (brief→script→render→COMPLETED→notification), and the full TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD regression (presigned upload→confirm→transcribe→analyze→script-ready→render→COMPLETED→export→credit-based download).
  - **4 real bugs found and fixed during this pass** (not pre-existing, all introduced by or exposed through M12's own shared-infrastructure changes): (1) `POST /api/billing/mock/confirm` treated "zero enabled PAYMENT provider rows" (a disabled-but-present leftover `razorpay` row) as "a real provider is active," blocking confirmation of payments actually created against the Mock fallback — fixed to mirror `getPaymentProvider()`'s own `default:`-case resolution exactly. (2) `suspendUser()`/`unsuspendUser()` used Prisma `update()` against a possibly-nonexistent id, throwing an unhandled `P2025` (empty 500) instead of a clean 404 — fixed to `updateMany()` + count-check, with a new `UserNotFoundError` caught in both admin routes. (3) Sitewide dark-mode contrast failure: marketing pages use PRD-mandated static/theme-independent color tokens, but the root `<ThemeProvider enableSystem>` plus a global `body { @apply bg-background }` rule let a dark OS preference flip the body to a dark navy background while text stayed light-calibrated — fixed with an explicit `bg-white` on the marketing layout wrapper, plus one literal hero-headline color fix (`text-accent-orange-dark` → `text-[#c2410c]`, 2.86:1 → passing 3:1) caught by the same Lighthouse pass. (4) `lib/observability/logger.ts`'s `pino` instance used `transport: { target: "pino-pretty" }`, which spawns pino-pretty in a worker thread and resolves that thread's own module path at runtime — under Next.js's Turbopack bundling that resolution breaks (`Cannot find module '...thread-stream/lib/worker.js'`), so the worker died immediately and every dev-mode structured log line was silently dropped (server still ran fine; only logging was affected). Caught only by actually starting the dev server and reading its console output, not by `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest`/`next build`, none of which exercise a live worker-thread spawn. Fixed by passing a `pino-pretty` stream instance directly (in-process, no worker thread) instead of the `transport` option — confirmed fixed by restarting and seeing the queue worker's startup log line actually print.
  - **Test data deliberately left in the dev DB** as live evidence of this verification pass (consistent with the pattern from prior milestones): two test users (one promoted to ADMIN), one referral relationship, one redeemed coupon (`TESTCOUPON1`), one cancelled subscription, two invoices with generated PDFs, one GENERATED-flow video project, one TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD project with a completed export, one suspend/unsuspend cycle, one `ContactMessage` (the XSS-payload test).
- **Phase I — Documentation**: this section; `LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md`, `SECURITY_CHECKLIST.md`, `BETA_TEST_PLAN.md`, `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` added alongside the existing `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` (Phase G).
- **Phase J — Final Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `next build` (real production build, not just inside Docker) green across every route, `vitest run` 159/159 passing, a targeted dead-code spot-check on every new M12 export (all referenced ≥1 call site beyond their own definition — none orphaned), `npm audit` showing 5 moderate advisories all confined to build-time-only transitive deps (`@prisma/dev`'s nested `@hono/node-server`, Next's bundled `postcss`) — neither reachable from the running production app, documented in `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` rather than force-upgraded this late in the milestone. Regression spot-check confirmed Milestones 1–11's GENERATED and TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD pipelines both still complete end-to-end unchanged.
- **Production readiness score: 9/10.** The one point held back is the honestly-scoped gap list in `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` (no managed autoscaling/CDN/automated off-box backup scheduling, single-instance Docker Compose deploy has a brief restart window, presigned-upload path skips magic-byte validation, legal pages are AI-drafted pending real review) — every one is a documented, deliberate scope cut for a self-hosted VPS launch, not an unknown risk.

### Milestone 13 — Admin Panel Enhancements (2026-06-29)
Extends the existing Admin Panel with the business-operations tooling a founder needs to run the SaaS day-to-day — payment management, subscription policy, a revenue dashboard, a founder dashboard, an operational command center, and a documented extensibility story. No second admin system: every page reuses the established four-layer shape (`page.tsx` → `*-dashboard.tsx` → `app/api/admin/*` → `lib/admin/*`), the `CONFIG_REGISTRY` pattern for every new setting, and the existing `ProviderConfig`/`PROVIDER_CATALOGUE` mechanism for provider selection (confirmed ~95% already built before this milestone — payments now get a dedicated lens on top of it, not a parallel mechanism). Two scope decisions were confirmed with the user up front: payment providers stay **single-active-driver** (`getPaymentProvider()`'s existing `[selection][0]` behavior, unchanged — the new UI only changes *which* driver is active, not true multi-vendor failover), and billing intervals get **real renewal-date math**, not just a UI dropdown.

- **Phase A — Schema foundation**: `BillingInterval` enum (`MONTHLY`/`QUARTERLY`/`HALF_YEARLY`/`YEARLY`) replacing `PricingPlan.billingInterval`'s free-text `String?`, migrated with a hand-written `ALTER COLUMN ... USING (...::"BillingInterval")` cast (not Prisma's auto-generated drop+recreate, which would have lost existing `"MONTHLY"` data — verified safe first by checking the live column only ever held `null`/`"MONTHLY"`). New `PricingPlan.trialDays` (default 0), `Subscription.isTrialPeriod`. New models `WebhookEvent`, `Refund`, `Dispute` (schema-only stub — no provider method yet, populated once a real dispute webhook exists).
- **Phase B — Billing interval math + refunds**: `lib/billing/interval.ts`'s `addBillingInterval()` (pure, all 4 intervals, vitest-covered) replaces two previously-hardcoded `setMonth(+1)` call sites in `fulfillment.ts` — a YEARLY plan now actually renews yearly. `trialDays > 0` correctly sets `isTrialPeriod`/an extended first `periodEnd`; cleared on the first real renewal. `PaymentProvider` interface gained `refund()`; implemented in Mock (instant) and Razorpay (real refund API, confirmed against `node_modules/razorpay`'s actual type signatures rather than assumed). `lib/billing/refunds.ts` (`createRefund()`/`listRefunds()`).
- **Phase C — Webhook event logging**: every inbound webhook is now persisted as a `WebhookEvent` row (signature-valid or not) before dispatch; the dispatch switch itself was extracted into a standalone `dispatchWebhookEvent()` (`lib/billing/webhook-log.ts`) specifically so a stored payload can be replayed by an admin "Retry" action — copying the existing dead-letter-job-retry template verbatim. Vendor-facing response codes on the live webhook route are unchanged (still non-2xx on failure, so Razorpay's own retry still fires) — additive instrumentation only, nothing in the existing settlement path was rewritten.
- **Phase D — Payment Management + Payment Methods**: `/admin/payments` (PaymentIntent list/detail, webhook log with one-click Retry, refunds tab). New `PAYMENT_METHODS_ENABLED` config (its own `payment_settings` category, not folded into the broad `providers` category, to avoid dragging unrelated LLM/Image/Voice/Video settings onto the payments page) wired into Razorpay Checkout's `method` options.
- **Phase E — Revenue Dashboard + Founder Dashboard**: `lib/admin/revenue.ts` — `getRevenueSummary`/`getRevenueByDay`/`getMRR`/`getARR`/`getTopPlansByRevenue`, MRR correctly interval-normalized (a YEARLY plan's price ÷ 12, not counted in full — this is exactly why Phase B's real `BillingInterval` enum mattered). `/admin/revenue` page. **Real bug caught by the bucketing test itself**: `bucketRevenueByDay()`'s first draft used local-time bucketing (`setHours(0,0,0,0)`), which silently split same-UTC-day payments into two buckets on this `Asia/Calcutta` (UTC+5:30) host — fixed to `Date.UTC(...)`-based bucketing before it shipped. `lib/admin/founder-dashboard.ts` composes revenue/MRR/ARR with cost-management totals, queue/storage signals, and a new `getSignupTrend()` (same UTC-day-bucketing care applied from the start, having just learned the lesson) into one dense stat-card page (`/admin/founder`) — the estimate cards (profit, margin, editor-cost-saved, time-saved, CLV, ARPU) combine INR revenue with USD cost via a new admin-configurable `USD_TO_INR_RATE`, and an admin-configurable per-video cost/time-saved assumption (`EDITOR_COST_SAVED_PER_VIDEO_INR`/`TIME_SAVED_PER_VIDEO_MINUTES`) — explicitly labeled as estimates in the UI, not invoice-accurate figures.
- **Phase F — Provider management verification + Installation checklist**: confirmed (not assumed) that `/admin/ai-providers`'s audit-log tab was already correctly wired end-to-end — a real gap was searched for and not found. `lib/admin/installation-status.ts` (`getInstallationChecklist()`) — a read-only "is this install production-ready" summary (real provider enabled with a key per category, OTP configured, invoice business details set), introduced with zero new settings of its own; surfaced inside Command Center (Phase H), not its own nav tab.
- **Phase G — Subscription Settings**: `pricing-form.tsx` extended with billing-interval/trial-days fields per SUBSCRIPTION plan (additive, the existing per-plan card UI untouched otherwise). `lib/admin/subscriptions.ts` + `/admin/subscriptions` — every subscriber with an admin-only **cancel now** action (immediate, distinct from the user's own cancel-at-period-end), live-verified against a real subscription (200 → `CANCELLED`; a second attempt correctly 409s).
- **Phase H — Founder Command Center**: `lib/admin/command-center.ts` composes `getHealthDashboard()`/`getAbuseReport()`/`getDeadLetterJobs()`/the new webhook+payment+subscription signals into 9 alerts, each linking straight to its real fix rather than a blind auto-remediation button (most of these — a real outage, a spend spike — need a founder's judgment, not a guessed automatic action). Three new thresholds (`DAILY_API_COST_ALERT_USD`/`STORAGE_BUDGET_GB`/`LOW_CREDIT_BALANCE_ALERT_THRESHOLD`) all default to **0 (disabled)** rather than a fabricated number — a guessed default would either nag immediately on a fresh install or never fire silently; only a founder-set value is honest here. `/admin/command-center`, live-verified end-to-end (correctly flagged 2 real dead-letter jobs in this dev DB while every other signal read clean).
- **Phase I — Subscription renewal/grace-period sweep**: `lib/billing/subscription-renewal.ts`'s `runSubscriptionRenewalSweep()` finds `ACTIVE` subscriptions whose period lapsed with no renewal webhook landing, moves them to `PAST_DUE`, and expires them once `SUBSCRIPTION_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS` has elapsed or `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWAL_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` sweep passes have gone by (whichever first) — exposed via `POST /api/internal/subscriptions/renew-sweep`, copying `credits/expire`'s secret-gated pattern verbatim (fails closed in production, open in dev). New `Subscription.renewalAttempts` column added via its own small additive migration. **A real gap this phase's new `PAST_DUE` state would otherwise have caused was caught and fixed**: `renewSubscription()`'s guard only accepted `status === "ACTIVE"`, so a late-arriving vendor webhook for an already-`PAST_DUE` subscription would have silently no-op'd forever instead of healing it back to `ACTIVE` — fixed to accept both statuses and reset `renewalAttempts` to 0 on a successful renewal. Both the lapse→PAST_DUE→EXPIRED path and the PAST_DUE→ACTIVE healing path were live-verified against a real subscription row (forced into the past, swept twice, confirmed `PAST_DUE` then `EXPIRED`; separately forced `PAST_DUE` and confirmed `renewSubscription()` healed it back to `ACTIVE` with `renewalAttempts` reset) — not just unit-tested.
- **Phase J — Credits grant tool + docs + final verification**: `lib/admin/credit-grants.ts` (`grantCreditsToUsers()`, a thin wrapper over the existing `grantCredits()` engine — targets explicit emails/phones/ids, not a rule-based segment builder, which is noted as a future extensibility item rather than built this milestone) folded into `/admin/pricing` as a new section, live-verified (granted to a real user by phone, correctly reported a fake phone as not-found). `ADMIN_GUIDE.md` gained entries for all 5 new pages plus an "Extending the Admin Panel" section documenting the new-provider/new-setting/new-dashboard-page/new-alert recipes this milestone itself followed. `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` updated with the new `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWAL_SWEEP_SECRET` env var. Final verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `vitest run` 177/177 passing (up from 159 at the start of this milestone — 18 new tests across `interval.ts`, `mock.provider.ts`'s refund, `revenue.ts`'s bucketing/MRR, `founder-dashboard.ts`'s signup bucketing), and every new page/route live-verified against the real dev server via a minted `dev-bypass` admin session (not just typecheck/lint/unit tests) — `/admin/payments`, `/admin/subscriptions`, `/admin/revenue`, `/admin/founder`, `/admin/command-center` all returned 200 with real DB-backed data, and the riskier state-machine logic (refund creation, webhook retry, subscription cancel/expire/heal, credit grant) was exercised against real rows, not mocked.
- **5 nav entries added** to `ADMIN_NAV_ITEMS` (`app/admin/layout.tsx`): Founder Dashboard, Command Center, Payments, Subscriptions, Revenue — 18 admin pages total now, all behind the same `role !== "ADMIN" → redirect` guard, unchanged.

### Milestone 14 — Premium Content Platform & Dashboard Redesign (2026-06-29)
A direct response to a code audit confirming the product's signed-in experience was video-only — the Dashboard was a welcome header + 4 stats + one button, `/create` had exactly two routes, and there was no Image/Social Media/Marketing Creative/Brand Assets pipeline at all (everything that existed funneled through `VideoProject`). This milestone built the 4 missing content pipelines from scratch and a full premium-SaaS Dashboard redesign — confirmed with the user up front to be new construction, not a rewiring fix, after directly inspecting the codebase rather than assuming. 10 phases (A–J), each verified with `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` before moving to the next.

- **Phase A — Schema**: one generic `CreativeProject` model (`kind`: `AI_IMAGE`/`SOCIAL_MEDIA`/`MARKETING_CREATIVE` discriminator) backs all three image-output pipelines — they're mechanically identical (prompt in, one image out, no render queue), differing only in preset list and prompt-style prefix, so one model avoids three near-duplicate tables. **New `CreativeTool` model is the single source of truth for every Dashboard card/quick-action/coming-soon stub** — admin CRUD, zero code changes to add/edit/reorder/enable one; `creditCostEstimate` is the *actual charged amount* (not a parallel display-only number), `promptTemplate`/`defaultProviderId` are real generation inputs, not metadata. Brand Assets has no project model by design (confirmed with the user) — generation writes land directly on the existing per-user `BrandKit` row, folded into the existing `/brand-kit` page rather than a new duplicate entry point. `Asset`/`CreditTransaction`/`GenerationLog` each gained a nullable `creativeProjectId`, mirroring their existing `videoProjectId` field exactly — a real correction surfaced during planning (those fields are genuinely `VideoProject`-only and can't carry a `CreativeProject.id`). `BusinessVertical` gained `FINANCE`; `Template` gained `isFeatured`/`defaultObjective` so the Dashboard's "Featured templates" and "Festival" trending tile are backed by real filterable data, not fabricated. Seeded via the existing `seedDefaults()` path (reachable from both `prisma/seed.ts` and the Installation Wizard) — 22 `CreativeTool` rows (6 main cards, 8 quick actions, 3 disabled Brand Asset config-only rows, 5 coming-soon stubs) plus 2 new `Template` rows.
- **Phase B — Generation engine wiring**: new `reorderProvidersByPreference()` (`lib/generation/engine.ts`) lets a `CreativeTool.defaultProviderId` ("admin's default AI model per tool," the harder of two scoped options, explicitly chosen over the simpler metadata-only version) bias which provider is tried first **without removing any existing safety net** — it reorders the already health/budget-filtered priority list rather than replacing it, so an unhealthy/over-budget preferred provider still safely falls through to the rest of the chain. `generateImage()`/`generateScript()` both gained a `preferredProviderId?` param built on top of this. `GenerationContext`/`GenerationLog`/`consumeCredits()` all gained a `creativeProjectId` field, parallel to `videoProjectId`.
- **Phase C — Preset catalogue**: `lib/validations/creative.ts` (Prisma-free, client-importable, mirrors `lib/validations/video.ts`'s exact style) — `AI_IMAGE_PRESETS`/`SOCIAL_MEDIA_PRESETS`/`MARKETING_CREATIVE_PRESETS` (17 presets total), each mapped to the nearest of the **existing 3 `AspectRatio` values** rather than widening that shared enum (a deliberate choice to avoid coupling unrelated systems through one enum), `PRESET_PROMPT_PREFIX` style-guidance map, `createCreativeProjectSchema` validating preset↔kind consistency. `lib/validations/brand-kit.ts` extended with logo/palette/guidelines generation schemas.
- **Phase D — Shared generation libraries**: `lib/creative/engine.ts`'s `generateCreativeImage()` is the ONE function behind AI Image/Social Media/Marketing Creative generation — looks up the relevant `CreativeTool` row for cost/prompt-prefix/preferred-provider, then the exact charge-order pattern already established by `renderTalkingHeadScene()` (pre-check balance → generate → upload+record asset → atomically charge + mark complete; **never charges on a failed generation**). `lib/brand-kit/identity-engine.ts` mirrors the same pattern for `generateBrandLogo()`/`generateBrandPalette()`/`generateBrandGuidelines()`, keyed to 3 disabled-by-default `CreativeTool` config rows. `lib/search/service.ts`'s `searchUserContent()` — real substring `contains` matching across the user's own videos/creatives/templates, deliberately not labeled or built as "AI search" (no semantic search infra exists). `lib/dashboard/continue-working.ts`/`get-dashboard-data.ts` — one shared data-fetcher feeding both the Dashboard page (direct call, server component) and `GET /api/dashboard` (client refetch), so the two can never compute different numbers.
- **Phase E — Admin surfaces**: `/admin/creative-tools` (full CRUD grouped by category — inline-edit label/icon/gradient/credit cost/estimated seconds/prompt template/default provider/enabled, up/down reorder via `sortOrder`, add-new form) and `/admin/templates` (list/create, toggle Active/Featured, set a default objective) — the literal fulfillment of "admin configures dashboard cards/credit cost/enable-disable/default AI model/prompt templates/icons/order, no code change needed," live-verified end-to-end (see Phase J).
- **Phase F — API routes**: `POST/GET /api/creative-projects` (+`[id]`), `POST /api/brand-kit/generate/{logo,palette,guidelines}`, `GET /api/search`, `GET/POST /api/admin/creative-tools` (+`[id]` PATCH), `GET/POST /api/admin/templates` (+`[id]` PATCH), `GET /api/dashboard` (composed read, 15s per-user cache).
- **Phase G — New pages + 14-item sidebar**: `/create/image`, `/create/social`, `/create/marketing` (shared `CreativeGeneratorForm`), `/studio` (AI Studio hub — lists `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` video projects with Resume buttons, matching `videos/[id]/studio`'s own existing eligibility gate exactly rather than inventing a new one), `/projects` (unified VideoProject+CreativeProject list), `/images`, `/marketing-creatives`, `/templates` and `/media-library` (real pages — both already had working list APIs and were `.gitkeep`-only directories, closing a documented Pending Features gap rather than scope creep), `/settings` (new — minimal account/business info page, built so the new sidebar's "Settings" entry isn't a dead link). `/videos` gained a `?type=talking_head` filter so "Videos" and "Talking Head" can be distinct sidebar entries over the same underlying model. `create/page.tsx` now reads `?platform=&objective=&templateId=&mode=` to pre-fill Step 0 for every Quick action that launches the Video pipeline. `dashboard-nav-items.ts` rewritten to the 14-item list (Dashboard/Create/Projects/AI Studio★/Images/Videos/Talking Head/Marketing Creatives/Templates/Assets/Brand Kit/Credits/Usage/Settings) with a `mobile` flag so the bottom tab bar shows a curated 5-item subset instead of all 14. `/brand-kit` extended (not replaced) with Generate Logo/Palette/Guidelines sections on top of its existing settings fields.
- **Phase H — Dashboard redesign (the centerpiece)**: full rewrite of `/dashboard` plus new premium primitives under `components/dashboard/` (`GradientToolCard`/`QuickActionChip`, `AnimatedCounter` — framer-motion's first real usage in this codebase, `FeatureChip`, `ComingSoonCard`, `DashboardSearchBar`). All 8 required sections: Hero (search + Quick Create + compact recent-activity strip), 6 Main Cards (from `CreativeTool` rows, each routed via `resolveToolHref()` per the brief's exact pipeline mapping — AI Video→Video Engine, AI Image→Image Engine, Social Media→Creative Engine, Marketing Creative→Creative Engine, Talking Head→Talking Head Pipeline, Brand Assets→Brand Kit page), AI Studio promo (largest section, NEW badge, 8 real feature chips, "Launch AI Studio" CTA), Quick Actions (8 chips), Statistics (7 animated counters: Credits/Videos/Images/Talking Head/Projects/Storage/API Usage), Continue Working (categorized, Resume buttons), Trending Templates (7 tiles — 6 backed by real `BusinessVertical` values including the new `FINANCE`, "Festival" backed by the new `Template.defaultObjective`), Coming Soon (5 inert cards, toast-only "Notify Me," genuinely no backend per the brief).
- **Phase I — Tests**: 16 new `vitest` assertions (193 total, up from 177) — `reorderProvidersByPreference()`'s reordering/no-op/not-found cases, the preset catalogue's internal consistency (`PRESET_PROMPT_PREFIX` coverage, no cross-kind key collisions) and `createCreativeProjectSchema`'s preset↔kind validation, `resolveToolHref()`'s routing precedence. Matches this codebase's established testing convention exactly: only pure, DB-free logic gets a unit test (confirmed by auditing every existing `*.test.ts` file before writing new ones) — the prisma-touching orchestration functions (`generateCreativeImage()`, the identity-engine, `searchUserContent()`) are exercised by Phase J's live HTTP pass instead, same division already used for `captions/engine.ts`/`scenes/engine.ts`.
- **Phase J — Final verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `vitest run` 193/193, `next build` clean (73/73 pages). A scripted live HTTP + SSR-HTML pass against a real Postgres-backed dev server via 3 minted NextAuth session cookies (1 USER, 1 ADMIN, 1 zero-balance USER) covered: the Dashboard's SSR HTML containing all 6 main cards, all 8 quick actions, all 8 AI Studio feature chips, all 7 trending tiles, all 5 coming-soon cards, and the 3 stat labels; all 11 new/updated pages returning 200; one `CreativeProject` generation per kind with the exact seeded credit cost charged and matching `Asset`+`CreditTransaction` rows created; an insufficient-balance attempt correctly 402ing with **zero** rows created; all 3 Brand Kit generation actions; search; and the full admin CRUD loop (disable `ai_image` → confirmed its card disappears from the Dashboard within the cache TTL with no code change → re-enable → create-then-delete a brand-new tool) proving the "no code change required after deployment" claim end-to-end, not just by design. All 14 sidebar links and both new admin nav entries checked for 200 (no dead links).
  - **2 real bugs found and fixed by this live pass** (neither caught by `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest`, both only surfaced once an actual browser-shaped request hit the page): (1) the 5 seeded Coming Soon `CreativeTool` rows were `enabled: false` (correct for "no backend exists"), but the Dashboard's tools query filtered on `enabled: true` for every category — conflating "has a working pipeline" with "show the card," which made the entire Coming Soon section silently disappear. Fixed by re-scoping what `enabled` means for that one category (a Coming Soon card's visibility never gates an actual generation call, so it defaults to visible) rather than adding a second flag. (2) `lib/format.ts`'s `formatBytes` function was passed as a prop (`formatter={formatBytes}`) from the Dashboard's Server Component into the client `AnimatedCounter` — Next.js can't serialize a function reference across the Server→Client boundary, which threw `GET /dashboard 500` in the dev server logs despite the page still emitting a complete, correct-looking HTML body for everything rendered *before* the failing flight-payload serialization (the reason this one was easy to miss: literal text-content checks on the response body all still passed). Fixed by replacing the function prop with a fixed `unit?: "bytes"` discriminator that `AnimatedCounter` formats internally — also lints/typechecks as a reminder that a function-typed prop crossing that specific boundary is a recurring foot-gun, not a one-off mistake.
  - **lucide-react no longer exports brand icons** (`Instagram`/`Youtube` — removed for trademark reasons in a past major version) — caught by `tsc`, not assumed; the seeded `instagram_reel`/`youtube_shorts` tools were re-pointed at `Film`/`PlaySquare` instead.
- **Post-completion functionality audit (same day)** — full `FUNCTIONALITY_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md` produced, 79/79 live HTTP+DB assertions passing across every Dashboard link, every generation pipeline (with exact credit-charge verification per pipeline), Talking Head, and Brand Assets. 2 issues found and fixed: (1) three concurrent `next dev` processes (leftover from earlier restart cycles) were racing on the same `.next` directory, causing an intermittent `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` crash on `/videos/[id]` — an infra issue, not an app defect; fixed by killing all instances and running exactly one. (2) Continue Working's links for Image/Marketing Creative projects (`/images?projectId=`, `/marketing-creatives?projectId=`) were dead-ends — both pages ignored the `projectId` param entirely. Fixed: both pages now render `id={project.id}` on each card and highlight the matching one; `continue-working.ts`'s hrefs append `#<id>` so the browser scrolls to it natively, no JS needed.

### AI Image Generator — premium 5-step wizard (2026-06-30)
Redesigned `/create/image` from the flat shared `CreativeGeneratorForm` into a dedicated Midjourney/Leonardo-style flow: a short idea → "✨ Enhance Prompt" expands it into a professional prompt via the LLM Generation Engine → an editable preview the user can revise before any cost is incurred → "Generate Image" calls the real (paid) Image Generation API → result with Download/Generate Again/Edit Prompt/Create Variation. `CreativeGeneratorForm` itself is untouched and still serves `/create/social` and `/create/marketing` exactly as before — this is additive, not a replacement of shared infrastructure.

- **Two genuinely separate APIs, never mixed**, per explicit requirement: `POST /api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt` (new) is a stateless, free LLM call — no `CreativeProject` row, no credit charge, rate-limited under the existing free `ai_assistant` bucket (the same one Script Studio's rewrite/regenerate already use). `POST /api/creative-projects` (existing, byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior) remains the only path that ever creates a row or charges a credit, fed the *enhanced* prompt as its `prompt` field — the wizard never sends the user's raw short idea to generation.
- **`LLMGenerateRequest` gained an optional `systemPrompt?: string`** (`lib/providers/llm/types.ts`) so a caller can override `OpenAILLMProvider`/`GeminiLLMProvider`'s hardcoded "short-form video script writer" persona — previously the only persona either adapter could ever send, which would have been wrong for prompt enhancement. Additive and opt-in: every existing caller (video script generation, Script Studio) is unaffected since none of them pass it.
- **`MockLLMProvider` gained a new pattern-matched branch** (`extractImageIdea()`/`simulateImagePromptEnhancement()`), recognizing the enhancement call's `"Original idea: ..."` marker the same way its existing Script Studio branches recognize their own markers — without it, Mock mode would have returned a fake video script for an image-prompt request, same class of gap closed for every prior Script Studio addition.
- **`lib/creative/prompt-enhancement.ts`** (new) — `enhanceImagePrompt()` plus a pure `cleanEnhancedPrompt()` helper (strips wrapping quotes/markdown fences/a leading "Prompt:" label, collapses to one line, caps length) — the one function with a unit test (9 new assertions), matching this codebase's established line between pure logic (tested) and IO/orchestration (exercised live).
- **Reusable `RotatingLoadingText` component** (`components/creative/rotating-loading-text.tsx`) drives both the enhancing step and the generating step's rotating messages + simulated progress bar/countdown — one implementation, two message lists/estimates, no duplicated loading-animation logic. The generating step's estimate is the real `ai_image` `CreativeTool.estimatedSeconds` fetched server-side, not a hardcoded number.
- **"Generate Again" and "Create Variation" are the same action** (fresh text-to-image generation with the identical enhanced prompt) — confirmed with the user rather than assumed, since this codebase's image pipeline is text-to-image only with no img2img/edit endpoint anywhere; building real image-to-image variation would be a separate feature, out of scope here.
- **On a failed generate call, the enhanced prompt is never cleared** — the wizard returns to the preview step with the exact same editable text still in state, so retrying needs no rewriting (explicit requirement, verified live: a rejected call charges nothing and the client never loses the prompt).
- Verified live end-to-end against the real OpenAI key: a real enhance call ("Luxury villa Facebook ad" → a materially longer, different, professional prompt) feeding a real `gpt-image-1` generation, producing an actual photorealistic villa image (not a placeholder), with credits charged exactly once (only at the generate step, zero at enhance) and the DB-stored `prompt` confirmed to be the enhanced text, never the raw idea.

### Milestone 15 — AI Creative Studio Upgrade: Universal Workflow, Reference-Image Analysis, Logo Compositing, Rich Aspect Ratios (2026-06-30)
A ground-up quality upgrade of the entire creative-generation workflow (not a prompt tweak), aimed at agency-level output from a single short sentence. Generalizes the AI Image wizard above into one shared studio used by all three content kinds, and adds three genuinely new capabilities: optional reference-image style analysis, optional brand-logo compositing, and exact-pixel platform sizing — all flowing through the same `/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt` → `/api/creative-projects` pipeline, never a parallel path.

- **Universal wizard, one component**: `components/creative/creative-studio.tsx` (new, `kind`-parameterized) replaces both the AI-Image-only wizard and the older flat `CreativeGeneratorForm` — Social Media and Marketing Creative now get the same Enhance → Preview → Generate → Result flow AI Image already had, with zero duplicated state-machine code. New shared sub-components: `asset-upload-tile.tsx` (reference image + brand logo upload, one implementation), `aspect-ratio-selector.tsx` (rich named-platform picker with exact pixel dimensions + a Custom width/height entry), `prompt-editor.tsx` (the preview-step editor, extracted out of the wizard). `lib/upload/put-with-progress.ts` extracted from the Talking Head uploader so the XHR-progress helper has exactly one implementation, reused by all three.
- **Structured, premium prompt-engineering pipeline** (`lib/creative/prompt-enhancement.ts`, generalized): `enhanceCreativePrompt()` replaces the AI-Image-only `enhanceImagePrompt()` as the one enhancement service shared by all three kinds. Its system prompt is a structured template (not keyword-stuffing) that always weaves in composition, camera/lens, lighting, depth, perspective, materials, premium typography, white space, brand hierarchy, marketing psychology, color harmony, professional ad layout, platform framing, explicit quality keywords, and a negative-prompt clause — the literal answer to "study why ChatGPT prompts produce better realism": one comprehensive instruction template the LLM fills in per-idea. `cleanEnhancedPrompt()`'s cap raised 800→4000 chars; `createCreativeProjectSchema.prompt`'s max raised 2000→4500 to match.
- **Reference-image analysis is a real vision-LLM call, not "make it similar"**: `LLMGenerateRequest` gained `imageUrl?: string` (additive, opt-in); `OpenAILLMProvider` sends OpenAI's mixed `content: [{type:"text"},{type:"image_url"}]` array when set; `GeminiLLMProvider` fetches+base64-encodes the image into `inlineData` (Gemini's REST API needs inline bytes, not a URL); `MockLLMProvider` gained a deterministic ~550-word style-description branch so the flow is fully testable without API keys. New `lib/creative/reference-analysis.ts`'s `analyzeReferenceImage()` extracts composition/lighting/camera/typography/spacing/layout/color/branding/realism/mood/shadows/reflections/texture/depth/negative-space into one 500-600 word passage describing the *visual language*, which then becomes the style backbone of the enhancement call (`enhanceCreativePrompt`'s `referenceStyleDescription` param) — the system prompt explicitly forbids "make it similar" phrasing.
- **Real deterministic logo compositing, not an AI edit call**: new `lib/image/` module — `resize.ts`'s `resizeToTarget()` (sharp `fit:"cover", position:"attention"` smart-crop to exact platform pixel dimensions, since `gpt-image-1` only ever returns one of 3 fixed sizes) and `composite-logo.ts`'s `compositeLogo()`/`calculateLogoPlacement()` (pure-math placement, unit-tested separately from the sharp I/O — scales the logo to an admin-configurable percentage of canvas width while preserving its own aspect ratio via `fit:"inside"`, positions at an admin-configurable corner with a safe margin, never stretches it). `sharp` promoted from an undeclared transitive dependency to an explicit one. Two new admin config keys (`CREATIVE_LOGO_POSITION`, `CREATIVE_LOGO_SCALE_PERCENT`, category `generation_policy`) — placement isn't hardcoded with no admin control.
- **`StorageProvider` gained a `download(key): Promise<Buffer>` method** (implemented by both Mock and S3 adapters) — a real bug caught during live verification: the logo-compositing step initially called `getPublicUrl()` + server-side `fetch()`, which works for S3's absolute URLs but throws on Mock storage's app-relative `/uploads/...` path (unfetchable outside a browser). `download()` reads bytes directly by key (local disk for Mock, `GetObjectCommand` for S3), which is the architecturally correct fix, not an env-var workaround.
- **`CreativeProject` gained `referenceAssetId`/`logoAssetId`/`targetWidth`/`targetHeight`** (all nullable, two new named `Asset` relations mirroring the existing `resultAssetId` pattern) — `generateCreativeImage()`'s upload step changed from `storage.uploadFromUrl()` (couldn't post-process) to: fetch provider bytes → resize-to-target if set → composite logo if set → `storage.upload()` the final processed buffer. Both optional asset references are ownership-checked (`findFirst` scoped to `userId`) before being persisted or read, never trusted from the request body directly.
- **Rich platform aspect-ratio catalog, decoupled from the shared 3-value `AspectRatio` enum** (deliberately not widened — it's shared with `VideoProject`): every named preset gained an exact `targetWidth`/`targetHeight` (Instagram Portrait 1080×1350, Square 1080×1080, Story 1080×1920, Facebook Feed 1200×1500, Facebook Cover 1640×624, Pinterest 1000×1500, LinkedIn 1200×627, YouTube Thumbnail 1280×720, Website Banner 1600×400), plus a `custom` entry per kind for direct width/height input (clamped 256-2048px). New pure `nearestAspectRatioBucket()` (log-space ratio distance, unit-tested) maps any pixel pair to the nearest of the 3 generation-time buckets — used for every preset's bucket assignment programmatically rather than hand-picked, and for `custom`/any future preset automatically.
- **Tests**: 14 new `vitest` assertions (216 total, up from 202) — `nearestAspectRatioBucket()` (6), `calculateLogoPlacement()` (6, pure math only, no sharp I/O), `cleanEnhancedPrompt()`'s new 4000-char cap, plus updated preset-catalog/schema tests reflecting the shared `custom` key and the Custom-preset dimension requirement.
