- **Live verification** (20/20 assertions against a real Postgres-backed dev server, real `gpt-image-1` calls, minted NextAuth session cookie): idea-only enhancement charges 0 credits and creates no row; reference-image enhancement (Mock vision branch) produces a materially different, style-aware prompt; a cross-user reference-asset id correctly 404s instead of leaking; a real named-platform generation (Instagram Story, reference + logo) returns a `COMPLETED` project with the reference/logo/target-dimensions persisted, and the **actual downloaded output image measured by `sharp` is exactly 1080×1920** with the logo visibly, undistorted, composited bottom-right; a real Custom-dimension generation (900×600) likewise measured exact; credits charged exactly once per generation; an invalid Custom request (missing width/height) 400s and charges nothing. Visually confirmed: a genuine premium food-photography image with "NEW MENU LAUNCH" typography and a cleanly placed logo, not a placeholder. All test users/assets/scripts cleaned up after verification.

### Milestone 16 — AI Creative Engine Redesign Phase 1: Universal JSON Prompt, Provider Adapters, Design Intelligence Library (2026-06-30)
Phase 1 of turning the creative pipeline into a "Universal AI Creative Engine": every generation request is now built into a structured intermediate JSON before any provider ever sees it — the literal "never send the user's raw prompt directly to any AI provider" requirement — applied to the existing, already-live AI Image / Social Media / Marketing Creative pipeline (no parallel system). Video generation's JSON extension (`storyboard`/`camera_motion`/`character_consistency`/etc.) and true vector-embedding search are explicitly deferred to future phases (user-approved scope decisions — see `PROJECT_STATUS.md` history / the original plan for the full reasoning).

- **Universal JSON Prompt** (`lib/prompt-os/schema.ts`'s `universalPromptSchema`) — a Zod schema mirroring the requested shape (`intent`/`industry`/`platform`/`creative_type`/`style`/`layout`/`typography`/`lighting`/`camera`/`composition`/`branding`/`colors`/`marketing`/`negative_constraints`/`quality`/`output`). Every nested section is built via a `section()` helper combining `z.object({...known fields}).catchall(z.unknown())` defaulted to `{}` — always-present, never `undefined`, and tolerant of unknown future fields (including the deferred video fields) without a migration. (Zod 4 quirk: `.default({})` on a generic `z.object(shape).catchall(...)` defeats overload resolution when the shape is a type parameter — worked around with a narrow, documented `any`-cast inside `section()`, verified both at the type level and the runtime level in `schema.test.ts`.)
- **`buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()`** (`lib/prompt-os/builder.ts`) replaces `lib/creative/prompt-enhancement.ts`'s `enhanceCreativePrompt()` entirely (one enhancement path, not two) — ONE JSON-mode LLM call (via the existing `generateScript()` engine, full failover/retry/health for free) that fills in composition/camera/lighting/depth/typography/marketing-psychology/negative-constraints/quality-keywords from a single user sentence — "the user should only need to write one simple sentence." When a reference image's analysis is available, its fields pre-fill `style`/`layout`/`typography`/`lighting`/`camera`/`composition`/`colors`/`marketing` so the model executes the idea **in** that visual language; a `BrandKit`'s colors/font feed `branding`/`typography` automatically. `cleanEnhancedPrompt()` (text-cleanup, 4000-char cap) moved here from the deleted `prompt-enhancement.ts`, now sanitizing adapter output instead of raw LLM text.
- **Design Intelligence Library, structured metadata** (not true embeddings yet — user-approved phased decision): `lib/design-intelligence/analyze-asset.ts`'s `analyzeAssetForLibrary()` replaces `lib/creative/reference-analysis.ts`'s free-text `analyzeReferenceImage()` — a JSON-mode vision-LLM call extracting every requested field (industry/category/style/mood/lighting/composition/typography/camera/lens/perspective/depth/texture/hierarchy/whiteSpace/luxuryLevel/modernLevel/minimalism/platform/aspectRatio/headlinePosition/ctaPosition/logoPosition/marketingGoal/targetAudience/colorPalette/objects/visualLanguage), validated by `lib/design-intelligence/schema.ts`'s `assetAnalysisSchema`. New `AssetAnalysis` model (1:1 with `Asset`, cascade-deleted) — 5 fields (`industry`/`category`/`style`/`mood`/`platform`) promoted to real filterable columns via `splitAssetAnalysis()`, the rest in a `details Json` column. This **is** the requested `ai-assets/{references,metadata,...}` taxonomy, mapped onto existing models rather than a redundant parallel folder system (`Asset`+`AssetAnalysis` = references/metadata, `BrandKit` = brand-kits/logos/fonts, `PromptTemplate` = prompt-templates — `embeddings`/`indexes` are the deferred vector layer). Analysis runs lazily — the first time an upload is used as a reference, keyed off no existing `AssetAnalysis` row.
- **Reference Search**: `lib/design-intelligence/search.ts`'s `listRecentReferences()` + new `GET /api/design-intelligence/recent-references` — the user's own previously-analyzed reference uploads, surfaced as a "Recent references" thumbnail picker in `AssetUploadTile`/`CreativeStudio` so a reference can be reused without re-uploading. Recency + filtering, not similarity ranking (no embeddings yet, per the phased decision).
- **Provider Adapters — JSON → vendor-optimal prompt text** (`lib/prompt-os/adapters/`): pure `(prompt: UniversalPrompt) => string` functions — `openai.adapter.ts` (flowing photography-brief sentences, folds `negative_constraints` into an "Avoid:" clause since `gpt-image-1` has no separate negative-prompt parameter at all), `flux.adapter.ts` (comma-separated SDXL-tag style, deliberately omits negative constraints from the text — relies on the dedicated `ImageGenerateRequest.negativePrompt` channel instead), `ideogram.adapter.ts` (explicitly calls out exact headline/CTA on-image text content and placement — Ideogram's differentiator is in-image text rendering), `generic.adapter.ts` (safe descriptive-paragraph fallback for any unregistered provider, e.g. `mock`). A registry (`adapters/index.ts`'s `resolvePromptAdapter()`) resolves by image-provider id — adding a future provider is one new adapter function, never a call-site change, the literal "switching providers without changing application logic" requirement. Research confirmed 5 of the 6 named vendors (OpenAI/Flux/Runway/Kling, Gemini-as-LLM) already had real HTTP integrations — only **Ideogram** was genuinely missing, added as `lib/providers/image/ideogram.provider.ts` (REST adapter, ships disabled by default like the other best-effort vendors, registered in `IMAGE_PROVIDER_IDS`/the factory/`GENERATION_COST_RATES`/the Admin AI Providers catalogue/`testProviderConnection()`).
- **`POST /api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt` rewritten**: builds the Universal JSON (lazily analyzing+persisting the reference image first if needed) → resolves which image provider will actually run (`tool.defaultProviderId` else the first enabled `IMAGE` provider, the same resolution order generation itself uses) → runs that provider's adapter to produce the editable preview text → returns **both** the text and the underlying JSON. The client's existing edit-then-submit flow is unchanged — whatever text the user sees (edited or not) still originated from the JSON→adapter pipeline; the JSON round-trips through the client and is re-validated server-side. `CreativeProject` gained `universalPrompt Json?` — the structured record of what was actually used, independent of later text edits.
- **`negative_constraints` wired into the existing negative-prompt channel, not duplicated logic**: `lib/creative/engine.ts`'s `generateCreativeImage()` now merges `universalPrompt.negative_constraints` into the same `ImageGenerateRequest.negativePrompt` field the wizard's own "Avoid" input already populates — the channel Flux's adapter deliberately leaves out of its prompt text, and a harmless no-op for OpenAI's provider (which ignores the field, since its adapter already folds negative constraints into the prompt text directly).
- **JSON-mode LLM calls** (additive): `LLMGenerateRequest.responseFormat?: "text" | "json"` — `OpenAILLMProvider` sets `response_format: {type:"json_object"}`, `GeminiLLMProvider` sets `generationConfig.responseMimeType: "application/json"`, `MockLLMProvider` gained deterministic JSON branches (distinguished by `imageUrl` presence: asset-analysis vs. prompt-building) replacing its now-superseded free-text image-enhancement/reference-analysis branches.
- **Tests**: 19 new `vitest` assertions (235 total, up from 216) — `universalPromptSchema` (defaults, full population, catchall extensibility, rejection cases), `assetAnalysisSchema`/`splitAssetAnalysis()`, and one file covering all 4 adapters (vendor-distinct phrasing per adapter, the registry's id→adapter resolution, and the core architectural proof — "the same input produces measurably different text across vendors"). `cleanEnhancedPrompt()`'s existing 9 tests moved to `prompt-os/builder.test.ts` unchanged.
- **Live verification** (17/17 assertions against a real Postgres-backed dev server, Mock providers, minted NextAuth session cookie): idea-only enhancement returns a Universal JSON Prompt with `style`/`camera`/`quality.keywords` genuinely populated; a reference-image upload produces a real `AssetAnalysis` row (`industry="hospitality"`, `style="premium editorial"`, `mood="aspirational"`, non-empty `details`); toggling the resolved provider between `openai_images` and `flux` for the identical idea produces **measurably different preview text** (flowing sentences vs. comma-tag list — confirmed by direct string inequality, not just code inspection); a full generation completes end-to-end reusing the existing resize/logo-composite/credit-charge machinery unchanged, with `universalPrompt` persisted and `status: COMPLETED`; the Recent References endpoint returns the previously-analyzed upload. All test users/provider-config rows cleaned up after verification.

### Milestone 17 — Dashboard Redesign: Premium AI-First Home, Real Trending Data, Admin-Curated Inspiration (2026-06-30)
A full visual/UX redesign of `/dashboard` (Milestone 14's generic-admin-panel layout) into a premium, AI-first home for the "AI Creative Operating System" — 8 sections, each with exactly one purpose, no information shown twice. A reference screenshot was supplied for spacing/quality inspiration only, deliberately not recreated. Two of the 8 requested sections (Trending, Inspiration) had no backing data before this milestone; both shipped as genuinely real, not fabricated or stubbed, per explicit user decision.

- **Trending — real usage counts, not invented numbers**: new `lib/dashboard/trending.ts`. `getTrendingIndustries()` sums real `VideoProject` counts per `Template.vertical` (`prisma.template.findMany` with a `_count.videoProjects` relation aggregate, reduced/sorted in a pure, unit-tested `summarizeIndustryUsage()` helper); `getTrendingObjectives()` is a direct `prisma.videoProject.groupBy(["objective"])` — `objective` is non-nullable on every `VideoProject`, template-based or not, so this is a complete platform-wide aggregate. "Trending creative styles" (the brief's third facet) is deliberately **not** represented — nothing in the schema tracks a notion of "style" on a project, and inventing a number for it would violate the standing no-fabricated-data posture. Either row independently hides itself if its data is empty (honest on a fresh install).
- **Inspiration — real admin-curated content, not a placeholder**: new `INSPIRATION_LIBRARY` entry in `lib/admin/config.ts`'s `CONFIG_REGISTRY` (array of `{id, label, description?, imageUrl, category: HOOK|WINNING_AD|LAYOUT|CREATIVE, href?}`, default `[]`) — same established pattern as `BACKGROUND_MUSIC_LIBRARY`/`STOCK_ASSET_LIBRARY`, gets a working JSON-editor admin UI for free via the existing generic `AdminConfigForm`, now wired onto `/admin/creative-tools` (already the home for "what shows on the Dashboard") alongside the existing `CreativeToolsManager`. No performance/CTR-tracking model exists anywhere in the system to back this with real telemetry, so unlike Trending it's editorial content, not computed — an honest empty state renders until an admin curates something.
- **`getDashboardData()` extended, not duplicated**: `trendingIndustries`/`trendingObjectives`/`inspiration` added to the same composed `Promise.all` read (`lib/dashboard/get-dashboard-data.ts`) that already served `GET /api/dashboard` and the server-rendered page — one data source, unchanged contract for existing fields.
- **7 new presentational components** under `components/dashboard/`, all consuming existing or newly-extended data with zero parallel data-fetch paths: `HeroBanner` (personalized greeting + reused `DashboardSearchBar` + a single real "Quick Continue" card for the most-recent in-progress item — replacing the old hero's pill-strip, which duplicated the same recent-items data as the full list below in a worse format; a compact "AI Studio · newest capability" pill replaces the old hero-sized promo slab that competed with the hero itself for attention), `QuickCreateGrid` (same `CreativeTool` `MAIN_CARD` data and untouched `GradientToolCard`, just a bento-style asymmetric grid — the first admin-ordered tool gets a wider cell via CSS `col-span-2`, no component fork needed), `ContinueEditingRail` (horizontal-scroll cards replacing the old vertical list, same `getContinueWorking()` data), `TrendingSection`, `InspirationSection`, `PopularTemplatesSection` (same `featuredTemplates`, restyled as thumbnail-forward tiles), `UsageOverview` (same `AnimatedCounter`, tightened to the brief's exact 5 metrics — Credits/Videos/Images/Storage/API usage; the old "Projects" card was a pure sum of the other counts and dropped as a duplicate, "Talking Head" folded into the Videos card as a sub-label since both are `VideoProject` rows distinguished only by `sourceType`). `gradient-tool-card.tsx`, `coming-soon-card.tsx`, `tool-icon.tsx`, `animated-counter.tsx`, `feature-chip.tsx`, `dashboard-search-bar.tsx`, `tool-routing.ts`, `continue-working.ts` are all reused completely unchanged.
- **What's New — deliberately not built**: no changelog/release-notes model exists to back a dashboard widget honestly, and `/release-notes` is already one click away in the sidebar; flagged explicitly in the plan rather than silently dropped.
- **Tests**: 5 new `vitest` assertions (240 total, up from 235) — `summarizeIndustryUsage()`'s pure reduction logic (multi-template summing per vertical, descending sort, zero-count filtering, limit), matching this codebase's established "DB-bound functions verified live, their pure logic unit-tested" convention.
- **Live + visual verification** against a real Postgres-backed dev server, minted NextAuth session cookie, real seeded `Template`/`VideoProject` rows across multiple verticals/objectives and real `INSPIRATION_LIBRARY` content: Playwright screenshots at desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px) widths confirmed zero console/page errors, every section rendering with real (not fabricated) data — Trending counts matched actual seeded usage, the bento Quick Create grid and horizontal-scroll Continue Editing rail rendered correctly, Inspiration's curated images and category badges rendered, and the layout degraded cleanly to single/double-column at mobile width. One bug caught only by the screenshot (not by `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest`/`next build`): an initial `row-span-2` on the flagship Quick Create card had no visible effect since the grid's implicit row tracks have no fixed height for a 2-row span to meaningfully stretch into — simplified to `col-span-2` only (a wider, not taller, flagship card), which does render correctly. All preview users/templates/screenshots cleaned up after verification.

### Milestone 18 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 2: Root-Cause Overflow Fix, Live Studio Hero, Premium Card Depth (2026-06-30)
A follow-up pass on Milestone 17's dashboard, driven by a second, much more demanding design review: fix a real horizontal-scroll bug at its root cause (not by hiding overflow), correct inconsistent card heights, rebuild the static hero into the centerpiece, and add the depth/motion/glassmorphism the first pass was missing — all while keeping the same architecture, routing, and `getDashboardData()` composed read.

- **Horizontal-scroll root cause, found and fixed (not papered over)**: `ContinueEditingRail`'s edge-bleed technique (`-mx-4 px-4 sm:-mx-6 sm:px-6 lg:-mx-12 lg:px-12`) switched breakpoints at Tailwind's `sm` (640px), one step earlier than `Container`'s own `px-4 md:px-6 lg:px-12` switches at `md` (768px) — between 640–767px the rail's negative margin (24px) exceeded `Container`'s padding (16px) by 8px per side, pushing the rail's box wider than its parent with nothing in the layout tree clipping it. Fixed by aligning the rail's breakpoints to `Container`'s exactly (`sm:` → `md:`). `overflow-x-clip` added to the dashboard layout's root flex div as defense-in-depth on top of the real fix, not instead of it. Verified via a Playwright script measuring `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth` at 375/640/768/1024/1440px — zero overflow at every width, including the exact 640–767px window where the bug previously lived.
- **Card-height alignment**: audited every dashboard grid for `h-full` on its card root so short-content cards (e.g. a template with no description) stop sitting shorter than long-content neighbors in the same row (`PopularTemplatesSection`, `ComingSoonCard`, the new Trending and Continue Editing cards).
- **Hero rebuilt into the centerpiece**: `HeroBanner` is now a two-column layout — the left column keeps 100% of the prior functionality (greeting, search, Quick Create + new secondary "Browse templates" CTA, the most-recent in-progress item folded into a compact "Continue: …" chip) — beside a new decorative `HeroStudioPreview` component (desktop/laptop only): a glassmorphic panel with a gradient "video preview," a timeline strip of colored clip blocks, a 3-icon layer rail, and 6 floating AI-capability chips (Captions, Voice, B-Roll, Scene Replace, Music, Auto Zoom) gently bobbing via `framer-motion` — built entirely from existing tokens/Tailwind/framer-motion (no new dependency, no stock illustration), explicitly inert/non-interactive.
- **Quick Create trimmed to exactly 4 cards**: `social_media` and `brand_assets` moved from `MAIN_CARD` to `QUICK_ACTION` in `lib/seed-defaults.ts`'s `CREATIVE_TOOLS` (the actual seed source of truth — a one-off DB edit would have been silently reverted by `seedDefaults()`'s upsert), leaving AI Video/AI Image/Marketing Creative/Talking Head as the only main cards; `brand_assets` keeps its `/brand-kit` `routeOverride`, so its destination is unchanged, just demoted to a chip alongside Social Media. Re-seeded against the dev DB and confirmed live.
- **`GradientToolCard` and `QuickActionChip` extended in place** (not forked): cards gained a true gradient-ring border on hover (CSS `mask-composite: exclude` trick, not a fake outline), a soft colored glow tied to each tool's own gradient via a CSS custom property, and a subtle abstract gradient-blob "preview illustration" — all derived from the tool's existing `gradientFrom`/`gradientTo`, no new image assets. Quick Action chips moved from a plain white pill to a softly gradient-tinted background with a scaling icon badge on hover.
- **Continue Editing rail**: wider (`w-72`) cards with a coarse status→percentage SVG progress ring (`DRAFT`→15%, `RENDERING`→80%, terminal statuses→100% — an honest stage indicator, not a fabricated frame-accurate percentage, since no real render progress is tracked anywhere), a distinct "Draft" badge specifically for genuinely-unstarted video drafts (`VideoProject.status === "DRAFT"` — `CreativeProject`'s own `DRAFT` status means "generating," a different semantic, so it's excluded from this treatment), and an explicit "Continue editing →" affordance inside the card.
- **Trending rebuilt as visual cards**: replaced the compact list rows with a card grid — a generated gradient tile + large icon stands in for a "thumbnail" (no per-vertical/objective photography exists, and none is fabricated), the real usage `count` from the unchanged `trending.ts` data layer is shown as "popularity," and only the top-ranked item per group gets a "Trending" badge — no invented week-over-week growth percentage, since no historical snapshot is tracked anywhere.
- **Inspiration categories extended**: `INSPIRATION_LIBRARY`'s category enum grew from `HOOK|WINNING_AD|LAYOUT|CREATIVE` to add `TRENDING_COLOR`/`TOP_TYPOGRAPHY` (additive — the config defaults to `[]` and is purely admin-curated, so nothing existing breaks), plus a shadow-lift hover to match the new depth language.
- **One honestly-grounded progress bar, not a fabricated one**: `getDashboardData()` gained one more query — the user's active `Subscription` joined to its `PricingPlan` (same pattern as `lib/billing/fulfillment.ts`) — so Usage Overview's "Credits remaining" card can show a real `balance / monthlyCredits` progress bar **only** for subscribed users; pay-per-download users (no monthly cap to chart against) keep a plain number. `StatCard` itself shrank (smaller icon, tighter padding, `text-heading-2` instead of `text-display-2`) per the "cleaner, smaller, modern, minimal" ask. Storage/API-usage/Images/Videos stay plain numbers — no real platform-wide caps exist for those today, so no bar was invented for them.
- **Depth pass**: dashboard page background moved from flat `bg-neutral-50` to a subtle `bg-gradient-to-b from-neutral-50 to-white`; card shadows and hover-lift treatments (`-translate-y-1`/`-translate-y-0.5` + richer shadow) made consistent across Quick Create, Continue Editing, Trending, Inspiration, and Popular Templates.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (240/240, unchanged — no new pure-logic modules needed dedicated tests this pass, consistent with the established "DB-bound/presentational code verified live" convention) all clean; `next build` clean; dev DB re-seeded; Playwright confirmed zero `scrollWidth` overflow at 375/640/768/1024/1440px, zero console errors, exactly the 4 specified Quick Create cards rendering live, and screenshots reviewed at all 5 widths. One real bug caught only by the screenshot (not by any automated check): the hero's first floating-chip layout had two compounding issues — `HeroStudioPreview`'s `max-w-md` (448px) exceeded its `420px` grid column, bleeding into the left column, and several chips' large `translate-x/y` offsets collided with each other and with the header badges; fixed by dropping the redundant `max-w-md` (the grid column already constrains width) and repositioning all 6 chips to modest, non-overlapping offsets around the panel's edges.

### Milestone 19 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 3: AI Command Center Hero, Unified Card System, Honest Progress Ring + Activity Chart (2026-06-30)
A third creative-direction pass: the hero becomes a real creation surface instead of a decorative preview, and every dashboard card is rebuilt onto one shared design-system primitive instead of seven components each repeating a slightly different `rounded-2xl border bg-white shadow-sm` recipe.

- **One shared card system, not seven copies**: new `dashboardCardClass()` (`components/dashboard/dashboard-card.tsx`) — one `rounded-2xl border border-neutral-200 bg-white shadow-sm` recipe, an 8px-aligned padding scale (`p-4`/`p-5`, replacing the mixed `p-3`/`p-3.5`/`p-4`/`p-5` that had accumulated), and the shared `transition-all hover:-translate-y-1 hover:shadow-lg` hover language. Every card-rendering component (`GradientToolCard`, `ContinueEditingRail`, `TrendingSection`, `InspirationSection`, `PopularTemplatesSection`, `usage-overview.tsx`'s `StatCard`, `ComingSoonCard`) now builds its className from this one function plus only its own unique extras — this is the concrete fix for "cards are inconsistent," including one real radius bug it caught: `PopularTemplatesSection` cards were `rounded-xl` while every other card was `rounded-2xl`. New `ProgressRing` (`components/dashboard/progress-ring.tsx`) similarly replaces two independent inline SVG ring implementations (Continue Editing's stage indicator, now joined by Usage Overview's credits ring) with one.
- **Tactile 3D micro-interaction, applied selectively**: new `TiltCard` (`components/dashboard/tilt-card.tsx`, framer-motion `useMotionValue`/`useSpring`) gives a subtle mouse-position rotateX/rotateY tilt + a cursor-following glow — wired onto the 4 Quick Create cards and the hero's studio-preview panel only, not site-wide, per the brief's own "avoid excessive motion" caution.
- **Hero rebuilt into a real AI Command Center**: new `HeroPromptBox` (left column) replaces the prior decorative greeting with a genuine creation surface — a large idea textarea, a styled-but-honest "coming soon" voice button (no speech-to-text exists anywhere in this codebase, so a working one would be new functionality, not a UI pass — confirmed via a full-codebase search before building this), and reference-image/brand-logo upload via new `CompactAssetUpload` (`components/dashboard/compact-asset-upload.tsx`) — a 3rd thin client-side caller of the *existing* presigned-upload sequence (`POST /api/assets/upload-url` → direct PUT → `POST /api/assets/[id]/confirm-upload`) that `AssetUploadTile` already wraps, behind a compact icon button instead of a drop-zone. Generate hands the idea/reference/logo off via a one-shot `sessionStorage` blob (`lib/dashboard/hero-handoff.ts`) and routes into the *existing* `CreativeStudio` flow (`/create/image` or `/create/marketing`, selected via 4 pipeline chips defaulting to Image) — `CreativeStudio` gained one additive prefill effect mirroring how `initialPresetKey` already works, reading+clearing that blob on mount; the Video pipeline gets the same idea text via a `?idea=` query param prefilling the wizard's existing `keyMessage` field (the same pattern its `objectiveParam`/`platformParam` already use). No new generation logic anywhere — every Generate path lands on an unchanged API contract. Suggested-prompt chips and the existing `recentItem` "Continue:" chip moved inside the new prompt box; `displayName`'s greeting moved into its subtitle.
- **`HeroStudioPreview` extended, not rewritten**: kept the prior pass's glass panel/timeline/floating chips/layer rail, added a looping "Analyzing brief…" AI-thinking indicator (pulsing dots) and a slim animated generation-progress bar — both purely decorative, framer-motion only, no new dependency.
- **Search bar relocated, not duplicated**: `DashboardSearchBar` (searches the user's *existing* content — a different job from the new prompt box, which *creates* new content) moved from the hero into the dashboard layout's header, restyled compact/light instead of dark/hero-tinted, so the hero doesn't carry two competing large inputs.
- **One real new chart, not a fabricated one**: new `lib/dashboard/recent-activity.ts` — `getRecentActivity()` buckets the same `GenerationLog` rows already counted for `apiUsageThisMonth` into the last 7 real calendar days (zero-filled, no gaps), rendered as a tiny sparkline in Usage Overview; `bucketDailyActivity()`'s pure bucketing logic gets 4 new unit tests (244 total, up from 240), matching the established "DB-bound functions verified live, pure logic unit-tested" convention.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (244/244) and `next build` all clean. Playwright re-confirmed zero `scrollWidth` overflow at 375/640/768/1024/1440px (re-checked specifically because a hero this much more complex — textarea, icon buttons, chip rows — is exactly the kind of change that could reintroduce the overflow bug fixed last pass) and zero console errors; screenshots reviewed at all 5 widths confirmed the new hero, unified cards, and sparkline all render correctly with no overlapping elements.

### Milestone 20 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 4: Premium Visual Polish — Uniform Card Grid, Layered Depth, Ambient Background (2026-06-30)
A pure visual-craft pass on top of the existing system (no new structure, no new components beyond what iteration 3 already built) — the user's review called out one explicit, objectively-fixable regression plus a general "still doesn't feel premium enough" direction.

- **Quick Create's bento layout removed — the explicit must-fix**: `QuickCreateGrid` ([quick-create-grid.tsx](src/components/dashboard/quick-create-grid.tsx)) dropped the `col-span-2` flagship treatment from iteration 1 entirely; the new explicit requirement is that every primary card have identical width *and* height. Now `grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` — deliberately skipping a 3-column breakpoint, since 4 cards only ever tile evenly at 2 or 4 columns; a 3-column step would always leave one orphaned cell in the last row, exactly the "broken row" being complained about. Verified live at all 5 breakpoints: a clean 2×2 at mobile/tablet, a clean 1×4 at desktop, no orphan cell anywhere.
- **`dashboardCardClass()` shadow upgraded** ([dashboard-card.tsx](src/components/dashboard/dashboard-card.tsx)): every card on the shared system moved from a flat `shadow-sm` to a layered shadow (tight contact shadow + soft diffuse shadow) plus an inset top hairline of white — the "frosted object catching light" cue — and a softer `border-neutral-200/70`. Added once at the shared primitive, so every already-migrated card (`GradientToolCard`, `ContinueEditingRail`, `TrendingSection`, `InspirationSection`, `PopularTemplatesSection`, `StatCard`, `ComingSoonCard`) got it for free with zero per-component edits.
- **`TiltCard` rotation capped at the explicit spec**: reduced from ±6° to ±2° ("1–2 degrees maximum") and applied more broadly — `TrendingSection` and `PopularTemplatesSection` cards now get the same mouse-tilt + cursor-glow treatment Quick Create and the hero panel already had, plus `TrendingSection` cards gained the same gradient-ring hover border (mask-composite "exclude" technique) `GradientToolCard` already used, reusing each card's own palette. Inspiration and Continue Editing deliberately keep their existing hover-lift-only treatment — not every card gets tilt, per the brief's own "avoid excessive motion" caution.
- **Ambient background, kept overflow-safe**: 3 very-low-opacity (4–6%) blurred gradient blobs added behind the dashboard's main content (same CSS technique as the hero's orbs, scaled down), positioned with percentage-based offsets (not fixed pixels, so they scale with page length) inside a `relative overflow-hidden` wrapper sized to the content column — re-verified zero `scrollWidth` overflow afterward specifically because an absolutely-positioned decorative element is the exact class of bug that broke this dashboard twice in earlier iterations. A near-invisible film-grain texture (new `NoiseOverlay`, [noise-overlay.tsx](src/components/shared/noise-overlay.tsx) — inline SVG `feTurbulence` data URI, no new asset or dependency, `position: fixed` so it can never affect scrollable content) applied once at the dashboard layout root.
- **Section dividers and icon-badge hairlines**: new `SectionDivider` ([section-divider.tsx](src/components/dashboard/section-divider.tsx)) — a 1px gradient-fade line between dashboard sections, replacing whitespace-only separation — plus a subtle `ring-1 ring-inset` hairline added to every gradient/tinted icon badge across the dashboard (`GradientToolCard`, `QuickActionChip`, Usage Overview's `StatCard`/sparkline) for a more "physical object" feel.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (244/244, unchanged — pure CSS/layout polish, no new logic to test) and `next build` all clean. Playwright re-confirmed zero `scrollWidth` overflow at 375/640/768/1024/1440px and zero console errors; screenshots at every width confirmed Quick Create's 4 cards are now pixel-identical in width and height with no orphaned row at any breakpoint, and the section-divider hairline renders correctly between sections.

### Milestone 21 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 5: AI Video Editor as Flagship Product, Dashboard-Only Dark Theme (2026-06-30)
Two changes, both explicitly scoped to the dashboard experience only — the rest of the application (marketing site, admin panel, auth, settings, billing, every `/create` flow) stays on the existing light theme; a full-application dark reskin was confirmed out of scope for this pass via a clarifying question, given how much carefully-tuned light-theme contrast work exists across 19 prior milestones.

- **Product hierarchy — AI Video Editor is now the unambiguous flagship**: `lib/seed-defaults.ts`'s `CREATIVE_TOOLS` (the real seed source of truth, re-seeded afterward) — `ai_video` relabeled `"AI Video"` → `"AI Video Editor"`; `talking_head` demoted from `MAIN_CARD` to `QUICK_ACTION` (one capability *inside* the Video Editor now, not a peer module — its real `/create/talking-head` route is completely unchanged) and relabeled `"Talking Head"` → `"AI Talking Head"`; `social_media` promoted back from `QUICK_ACTION` to `MAIN_CARD`. Quick Create's 4 main cards are now exactly **AI Video Editor, AI Image, Marketing Creative, Social Media**, matching the brief verbatim — verified live via Playwright after re-seeding.
- **Flagship visual weight, not size**: `GradientToolCard` ([gradient-tool-card.tsx](src/components/dashboard/gradient-tool-card.tsx)) gained an optional `flagship` prop — wired in `QuickCreateGrid` via `tool.pipeline === "VIDEO"` (data-driven, not hardcoded by card position) — giving the AI Video Editor card a small "Flagship" badge, a persistent (not hover-only) soft glow ring, and a richer 3-stop gradient, while staying the exact same width/height as its siblings, preserving iteration 4's "every primary card identical size" rule.
- **Hero re-emphasis**: `HeroPromptBox`'s default pipeline changed from Image to Video, and its pipeline chip relabeled to "AI Video Editor" — the prompt box now opens already pointed at the flagship pipeline. `HeroStudioPreview`'s floating-chip set (Captions, Voice, B-Roll, Scene Replace, Music, Auto Zoom) was deliberately left untouched — it already reads as a professional video-editing workspace, and chip repositioning has caused two real overlap regressions in earlier iterations.
- **Dashboard dark theme, extended from the hero's existing glass language, not reinvented**: 3 new static tokens in `globals.css` (`--color-surface-0: #09090b`, `--color-surface-1: #0f172a`, `--color-surface-2: #111827` — additive, registered in `lib/utils.ts`'s `CUSTOM_COLORS`, nothing existing changed so the rest of the still-light application is unaffected). `dashboardCardClass()` — the single shared primitive every dashboard card already runs through — switched from `bg-white border-neutral-200/70` to `bg-white/[0.04] backdrop-blur-xl border-white/10`, the exact glass recipe `HeroStudioPreview`/`HeroPromptBox` have used since iteration 2, propagating to every already-migrated card with one change. The dashboard layout shell (header, sidebar, mobile nav, notification bell, search bar — confirmed used only by the dashboard layout, not shared with admin/marketing/auth) and every section component had their light-theme text/surface classes swapped for dark equivalents (`text-neutral-900` → `text-white`, pastel icon-badge tints like `bg-accent-orange-light` → low-opacity tints of the saturated color itself, `border-neutral-200` → `border-white/10`). Components reused on still-light pages (`SignOutButton`, `Badge`, `Button`) were **not** forked or globally changed — `SignOutButton` gained an optional `className` prop so the dark header can override its colors while `/settings`' light-theme usage stays default, and dark-context `Badge`/`Button` instances get local `className` overrides instead.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (244/244) and `next build` all clean. Re-seeded the dev DB and confirmed via Playwright that Quick Create renders exactly `["AI Video Editor", "AI Image", "Marketing Creative", "Social Media"]` with `"AI Talking Head"` present among the quick-action chips. Re-ran the `scrollWidth` overflow check at 375/640/768/1024/1440px (re-checked again — background/surface changes are exactly the risk class that caused regressions twice before) — zero overflow at every width, zero console errors, screenshots confirmed legible contrast throughout the new dark surfaces and the flagship card's badge/glow rendering correctly without changing its size.

### Milestone 22 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 6: Quick Create Architecture Lock, Cinematic Ambient Background (2026-06-30)
A clarification pass on iteration 5's product hierarchy (the real flagship is the editing-workspace pipeline, not the plain video-generation one) plus a layered, almost-imperceptibly-animated background system replacing the static blobs added in earlier passes.

- **Quick Create's final structure — 3 cards, no genuine peers left unmerged**: `lib/seed-defaults.ts`'s `CREATIVE_TOOLS` (re-seeded afterward) — `ai_video` relabeled `"AI Video Editor"` → `"AI Video"` (plain generation pipeline, no longer flagship); `talking_head` **promoted** `QUICK_ACTION` → `MAIN_CARD` and relabeled `"AI Talking Head"` → `"AI Video Editor"` (the real flagship now — the editing-workspace pipeline that leads into the actual timeline/editor experience; its `/create/talking-head` route is unchanged); `marketing_creative` and `social_media` both demoted `MAIN_CARD` → `QUICK_ACTION` (output types of the same Universal Creative Engine that already powers AI Image — `CreativeStudio` already serves `AI_IMAGE`/`SOCIAL_MEDIA`/`MARKETING_CREATIVE` `kind`s through one shared wizard, so this is a presentation change, not a new engine); `ai_image`'s description rewritten to communicate that Universal Creative Engine framing directly. Quick Create now shows exactly `["AI Video Editor", "AI Video", "AI Image"]` — verified live via Playwright after re-seeding.
- **Grid re-tuned for 3 cards, same "no broken rows" discipline**: `QuickCreateGrid` ([quick-create-grid.tsx](src/components/dashboard/quick-create-grid.tsx)) moved from `grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` (tuned for 4 cards) to `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3` — 3 cards only tile evenly at 1 or 3 columns; a 2-column step would always leave an orphan cell, exactly the class of bug iteration 4 fixed once already. `GradientToolCard`'s `flagship` prop (badge, persistent glow, richer gradient, same size as siblings — built last iteration) needed no changes, just its wiring flipped from `tool.pipeline === "VIDEO"` to `tool.pipeline === "TALKING_HEAD"`. `HeroPromptBox`'s pipeline chips reordered/relabeled to match, with the default pipeline now `TALKING_HEAD`.
- **Cinematic ambient background, one shared layered system**: new `AmbientBackground` ([ambient-background.tsx](src/components/dashboard/ambient-background.tsx)) replaces the static blob markup that previously lived separately in both `HeroBanner` and the dashboard body — 4 large blurred mesh blobs (indigo/purple/cyan/blue) drifting an extremely small amount on long (28-38s), staggered framer-motion loops; a near-invisible (2.5% opacity) structural grid; and a sparse 6-node network layer with a slow opacity-only pulse (no position movement, per the brief's explicit "avoid obvious particles/gaming effects" caution). Reusing one component for both the hero and body gives the "hero casts ambient light onto nearby sections" continuity the brief asked for, since both regions now draw from the same palette instead of two independently-tuned blob sets.
- **One real bug caught only by the screenshot** (not by any automated check): the node layer's dots, drawn as SVG `<circle>` elements inside a `viewBox="0 0 100 100"` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, rendered as stretched comet/teardrop shapes instead of circles — the non-uniform scaling needed to stretch a square viewBox across the page's actual (very tall, much-wider-than-square at the time of measurement) aspect ratio distorted them. Fixed by moving dots out of the SVG into separate fixed-size (`size-1`) absolutely-positioned `<span>` elements (true circles regardless of container aspect ratio), keeping only the connecting lines — which skew acceptably — in the SVG. Also lowered the layer's opacity range (0.08 peak → 0.05 peak) after seeing it read more prominently than intended in a static screenshot, where the slow pulse animation isn't visible to soften it.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (244/244, unchanged) and `next build` all clean. Playwright re-confirmed zero `scrollWidth` overflow at 375/640/768/1024/1440px (re-checked again — ambient background changes are exactly the decorative-absolutely-positioned-element class that has caused regressions multiple times before) and zero console errors; screenshots at every width confirmed the 3-card grid has no broken rows, the flagship card reads as visually dominant without being a different size, and the ambient layer reads as a subtle premium texture after the dot-rendering fix rather than a distraction.

### Milestone 23 — Dashboard Redesign Iteration 7: Scroll-Reactive Ambient Environment, Parallax Depth (2026-06-30)
A single-component rewrite of `AmbientBackground` ([ambient-background.tsx](src/components/dashboard/ambient-background.tsx)) — the static/time-looped layer system from iteration 6 becomes scroll-reactive, using framer-motion's `useScroll`/`useTransform` (already a dependency, no new package, no other files touched).

- **`useScroll()` with no target tracks the whole document automatically** — `HeroBanner` and the dashboard body each render their own `<AmbientBackground />` instance (unchanged from iteration 6), but since both read the same global window scroll progress independently, the hero and body evolve in sync without lifting state up or adding a context provider.
- **Parallax mesh blobs**: each of the 4 existing blobs gained a `useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0,1], [0, depth])` driving its `y` — different depth per blob (70/45/25/15px) gives "near layers move faster, far layers move slower," the classic depth-illusion cue. Each blob keeps its pre-existing independent opacity-breathing loop (a different style property, no conflict with the scroll-driven `y`).
- **Scroll-evolving color wash — the literal "section transitions" ask**: one new full-bleed, near-invisible (~5% opacity) layer whose `backgroundColor` is `useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 0.33, 0.66, 1], [indigo, blue, cyan, purple])` — framer-motion interpolates between color strings natively, so the hero's indigo tone continuously evolves into blue, then cyan, then purple by the bottom of the page, never an abrupt cut. Verified live via scroll-position screenshots (top/middle/bottom) showing the visible color shift.
- **Drifting grid + holographic ring**: the previously fully-static structural grid now drifts via a 60s `backgroundPositionX/Y` loop (explicitly GPU-cheap, listed as an approved property in the brief itself); one new radial-gradient "holographic ring" near the hero scales up and fades as the user scrolls away (`useTransform` on `scale`/`opacity`), a cheap single-element stand-in for "volumetric lighting."
- **Card light interaction relies on the existing glass material, not new per-card code**: every dashboard card already uses `bg-white/[0.04] backdrop-blur-xl` (`dashboardCardClass`, iteration 5). Since the ambient layers paint behind the cards, the backdrop-blur already optically picks up the evolving wash color as it shifts — confirmed in the bottom-of-page screenshot, where cards visibly carry a violet cast matching the wash's color at that scroll position. This is the passive glassmorphism mechanism doing the "cards react to the environment" work, not a new scroll-binding added to the shared card primitive (lower risk, no extra files touched).
- **Performance discipline**: every animated property is `transform` (blob `y`, ring `scale`), `opacity`, `background-color`, or `background-position` — no animated `filter` (blur stays a static Tailwind class, never recomputed per frame) and nothing that triggers layout, per the brief's own GPU-only constraint.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (244/244, unchanged — pure animation logic, nothing new to unit-test) and `next build` all clean. Playwright re-confirmed zero `scrollWidth` overflow at 375/640/768/1024/1440px (re-checked again — this exact change class, decorative absolutely-positioned background elements, has caused regressions multiple times before) and zero console errors; scroll-position screenshots at top/middle/bottom of the page confirmed the color wash visibly evolves, blobs have parallax-shifted, and all dashboard content/cards stayed perfectly stable — only the background moved.

### Phase 2 — Universal Creative Engine: Zero-Config Kind/Preset Auto-Inference (2026-06-30)
A 3-agent parallel codebase audit (creative generation flow, provider abstraction, storage/schema/routing) preceded any code change, per the user's explicit "audit first, wait for architecture approval" process. The audit's headline finding, presented and approved before implementation: the Creative Brain (Universal JSON Prompt), Prompt Intelligence (per-provider adapters), and Provider Engine (admin-configured failover across 4 image providers, never raw-text-to-provider) already existed and were production-grade (Milestones 14–16) — the only real gap was that *kind* (AI Image/Social Media/Marketing Creative) and *preset/platform* were still user-selected instead of AI-inferred, and the prompt-preview step was mandatory rather than optional. This milestone closes exactly that gap, additively, with the entire pipeline below it untouched.

- **The Creative Brain now infers kind + preset, not just style/mood/layout**: `universalPromptSchema`'s `output` section gained two additive optional fields, `recommendedKind`/`recommendedPresetKey` (every section already used `.catchall(z.unknown())` specifically to allow this kind of schema evolution with zero migration). `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()`'s `kind` input became optional — when omitted, an additive system-prompt suffix (`AUTO_KIND_SUFFIX`, appended only in that branch, so the explicit-kind call sites get byte-identical LLM behavior to before) asks the model to also decide which of the 3 kinds and which preset best fits the idea, in the same single LLM round trip — not a second call.
- **A hallucinated/invalid AI recommendation can never reach generation**: new `lib/prompt-os/resolve-kind.ts` — a pure, dependency-free function, `resolveKindAndPreset()` — validates the model's `recommendedKind` against the real `CreativeProjectKind` enum and `recommendedPresetKey` against the real per-kind preset catalogs (`PRESETS_BY_KIND`) before trusting either. Falls back, in order: a valid AI recommendation → keyword-matching the user's own raw idea text → keyword-matching the model's `creative_type`/`platform` fields → a safe per-kind default (`square`/`instagram_post`/`poster`). Checking the user's **own idea text**, not just the LLM's output fields, was added after live verification surfaced a real robustness gap: this dev environment runs a Mock LLM provider (no real OpenAI credential configured) whose generic `creative_type` carried no real signal — without the idea-text fallback, every auto-mode request would have silently defaulted to AI_IMAGE regardless of what the user actually typed. 22 new unit tests cover every keyword bucket, the hallucination-rejection paths, and all 4 example ideas from the brief.
- **`enhance-prompt` accepts kind as optional, every existing caller unaffected**: `kind` in `enhanceCreativePromptSchema` became optional; the route resolves `resolvedKind`/`resolvedPresetKey` via the new resolver only when kind was omitted — when a caller (the 3 existing `/create` routes, every quick-action chip) passes kind explicitly, behavior is provably unchanged: same preset lookup, same `TOOL_KEY_BY_KIND` provider-adapter resolution, same response shape plus the two new informational fields. `/api/creative-projects` (the actual generation-triggering endpoint) and `generateCreativeImage()` were **not touched at all** — by the time generation is triggered, a concrete kind+presetKey has always already been resolved upstream.
- **The dashboard hero becomes the Universal Creative Engine's real entry point**: `HeroPromptBox` gained a 5th pipeline option, `"AUTO — AI decides"`, now the default (replacing the prior flagship-pipeline default) — selecting it and clicking Generate calls `enhance-prompt` with no kind/presetKey, stores the resolved `enhancedPrompt`/`universalPrompt`/`presetKey` in the existing `HERO_HANDOFF_KEY` sessionStorage handoff (extended with 3 new optional fields), and routes to whichever of `/create/image`/`/create/social`/`/create/marketing` the brain resolved. `CreativeStudio`'s handoff effect, when it sees a pre-resolved `enhancedPrompt`, skips the empty "input" step and the manual "preview" click entirely and calls generation immediately — the literal "type one sentence, get a result" experience, with the existing "Edit Prompt" button on the result screen still available for anyone who wants to inspect or change what the brain produced (prompt engineering optional, never forced, exactly as specified). `handleGenerate()` gained an optional `overrides` parameter so it can be invoked with not-yet-committed state from the handoff effect — every pre-existing `onClick={handleGenerate}` call site keeps working unchanged, since a `MouseEvent` has none of the override properties and every value falls through to current state.
- **Live + visual verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (266/266, up from 244 — 22 new resolver tests) and `next build` all clean. Live API verification: all 4 example ideas from the brief ("Create a Mutual Fund advertisement", "Generate a luxury villa campaign", "Restaurant offer", "Jewellery promotion") correctly resolved to `MARKETING_CREATIVE`/`poster`; an explicit `kind=AI_IMAGE&presetKey=youtube_thumbnail` request confirmed zero drift (stays locked, exactly as before); a full auto-resolved generation completed end-to-end through the unchanged provider/credit/storage pipeline (`status: COMPLETED`, real `resultAssetId`). Playwright confirmed the full UI vertical slice live: typing "Jewellery promotion" in the hero with Auto selected, clicking Generate once, and landing on `/create/marketing` with the result already generated — zero console errors, zero extra clicks.

### Phase 2.2 — Reference Intelligence: Extended Creative DNA Extraction (2026-06-30)
Audited before any code change, per the user's explicit "inspect first, reuse everything" instruction: the Design Intelligence Library built in Milestone 16 (`lib/design-intelligence/`) already *was* this phase's "Reference Intelligence" step — every uploaded reference image already goes through a vision-LLM analysis producing a structured, reusable "Creative DNA" object (`AssetAnalysisResult`), lazily computed once and cached (`AssetAnalysis`), fed into `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` as a distinct input alongside the idea — never as raw image bytes, and the existing vision system prompt already explicitly forbade self-referential "similar to the reference" language in favor of describing the visual language itself. Comparing the brief's "Extract" field list against the existing schema field-by-field found exactly 3 gaps.

The vision system prompt (`lib/design-intelligence/analyze-asset.ts`) was extended to actually ask the model for them, and now explicitly frames the reference image as "a style reference, a product photo, or any visual the user wants the generation to learn from" and adds "never an instruction to copy or recreate the image" alongside the existing anti-copying language.

Adding a second, behaviorally-identical upload button would be UI duplication for zero functional difference, so `CreativeStudio`'s existing "Reference image" helper copy was broadened ("An ad, design, product photo, or any visual to match the style of") instead of adding new UI.
- **Zero changes to the generation pipeline itself**: `lib/prompt-os/builder.ts`'s integration point, `enhance-prompt`'s route logic, `generateCreativeImage()`, every provider, and storage were not touched — exactly as instructed.
- **Live verification — the brief's exact 5-case matrix**: no reference uploaded; logo only; reference only; reference + logo; reference + Brand Kit — all 5 completed successfully through the unchanged `/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt` → `/api/creative-projects` pipeline. A real reference image and logo were uploaded through the existing 3-step presigned-upload flow to get genuine asset IDs (not fabricated ones); a full Reference + Logo generation completed end-to-end (`status: COMPLETED`, real `resultAssetId`, correct 1-credit charge); the `AssetAnalysis` row was confirmed created and cached for the uploaded reference, proving the lazy-analysis code path actually executed. The 3 new schema fields were directly verified at the schema layer (`assetAnalysisSchema.parse()` round-trips `contrast`/`visualBalance`/`marketingFeel` correctly) — this dev environment's Mock LLM provider (no real OpenAI/vision credential configured) returns a fixed canned response regardless of input, so a *real* vision model actually populating these 3 fields from a real photo couldn't be observed here; the schema and prompt changes are correct and will populate the moment a real vision-capable provider is configured. `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (269/269, up from 266) and `next build` all clean.

### Phase 2.3 — Universal Prompt Intelligence (2026-06-30)
Direct inspection (no agent audit needed — the relevant files were already known from Phase 2/2.2) confirmed the brief's central architectural requirement — "the app must never build a provider-specific prompt directly, every request first becomes one Universal JSON object" — was already exactly how the pipeline worked since Milestone 16: `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` is the only place that calls the LLM and produces a `universalPromptSchema`-validated object, and `enhance-prompt`'s route always converts JSON → text through a resolved provider adapter, never the reverse. Comparing the brief's suggested JSON field names against the existing schema field-by-field found that nearly every concept already existed under already-shipped names (`creative_type`, `negative_constraints`, `marketing.goal`, etc.) — renaming any of them to match the brief's exact casing would have touched every adapter, the builder, the resolver, and already-persisted `CreativeProject.universalPrompt` rows, directly violating "everything already working must continue working." Every existing field name was kept exactly as-is; only the genuinely missing pieces were added.

- **Two new additive Universal JSON fields**: `objects` (array of strings — the literal physical elements expected in the scene, inferred by the Creative Brain from the idea text) and `referenceAnalysis` (echoes the exact Design Intelligence Library "Creative DNA" object used for this generation, when a reference was supplied). `referenceAnalysis` closes the one real gap found: the reference analysis already *influenced* other fields during the LLM call, but was never retained in the output JSON itself, so nothing downstream (a debugger, a future AI module) could see what reference data actually shaped the result. The brief's `creativeDNA` and `referenceAnalysis` are the same underlying concept — implementing two fields for one object would have been exactly the duplication the brief explicitly forbids, so only one field exists. `builder.ts`'s final merge step now sets `objects` from the model's own inference, falling back to the reference's analyzed objects only when the model named none, and echoes `referenceAnalysis` straight through. No new LLM call, no schema renames — purely extending the existing merge.
- **Gemini provider adapter, prompt-formatting only**: `lib/prompt-os/adapters/gemini.adapter.ts` (new), built the same way every existing adapter is — reusing the shared `describeX` extraction helpers from `generic.adapter.ts`, zero duplicated logic — and registered in `ADAPTERS` alongside OpenAI/Flux/Ideogram. This is explicitly *not* a real Gemini API integration (no provider class, no credentials, no admin wiring) — out of scope per the brief's own "do not replace any provider integration." The adapter map is already `Record<string, AdapterFn>`, so registering a new id required touching no other type or call site, exactly the "adding a provider's adapter never requires touching application logic" property the existing code already promised.
- **A `video` placeholder section was deliberately not added**: every section already uses `.catchall(z.unknown())`, so video-specific sub-fields can be added later to existing sections with zero migration — the schema is already structurally video-ready without empty scaffolding.
- **New "Prompt Intelligence (advanced)" panel — collapsed by default, never forced**: `components/creative/prompt-preview-panel.tsx` (new), built on the existing `Accordion` primitive (`components/ui/accordion.tsx`, not previously used in the creative flow), showing 4 read-only sections from data `CreativeStudio` already has in state — no new fetches: Marketing Strategy (industry/goal/audience/psychology hooks), Creative Summary (type/platform/mood/aesthetic/layout/colors), the raw Universal JSON, and the exact Provider Prompt text. Wired into `CreativeStudio`'s existing "preview" and "result" steps, directly below the existing content — an addition, not a redesign, matching the brief's explicit "do not redesign the UI" stop condition. `universalPrompt` state was retyped from `unknown` to the real `UniversalPrompt` type for this.
- **Live verification — the brief's exact test matrix**: simple prompt (auto mode), reference image, an explicit-kind request standing in for the logo/brand-kit case (logo and Brand Kit don't change `enhance-prompt`'s inputs, confirmed in Phase 2.2), Marketing Creative, Social Media, poster preset, and banner preset — all 8 cases succeeded through the unchanged `/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt` pipeline. The reference-image case is the clearest proof the new merge logic actually executes: `referenceAnalysis` was present and non-empty only for that case, and `objects` was populated from the reference's cached analysis (the Mock LLM's canned response carries no `objects` of its own, so the fallback path visibly engaged) — every other case correctly showed `objects: []`/`referenceAnalysis` absent. Same caveat as every prior phase: this dev environment's Mock LLM provider returns canned text regardless of input, so this verifies the **code path** end-to-end (schema validation, merge logic, route forwarding), not a real model's semantic quality. `/create/talking-head` (the separate AI Video pipeline, untouched by any prompt-os files) was confirmed to still load with no regression. `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (275/275, up from 269 — 6 new tests across `schema.test.ts`, `adapters.test.ts`, `builder.test.ts`) and `next build --turbopack` all clean (one transient turbopack prerender glitch on the first build attempt, unrelated to this change, resolved cleanly on retry).
- **Stopped here per the brief's explicit STOP CONDITION** — no AI Critic, no video-generation logic, no UI redesign beyond the contained Prompt Intelligence panel.

### Phase 2.4 — AI Creative Director (2026-06-30)
The brief asked for human-like strategic thinking — marketing objective, target audience, emotional direction, brand personality, visual/messaging/layout strategy — to happen *before* any prompt JSON is built, as its own pipeline stage: User Idea → Creative Brain → Reference Intelligence → **Creative Director** → Universal Prompt Intelligence → Provider Adapter → Generation. An audit (`lib/brand-kit/identity-engine.ts`, `lib/prompts/optimizer.ts`, `lib/talking-head/context-analysis.ts`, `lib/talking-head/visual-planner.ts`, `lib/ai/script-studio.ts`, the `CreativeProject` Prisma model) confirmed no existing code does this — `identity-engine.ts` generates brand *assets* (logo/palette/guideline text), not a structured strategy brief, and `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` was the only "thinking" step, inferring style/layout/marketing fields directly with no separate strategic pass first. This is genuinely new logic, built the same way every other intelligence step in this pipeline already is: a standalone, provider-agnostic `generateScript()` call producing a schema-validated structured object — the exact pattern `analyzeAssetForLibrary()` (Reference Intelligence) already established.

- **New `lib/prompt-os/creative-director.ts`**: `creativeBriefSchema` (Zod) matching the brief's literal `CreativeBrief` shape — `businessSummary`, `marketingObjective`, `creativeObjective`, `targetAudience`, `brandPersonality`, `colorPsychology`, `layoutDirection`, `typographyStrategy`, `callToAction`, `attentionHook`, `platformOptimization`, `creativeConfidence` as flat fields, plus `visualStrategy`/`messagingStrategy`/`compositionStrategy` as nested catchall-extensible sections (via `schema.ts`'s `section()` helper, now exported for reuse) so all 21 of the brief's named responsibilities (Primary/Secondary Message, Emotional Direction, Luxury/Minimalism/Realism Level, Story Direction, Trust Signals, Composition Priority, Headline Direction, etc.) have a real field, not just the 15 example keys. `buildCreativeBrief()` is one `generateScript()` call — provider-independent by construction (it imports nothing from `lib/providers/image` or `lib/prompt-os/adapters`, only the same provider-agnostic LLM entry point every other intelligence step uses) — cast as a senior agency Creative Director who infers everything from the idea alone, never asks the user questions.
- **No duplicated logic**: `parseJsonLoose` (JSON-fence-stripping parse) and the idea/kind/reference/brand-kit context-line builder were extracted out of `builder.ts` (exported as `parseJsonLoose` and `buildContextLines`) and reused by `creative-director.ts` instead of being redefined — the brief's "do not duplicate logic" requirement applied literally to the one piece of real overlap between the two modules.
- **Wired as one new upstream input, not a rewrite**: `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` (`builder.ts`) gained an optional `creativeBrief` input — when present, a short system-prompt addition tells the model to treat it as binding strategy and translate it into the structured visual/technical fields rather than re-deciding strategy itself; the final merge echoes `creativeBrief` straight through (same pattern as Phase 2.3's `referenceAnalysis`). `enhance-prompt/route.ts` calls the new `buildCreativeBrief()` once, right after resolving `referenceAnalysis`/`brandKit` and before `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` — the single integration point. `/api/creative-projects` (the generation-triggering endpoint) needed zero changes: it persists `universalPrompt` as an opaque `Json` column (confirmed via `lib/creative/engine.ts`), so `creativeBrief` round-trips through automatically with no Prisma migration.
- **One new LLM call per generation** — the deliberate, justified cost of true separation between "think strategically" and "build the structured fields," matching the brief's own pipeline diagram drawing Creative Director as a distinct stage.
- **Prompt Preview panel expanded, not redesigned**: `prompt-preview-panel.tsx` gained a "Creative Brief" section (marketing/creative objective, target audience, brand personality, visual direction, primary message, CTA, attention hook, creative confidence), rendered first per the brief's listed order, inside the same collapsed-by-default `Accordion` — no new UI surface.
- **Live verification — the brief's exact 8-idea matrix**: Mutual Fund Advertisement, Luxury Villa Campaign, Restaurant Offer, Jewellery Launch, Dental Clinic Promotion, Hospital Awareness, Fashion Sale, Real Estate Lead Generation — all 8 succeeded through `/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt`, each returning a `universalPrompt.creativeBrief` that validated and round-tripped correctly. As with every prior phase, this dev environment's Mock LLM provider returns the same canned JSON regardless of input — confirmed directly (the canned response carries none of `creativeBriefSchema`'s field names, so every case correctly defaulted to empty nested sections) — so live testing here proves the **code path** (the new LLM call fires, the brief validates, echoes through, persists), not real strategic variation per idea. That variation was instead proven correctly with a unit test: `creative-director.test.ts` mocks `generateScript` to return *different* canned briefs for "Mutual Fund Advertisement" vs. "Jewellery Launch" and asserts `buildCreativeBrief()` faithfully returns each one unmodified — proving the wiring carries through whatever a real model decides. A full end-to-end generation (`/api/creative-projects`) was confirmed to reach `status: COMPLETED` with `creativeBrief` present in the persisted `universalPrompt` Json column (after granting the test user credits via the real `grantCredits()` engine function, not a raw row insert, since `CreditAccount.balance` is a denormalized cache `grantCredits()` is the only correct writer for). `/create/talking-head` (AI Video, untouched by any prompt-os files) was confirmed to still load with no regression.

### Post-Phase-2.4 hotfixes — real-provider pipeline bugs (2026-06-30)
Two user-reported bugs, both root-caused by switching from this dev environment's Mock providers to real ones for the first time — every prior phase's "verified live" claims were honest about testing the *code path* through Mock, never a real model/API, since neither was configured until now.

- **Broken image icon instead of a generated image**: traced end-to-end (provider response → buffer → storage → DB → API → `<img>`) per the user's exact audit checklist. Root cause: the Mock Image Provider's `placehold.co` URLs (no file-extension suffix) serve **SVG** by default — confirmed by curling the URL directly (`Content-Type: image/svg+xml`). `lib/creative/engine.ts` only forced a real JPEG re-encode via sharp when a preset had fixed target pixel dimensions or a logo was composited; presets without either (`square`/`portrait`/`landscape`, `poster`/`flyer`, `facebook_post`, etc. — used by nearly every test this session) uploaded the raw SVG bytes unconverted under a hardcoded `.jpg` key, served with a lying `Content-Type: image/jpeg` that no browser can decode. Fix: new `normalizeToJpeg()` (`lib/image/resize.ts`) — sharp re-encode, no resize — called whenever neither of the existing JPEG-guaranteeing paths already ran, so the upload is **always** genuinely JPEG bytes regardless of what format the provider actually returned. Verified with real OpenAI Images enabled too (gpt-image-1's b64_json PNG output correctly normalizes to real JPEG) — confirmed via raw-byte inspection (`ffd8ff` magic bytes) on Mock, a fixed-dimension preset, a no-dimension preset, the logo-composite path, and real OpenAI.
- **Generic "fashion portrait" output regardless of business type** (e.g. "Dental clinic Instagram post" → unrelated generic content): traced per the user's exact checklist (Creative Brain → Creative Brief → Universal JSON → Provider Prompt → raw OpenAI request), printing real values at every stage. Root cause: the active LLM provider was **Mock** (`lib/providers/llm/mock.provider.ts`'s `simulateUniversalPromptJson()`), which is a fixed, deterministic JSON object — it interpolates the idea only into `intent` (a literal echo, never used downstream) and never reasons about it at all; every other field (style, mood, colors, marketing goal/audience) is hardcoded identically for any input. Confirmed live: the final provider prompt for "Dental clinic Instagram post" contained zero dental/medical/healthcare terms. This is not a code bug in the reasoning pipeline (Creative Brain/Creative Director/Universal Prompt Intelligence) — Mock is incapable of reasoning by design. Enabled the already-configured, already-tested real `openai` LLM provider (`gpt-4o-mini`) and discovered its priority (`1`) sorted *after* Mock's (`-1`) in the ascending-priority failover chain — meaning Mock (which never throws) would always win even with a real provider enabled simultaneously; reprioritized `openai` to `-2` so it's actually tried first, Mock remaining as a genuine last-resort fallback.
- **A real schema-validation bug surfaced once a real model was actually answering**: gpt-4o-mini's response correctly reasoned about industry/audience/objects (e.g. dental: `["bright smile","dental professionals",...]`; mutual fund: `["upward trending graph","client testimonials",...]`) but sometimes shaped `quality` as a bare array instead of the documented `{ keywords: [...] }` object, and sometimes collapsed a single-item array-of-strings field (`marketing.psychologyHooks`, etc.) into a bare string — both previously threw the *entire* Universal JSON out via `ZodError`, discarding an otherwise excellent, on-topic response. Fixed at the schema level (`lib/prompt-os/schema.ts`): new `stringArray()` helper coerces a bare string into a single-element array, applied to every LLM-produced array-of-strings field (`negative_constraints`, `objects`, `colors.palette`, `branding.brandColors`, `marketing.psychologyHooks`, `quality.keywords`, and `creativeBriefSchema`'s `trustSignals`); `quality` additionally normalizes a bare array into `{ keywords: [...] }` before validating. Also clarified the system prompt's `quality` field instruction in `builder.ts` to reduce recurrence (the original "keywords array: ..." phrasing was genuinely ambiguous). This is defensive, schema-level robustness — not "random prompt changes" — since real LLM output is inherently non-deterministic in pluralization at this level of detail; the schema should tolerate it rather than reject correct, hard-won reasoning over a shape technicality.
- **Live verification — all 4 of the user's named examples, with real OpenAI for both LLM and Images**: Dental clinic Instagram post, Mutual Fund advertisement, Restaurant offer, Luxury villa campaign — each now produces genuinely distinct, business-specific `industry`/`style`/`marketing`/`objects`/`creativeBrief` fields and a provider prompt explicitly reflecting its category (e.g. luxury villa → "The villa at sunset"; restaurant → "Signature dish image"; dental → "Smiling family in the dental clinic"). All temporary diagnostic `console.log` instrumentation was added, used to capture exact raw values, then removed before final verification — none shipped.
- **Verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (292/292, up from 283 — 6 new tests covering the `stringArray`/`quality` coercion behavior in `schema.test.ts` and `creative-director.test.ts`, plus the 3 `normalizeToJpeg` tests from the image fix) and `next build --turbopack` clean.
- **Provider state left as found, except**: `STORAGE`→`s3` (R2) remains disabled (Mock local-disk storage active) — not touched, out of scope for either bug. `IMAGE`→`openai_images` was enabled only for diagnostic verification and restored to its prior disabled state afterward (Mock Image Provider is active again — the JPEG fix applies equally to Mock). `LLM`→`openai` (`gpt-4o-mini`) was left **enabled** at priority `-2` per explicit user instruction, since Mock cannot perform the reasoning this product's core architecture depends on — this now makes real, billed OpenAI calls for every prompt enhancement; disable it in Admin → AI Providers to return to free Mock-only text generation.

### Config-only fixes — IMAGE provider left disabled, then a too-tight timeout (2026-06-30)
User report: "Something went wrong generating your creative." Root-caused two separate config issues, no code changes:
- `IMAGE`→`openai_images` had been left `enabled: false` after the prior hotfix's diagnostic — since a real `ProviderConfig` row exists at all (vs. none), the engine no longer falls back to Mock, so generation failed outright with `AllProvidersFailedError: no providers configured`. Per explicit user instruction, enabled it permanently.
- Once actually reached, `openai_images` started timing out: `GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS_IMAGE` defaults to 30,000ms, but gpt-image-1's real measured latency (23-28s in earlier live tests) left almost no margin. Raised to 90,000ms via the real `setConfig()` admin-config function (proper validation + cache invalidation, not a raw DB write).
- Verified live: a real end-to-end generation completed (`status: COMPLETED`, valid JPEG). No source files touched — both fixes were admin configuration corrections.

### Prompt Expander Engine (2026-06-30)
With real OpenAI working, the pipeline was confirmed producing genuinely business-specific structured data (e.g. `industry: "Healthcare"`, relevant `objects`/`targetAudience` for "Dental clinic Instagram post") — but the final text reaching the image provider stayed short and mechanical, because the Provider Adapters (`lib/prompt-os/adapters/*.ts`) are terse field-concatenators (`describeSubject`/`describeComposition`/etc. in `generic.adapter.ts` just join short field values with commas). The brief's hard constraints — do not modify Provider Adapters, do not change the generation pipeline, do not touch OpenAI integration — ruled out the obvious fix (rewriting the adapters to be more verbose). The only design satisfying every constraint at once: a pure, deterministic function that takes a `UniversalPrompt` and returns a new one of the **identical shape**, with the exact fields the adapters already read replaced by much richer agency-quality phrasing — so the unmodified adapters mechanically produce a dramatically richer final prompt purely because their inputs got richer.

- **New `src/lib/prompt-os/prompt-expander/`** (8 files, every function pure — no I/O, no `generateScript` calls, exhaustively unit-testable like `resolve-kind.ts`): `types.ts` (`PromptRichnessTier`, `IndustryProfile`); `industry.ts` (8 curated visual-language profiles — Dental, Restaurant, Real Estate, Finance, Salon, Jewellery, Hospital, generic-product fallback — each with genuinely distinct atmosphere/palette/materials/trust-element phrase banks, matched via word-boundary keyword search against intent/industry/creative_type, intent-text checked **first** since a real LLM's own `industry` classification can be too broad, e.g. "Healthcare" for a dental-specific idea — confirmed live this session); `quality.ts` (`determineRichnessTier` — simple/marketing/luxury/cinematic, a pure function of luxury signal + industry, not a character-count target; `buildQualityKeywords` merges curated premium-quality phrases scaled by tier); `composition.ts` (visual-impact phrasing — scroll-stopping composition, reserved safe space for logo/CTA/headline); `lighting.ts` (photography-style + industry atmosphere, blends `referenceAnalysis` when present — Reference Intelligence's existing analysis text, never the raw image); `marketing.ts` (reads the Creative Director's already-echoed `creativeBrief` rather than re-inferring marketingObjective/targetAudience/brandPersonality, which would duplicate Phase 2.4's exact responsibility); `negative.ts` (merges existing `negative_constraints` with a curated avoid-bank, case-insensitive de-dupe); `expand.ts` (`expandUniversalPrompt()`, the orchestrator). Every enrichment **weaves in** the Creative Brain's own already-inferred value rather than discarding it (e.g. `framing: "low-angle hero shot"` becomes `"low-angle hero shot, a scroll-stopping composition with a strong, immediate focal point"`) — so two different ideas still read distinctly even after enrichment, never shared boilerplate alone.
- **Integration — one line, one file outside the new folder**: `enhance-prompt/route.ts` calls `expandUniversalPrompt(universalPrompt)` immediately after `buildUniversalPromptFromIdea()` returns, then passes the expanded object into the existing `resolvePromptAdapter(...)(expandedPrompt)` call and returns it as the response's `universalPrompt`. `builder.ts`, `creative-director.ts`, every adapter file, `lib/generation/*`, `lib/creative/engine.ts`, `/api/creative-projects`, and `openai-images.provider.ts` were **not touched at all**.
- **2 real bugs found by the new unit tests themselves** (not edge cases invented after the fact — the tests caught them on first run): (1) naive substring keyword matching false-positived "golden retriever puppy" into the jewellery profile via "gold" inside "golden" — fixed with word-boundary regex matching; (2) profile-array-outer/candidate-inner iteration let a lower-priority candidate's keyword (e.g. "villa" in raw idea text) win over a higher-priority candidate's real signal — fixed by iterating candidates(intent → industry → creative_type) outer, profiles inner.
- **Live verification — all 8 of the brief's named ideas**: Dental implant informative creative, Luxury villa advertisement, Mutual fund campaign, Restaurant offer, Salon promotion, Jewellery launch, Hospital awareness, Product launch — every one succeeded through `/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt`, landing at 2100-2440 characters (within/above the brief's own "cinematic advertising" tier guidance), each containing genuinely distinct, non-overlapping industry-specific language (e.g. dental → "premium dental equipment with polished chrome surfaces... a luxury medical interior"; restaurant → "visible steam rising off the dish, glistening textures"; jewellery → "macro-level material detail — faceted gemstone reflections"). This live run happened to execute while the configured OpenAI account was mid-quota-exhaustion (see below) — the LLM layer had silently failed over to Mock, yet the Expander still produced fully distinct, richly differentiated output per industry, since it reads the user's raw idea text directly rather than depending entirely on upstream LLM reasoning — a real resilience property, not a planned test condition.
- **External blocker surfaced, not caused, by this verification**: mid-testing, the OpenAI account hit its API quota (`429 insufficient_quota`, LLM) and then its billing hard limit (Images) — confirmed via `ProviderHealth` rows and raw provider error messages, not guessed. This blocks all real generation, independent of this phase's code. Per explicit user instruction, left as-is (no config changes) for the user to resolve via platform.openai.com billing — the Prompt Expander Engine's own correctness was already fully demonstrated by the unit suite (pure functions, no provider dependency) and the live trace above.
- **Verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (329/329, up from 292 — 37 new tests across 7 new test files covering every submodule plus the `expand.ts` integration) and `next build --turbopack` clean.
- **Stopped here per the brief's STOP CONDITION** — no AI Critic, no UI changes, no video-generation work, no Provider Adapter edits, no OpenAI integration edits.

### Pipeline Audit — real production data trace (2026-06-30)
Pure investigation, no code changes (per explicit instruction), tracing the user's own real account/project (`cmr0wey91002o9gu74z7a9ytq`, "Dental implant informative creative" with a real uploaded reference image) end-to-end through every stage.
