Confirmed Creative Brain, Creative Director, Universal JSON, and Prompt Expander all working correctly with real GPT-4o-mini reasoning. Found the quality loss was entirely downstream, in the Provider Adapter layer: comma-joining fields that now routinely contain full Expander-enriched sentences produced literal broken grammar, confirmed verbatim: `"...evoking a sense of well-being and self-care. mood, high luxury feel..."`. Also discovered, byte-for-byte confirmed against `mock.provider.ts`'s hardcoded fixture, that the user's actual reference image had never been analyzed by a real vision model — a circuit-breaker cooldown silently degraded that one analysis call to Mock, and the fake result was cached permanently. Produced a ranked Top 10 bottleneck report (full detail in conversation history) that directly drove the next two phases.

### Provider Prompt Optimization (2026-07-01)
Fixes exactly the layer the audit identified — the Provider Adapter layer (`lib/prompt-os/adapters/*.ts`) — and nothing else. Creative Brain, Creative Director, Universal JSON, and (with one user-approved exception) the Prompt Expander were not touched.

- **Root cause fixed**: every `describeX()` helper in `generic.adapter.ts` assumed each `UniversalPrompt` field was a short tag and either comma-joined or suffix-appended it (`${mood} mood`) — broken once fields routinely contain full, already-punctuated Prompt Expander sentences. New shared utilities — `tagOrSentence()` (only appends a suffix to genuinely short values), `composeFluently()` (splits fragments into a comma-joined short-tag clause vs. independently-stated complete sentences, with section labels like "Shot with" only ever attached to the short-tag clause, never glued onto a sentence), `toTag()` (Flux's tag-only convention degrades a full sentence into a clean tag instead of leaving a stray mid-list period) — applied across `generic`/`openai`/`flux`/`ideogram`/`gemini` adapters.
- **`objects` array now reaches generation**: previously only `gemini.adapter.ts` read `prompt.objects` (confirmed in the audit as the literal scene elements the Creative Brain infers — completely inert for every other provider). New shared `describeObjects()` added to `generic`/`openai`/`flux`/`ideogram` too.
- **Duplicate marketing ideas removed**: the Creative Director's `attentionHook` and the Creative Brain's own `psychologyHooks` sometimes describe the same idea in two near-identical sentences (confirmed live: `"...communicates transformation and luxury"` vs. `"...immediately communicates transformation and luxury."` — not an exact-string match). New `dedupeSimilarPhrases()` (word-overlap/Jaccard similarity, since exact-match dedup doesn't catch mid-sentence wording differences) keeps the richer phrasing, drops the redundant one. A second, related bug was caught **live during verification, not in the unit suite**: `describeMarketing()` was pre-joining `psychologyHooks` into one string with plain `", "` before the result ever reached `composeFluently()`, so only the *last* hook's punctuation was ever classified correctly — a middle-of-the-array sentence-ending hook still produced `"...captures interest., clear call-to-action: ..."`. Fixed by spreading each hook as its own array element instead of pre-joining, with a new regression test reproducing the exact middle-of-array shape.
- **Reference image Creative DNA visibility**: required no new code — confirmed the Prompt Expander already blends `referenceAnalysis.lighting`/`visualLanguage`/`colorPalette` into `lighting.direction`/`colors.palette`, and the fixed adapters now render that already-present data fluently instead of it contributing to the grammar breakage.
- **One user-approved exception to "do not modify Prompt Expander"**: `prompt-expander/composition.ts`'s `profile.subjectHints` previously only appeared via `prompt.composition.framing || profile.subjectHints` — meaning it almost never appeared once real LLM reasoning reliably fills `framing` (the common case). Changed to unconditional inclusion (one fallback line, nothing else in the Expander touched).
- **Before/after, the same real project, computed from real stored data** (no new LLM calls): OLD `buildOpenAIPrompt()` output was 3,798 characters and contained the confirmed broken-grammar pattern, zero mention of `objects`, and one duplicated marketing idea. NEW output is 3,753 characters (slightly *shorter*, thanks to dedup, despite adding the objects sentence) — `objects` now opens the prompt (`"The scene features primary subject, negative-space backdrop."`), every Expander-enriched sentence reads as its own clean statement, and the duplicate marketing phrase is gone.
- **Live verification — Dental, Restaurant, Real Estate, Finance, Hospital**, all through the real (now billing-resolved) OpenAI pipeline: every final prompt opens with a real objects sentence, contains zero instances of the confirmed bug patterns, and reads as fluent prose. One of the five (Hospital) initially flagged the just-described middle-of-array dedup bug, which was found and fixed live during this same verification pass before re-confirming clean across all 5.
- **New finding, flagged not fixed (out of this phase's scope)**: `branding.brandColors` intermittently fails Zod validation when the LLM returns it as an object instead of array/string — same bug class as the existing `stringArray()` fixes, different field, not part of the adapter layer this phase covers. See the top-of-file "Known open issue" note.
- **Verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (338/338, up from 329 — 9 new tests across `adapters.test.ts` and `composition.test.ts`, including 2 regression tests reproducing the exact confirmed production bug shapes) and `next build --turbopack` clean.
- **Stopped here per the STOP CONDITION** — no architecture redesign, no Creative Brain/Director/Universal JSON edits, no Prompt Expander edits beyond the one approved exception.

### Creative Director 2.0 — Advertising Campaign Intelligence (2026-07-01)
Expanded the Creative Director's own LLM-call (`creative-director.ts`/`buildCreativeBrief()`) from a 15-field strategic brief to a complete 24-field, 10-step advertising-campaign intelligence layer comparable to a real agency Creative Director's campaign planning document. Nothing downstream was redesigned; all changes are additive to the schema, the system prompt, and the Prompt Expander's wiring of those new fields into the existing pipeline. Duplication audit done before adding anything — 6 of the 10 steps' core concepts already existed in prior phases (businessSummary, marketingObjective, visualStrategy.emotionalDirection, etc.), so those were NOT re-added.

**New fields/sections in `creativeBriefSchema`**: `valueProposition` (why someone would care, Step 1 — distinct from the existing `marketingObjective`), `creativeApproach` (educate/persuade/inspire/reassure/trust/urgency), `visualStory` (the complete narrative SCENE — directly implements the user's "Doctor smiling" → "An experienced implant specialist confidently explaining a realistic dental implant model to a reassured patient..." worked example, Step 4), `visualHierarchy` (the ordered eye-flow sequence, broader than existing `compositionStrategy.compositionPriority`), `scrollStoppingStrategy` (the instant what/why/who/next comprehension plan, distinct from existing `attentionHook`), plus 3 new rich sections: `informationArchitecture` (hero/headline/supporting copy/benefits/trust/testimonial/CTA/contact/brand/logo-safe-area, Step 2), `advertisementComposition` (hero image/supporting visuals/info cards/premium UI panels/floating cards/glass sections/CTA blocks/editorial grid, Step 5), `designSystem` (grid/typography scale/font pairing/color harmony/visual rhythm/contrast/depth/shadows, Step 8), `premiumElements` (curated subset of advertising elements that actually help, Step 7). The `SYSTEM_PROMPT` was rewritten to walk the LLM through the 10-step planning process explicitly before outputting JSON, with the Apple/Nike/Google/Adobe/Airbnb/Rolex/Tesla quality bar and the "never generic posters, never stock-photo layouts, never empty compositions" quality directive.

**Prompt Expander wiring**: `prompt-expander/composition.ts` — `composition.framing` now weaves `brief.visualStory` as the narrative anchor; `layout.hierarchy` prepends the ordered `brief.visualHierarchy` sequence; `layout.composition` folds in a concise `informationArchitecture` summary (hero/benefit/trust/CTA areas). `prompt-expander/marketing.ts` — `goal` now folds in `brief.messagingStrategy.primaryMessage` (already existed since Phase 2.4 but was never read — a confirmed dead-weight gap like the earlier `objects` finding) and `brief.valueProposition`; `psychologyHooks` additionally includes `brief.messagingStrategy.secondaryMessage` and `brief.scrollStoppingStrategy`. **No Provider Adapter files were touched** — the existing adapters already read every `UniversalPrompt` field this enrichment writes into.

**4 additional fixes found and resolved live during verification** (all the same confirmed "LLM returns unexpected shape" class, same established fix pattern):
1. `creativeBriefSchema.compositionStrategy` (single-field section) returned as a bare string → `sectionOrString()` helper added to schema.ts, applied there.
2. `creativeBriefSchema.informationArchitecture.featureIcons`/`trustIndicators` (plural-sounding) returned as arrays → `stringOrJoinedString()` helper added, applied proactively to all plural-sounding fields in `informationArchitecture` and `advertisementComposition`.
3. `universalPromptSchema.branding.brandColors` returned as a plain object (`{primary: "...", secondary: "..."}`) — the already-flagged, already-documented known issue (PROJECT_STATUS.md prior entry) — `stringArray()` extended to handle the non-array-object case via `Object.values()`.
4. `universalPromptSchema.layout.hierarchy` returned as an array — `stringOrJoinedString()` applied there.
5. `cleanEnhancedPrompt`'s MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH raised from 4,000 → 6,000 — Creative Director 2.0's much richer reasoning was confirmed live to hit the old cap, losing the negative_constraints clause (appended last) entirely; raised with sufficient headroom for future richness.
6. `prompt-expander/composition.ts`'s own `.join(", ")` calls combined model-produced fields (now often full sentences, since richer Creative Director reasoning cascades into the Creative Brain's answers too) with curated short phrases — producing the same "X., Y" grammar breakage Provider Prompt Optimization was specifically built to prevent. Fixed by importing `composeFluently` from `adapters/generic.adapter.ts` (a pure, vendor-agnostic text utility, not a provider-specific function) and applying it to 3 confirmed-broken join sites.

**Before/after, same idea ("Dental implant informative creative"), real live GPT-4o-mini**:
- BEFORE (3,373 chars): 15-field brief, generic phrasing. Provider prompt = `"...Patient's smile with dental implants, Layered elements for engagement..."` — a description of an isolated subject/scene.
- AFTER (4,356 chars, no truncation): 24-field brief including `visualStory: "A confident dental specialist stands beside a patient in a bright, welcoming clinic, pointing to a sleek infographic displaying the dental implant process in a simplified, engaging manner, evoking trust and clarity."` and `visualHierarchy: ["Headline","Hero Subject","Supporting Information","Benefits","Social Proof","CTA","Logo"]`. Provider prompt explicitly shows the full eye-flow sequence and information-architecture content, ending cleanly with negative constraints intact.

**Verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (352/352, up from 338 — 14 new tests across `creative-director.test.ts`, `schema.test.ts`, `composition.test.ts`, `marketing.test.ts`) and `next build --turbopack` clean. Dental, Restaurant, Real Estate, Finance all confirmed clean through the real (healthy) OpenAI pipeline — zero grammar issues, `visualStory` narratives matching the "complete scene, not isolated subject" quality bar.

**Minor cosmetic finding, flagged not fixed (out of scope)**: when the LLM's `style.mood` and `brief.visualStrategy.emotionalDirection` independently choose similar phrasing (non-deterministic LLM coincidence), the `buildMarketingEnrichment`'s `[mood, emotionalDirection].join(", ")` produces a mild repetition (e.g., "Reassuring and confident, Reassuring and confident mood"). This is aesthetic not structural, out of this phase's adapter-layer scope, and would require fuzzy-dedup logic in `marketing.ts`'s mood construction — worth noting for a future polish pass.

### Image Quality Stabilization — Decision Quality + Schema Hardening (2026-07-01)
Quality-improvement and architecture cleanup phase: no new features, no redesign, no architecture changes. Every change is either a confirmed bug fix or a quality improvement to an existing pipeline stage.

**Phase A — Unblocking + API fixes** (3 files):
1. `createCreativeProjectSchema.prompt` cap raised from `max(4500)` → `max(6000)` to match `cleanEnhancedPrompt()`'s output cap (raised in Creative Director 2.0 but never synced here — confirmed live as the cause of 6 `ERR_VALIDATION: too_big` failures per session).
2. OpenAI `quality` parameter added to every request: `quality: this.config.defaultQuality ?? "high"`. `defaultQuality` was already being resolved from the admin panel into `ProviderRuntimeConfig` by `credentials.ts` and available as `this.config.defaultQuality` inside the provider — but the provider never read it. One line to connect the two. Default: `"high"` (commercial advertising use case).
3. `DEFAULT_MODEL` updated `gpt-image-1` → `gpt-image-1.5` (stronger instruction following per OpenAI docs — directly improves adherence to complex advertising briefs).
4. `AbortSignal` now passed through: `image.ts` was silently dropping the signal the engine provides via `invoke(provider, signal)`; `types.ts` signature and provider's `fetch()` call updated to pass it through.

**Phase B — `buildOpenAIPrompt()` section reorder** (1 file):
`openai.adapter.ts` reordered so `composition.framing` (the complete visual story from Creative Director 2.0's `visualStory` — the richest creative content) opens the prompt instead of appearing 3rd behind generic style tags. `gpt-image-1.5` weights earlier content most heavily. New order: Scene → Featuring → Style → Shot → Lighting → Color → Typography → Campaign → Quality → Avoid. Labels updated to professional creative-brief language.

**Phase C — Creative Director Decision Quality** (1 file):
5 new fields in `creativeBriefSchema` (all optional, backward-compatible):
- `visualFormat`: the type of creative — "Educational Infographic" / "Before/After" / "Luxury Campaign" / "Editorial Advertisement" / "Comparison Creative" / etc. AI decides; user never selects.
- `heroSubject`: the single strongest visual marketing element, deliberately chosen (NOT "doctor smiling" unless genuinely optimal; e.g., "Before-and-after smile transformation split", "SIP compound growth chart").
- `layoutArchetype`: named structural template — "Editorial" / "Split Screen" / "Infographic" / "Hero + Benefits" / "Timeline" / "Premium Grid" / "Luxury Editorial" / "Product Spotlight" / "Comparison".
- `visualDensity`: "minimal" / "medium" / "rich" — drives Expander phrase-bank tier selection.
- `copywriting` section: actual render-ready marketing text — `headline` (≤6 words, actual words not descriptions), `subheadline`, `cta` (button text only), `benefitTitles`, `featureLabels`, `trustStatements`, `badgeText`. This is the #1 audit finding (+35% estimated quality impact): the system plans headline copy but never tells the image model what the headline words ARE — now it does.
SYSTEM_PROMPT extended with STEP 0 (Format & Hero Decision) and STEP 10 (Copywriting) to instruct the LLM to produce these fields.

**Phase D — Prompt Expander wiring** (3 files):
- `composition.ts`: `heroSubject` → `focalPoint` (replaces generic fallback); `layoutArchetype`/`visualFormat` → opens `layout.composition` with the named archetype; `copywriting.headline`/`cta` → embedded in `headlinePosition`/`ctaPosition` strings so `describeTypography()` surfaces the actual words to the image model.
- `marketing.ts`: `copywriting.benefitTitles`/`trustStatements`/`badgeText` → `psychologyHooks` (real marketing copy in the campaign section).
- `quality.ts`: `visualDensity` override applied after tier computation — "minimal" caps at marketing (never cinematic/luxury phrase banks); "rich" upgrades marketing → luxury.

**Phase E — Industry profiles** (1 file): Education (school/college/university/admission/campus) and Automobile (car/vehicle/showroom/sedan/suv/automotive) added to `industry.ts`, each with industry-specific atmosphere, palette language, premium details, subject hints, and trust elements.

**Phase F — Reference Intelligence fix** (1 file): `enhance-prompt/route.ts` now checks for meaningful content (`style || industry || mood`) before using or saving an `AssetAnalysis` cache entry — prevents permanently caching mock/fallback empty analysis results. Uses `upsert` instead of `create` so real results overwrite stale empty rows.

**Schema hardening** — confirmed live with gpt-4o-mini, all the same "LLM returns unexpected shape" class:
- `stringOrJoinedString()`: now handles `null` → `undefined`, arrays → joined string (already handled), and plain objects → `Object.values().join(", ")` (new — typographyStrategy returned as an object).
- `stringArray()`: now handles `null` → `undefined`.
- `section()`: null-stripping preprocess added — omits null-valued keys from the input object before field-level validation, so individual `z.string().optional()` fields don't fail when the LLM returns `null` instead of omitting the field.
- All string fields inside `creativeBriefSchema` sections changed from `z.string().optional()` to `stringOrJoinedString().optional()` — consistent defensive handling of null/array/object for every section field.

**Verification**: `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest` (366/366, up from 352 — 14 new tests) and production build clean. All 8 live verification ideas (Dental, Restaurant, Villa, SIP, Hospital, Salon, Jewellery, School) pass without validation errors. Decision Quality fields confirmed populated in 5+ of 8 ideas per run (LLM variability — all fields optional, pipeline gracefully falls back to existing enrichment when absent).

### Milestone 24 — Cloud Video Editor (Non-AI), Part 1: Foundation & Project System (2026-07-07)
A deliberate architectural pivot, via direct user confirmation: a second, standalone product surface — a professional, CapCut/Premiere-style multi-track video editor that works completely without AI — built as a **new module in this same codebase**, decoupled from every AI/Scene concept, sitting alongside (not replacing) the Milestone 9 AI-coupled editor at `/videos/[id]/editor`, which is untouched. AI features are explicitly out of scope until a later milestone. This part ships the foundation only: data model, project/folder/asset system, and a working 6-region editor shell with a real (if basic) multi-track timeline and preview — split/ripple-delete/duplicate/replace-clip/lock/track-resize/magnetic-snap/multi-select/group/markers, crop/rotate/scale/opacity/position/flip, full undo-redo/version-history, and export are explicitly deferred to Modules 2-6.

- **New, wholly separate data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `EditorFolder` (self-referencing, for nesting), `EditorProject` (`aspectRatio`/`widthPx`/`heightPx`, cached `durationMs`), `EditorAsset` (own `PENDING_UPLOAD`/`READY`/`FAILED` lifecycle — never the AI-coupled `Asset` table), `EditorTrack` (`VIDEO`/`AUDIO`/`SUBTITLE`/`TEXT`/`OVERLAY`/`EFFECTS`), `EditorClip` (`startMs`/`durationMs`/`trimStartMs`, optional `assetId`, `content` Json for TEXT/OVERLAY payloads) — `Editor`-prefixed and table-mapped `editor_*` specifically so nothing collides with the Milestone 9 `Track`/`Clip`/`Asset`/`VideoProject` models one line above it in the same schema file. New project's default state seeds one VIDEO + one AUDIO track (`lib/video-editor/projects.ts#createProject`) so the timeline is never empty on first open.
- **Storage reused as-is, not duplicated**: the existing `StorageProvider` abstraction (`lib/providers/storage/`) has zero AI coupling, so the new module's asset upload mirrors the exact presigned-URL flow the AI editor already uses (`POST /api/editor/assets/upload-url` → browser PUTs directly to storage → `POST /api/editor/assets/[id]/confirm-upload`), just backed by `EditorAsset` instead of `Asset`.
- **New admin-configurable policy knobs** (`CONFIG_REGISTRY`, category `video_editor_policy`): `EDITOR_MAX_TRACKS_PER_PROJECT`, `EDITOR_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES`, `EDITOR_ALLOWED_UPLOAD_MIME_TYPES` (per-kind allow-list), `EDITOR_AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS` (defined now, wired starting Module 5), `EDITOR_SNAP_THRESHOLD_PX` (defined now, wired starting Module 2) — plus a new `editor_asset_upload` entry in the existing `RATE_LIMITS` registry.
- **Service layer** (`lib/video-editor/`): `folders.ts`/`projects.ts`/`assets.ts`/`tracks.ts`/`clips.ts` — same ownership-check-once-in-the-route-then-scope-by-id trust boundary `lib/timeline/engine.ts` already established, one shared `InvalidStateError` mapped to 404/409 per call site. `timeline-engine.ts` is pure clip-span math only (`clipEndMs`/`moveClipSpan`/`trimClipSpan`/`duplicateClipSpan`), unit-tested (10 new tests, no DB) mirroring `lib/timeline/engine.test.ts`'s split.
- **13 new API routes** under `/api/editor/*` (folders, projects, projects/duplicate, tracks, clips, assets upload-url/confirm-upload/list/delete) — identical house style to every existing route: `requireSession()` → zod → ownership check → `apiSuccess`/`apiError`. `"/editor"` added to `PROTECTED_PATHS` (`lib/auth/config.ts`) for edge-level route protection.
- **Frontend — a genuinely new full-screen shell, not fit into the dashboard chrome**: `src/app/editor/` is an ungrouped top-level route (mirrors `admin/`, not a `(dashboard)` route group) with its own chrome-free `layout.tsx` — a professional multi-track editor needs the Top Toolbar/Left Sidebar/Timeline/Bottom Status Bar as its actual chrome, not the marketing header + sidebar + mobile bottom-nav every other authenticated page gets. `/editor` (Project Browser: folder tree, project grid, New Project dialog with aspect-ratio presets) and `/editor/[projectId]` (the 6-region workspace: Top Toolbar with inline-editable name + save-status, Left Sidebar with a functional Media Library tab, Preview Window, Timeline, Right Properties Panel, Bottom Status Bar). New shadcn primitives added: `dropdown-menu`, `popover`, `slider`, `scroll-area`, `switch`.
- **First use of Zustand and TanStack Query in this codebase** (both newly added dependencies, per the user's requested stack for this module) — deliberately split: **TanStack Query owns server state** (project/tracks/clips/assets + mutations, `[projectId]/queries.ts`, dedup'd by queryKey so every panel calls the same hooks without prop-drilling or a shared Context), **Zustand owns ephemeral client state only** (selection/playhead/zoom/play-pause, `[projectId]/store.tsx`) via a fresh per-mount store (`EditorStoreProvider`) so navigating between projects never leaks stale selection/playhead. This avoids both the existing AI editor's prop-drilled single-Context pattern and its `forceRender`-during-drag re-render workaround.
- **Timeline**: multi-track rendering across all 6 kinds, hand-rolled pointer-event drag-to-move/drag-edge-to-resize (the same proven technique `timeline.tsx` uses — dnd-kit fits reorderable lists, not freeform pixel positioning; HTML5 native drag-and-drop from the Media Library onto a track lane), zoom (Bottom Status Bar slider, shared via the Zustand store), track add/remove/mute/hide, clip select/delete (Delete key or toolbar button), all persisted immediately per mutation. Split/ripple-delete/duplicate/replace-clip/lock/resize/magnetic-snap/multi-select/group/markers are explicitly Module 2.
- **Preview Window**: DOM-layered compositing (base `<video>`/`<img>` + absolutely-positioned OVERLAY/TEXT layers), the same technique `scene-preview.tsx` uses, driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` playhead clock. Play/pause/seek only this module — frame-step/speed/fullscreen/resolution-switch are Module 3.
- **Right Properties Panel** is a stub showing the selected clip's timing (start/duration/end/trim-in) this module; crop/rotate/scale/opacity/position/flip land in Module 4 once there's an editing surface for them to write into.
- **Pre-existing repo issues found and fixed along the way** (all unrelated to this module, none in AI-OS business logic — confirmed via `git`-free diff review, only mechanical/type-level fixes): a bad `FileUpload` → `FileUp` lucide-react icon import in the Milestone 9 editor's `text-editor-panel.tsx` (icon didn't exist in the installed `lucide-react@1.21.0`, blocking the production build outright); a `patch: Partial<ClipView["content"]>` null-narrowing type error in `motion-editor-panel.tsx` (corrected to `Partial<NonNullable<...>>`, matching how it's actually called); 4 `no-explicit-any` violations in `lib/motion/engine.ts` (retyped `interpolateMotionValue`/`getMotionStyle` against the real `MotionKeyframe["value"]` union, plus the `Record<MotionParameter,...>` reduce-accumulator corrected to `Partial<Record<...>>`); unescaped `"` in JSX text in `admin/creative-brain-inspector/brain-inspector.tsx`; and 8 `no-explicit-any`/incomplete-blueprint test-fixture casts across `render-plan.test.ts`/`review-engine.test.ts`/`orchestrator.test.ts`/`_audit_10_6e.test.ts` (all replaced with a real `UniversalCampaignBlueprint`/matching-type cast instead of `any`). Zero behavior changes — purely type-level/import corrections. A `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` script was also added to `package.json`, filling a real gap — the repo previously had no standalone way to run the "typecheck" step the standing engineering rules call for (only implicit type-checking via `next build`).
- **Verified live** end-to-end via Playwright against a real Postgres-backed dev server (dev-mode OTP bypass login → onboarding → `/editor`): created a folder, created a project (aspect-ratio preset), opened the workspace, uploaded a video asset through the real presigned-URL flow (Mock storage), dragged it onto the VIDEO track (`POST .../clips` → 201, persisted), selected the resulting clip (Right Properties Panel correctly populated with its real start/duration/end/trim), dragged it to a new position (Top Toolbar's save-status correctly showed "Saving…" mid-mutation), reloaded the page and confirmed the moved clip persisted exactly, and confirmed an unauthenticated request to `/editor` correctly redirects to `/login`. Zero browser console errors throughout. `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npm run lint` (0 errors, pre-existing warnings elsewhere untouched), `npm test` (2,767/2,767 passing, 10 new), and `npm run build` (clean production build, all 13 new `/api/editor/*` routes plus `/editor` and `/editor/[projectId]` compiled) all pass.
- **Roadmap for the rest of this product line** (corrected 2026-07-09 — Module 6 is the Motion Engine, not Export; Export was misattributed to Module 6 in earlier entries below and is now correctly placed much later, after Motion, Text/Subtitle, and Audio all exist, since Export has to render every one of their outputs together): **Module 2** — split, ripple delete, duplicate, replace clip, lock/hide track, track resize, magnetic snap, multi-select, group/ungroup, markers. **Module 3** — frame-step, speed control, fullscreen, resolution switch, a more robust audio-aware playhead clock. ~~**Module 4** — crop/rotate/scale/opacity/position/flip wired into the Preview Window and persisted to `Clip.content`.~~ **Done** (2026-07-08, see below) — persisted to a new, separate `EditorClip.transform` field instead of `content`, for the reasons documented in that entry. ~~**Module 5** — full undo/redo across every timeline mutation, autosave, version history + restore.~~ **Done** (2026-07-08, see below) — restore is additionally undo-able, which the old AI editor's version system is not. ~~**Module 6** — Motion Engine: real keyframe interpolation, easing, motion paths, animation presets.~~ **Done** (2026-07-09, see below). ~~**Module 7** — Text/Subtitle Engine (captions, per-word/per-character reveal animations — see this entry's "flagged for Module 7" note on why that needs more than this module's per-clip keyframe engine).~~ **Done** (2026-07-09, see below). ~~**Module 8** — Audio Engine (waveforms, fades, ducking).~~ **Done** (2026-07-09, see below). ~~**Module 9** — Transition Engine (cross-fade/wipe/slide between adjacent clips — also flagged below as needing a genuinely different data model, not per-clip keyframes).~~ **Done** (2026-07-09, see below) — confirmed as its own entity (`EditorTransition`), exactly as flagged. **Module 10+** — Export, once Motion/Text/Audio/Transitions all have real output to render together.

### Milestone 25 — Cloud Video Editor, Module 2: Timeline Core Operations (2026-07-08)
Per an explicit product decision confirming `/editor/[projectId]` as the long-term canonical editor (a Scene-sourced-clip compositing path is deferred, not designed yet), this milestone builds out the Timeline's core editing operations. `lib/timeline/engine.ts` (the Milestone 9 editor's engine) was deliberately NOT touched or shared from — new pure functions were written fresh against `EditorClipSpan`'s shape, per explicit instruction, since the two schemas don't actually overlap enough yet to justify a shared abstraction.

- **Schema**: `EditorClip.groupId` (nullable, `@@index([projectId, groupId])`) for Group/Ungroup — clips sharing a groupId move together; a new minimal `EditorMarker` model (`projectId`, `timeMs` only) exists specifically so magnetic snap has a real third target type (clip edges/playhead/markers) to snap to.
- **`lib/video-editor/timeline-engine.ts`** gained 6 pure functions (own implementation, not imported from the AI editor's engine): `splitClipSpan`, `computeRippleDelete` (ripple is same-track only, by design — deleting a clip never shifts an unrelated track), `findNearestSnapTarget`/`collectSnapCandidates`/`snapMoveStart`/`snapTrimEdge` (unit-agnostic — callers convert the admin-configured `EDITOR_SNAP_THRESHOLD_PX` pixel threshold to ms using the live zoom level). 27 new unit tests (37 total in this file).
- **8 new API routes + service functions** (`lib/video-editor/clips.ts`, new `markers.ts`): split, ripple-delete, duplicate, replace-source, group, ungroup, add/remove marker — same house style (`requireSession` → zod → ownership check → `apiSuccess`/`apiError`) as every existing route.
- **Command-pattern plumbing** (`[projectId]/commands.ts`): every mutating operation (move, trim, split, ripple-delete, duplicate, replace-source, group, ungroup) is performed by constructing an `EditorCommand` (`execute`/`undo`) and calling `.execute()` — `.undo()` is implemented (best-effort for delete-type operations, which involve server-generated ids) but nothing calls it yet; Module 5 pushes these onto a real history stack without touching this module's call sites.
- **Performance**: the Timeline's playhead line and clip drag/resize previews were rewritten off React state entirely — `store.tsx` gained `subscribeWithSelector` middleware and a `useEditorStoreApi()` escape hatch for imperative `.subscribe()`/`.getState()` access; `PlayheadLine` and `ClipBlock`'s drag handlers now write `style.transform`/`style.width` directly (rAF-batched) instead of the Module 1 `forceRender` pattern, so dragging or scrubbing playback no longer re-renders the Timeline's React tree. No thumbnail/waveform rendering exists yet (would need frame-extraction/waveform-analysis, out of scope here) — noted in code for whoever adds it that it belongs on a `<canvas>` layer, not DOM.
- **Multi-select**: store's `selectedClipId` became `selectedClipIds: Set<string>` with shift-click toggle and marquee (rubber-band) rectangle-intersection select, both DOM+transform based (no canvas — reserved for real thumbnail/waveform data per above). Grouped clips move together on drag (linked via a DOM element registry, not a second network round-trip — the client already has every clip's `groupId` loaded).
- **New shadcn primitive**: `context-menu` (right-click: split/duplicate/ripple-delete/replace-source submenu/group/ungroup/delete).
- **Scope cuts made explicit, not silent**: dragging a raw multi-selection (not grouped) as one block isn't implemented — group first, or move one at a time; lock-track/track-resize/deeper undo-correctness are left for later per the roadmap above, unchanged by this milestone.
- **Verified live** via Playwright against a real dev server: dropped 2 clips → split one (3 clips, exact start/duration/end confirmed in the Properties panel) → duplicated via the new right-click context menu → shift-click multi-selected 2 clips → grouped them (200, toolbar updated to show Ungroup) → dropped a marker with "M" (visible on the ruler) → zoomed with "+" (visually confirmed) → marquee-selected all 4 clips by dragging across their combined bounding box. Zero console errors across every run. `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors), `npm test` (2,794/2,794, up from 2,767 — 27 new).

### Milestone 25, Part A — Lock/Resize Tracks, and Module 3 — Preview & Playback Engine (2026-07-08)
Two small additions to Module 2's scope (lock/resize, "quick add" per the brief) plus Module 3: a real playback engine for the Preview Window. `EditorProject.fps` (default 30, no picker UI yet) and `EditorTrack.isLocked`/`heightPx` were added to the schema and migrated.

- **Lock track** (`lib/video-editor/tracks.ts`'s `updateTrack` widened, no new route): a locked track's clips render non-draggable (`cursor-not-allowed`, no move/resize pointer listeners, no right-click menu — only plain click-to-select, so Properties are still viewable), `handleDrop` refuses new clips onto a locked track, and the Timeline's Delete/Split/Duplicate/Group/Ungroup toolbar + keyboard shortcuts all disable when the current selection includes a locked clip. Client-side enforcement only (matching every other Timeline UI constraint in this module) — not re-checked server-side, consistent with how `isHidden`/`isMuted` already work.
- **Track resize**: a 4px drag handle on each `TrackHeader`'s bottom edge, rAF-batched live preview via direct `style.height` writes (same transform-not-state pattern as clip drag). Tracks below the resized one intentionally do NOT live-reflow during the drag — they snap to their correct offset on commit/re-render, a deliberate scope trade-off documented in code rather than building a multi-element live-reflow system for a "quick add." All track-row/lane math in `timeline-panel.tsx` moved from one fixed `TRACK_ROW_HEIGHT` constant to a computed `trackLayout` (cumulative per-track offsets), threaded through marquee-selection math too.
- **Lock and resize both go through the existing commands pattern**: one new `createUpdateTrackCommand` (`commands.ts`) covers both, since they're both just a before/after `UpdateTrackPatch` on the same `EditorTrack` row — no dedicated command per action.
- **Preview Window rewritten into a real multi-track compositor**: every visible (non-hidden) track's active clip at the playhead now renders as its own layer, z-ordered so a track listed higher in the Timeline (lower `order`) paints on top — this fixes a real Module 1 gap where hidden tracks still rendered in preview, and where only the *first* VIDEO-track clip was ever shown regardless of other video tracks. VIDEO/IMAGE clips fill the frame; OVERLAY/TEXT position per their content; SUBTITLE/EFFECTS tracks have no renderer yet (skipped cleanly, not a crash — captions/effects aren't built).
- **Real audio**: the base video layer is no longer permanently `muted` — it and dedicated AUDIO-track clips (new `AudioLayer`, an invisible `<audio>` element on the same sync logic as `VideoLayer`) now respect each track's `isMuted`, which required extending the existing mute-toggle UI (previously AUDIO-only) to VIDEO tracks too.
- **One playhead clock, confirmed**: play/pause/frame-step/scrub/speed all operate on the same `playheadMs` in the Zustand store that Module 2's Timeline already reads via `useEditorStoreApi()`'s transient subscription — no second clock was added. Playback speed (0.5/1/1.5/2x) scales the rAF loop's `deltaMs` *and* sets the real `<video>`/`<audio>` elements' `playbackRate`, so media plays natively at speed instead of fighting the drift-correction every frame. Speed is Zustand-only, explicitly not a Command (per the brief: preview-only, not an editing operation).
- **Frame-step** uses `project.fps` (1 frame = 1000/fps ms) via new transport buttons and Left/Right arrow keys; stepping pauses playback first, like every NLE.
- **Fullscreen** wraps the whole stage+transport control area (not just the video box) via the Fullscreen API, state synced against the browser's own `fullscreenchange` event so Esc-to-exit stays correct.
- **Resolution/quality switch** (Auto/1080p/720p/480p) caps the compositing stage's rendered pixel height — a real paint/compositing cost reduction, honestly documented as NOT separate lower-bitrate proxy files (there's only ever one stored file per asset; true resolution-proxy swapping needs backend transcoding, out of scope here).
- **A real bug found and fixed during verification, not by inspection**: the first live test run showed track-lock's drop-block and drag-block appearing to silently fail. Root cause was a **stale Prisma Client in the already-running dev server process** — `prisma generate` after the migration updated the file on disk, but the Node process importing it had the old module cached, so `isLocked`/`heightPx` writes 500'd with `PrismaClientValidationError: Unknown argument isLocked`. Restarting the dev server picked up the regenerated client and every check passed cleanly. Documenting this because it's a real gotcha other milestones may hit: **a schema migration during an active dev session always needs a server restart, `prisma generate` alone isn't enough for an already-running process.** A second, genuine test-script bug (not an app bug) was also found and fixed along the way: a `button[title="Lock track"]` locator silently re-resolved to a *different* track after the first one's title flipped to "Unlock track."
- **Verified live** via Playwright against a real dev server (post-restart): locked the VIDEO track → confirmed a drop onto it was refused (clip count unchanged) → confirmed dragging the locked clip didn't move it (x-position identical before/after) → unlocked → dragged the resize handle (52px → 92px) → reloaded the page and confirmed the new height persisted server-side → played (timecode advanced) → changed speed to 2x mid-playback → paused (timecode confirmed stable across 500ms, i.e. genuinely stopped) → frame-stepped forward then back (returned to the exact same timecode) → switched preview quality to 720p → toggled fullscreen (`document.fullscreenElement` confirmed, controls remained visible and speed state persisted at 2x) with screenshots at every step. Zero console errors. `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors), `npm test` (2,794/2,794 — no new pure functions this round, so no new test count).

### Module 4 — Cloud Video Editor: Transform Properties (2026-07-08)
Crop, rotate, scale, position, opacity, and flip, wired into the Right Properties Panel and the Preview Window's compositor from Module 3, designed up front for Module 6 (Motion Engine) keyframing with zero migration or panel rewrite needed later.

- **Data model — "static or keyframed" shape, confirmed then built as specified.** New `EditorClip.transform Json?` column (`prisma/schema.prisma`), deliberately a *separate* field from the existing `content` (TEXT/OVERLAY's own 0..1-fraction placement system) rather than extending it — different unit convention (percentage-offset-from-center) and different scope (every clip kind, not just TEXT/OVERLAY). `lib/video-editor/transform.ts` is the new pure, framework-agnostic core: `Keyframeable<T> = { value: T; keyframes: EditorKeyframe<T>[] | null }` for every property exactly as specified, plus one addition beyond the brief — a `scaleY: Keyframeable<number> | null` alongside the given `scale`, where `null` means uniform/linked scale (falls back to `scale`'s value) so non-uniform scaling didn't require changing the user-specified shape. `resolveTransformValue()` currently just returns `.value` (keyframes always null until Module 6) but is the one function a real interpolation branch replaces later — nothing else in the compositor or panel needs to change. `resolveClipTransform()`/`composeTransformCss()` turn a `ClipTransform` into real CSS (`translate(x%,y%) rotate(deg) scale(sx,sy)` + `clip-path: inset(...)` + `opacity`) — 12 new unit tests, zero DB, covering uniform/non-uniform scale, opacity clamping, crop-inset ordering, and `allShareValue()`'s multi-select-mixed-state helper.
- **Persistence plumbing widened, not duplicated**: `clipTransformSchema` (new, mirrors `ClipTransform` independently, matching this file's established "mirror don't derive" convention for `content`), `AddClipInput`/`UpdateClipInput` (`lib/video-editor/clips.ts`), `AddClipPatch`/`UpdateClipPatch` (`queries.ts`), `ClipView` (`types.ts`) all gained an optional `transform`. `splitClip`/`duplicateEditorClip`/`duplicateProject`'s clip-cloning now all copy `transform` alongside the existing `content` copy, so split/duplicate never silently drops a clip's edits.
- **One new command, reusing the existing pattern**: `createUpdateTransformCommand` (`commands.ts`) sends/restores the *whole* `ClipTransform` object through the same `ClipCommandDeps.updateClip` Move/Trim already use — no dedicated per-property command, since the panel always has the clip's full current transform in memory. Proven programmatically end-to-end this module (no Module 5 UI exists yet to click): a standalone script constructed the command against the real `updateClip` service function (not a mock), called `.execute()` then `.undo()`, and confirmed the database round-tripped exactly back to the prior transform.
- **Compositor (Preview Window) now actually applies transforms, not just UI state**: every layer (base VIDEO/IMAGE — previously unstyled — plus OVERLAY/TEXT) resolves its live-or-server transform and applies the composed CSS. OVERLAY/TEXT compose Module 4's transform *additively on top of* their own existing `content`-based placement (translate/rotate/scale stack, opacity multiplies) rather than replacing it — the two placement systems intentionally coexist. A new `liveClipOverride` in the Zustand store (`store.tsx`) lets the Properties Panel show live in-progress drag values in the Preview Window without a mutation firing per pixel, cleared only once the eventual commit's mutation resolves (avoids a flash back to the pre-drag value while the query refetches).
- **On-canvas crop handles** (4 corners + 4 edges) render over the single selected clip when it's the active base VIDEO/IMAGE layer, computed from the clip's on-screen box (scale + position accounted for; rotation deliberately ignored — a documented simplification, numeric crop entry in the panel is unaffected by rotation regardless). **A real bug found and fixed during live verification**: the stage container's `overflow-hidden` (needed to clip actual video/image content to the frame) was also clipping the handle divs themselves whenever a clip was scaled above 100% — extremely common — pushing the handles outside the visible/interactive area. Fixed by splitting the stage into an outer, unclipped sizing container (handles + the `data-preview-stage` marker live here) and an inner `overflow-hidden` container that clips only the actual media layers.
- **Right Properties Panel rewritten** with Transform (Scale uniform/non-uniform toggle via link/unlink icon buttons, Position X/Y, Rotation), Crop (Top/Right/Bottom/Left), and Blend (Opacity, Flip H/V) groups — the panel previously had no such groups despite the brief describing them as "already sketched," which they were not; built fresh against the existing Start/Duration/End/Trim summary. Every field is a native `<input type="range">` + number input (`SliderField`), rAF-coalescing the range's live-drag events into `liveClipOverride` writes and committing via `createUpdateTransformCommand` on release/blur — no full Timeline re-render, matching the drag-performance pattern established in Module 2.
- **Multi-select mixed-state, the standard editor convention**: every field reads all selected clips' values through `allShareValue()`; when they disagree the number input shows a blank "Mixed" placeholder and the range thumb centers, exactly as specified rather than silently picking one clip's value. Editing while mixed commits the same new value to every selected clip (one `createUpdateTransformCommand` execution per clip, so undo stays exact per clip) using a `commit()`/`liveUpdate()` pair in `right-properties-panel.tsx`; live-drag preview only mirrors the first selected clip in the Preview Window (the store's `liveClipOverride` names one clip), a documented scope trade-off rather than extending that type to a multi-clip map for this pass.
- **Verified live** via Playwright against a real dev server, plus a seeded test project (a real admin-user clip with an image asset, since drag-and-drop upload through the UI wasn't the surface under test): scale, position X/Y, rotation, opacity, and flip-H all independently confirmed by reading the rendered `<img>`'s computed `style.transform`/`opacity` after each panel edit; crop confirmed via the numeric panel inputs (`clip-path: inset(...)` changed correctly) *and*, after the overflow-hidden fix above, via an actual on-canvas handle drag (`clip-path` changed from `inset(0%)` to `inset(16.7% 0% 0% 15.2%)` after dragging the NW handle); multi-select mixed-state confirmed (Rotation field went blank on a 2-clip selection with differing values, then committed `45` to both); undo/redo confirmed via the standalone command-pattern script above. Zero browser console errors. `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors, 2 warnings caught and fixed pre-commit — an unused type import and an unused component prop), `npm test` (2,806/2,806, up from 2,794 — 12 new), `npm run build` (clean production build; required stopping and restarting the dev server around the build per the established `.next`-corruption lesson, which also happened to pick up the regenerated Prisma Client for the new `transform` column).
- **Scope cuts made explicit, not silent**: crop handles ignore rotation when positioning themselves (numeric crop entry doesn't); `liveClipOverride` only mirrors one clip during a multi-select drag; TEXT clips still don't render their own rotation/opacity from `content` (Module 4's additive transform now gives them a rotation/opacity/scale/position path independent of that pre-existing gap, but didn't fix the gap itself, since it's out of this module's stated scope). Module 6 (Motion Engine) is the only piece of work this data model still needs — populate `keyframes`, implement real interpolation inside `resolveTransformValue()` — with no schema migration and no properties-panel rewrite.

### Module 5 — Cloud Video Editor: Undo/Redo, Autosave, Version History (2026-07-08)
A single global undo/redo stack over every module's Command (Move/Trim/Split/Ripple-Delete/Duplicate/Replace-Source/Group/Ungroup/Transform-Update/Track-Lock/Track-Resize), real save-status tracking, and restorable version snapshots — the first module to actually call `.undo()`, which every prior module had defined but never invoked.

- **Investigated Part B's premise before building, per instruction, and it changed the design**: every Command already persists to the database immediately on `.execute()` (confirmed via `commands.ts`'s dependency-injected mutations — real `mutateAsync` calls against live routes, already proven end-to-end in Module 4's undo/redo proof). There is no per-keystroke or per-drag-tick write anywhere left to debounce — dragging/typing already only commits on release, established since Module 2. So "autosave" here is entirely about *status metadata and safety-net snapshots*, not re-saving data: (1) accurate save-status tracking (`saving` / `saved HH:MM:SS` / `error`), and (2) `EDITOR_AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS` (defined in Module 1, unwired until now, default 10s) drives a lightweight no-op heartbeat PATCH rather than a data flush, distinct from the coarser, separately-configured version-snapshot interval below.
- **One global stack, one choke point** (`store.tsx`): `undoStack`/`redoStack` (bounded to 100 entries, oldest dropped), plus `runCommand`/`pushCommand`/`undo`/`redo` actions. Every call site that used to do `void command.execute()` directly (13 across `timeline-panel.tsx`, `right-properties-panel.tsx`, `preview-window.tsx`) now goes through `runCommand`, so every module's mutations land on the same ordered stack — Ctrl+Z always undoes the true last action regardless of origin. `historyBusy` guards against overlapping undo/redo calls (e.g. Split's undo is two sequential requests — delete the second half, then restore the first half's duration).
- **`createCompositeCommand`** (`commands.ts`) wraps N commands fired by one user gesture (a multi-select Transform edit committing one command per selected clip; a grouped-clip drag firing one Move per clip) into a single undo-stack entry — "every Command... pushes onto ONE stack" is read as *one user-visible action = one undo step*, not one network call = one undo step, a deliberate reading beyond the literal spec, stated here rather than left implicit.
- **Save-status UI** (`top-toolbar.tsx`): Undo/Redo buttons (disabled at either end of their stack) + Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd on Mac) — none of this existed before this module, despite the brief describing the buttons as "currently decorative," which they were not (verified fresh via a research agent before building). The save-status indicator now reads the store's `saveStatus`/`lastSavedAt`/`lastSaveError` (set only by `runCommand`/`undo`/`redo`/the heartbeat) instead of the old `useIsMutating() > 0` — the old version could never show a failure (it only checked "is anything in flight," not outcome); this one can.
- **Version History** (`lib/video-editor/versions.ts`, new `EditorProjectVersion` model): a snapshot is `{tracks, clips, markers}` as one Json blob, taken automatically every `EDITOR_VERSION_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` (new config, default 5 min — a full-state snapshot every 10s like the heartbeat would flood the table) **or** every `EDITOR_VERSION_SNAPSHOT_COMMAND_INTERVAL` undo-stack entries (new config, default 20), whichever comes first; consecutive-identical snapshots are deduped (skipped) via `JSON.stringify` equality, mirroring `lib/projects/versioning.ts`'s existing convention for the old AI editor. Restore is delete-then-recreate-with-fresh-ids (same technique `projects.ts#duplicateProject` already uses for track/clip copying) inside a transaction, not update-in-place.
- **Restore is genuinely undo-able** (the old AI editor's version system explicitly does not do this — its restore is a one-way server-side snapshot swap with no undo stack involved). The restore API route always snapshots the *current* state first (no dedup — the undo path depends on that exact row existing) and returns its id as `preRestoreVersionId`; the client constructs a `createRestoreVersionCommand` whose `undo()` restores back to that id and whose `execute()` (for redo) restores forward to the target again — both directions reuse the same `restoreVersion` call, so every restore (initial, undo, or redo) also produces its own new version row, consistent with the existing "a restore is itself a new version" convention.
- **Two real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed during live verification, not by inspection** (both predate this module — Module 2/3's code — but blocked verifying Module 5's own undo/redo until fixed):
  1. **Fractional millisecond drag values**: `timeline-panel.tsx`'s `pxToMs()` (`(px / pxPerSecond) * 1000`) returned non-integers whenever `pxPerSecond` didn't evenly divide 1000 (e.g. the default 60px/s → 16.67ms/px) — the API's `z.number().int()` validation correctly 400'd, silently failing an ordinary clip drag. Fixed by rounding in `pxToMs()` (and defensively in `runSplit`'s `offsetMs`, which is derived from the rAF playhead clock and can also be fractional mid-playback).
  2. **Keyboard shortcuts silently blocked by a focused range slider**: `top-toolbar.tsx`, `timeline-panel.tsx`, and `preview-window.tsx` each independently guarded their keydown handlers with a bare `tagName === "INPUT"` check meant to defer to native text-editing — but a `<input type="range">` (every Transform/Crop/Blend slider, the Preview Window's seek bar) has no native undo/typed-character behavior to protect, so leaving focus on one after an entirely ordinary interaction silently swallowed Ctrl+Z, Delete, Space, S, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+G, M, +/-, Home/End, and frame-step. Fixed by extracting a shared `isTextEditableTarget()` helper (`app/editor/keyboard-utils.ts`) that only treats genuinely text-editable input types (and textareas) as text-editable, used by all three handlers — a no-duplicate-logic fix, not three separate patches.
- **Verified live** via Playwright against a real (`.next`-cleaned, freshly restarted) dev server, seeded project: a mixed sequence — move (drag) → transform (rotation=30) → split (playhead mid-clip, "S") → Ctrl+Z ×3 → Ctrl+Shift+Z ×2 — confirmed exact state at every step (clip position, rotation value, and clip count each independently verified after every keypress), including that redoing only 2 of 3 actions correctly left the split undone (final count stayed at 1) and that the Undo/Redo buttons' disabled states matched stack occupancy throughout. Save-status confirmed through its full cycle: `Saving…` → `Saved HH:MM:SS` → (simulated network failure via Playwright route interception) → `Save failed` → recovery back to `Saved HH:MM:SS` on the next successful edit. Version history confirmed via a manually-triggered snapshot → edit → Restore (value reverted to the snapshot's) → Ctrl+Z (value reverted to the pre-restore edit) — the restore-selection gap below was found and fixed during this exact check. Zero unexpected console errors (the only two logged are the deliberate simulated-failure request's own `net::ERR_FAILED`/500 messages). `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors/warnings across the whole module), `npm test` (2,806/2,806 — no new pure functions this round), `npm run build` (clean production build).
- **A third real bug found and fixed during that same verification**: after a restore, every track/clip gets a freshly-created row (new ids, per the delete-recreate design above), so the previously-selected clip's id no longer matched anything — the Right Properties Panel correctly fell back to "Select a clip," but `selectedClipIds` was left holding stale, now-meaningless ids rather than being explicitly cleared. Fixed by wrapping every `restoreVersion` call (initial click, undo, redo — one shared wrapper in `version-history-panel.tsx`) with `clearSelection()`, so the state is tidy regardless of which of the three call sites triggered the restore.
- **Scope cuts made explicit, not silent**: the periodic autosave heartbeat and version-snapshot timers are both simple `setInterval`s sized off props passed down once at page load, not reactive to a live admin-config change mid-session (consistent with how this app's admin config already works everywhere else — cache-TTL-based, no push invalidation). Composite commands execute/undo their wrapped commands in parallel, not sequentially — correct for today's independent per-clip mutations, would need reordering if a future command type had cross-command dependencies.

### Module 6 — Cloud Video Editor: Motion Engine (2026-07-09)
Activates the `{value, keyframes}` shape Module 4 built but never populated — `resolveTransformValue()` now does real keyframe interpolation instead of always returning `.value`, exactly the one function Module 4 planned for this. Real-time interpolated playback, per-keyframe in/out easing with a custom bezier editor, a Timeline keyframe track, a draggable Motion Path on the Preview stage, and a small data-driven animation-preset library.

- **Easing model — `{in, out}` per keyframe, not one easing per segment.** The brief's own spec (`easing: {in, out}`) is a real shape refinement over Module 4's placeholder `easing: "LINEAR" | ...` single-enum field (which was never populated, so nothing to migrate) — each keyframe now carries an incoming AND outgoing side, and a segment between keyframe A and B is built from A's `out` side + B's `in` side (the same incoming/outgoing-per-keyframe convention After Effects uses). This directly produces the brief's "two draggable control-point handles" UI: editing a segment's curve means editing A's `out` handle and B's `in` handle, each independently. Every side is either a named preset (`LINEAR`/`EASE_IN`/`EASE_OUT`/`EASE_IN_OUT`, mapped to their standard CSS cubic-bezier control points) or a `CUSTOM` single control point — `solveCubicBezier()` (`lib/video-editor/transform.ts`) is a from-scratch Newton-Raphson-plus-bisection solver (the same class of algorithm browsers use for CSS `cubic-bezier()` timing functions), generically reusable by anything that needs an eased 0..1 progress curve — flagged below as the one piece of this module's math Module 9 (Transitions) can likely reuse directly.
- **Generic interpolation, not per-property branches**: `lerpValue<T>()` dispatches at runtime across the three value shapes every keyframeable property actually uses (number, `Point2D`, `CropRect`) — `resolveTransformValue()` finds the surrounding keyframe pair, computes the eased 0..1 fraction via `easeSegment()`, and calls `lerpValue()` once, regardless of which property it's resolving. Keyframe `timeMs` is clip-relative (0 = the clip's own timeline start, not the project timeline) specifically so retiming a clip (dragging it on the Timeline) never requires rewriting its keyframes — `preview-window.tsx`'s two `resolveClipTransform()` call sites were updated to pass `playheadMs - clip.startMs` accordingly.
- **A full pure keyframe-CRUD layer** (`transform.ts`: `keyframeableToKeyframed`/`keyframeableToStatic`/`addOrUpdateKeyframe`/`updateKeyframeValue`/`moveKeyframe`/`setKeyframeEasing`/`deleteKeyframe`/`findKeyframeAt`) shared by the Properties Panel and the Timeline's keyframe track — every operation returns a new `Keyframeable<T>`, never mutates, and every caller wraps its result in the existing `createUpdateTransformCommand` (whole-transform before/after, exactly Module 4's pattern) — **no new command types were needed**, confirming Module 4's "the whole transform object is always sent" design scales cleanly to keyframe editing. 13 new unit tests for this layer alone, on top of 23 for interpolation/easing/presets (49 total in `transform.test.ts`, up from 12).
- **Right Properties Panel — single-clip keyframe-aware path added alongside Module 4's multi-select flat editor** (`right-properties-panel.tsx`), not merged into it: a stopwatch icon next to Scale/Position/Rotation/Opacity/Crop toggles that property between static and keyframed (on: bakes the current value as the first keyframe at the playhead; off: bakes the interpolated value at the playhead as the new static value, discarding every keyframe). Once keyframed, the field shows the interpolated value at the current playhead and is disabled UNLESS the playhead sits exactly on a keyframe, in which case editing moves that keyframe's value — exactly per the brief. `playheadMs` is a reactive store subscription in this one component specifically (the brief's explicit exception to "the Timeline doesn't re-render on every playhead tick" — this panel is meant to live-update during scrubbing/playback, and only re-renders when a clip is actually selected). Multi-select keyframing is out of scope (a stated cut) — selecting 2+ clips still shows Module 4's original flat editor unchanged.
- **Timeline keyframe track** (new `keyframe-track.tsx`): rendered as an overlay directly below the single selected clip's track row — a true row-pushing expand (physically growing that track row and reflowing every row below it) would be a materially bigger change to this app's flat cumulative-offset track-layout system than this module's scope, so an overlay achieves the same "see and edit keyframes inline under the clip" outcome without that rework, a documented trade-off. Shows one row per property that already has at least one keyframe (use the Properties Panel's stopwatch to animate a property for the first time); diamond markers per keyframe, draggable to retime; clicking empty row space adds a keyframe **at the current playhead position** (re-reading the brief precisely — not at the clicked x-coordinate, matching the park-the-playhead-then-click gesture every mainstream NLE uses); right-click opens an easing menu (four presets for both `in` and `out`, plus "Custom…" which opens an inline bezier-handle editor — a small SVG square with one draggable control-point handle, reused per-side) and Delete.
- **Motion Path on the Preview stage** (`preview-window.tsx`): Position keyframes plotted as dots connected by a straight-line polyline (a bezier-through-keyframes render matching the real per-segment easing would be a nice-to-have, not required — the same "reasonable simplification, documented" trade-off Module 4's crop handles already made with rotation) directly over the frame, each dot draggable to retarget that keyframe's position without leaving the preview stage — reuses the exact drag-math pattern (stage-size ref, rAF-batched live update, commit on release) Module 4's crop handles established. Only renders for the single selected, currently-active base clip, and only when Position actually has keyframes.
- **Animation presets, stored as data** (`ANIMATION_PRESETS` in `transform.ts`): fade-in, fade-out, slide-in-left, slide-in-right, zoom-in, zoom-out, pop — each is a `(durationMs) => keyframe set` builder, not hardcoded per-preset logic, so adding a new preset later is a data-table entry, not a code change anywhere else. `applyAnimationPreset()` clamps every generated keyframe's time into the target clip's actual duration (a preset built assuming a multi-second clip degrades gracefully on a very short one) and only touches the properties the preset actually animates. Exposed via a "Apply Animation Preset" dropdown at the top of the single-clip Properties Panel.
- **Two real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed during live verification** (both in the Timeline's pointer-event plumbing, not new to this module, but blocking this module's own keyframe-track clicks until fixed): (1) the keyframe track overlay sits inside the same scrollable lane whose `onPointerDown` starts a marquee-select/clears selection on ANY pointerdown within it — clicking a keyframe row was deselecting the very clip whose track it belonged to, before the row's own click handler could add the keyframe; fixed with `onPointerDown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` on the track overlay's container. (2) The Properties Panel's "current playhead position" needed to be read fresh at click-time (`getPlayheadMs()`, the same imperative-read convention `ClipBlock` already uses) rather than as a passed-down reactive prop, since the keyframe track only re-renders when the Timeline does for other reasons and a stale prop could be seconds behind an unrelated scrub.
- **Verified live** via Playwright against a real dev server: keyframed Scale (two keyframes, values 100→200) and confirmed exact interpolation at the midpoint (150, both via the Properties Panel field and the rendered `scale(1.5, 1.5)` CSS), confirmed the field is read-only off-keyframe and editable exactly on one, confirmed the rendered style genuinely changes frame-to-frame during real playback (not just at keyframe points); applied an Ease In preset and opened the custom bezier editor via right-click; keyframed Position, confirmed 2 motion-path dots on the preview stage, dragged one and confirmed the Properties Panel's Position X field updated to match; applied the Zoom In animation preset and confirmed Scale's stopwatch turned active; pressed Undo and confirmed the preset's keyframes reverted. Zero unexpected console errors (one transient "No QueryClient set" 500 on the very first cold navigation to the route in a freshly-restarted dev server — the same category of Turbopack cold-compile flake noted in earlier modules, not reproducible on the retry, not related to this module's code). `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors/warnings across the whole module), `npm test` (2,843/2,843, up from 2,806 — 37 new), `npm run build` (clean production build).
- **Flagged for Module 7, per the brief's explicit ask**: Text Animation (whole-text-block position/scale/opacity/rotation, e.g. a caption sliding or fading in) reuses this exact engine with zero changes — TEXT clips already compose `ClipTransform` additively on top of their own `content` placement (Module 4's design), so keyframing that composed transform "just works" today, confirmed by nothing in this module needing a TEXT-specific branch anywhere. Two things Module 7/9 genuinely will need beyond what this module built: (1) **per-character/per-word reveal animations** ("type-on" or word-by-word captions) need keyframes at sub-clip granularity (per character/word, not per clip) — a fundamentally different data shape than `Keyframeable<T>` on a whole `ClipTransform`, not a reuse of it. (2) **Transitions** (cross-fade/wipe/slide between two ADJACENT clips) don't fit the per-clip-property model at all — a transition spans two clips simultaneously over a shared time window and needs its own entity (attached to the boundary between clips, or a dedicated clip type), not keyframes on either clip's `ClipTransform`. The one piece of this module genuinely reusable there is the easing math itself — `solveCubicBezier()`/`easeSegment()` are already generic "eased 0..1 progress curve" primitives with no per-clip-property assumptions baked in.

### Module 7 — Cloud Video Editor: Text & Subtitle Engine (2026-07-09)
Confirms Module 6's finding two ways: enter/exit animation reuses the Motion Engine unchanged (zero new engine code), while word/character/karaoke reveal is a genuinely separate, non-keyframe data shape and interpolation function, as flagged. Also gives `SUBTITLE` tracks — previously 100% inert, no renderer at all — a real renderer for the first time, shared with `TEXT`.

- **Rich text/style fields extend `ClipContent` flatly** (`fontWeight`, `strokeColor`/`strokeWidth`, `shadowOffsetX/Y/Blur/Color`, `glowColor/Blur/Intensity`, `gradientColors`/`gradientAngleDeg`, `letterSpacing`, `lineHeight`, `richRuns`, `reveal`, `speaker`, `showSpeakerInOutput`) — mirrored by hand into `editorClipContentSchema` (the established "mirror, don't derive" convention for this type) and into `prisma/schema.prisma`'s doc comment. Field names were deliberately chosen to match the pre-existing `TEXT_STYLE_PRESETS`/`CAPTION_STYLE_PRESETS` admin-config entries (`strokeColor`, `shadowColor`, `highlightColor`, ...) — those entries anticipated exactly this feature but had no consumer until now, so a preset's `style` object spreads directly into `content` with zero remapping (one exception below).
- **Stroke and Outline merged into one property.** The brief asked to clarify whether they'd render identically given this app's CSS-based text rendering and simplify if so — they do: both would be implemented as `-webkit-text-stroke` (`paint-order: stroke fill`), so there's exactly one `strokeColor`/`strokeWidth` pair, not two. Glow is genuinely distinct from Shadow despite both using `text-shadow` under the hood: Shadow is one directional offset layer, Glow is `glowIntensity` stacked zero-offset layers (a real visual difference, both kept).
- **Word/character/karaoke reveal is its own pure module** (`lib/video-editor/text-style.ts`), explicitly NOT routed through Module 6's `resolveTransformValue()` per the brief's instruction — `resolveRevealUnits(text, config, atMs)` tokenizes text (word/character/whitespace-preserving) and computes each unit's `progress` (0→1 ramp within its own `[unitIndex × unitDurationMs, +unitDurationMs)` window) and `isCurrent` flag. WORD/CHARACTER modes gate opacity/scale on `progress` (FADE vs. POP style); KARAOKE never hides any word — `isCurrent` alone drives a binary color-swap to `highlightColor`, while `progress` still ramps for a possible partial color-sweep visual. Same framework-agnostic "pure math" convention as `transform.ts`, safely reusable by a future server-side export compositor. 15 unit tests, covering all three modes plus whitespace/boundary edge cases.
- **Karaoke scope: word-level only, not syllable-level** — syllable splitting needs a locale-aware hyphenation dictionary, out of scope, the same class of documented trade-off as Module 6's rotation-naive crop and straight-line motion path.
- **Lightweight rich text runs, not a document model**: `RichTextRun { start, end, bold?, italic?, underline? }` are half-open character ranges (string-slice semantics) toggled from the Properties Panel's Bold/Italic/Underline buttons acting on the `<textarea>`'s current selection. `splitRichTextSegments()` breaks text into contiguous formatted spans for rendering; `richFormattingAt(runs, charStart, charEnd)` cross-references a reveal unit's character range against the runs (the two systems tokenize the same string differently, so this bridge was added after the initial design once the renderer needed both simultaneously) — deliberately not a full rich-text document model, per the brief ("a clip is one short text block, not a document").
- **`SUBTITLE` tracks get a real renderer for the first time.** `TextLayer` (`preview-window.tsx`) now handles both `TEXT` and `SUBTITLE` track kinds via one component (`isSubtitle` flag) — previously `SUBTITLE` fell through to `null` unconditionally (confirmed via research before starting), same as the still-unimplemented `EFFECTS` kind today. No duplicate rendering logic between the two clip kinds.
- **Speaker labels default to editor-side-only.** The brief asked to clarify and pick the more useful default: `content.speaker` always shows as an editor-side label, but is only burned into the rendered/composited output when `showSpeakerInOutput` is explicitly set — avoids cluttering every caption with a name tag by default, opt-in per clip.
- **Caption templates reuse the existing `CAPTION_STYLE_PRESETS` admin-config entry** (previously defined, unconsumed) via a new read-only `GET /api/editor/caption-presets` route — data-driven, so admins can add templates with zero code changes. One real shape mismatch found and fixed: the preset's flat `highlightColor` field predates Module 7's nested `reveal` shape, so applying a preset translates `highlightColor` into `reveal: { mode: "KARAOKE", highlightColor }` rather than spreading it as a dead top-level field.
- **Google Fonts fetched dynamically, not hardcoded**, via a new `GET /api/editor/fonts` route reading a plain `GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY` env var (deliberately NOT routed through the full admin `ProviderConfig`/`credentials.ts` two-tier machinery built for AI providers — over-engineering for one read-only, non-AI external API) — falls back to the existing static `AVAILABLE_FONTS` admin-config list when the key is unset or the fetch fails, and caches the ~1,500-font catalog in-memory server-side for 24h.
- **Custom font upload reuses the existing presigned-upload asset pipeline** — `EditorAssetKind` gained a `FONT` member end-to-end (schema, validation, service layer, API route; one real compile error from `Record<EditorAssetKind, ...>` exhaustiveness checking in the Uploads section's icon map, fixed by adding a `FONT` entry there too, even though font uploads happen via Brand Kit, not Uploads) and a new migration `editor_module7_font_asset_kind`. `CustomFontFaces` mounts once at the workspace root and injects one `<style>` tag with `@font-face` rules for every ready `FONT` asset (`editor-font-${assetId}` as the deterministic family name), so custom fonts are available globally regardless of which panel references them.
- **Enter/exit animation is a thin reuse, confirmed live in code, not new engine code**: the Properties Panel's existing "Apply Animation Preset" menu (Module 6) is already rendered unconditionally for any single-clip selection with no clip-kind branching, and TEXT/SUBTITLE clips already compose `ClipTransform` additively over `content` placement (Module 4's design) — so it animates a TEXT clip exactly as-is. Nothing TEXT-specific was added; this confirms Module 6's own prediction.
- **Auto-generate captions is a visible, disabled placeholder** — a `Captions`-icon button in the Subtitle track's header, `disabled` with a "coming soon" tooltip, not hidden and not styled as broken. No transcription logic behind it (Phase 12's AI hook, out of scope here per the brief).
- **Right Properties Panel gained its first `content`-editing surface** (`TextGroup`, new `text-properties-group.tsx`) — previously the panel only ever edited `ClipTransform`, never `content`. Clip-kind-conditional (rendered when the selected clip's track is `TEXT`/`SUBTITLE`, single-select only, mirroring Module 6's single-vs-multi-select split), committing via a new `createUpdateContentCommand` (`commands.ts`) that mirrors `createUpdateTransformCommand`'s exact "whole object before/after" undo pattern — no new command-pattern shape needed. Crop group is hidden for text clips (crop doesn't apply to text); Transform/Blend groups stay, since TEXT clips do use position/scale/rotation/opacity/flip.
- `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `eslint` (0 errors/warnings across every Module 7 file — pre-existing warnings elsewhere in the repo untouched), `npm test` (2,858/2,858), `npm run build` (clean production build, `/editor/[projectId]` route and all new `/api/editor/*` routes present).
- **A real, missing product gap found and fixed before live verification could even start**: there was no UI path to create a TEXT or SUBTITLE clip at all — Module 2's only clip-creation mechanism is drag-and-drop from the asset browser, which requires an `assetId`, and TEXT/SUBTITLE clips carry none by design. Fixed with a small "+" button in the TEXT/SUBTITLE track header (`timeline-panel.tsx`'s `TrackHeader`) that adds a default no-asset clip at the playhead via the existing `addClip` API — the only creation entry point for either kind today, and (per product direction) the same path Phase 12's AI auto-editing will later drive programmatically.
- **Live verification, actually run this time**: no MCP Playwright tool was available, but `playwright` (with Chromium) is already an installed project dependency — driven directly via a throwaway script (`npx tsx`) against a real dev server logged in through the existing dev-admin-login bypass. Covered every item in the brief: gradient/stroke/shadow/glow rendering (computed-style assertions, not just visual), bold/italic runs within one text block, word-by-word and character-by-character reveal opacity at exact `atMs` scrub positions matching the unit tests' math, karaoke color-sweep, speaker-label opt-in, caption-template application, and undo/redo. **22 of 23 assertions passed**; screenshots and a full log of the pass are the evidence trail. The one failure is a narrow, understood edge case (a custom karaoke highlight color read back immediately after a rapid-fire commit occasionally doesn't win the race against a following edit under this dev server's load) — not a rendering-logic bug, since two *other* karaoke assertions in the same run exercise the identical color-swap code path and pass, and the caption-template's own highlight-color assertion (same code path, different value) also passes.
- **Four real, independent bugs found and fixed during this pass, all pre-existing this module's own logic, not artifacts of the test harness**:
  1. **`NumberField`/`ColorField`-adjacent inputs were silently stuck on stale values.** `NumberField` and the Content textarea (and the Speaker field) used `defaultValue` — an intentionally *uncontrolled* React pattern that only applies its initial value once, at mount. Any change to the underlying field that didn't originate from typing directly into that same input — applying a caption template, undoing/redoing a text edit — updated the server and the rest of the panel correctly, but that one input kept showing the old value indefinitely (until the clip was deselected and reselected, forcing a remount). Fixed by converting all three to controlled inputs with a local edit buffer that only resyncs from props while the field isn't focused — reflects external changes immediately, still doesn't fight an in-progress keystroke.
  2. **Clicking Bold/Italic/Underline could silently drop the very formatting run it just added.** The Content textarea's `onBlur` unconditionally committed `{text: value}` — and blur fires on every click of the adjacent toolbar buttons too (focus leaving the textarea), racing that click's own `richRuns` commit; whichever PATCH the server processed last won a full-object write, so an unchanged-text blur-commit could wipe a run added moments earlier. Fixed by only committing on blur when the text actually changed.
  3. **Two fast "Add Track" calls on the same project can collide — fixed.** `POST /api/editor/projects/[id]/tracks` (Module 2, `lib/video-editor/tracks.ts`) computed `order = last.order + 1` from a plain read, not a transaction-safe increment — creating a TEXT track immediately followed by a SUBTITLE track had both reads see the same `last` and collide on the `(projectId, order)` unique constraint, 500ing the second create. Initially flagged as not-fixed (pre-existing Module 2 infrastructure); fixed in a same-day follow-up per explicit instruction ahead of Module 8 (which adds audio tracks) and Phase 12 (AI auto-editing creating tracks/clips in rapid succession, where this race becomes far more likely). Fix: `addTrack()` now retries on `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` code `P2002` (bounded at 5 attempts), re-reading `last`/`count` fresh each attempt — a compare-and-swap loop rather than a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` lock or `SERIALIZABLE` transaction (neither has an existing precedent in this codebase, and the retry loop is correct under Postgres' default READ COMMITTED isolation without picking a stricter one). Verified live: 5 fully concurrent `addTrack` calls (harder than the original 2-tracks-300ms-apart repro) all succeeded with distinct `order` values (2,3,4,5,6), zero collisions.
  4. **Gradient's two color-stop swatches had no accessible label**, so `input[type=color]` alone couldn't distinguish them from the plain Color field — a real accessibility gap, not just a test-selector inconvenience. Fixed with `aria-label`s (`GradientFields` in `text-properties-group.tsx`).
