- **Admin "grant a free download"** (`adminGrantDownload()` in `download-service.ts`) and **download history** (`listDownloads()`) exist as functions but have no admin UI or user-facing route calling them yet.
- ~~SMS delivery. MSG91_AUTH_KEY/Twilio failover are env vars with no implementation yet.~~ **Done 2026-07-24** — real MSG91-primary/Twilio-failover implementation, see the Codebase Health-Check Fixes entry above. Still needs the founder's own real MSG91 DLT template registration + Twilio account setup to actually deliver (code is real and ready; the accounts/registration are a real-world step this can't complete).
- ~~Scaffolded-but-empty dashboard sections: Brand Kit, Media Library, Settings, Templates.~~ **Done in Milestone 14** — all four now have real pages, linked from the rewritten 14-item sidebar. **Team is still scaffolded** (`.gitkeep` only) — real collaboration UI is gated on `ProjectCollaborator` getting actual invite/accept routes, see the Collaboration entry below.
- ~~Containerizing the Next.js app itself.~~ **Done in Milestone 12** — multi-stage `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.yml` (`app`/`postgres`/optional `redis`).
- ~~Real distributed config cache.~~ **Done in Milestone 12** — `lib/cache/cache.ts` backs `lib/admin/config.ts` with Redis when `REDIS_URL` is set (in-process fallback otherwise); still no pub/sub cross-instance invalidation push, so a multi-instance deployment picks up admin config changes on each instance's own cache TTL rather than instantly — see `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md`.
- ~~Refunds.~~ **Done in Milestone 13** — admin-initiated refunds (`lib/billing/refunds.ts`, `/admin/payments`) call the active provider's real refund API. **Proration still isn't implemented**: the user-facing cancel is still cancel-at-period-end only, and Milestone 13's admin "cancel now" (`/admin/subscriptions`) ends access immediately without calculating/issuing a partial refund for the unused remainder — a deliberate scope cut for both, not an oversight.
- **Self-hosted Image/Voice/Video adapters.** Only the LLM category has a concrete self-hosted adapter (`SelfHostedLLMProvider`); Image/Voice/Video would follow the identical pattern (env-var base URL + minimal REST contract) but aren't implemented yet — see Milestone 6 notes.
- **Cost-rate accuracy.** `GENERATION_COST_RATES` ships with illustrative default $/unit figures (admin-editable) — they're not pinned to each vendor's live pricing page and will drift; treat the resulting `costUsd` figures as directionally useful, not invoice-accurate, until an admin tunes them.
- **No real-vendor failover has been exercised against an actual API outage** — verified live only with a missing-credential failure (a real, common failure mode) and via unit tests with fakes; a genuine network-timeout/5xx scenario against e.g. real OpenAI/Gemini hasn't been observed in this environment (no live vendor credentials configured).
- **Real ffmpeg-based scene merge for a real video vendor.** `MockVideoProvider.mergeScenes()` fakes it end-to-end; `ReplicateVideoProvider.mergeScenes()` honestly throws since Replicate's text-to-video API has no generic clip-concatenation capability — a real deployment using Replicate would need a dedicated video-editing/concat adapter (Shotstack, ffmpeg-on-Lambda, etc.) behind the same `VideoProvider` interface.
- **Scene decomposition is deterministic, not LLM-planned.** Splitting on `[HOOK]/[BODY]/[CTA]` markers (falling back to paragraphs, then a single scene) is a scope choice for this milestone, not a limitation of the architecture — `lib/scenes/engine.ts`'s `splitScriptIntoSceneTexts()` is the one function an LLM-based scene planner would replace, with nothing downstream needing to change.
- **No preemption of in-flight render/merge jobs.** Pause/Cancel only affect not-yet-claimed (`PENDING`) jobs — a job already `PROCESSING` when the user acts finishes naturally. True cancellation would need the same `AbortSignal`-wiring gap already documented for Generation Engine timeouts (Known Issues #7) to be closed first.
- **Live scene progress is SSE-over-DB-polling, not true pub/sub.** `GET /api/videos/[id]/scenes/stream` polls every 1.5s server-side and pushes diffs — real-time-feeling to the client, but the same kind of "simple now, swap for Redis/pub-sub later if it doesn't scale" trade-off already made for the admin config cache.
- **Collaboration is schema-only.** `ProjectCollaborator` (Milestone 8) has no invite UI, no API routes, and isn't checked anywhere — `VideoProject.userId` is still the only real ownership/authority check. A deliberate scope cut per the user's explicit choice, not an oversight.
- **No live preview generation in Prompt Studio.** Image/video prompt edits are saved and used at actual render time, but there's no "generate a quick preview from this prompt" button — generation stays exclusively inside the existing render pipeline (Requirement 11's scope, by design).
- **Undo/redo is client-side and session-scoped.** The Studio's undo/redo command stack lives in browser memory only (no backend endpoint, nothing persisted) — a page refresh clears it; the durable safety net for "I want an old version back" is the Version History panel (`ProjectVersion`), not undo/redo.
- **Script Studio's Rewrite/Expand/Shorten/Translate/Hook/CTA are generate-only.** They return candidate text for review; applying a result re-uses the existing script-edit route rather than auto-saving — by design (avoids a second save path), but means there's no one-click "regenerate and keep" flow yet.
- **Real video compositor for Export.** `MockVideoProvider.composeTimeline()` fakes a full multi-track composite end-to-end; `ReplicateVideoProvider.composeTimeline()` honestly throws — a real deployment needs a dedicated video-editing/compositing adapter (Shotstack, ffmpeg-on-Lambda, Remotion Lambda) behind the same `VideoProvider` interface. Same documented gap as Milestone 7's `mergeScenes()`, now also true of Export.
- **Scene Preview is a browser-side approximation, not the real render.** It composites VIDEO/IMAGE + TEXT/STICKER overlays live in the DOM via one `playheadMs` clock, useful for editing feedback, but it is not frame-accurate to what `composeTimeline()` will actually produce (no real alpha compositing, no codec-accurate timing) — treat it as a preview, not a proof of the final export.

### AI OS Phase 1 — Core Foundation (2026-07-01)
Created the `src/lib/ai-os/` module namespace with three clean modules and typed contracts between them. Everything existing continues working byte-for-byte; Phase 1 is purely organizational.

- **`lib/ai-os/types.ts`** — Core boundary interfaces: `CreativeRequest` (normalized request), `UserIntent` (Phase 1 lightweight signals), `BrandContext`, `AssetIntelligence`. The single source of truth for AI OS contracts.
- **`lib/ai-os/request-manager/index.ts`** — Extracts rate-limit check + Zod validation from `enhance-prompt/route.ts` into a typed `buildEnhancePromptRequest()` returning `BuildRequestResult` (ok/error discriminated union). Route handler delegates to this instead of running these inline.
- **`lib/ai-os/user-understanding/`** — Phase 1 lightweight engine (`analyzeUserIntent()`) with 6 detectors: language, industry, intent type, business goal, platform signal, confidence. Pure functions, no I/O.
- **`lib/ai-os/asset-understanding/`** — Façade over `lib/design-intelligence/`: wraps reference asset DB lookup + analysis + cache guard + brand kit fetch into `resolveAssetIntelligence()`. ~50 lines previously inline in the route.
- **`enhance-prompt/route.ts`** — Refactored to delegate to all three modules; behavior and HTTP contract identical. Creative Brain, Creative Director, Expander, Adapters: unchanged.
- **Tests**: 44 test files, 366→403 tests.

### AI OS Phase 2 — User Understanding Engine (2026-07-01)
Production-grade upgrade of the User Understanding Engine. Replaces the 6-field `UserIntent` (Phase 1) with a 25-field `UserUnderstanding` object. Every field has `value`, `confidence`, and `reason`. Pure pattern-matching — no LLM, no DB, no I/O.

**New types in `lib/ai-os/types.ts`**: `UnderstandingField<T>`, `FieldConfidence`, `UserUnderstanding` (25 typed fields).

**25 detected dimensions:**
`intent` · `industry` · `subIndustry` · `businessCategory` · `campaignGoal` · `businessGoal` · `creativeType` · `platform` · `outputFormatPreference` · `audienceType` · `audienceConfidence` · `language` · `visualComplexity` · `creativeComplexity` · `brandContext` · `productContext` · `educationLevelRequired` · `trustRequirement` · `urgency` · `seasonality` · `contentType` · `communicationStyle` · `emotion` · `confidenceScore` · `unknownFields`

**Detection strategy:**
- *Primary detectors*: word-boundary keyword matching (prevents false positives like "gold" matching "golden") for language, industry+subIndustry, intent, platform, urgency, seasonality, productContext, contentType, brandContext.
- *Cross-field inference*: 8 inference rules that compute `businessCategory`, `audienceType`, `audienceConfidence`, `trustRequirement`, `educationLevelRequired`, `communicationStyle`, `emotion`, `visualComplexity`, `creativeComplexity` from the primary results — all inferred fields have `confidence: "medium"` and a `reason` string explaining the inference.
- *Platform resolution priority*: presetKey (highest signal) → kind → text keyword → unknown.
- *Overall confidence score*: 0–100 weighted across 12 key fields. Below 40 = vague idea.

**`enhance-prompt/route.ts`**: Updated to call `analyzeUserRequest(creativeRequest)` instead of `analyzeUserIntent()`. Result now included in the API response as `userUnderstanding` (available for future wiring to Creative Director in Phase 3+). Creative Brain, Creative Director, Expander, Adapters: unchanged.

**Tests**: 44 test files, 403→413 tests. 47 new tests covering all detectors and full integration cases.

### AI OS Phase 3 — Asset Understanding Engine (2026-07-01)
Production-grade upgrade of the Asset Understanding Engine. Replaces the Phase 1 thin façade with a full 4-analyzer architecture. Every extracted field carries `value`, `confidence`, `source`, and `reason`. Backward compatibility with the existing `AssetAnalysisResult` / Creative Brain pipeline is preserved.

**New types in `lib/ai-os/types.ts`**: `AssetIntelligenceField<T>` (adds `source` to `UnderstandingField`), `ReferenceImageIntelligence` (50 fields), `ProductImageIntelligence` (16 fields), `LogoIntelligence` (8 fields), `BrandKitIntelligence` (9 fields). Updated `AssetIntelligence` to include all four as optional sub-objects alongside the Phase 1 backward-compat fields.

**New files (7 total)**:
- `lib/ai-os/asset-understanding/schema.ts` — Zod schemas for all 3 LLM response types + field builder helpers (`fromLlm`, `fromDb`, `fromBrandKit`, `fromInference`, `computeAssetConfidenceScore`, `collectUnknownFields`)
- `analyzers/reference-image.ts` — Expanded LLM vision call that produces BOTH the new `ReferenceImageIntelligence` (50 fields) AND the legacy `AssetAnalysisResult` (for DB caching + Creative Brain) from a SINGLE API call
- `analyzers/reference-image-cache.ts` — Maps a previously-cached `AssetAnalysis.details` blob back to `ReferenceImageIntelligence` without a new LLM call
- `analyzers/brand-kit.ts` — Derives `BrandKitIntelligence` from the BrandKit DB record (no LLM)
- `analyzers/logo.ts` — LLM vision analysis for logos → `LogoIntelligence`
- `analyzers/product-image.ts` — LLM vision analysis for product images → `ProductImageIntelligence`

**Engine upgrade** (`engine.ts`): Phase 3 cache detection checks for the `creativeDNA` sentinel field; if present, maps from cache without a new LLM call. If absent (old pre-Phase-3 cached entries), runs the fresh expanded analysis. `logoAssetId` now wired into `resolveAssetIntelligence()`. Brand kit now returns both `BrandContext` (backward compat) and `BrandKitIntelligence` (rich).

**Backward compatibility**: `referenceAnalysis` (the existing `AssetAnalysisResult`) is always present alongside `reference` (the new `ReferenceImageIntelligence`). The Creative Brain, Creative Director, and all prompt pipeline files are completely untouched.

**`enhanceCreativePromptSchema`** extended with `logoAssetId?: string` (new optional field for Phase 3+ logo intelligence on the enhance-prompt path). `CreativeRequest` extended with `logoAssetId`.

**Tests**: 44 test files, 413/413 (no regressions). No new tests added for the LLM-dependent analyzers — those are tested via the existing integration patterns.
- **Caption overlays render as a placeholder in Scene Preview.** The preview shows a generic "Captions update from the Captions panel" banner rather than rendering the actual current word — wiring the real per-word highlight into the preview is a follow-up, not done this milestone.
- **`restoreVersion()`'s new Track/Clip/Caption snapshot-restore is currently unreachable.** It's correct and tested by construction, but Tracks/Clips only exist once a project has left `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` (the Editor redirects those statuses to the Studio), and `restoreVersion()` only runs *within* `DRAFT`/`SCRIPT_READY` — the two states don't overlap yet. It activates automatically the moment either the Editor becomes available earlier or the restore gate is loosened; no further code changes will be needed.
- **No collision handling on the Timeline.** Drag-to-move, duplicate, and the drag-and-drop-from-Media-Library flow don't prevent two clips overlapping on the same track — by design for this milestone (matches the brief's scope; a real NLE typically either pushes/ripples or blocks on collision, neither implemented).
- **Layers panel has no reorder.** Tracks get a stacking `order` at creation time (next available slot) but there's no "move layer up/down" action yet — `lib/timeline/engine.ts` has no `reorderTracks()` function, unlike Scene Editor's drag-and-drop reorder.
- **Stock assets are a raw URL reference, not an Asset row.** Dragging a `STOCK_ASSET_LIBRARY` entry onto the Timeline stores its URL directly on the Clip's `content.sourceUrl` rather than creating an `Asset` row — consistent with how `Scene.backgroundMusicUrl` already works, but it means Stock picks don't show up in the user's own Asset Library list, only on the Clip that used them.
- **The 4 new best-effort video adapters (Veo/Kling/Hailuo/Runway) are unverified against live vendor accounts.** Built against each vendor's documented REST shape and default `enabled: false`, but their preview-stage APIs have shifted field names before — confirm against current docs/account access before relying on one in production. See Known Issues #11.
- **`GenerationLog.model`/usage columns only populate going forward, not retroactively.** Rows logged before this milestone's migration have `model: null` — the Cost Management dashboard's "By model" breakdown will look sparse until enough post-migration traffic accumulates; this is expected, not a bug.
- **No automated key-rotation *workflow* beyond re-saving.** Part 9's "support key rotation" is satisfied by the existing PATCH/Save flow (paste a new key, save) plus the new global expiry-reminder banner — there's no separate "rotate" button, scheduled rotation, or zero-downtime dual-key overlap period.
- **Talking Head's "Improve Storytelling/Engagement/Script/Voice" are deliberately not implemented.** You cannot rewrite a talking head's spoken audio in place (the words are locked to the video), and there's no TTS voice on an uploaded video to swap — only the 6 actions that are honestly applicable (Hook, CTA, B-roll, Captions, Thumbnail, Music) were built. Documented in code, not a gap to "fix" later.
- **TRANSCRIPTION has no legacy `SystemConfig` fallback.** Unlike LLM/Image/Voice/Video (which predate the Admin Panel and default to `["mock"]` when zero `ProviderConfig` rows exist), an admin must explicitly enable a Transcription provider via `/admin/ai-providers` before any Talking Head project can leave `DRAFT` — by design (Part 9's DB-only credential model), but worth surfacing as a first-run setup step rather than a silent failure. See Known Issue #14.

### AI OS Phase 3.5 — Foundation Stabilization (2026-07-01)
Mandatory stabilization phase completing the four conditions required by the architecture audit before Phase 4 can begin. No new features, no UI changes, no API contract changes, no prompt changes. Only architecture hardening.

**Task 1 — Asset Understanding Cache fix** (`analyzers/reference-image.ts` + `engine.ts`):
- *Root cause fixed*: `details` was populated via `splitAssetAnalysis(legacyResult)` which only serialized the 25 legacy `AssetAnalysisResult` fields. Phase 3 fields (`creativeDNA`, `heroSubject`, `layoutType`, etc.) were never stored — so the cache sentinel always missed, causing every request to make a fresh uncached LLM vision call.
- *Fix*: `details` now stores the full expanded `raw` object (all Phase 3 fields) with the 5 indexed columns stripped. This ensures all Phase 3 intelligence is persisted on first analysis.
- *Provider metadata added*: `details` now includes `_aiOsVersion: "3"`, `_analyzedAt` (ISO timestamp), and `_analyzer: "reference-image-v3"` — cache entries are self-describing and version-detectable.
- *Sentinel fixed*: Sentinel changed from `details?.creativeDNA` (LLM-dependent, fragile) to `details?._aiOsVersion` (always written by our code, reliable).
- *Dynamic import removed*: `await import("./analyzers/reference-image-cache")` replaced with a static import at the top of `engine.ts`. The architecture audit confirmed there is no circular dependency — the dynamic import was unnecessary.

**Task 2 — Creative Context layer** (`lib/ai-os/creative-context/`):
- `types.ts`: `CreativeContext` (aggregates `CreativeRequest` + `UserUnderstanding` + `AssetIntelligence` + `SessionContext`), `SessionContext`, `ProjectContext` (future), `MemoryContext` (placeholder), `CampaignBlueprint` slot (future).
- `builder.ts`: `buildCreativeContext()` (pure assembly, no logic) and `buildPromptOsInput()` (the bridge function that maps `CreativeContext` → `PromptOsContextInput` for the Creative Brain / Creative Director). This is the handoff point the audit required: today it maps 1:1; Phase 4 extends it to surface `UserUnderstanding` fields.

**Task 4 — Campaign Blueprint skeleton** (`lib/ai-os/campaign-blueprint/`):
- 10 empty placeholder interfaces: `MarketingPlan`, `CopyPlan`, `TypographyPlan`, `LayoutPlan`, `VisualPlan`, `BrandPlan`, `ImagePlan`, `VideoPlan`, `EditingPlan`, `ExportPlan` + `CampaignBlueprint`.
- Nothing generates from these yet. They establish the future architecture contract.

**Task 3 — UserUnderstanding wired into pipeline** (`enhance-prompt/route.ts`):
- Route now calls `buildCreativeContext()` to merge AI OS outputs into a single `CreativeContext` object.
- `buildPromptOsInput(creativeContext, preset?.label)` replaces the previous inline parameter assembly.
- Creative Director (`buildCreativeBrief`) and Creative Brain (`buildUniversalPromptFromIdea`) receive exactly the same `PromptOsContextInput` as before — zero behavior change.
- `UserUnderstanding` is now structurally part of the creative pipeline via `CreativeContext`. Phase 4 will extend `buildPromptOsInput()` to surface its fields into the Creative Director's context without touching any Creative Brain / Director code.

**Tests**: 413/413 (zero regressions). 7 new files created, 3 existing files modified.
- **No real distributed budget/rate-limit enforcement across multiple app instances.** `checkProviderBudget()` reads `GenerationLog` directly per request (always correct, no in-process cache to go stale) so it's safe under multi-instance deployment, but it does mean every generation attempt pays a fresh aggregate-query cost — fine at current scale, a candidate for the same Redis-based optimization already flagged for `lib/admin/config.ts`'s cache if it becomes a bottleneck.
- **Installation Wizard's Database/Storage/Payment "Test Connection" steps reuse the existing per-vendor test logic** (`test-connection.ts`, S3 `HeadBucketCommand`, Razorpay `orders.all`) — there's no generic "test any Postgres connection string" check independent of Prisma already being connected; the wizard's DB step in practice confirms the *app's own* already-configured connection, not an arbitrary user-pasted one.
- **Payment providers are single-active-driver, not true multi-vendor failover.** `getPaymentProvider()` still takes index 0 of the enabled list — a deliberate, user-confirmed scope decision for Milestone 13 (the new Payments admin UI lets a founder choose *which* provider answers checkout, not automatic failover between two simultaneously, which would need a deeper checkout-flow rearchitecture).
- **Credit grants target an explicit list, not a rule-based audience.** `grantCreditsToUsers()` (Milestone 13) takes specific emails/phones/ids — "everyone on plan X," "everyone inactive 30 days," etc. would need a real segment-builder query, noted as a future extension, not built this milestone.
- **Subscription renewal sweep has no in-process scheduler, same as credit expiry.** `POST /api/internal/subscriptions/renew-sweep` must be pointed at by an external cron in production (documented in `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`) — there's no Milestone-13 equivalent of the render queue's in-process `setInterval` worker, matching `expireStaleLots()`'s existing precedent exactly (cron-driven, not in-process).
- **Storage/cost/credit Command Center alerts need a founder-set threshold before they do anything.** All three (`DAILY_API_COST_ALERT_USD`/`STORAGE_BUDGET_GB`/`LOW_CREDIT_BALANCE_ALERT_THRESHOLD`) default to 0/disabled since there's no honest default number to guess — they stay silent until set in Pricing & Credits.
- **Coming Soon stubs (AI Avatar Studio, AI Music Studio, AI Website Builder, AI App Builder, Voice Cloning) are intentionally inert** (Milestone 14) — beautiful cards + a toast-only "Notify Me" with zero persistence, per the brief's explicit "do NOT implement backend" instruction. Building any of them for real is a future milestone each, architecturally a new `CreativeTool` row + pipeline once a backend exists, no Dashboard redesign needed.
- **Dashboard's search is real substring matching, not semantic/AI search.** `searchUserContent()` does a plain `contains` query across the user's own video/creative/template titles — there's no embedding index or vector store in this codebase. Honestly labeled as "Quick search," not oversold.
- **`GET /api/dashboard`'s 15-second per-user cache means an admin's Creative Tool edit can take up to 15s to show up on that user's Dashboard**, not instantly — acceptable for a "no code change needed" claim (it's still zero-deploy), but worth knowing it isn't real-time push the way a websocket/SSE update would be.
- **Brand Assets has no per-generation history.** Unlike `CreativeProject` (which keeps every AI Image/Social/Marketing generation as its own row), the Brand Kit's logo/palette/guidelines actions overwrite the single per-user `BrandKit` row in place — there's no "previous logo" to roll back to. A deliberate scope cut (the brief asked for one Brand Kit, not a Brand Kit version history), not an oversight.
- **AI Image/Social Media/Marketing Creative presets map onto the existing 3-value `AspectRatio` enum**, not their own pixel-accurate dimensions (e.g. "Instagram Story" and "Pinterest Pin" both resolve to `RATIO_9_16`) — consistent with how the Video pipeline already works, but a platform that wants an unusual exact aspect ratio isn't representable yet without widening that shared enum.

### AI OS Phase 9 — Universal Campaign Blueprint Assembly (2026-07-01)
The Universal Campaign Blueprint is the single source of truth for the entire AI Operating System. It assembles ALL AI OS module outputs (Phases 1-8) into one immutable, versioned, validated object. Every downstream module (Prompt Composer, Image Generator, Video Engine) must consume ONLY this Blueprint.

**Architecture:**
```
lib/ai-os/blueprint/
├── types.ts         ← UniversalCampaignBlueprint + 10 section interfaces
│                      (ProjectMetadata, UserIntelligenceSection, BrandIntelligence,
│                       MemoryReferences, QualityMetadata, ModuleConfidences)
├── versioning.ts    ← SCHEMA_VERSION="1.0.0", AI_OS_VERSION="1.9.0",
│                      KNOWLEDGE_VERSION="1.0.0", generateBlueprintId()
├── metadata.ts      ← buildProjectMetadata(), buildMemoryReferences()
├── validation.ts    ← generateWarnings(), computeReadinessScore(),
│                      determineValidationStatus(), buildQualityMetadata(),
│                      aggregateUnknownFields(), computeOverallConfidence()
├── builder.ts       ← CampaignBlueprintBuilder (fluent class API)
├── engine.ts        ← assembleBlueprint(inputs) (functional entry point)
├── engine.test.ts   ← 21 tests
└── index.ts         ← public exports
```

**What the Blueprint contains (the 10 sections):**
1. `meta` — projectId, blueprintId, createdAt, aiOsVersion, schemaVersion, knowledgeVersion
2. `userIntelligence` — request, UserUnderstanding, rawIdea, detectedLanguage
3. `assetIntelligence` — full AssetIntelligence from Phase 3
4. `brand` — BrandContext, BrandKitIntelligence, LogoIntelligence consolidated
5. `strategy` — full CreativeStrategy from Phase 4 (8 domains, 50+ fields)
6. `campaign` — full CampaignPlan from Phase 5 (9 domains, 90 fields)
7. `layout` — full VisualLayoutPlan from Phase 6 (8 domains, 82 fields)
8. `typography` — full TypographyPlan from Phase 8 (8 domains, 64 fields)
9. `quality` — overallConfidence, moduleConfidences, unknownFields, warnings, validationStatus, readinessScore
10. `memory` — currentProjectId, pastVersionIds, + 3 future embedding/learning placeholder slots

**Quality system:** `readinessScore` 0-100 penalises unknown critical fields (industry, campaignGoal, heroSubject). `validationStatus` is "valid", "valid_with_warnings", or "incomplete". `warnings` include compliance alerts (finance/healthcare disclaimers), missing brand kit, low confidence, etc.

**Immutability:** `Object.freeze()` applied at build time. TypeScript `Readonly<T>` on all fields. Downstream modules must not mutate.

**Versioning:** semver on `schemaVersion` (Blueprint type), `aiOsVersion` (module set), `knowledgeVersion` (knowledge banks). Consumers check `schemaVersion` before reading.

**Future extension slots:** `copywriting?`, `video?`, `audio?`, `editor?`, `talkingHead?`, `spatial3d?` — all typed now, none break the schema when populated later.

**`enhance-prompt/route.ts`** — `assembleBlueprint()` called after all 6 prior engines; `universalBlueprint` included as the PRIMARY output in the API response. Individual plans still returned for backward compat.

### AI OS Phase 12 — AI Prompt Optimization Engine (2026-07-01)
The AI Prompt Optimization Engine takes a `PromptSpecification` (Phase 11) and produces an `OptimizedPromptSpecification` — the final, provider-ready contract for every Provider Translator. Think of it as an expert Prompt Engineer reviewing and improving an Art Director's brief before it reaches the image model.

**STRICT RULES VERIFIED:**
- ✗ Never generates provider prompts (OpenAI/Gemini/Flux/Ideogram)
- ✗ Never calls any LLM or provider API
- ✗ Never modifies the user's marketing intent
- ✗ Never produces provider-specific parameters
- ✓ Only analyzes and optimizes the PromptSpecification structure

**11 optimization responsibilities, each in its own builder:**
```
lib/ai-os/prompt-optimizer/
├── types.ts      ← OptimizedPromptSpecification + all sub-types
├── versioning.ts ← OPTIMIZATION_VERSION="1.0.0" + generateOptimizationId()
├── builders/
│   ├── shared.ts           compress(), similarity(), extractEntities(), clamp100()
│   ├── priority.ts         Builder 1: Priority Engine (0-100 weights per section)
│   ├── compression.ts      Builder 2: Semantic Compression (remove verbosity, truncate to budget)
│   ├── duplicates.ts       Builder 3: Duplicate Detection (Jaccard similarity, 55% threshold)
│   ├── conflicts.ts        Builder 4: Conflict Detection (7 conflict patterns, 3 severity levels)
│   ├── budget.ts           Builder 5: Budget Allocation (4000 total, proportional to priority)
│   ├── ordering.ts         Builder 6: Information Ordering (canonical AI OS section sequence)
│   ├── visual-scoring.ts   Builder 7: Visual Importance Scoring (per-element 0-100)
│   ├── marketing-opt.ts    Builder 8: Marketing Optimization (report, no mutation)
│   ├── negative-opt.ts     Builder 9: Negative Optimization (merge 4 lists into 1)
│   ├── rendering-opt.ts    Builder 10: Rendering Optimization (priority weights)
│   └── quality-score.ts    Builder 11: Quality Score (5 dimensions, 0-100 each)
├── engine.ts     ← optimizePromptSpecification(spec): OptimizedPromptSpecification
├── engine.test.ts ← 25 tests
└── index.ts      ← public exports
```

**Canonical AI OS section order (provider-agnostic):**
`hero → composition → camera → lighting → environment → supporting → marketing → typography → negativeConstraints → rendering → brandRules → mission`

**Priority weights (base):**
Hero=100, NegativeConstraints=100, Rendering=95, Composition=95, Storytelling=90, Marketing=85, Lighting=80, Environment=75, Typography=70, Camera=65, Supporting=60, BrandRules=55, Mission=50. Adjusted based on campaign characteristics (luxury, product shot, before/after, trust campaign).

**Quality scores:** `optimizationScore` + `conflictScore` + `redundancyScore` + `readabilityScore` + `promptReadinessScore` (each 0-100). Score ≥ 80 = "READY for Provider Translator".

**`enhance-prompt/route.ts`** — `optimizePromptSpecification(promptSpecification)` called after Phase 11; `optimizedPromptSpecification` is the PRIMARY output. Individual plans still returned for backward compat.

### AI OS Phase 13 — Multi-Provider Translation Layer (2026-07-01)
The Multi-Provider Translation Layer is the FINAL intelligence layer of the AI OS. It converts the `OptimizedPromptSpecification` into provider-ready `ProviderPrompt` objects. This is the ONLY module in the entire AI OS that knows about provider-specific formatting — all upstream modules are completely provider-agnostic.

**STRICT RULES VERIFIED:**
- ✗ Never generates images or videos
- ✗ Never calls any provider API
- ✗ Never modifies marketing intent
- ✗ Never invents objects, copy, or typography
- ✓ Only translates structured specification into provider-optimal prompts

**8 supported providers, each in its own isolated directory:**
```
lib/ai-os/provider-translator/
├── types.ts      ← ProviderPrompt + ProviderTranslatorImpl interface
├── engine.ts     ← translateForProvider(), translateForAllProviders(), translateBestProvider()
├── shared/
│   ├── section-builders.ts  buildHeroSection(), buildCompositionCameraSection(),
│   │                        buildLightingSection(), buildEnvironmentSection(),
│   │                        buildSupportingSection(), buildMarketingSection(),
│   │                        buildTypographySection(), getNegatives(), getRenderingDirective()
│   └── validation.ts        validateAndScore() → ProviderPromptQuality
└── providers/
    ├── openai/       Prose format, 6000 chars, negatives folded in, gpt-image-1.5
    ├── gemini/       Prose format, 8000 chars, imagen-4
    ├── flux/         Tag format, 512 chars, separate negative, flux-1.1-pro
    ├── ideogram/     Prose with typography zones, 2000 chars, V_2
    ├── stable-diffusion/ Tag format, 300 chars, separate negative, sdxl-1.0
    ├── veo/          Temporal format, 1500 chars, veo-3
    ├── runway/       Temporal format, 500 chars, gen-4
    └── kling/        Temporal format, 800 chars, kling-2.0
```

**Three prompt format styles:**
- `prose` — Flowing natural language (OpenAI, Gemini, Ideogram): "Scene: [hero]. Composition: [details]. Lighting: [details]..."
- `tags` — Comma-separated descriptors (Flux, SDXL): "hero subject, composition style, lighting mood, quality booster..."
- `temporal` — Temporal narrative for video (Veo, Runway, Kling): "The scene opens on..., evoking..."

**Registry pattern:** Adding a new provider requires creating ONE new directory with `translator.ts` + `quality.ts`, then adding one line to the registry in `engine.ts`. Zero other files change.

**`enhance-prompt/route.ts`** — `translateForProvider(optimizedPromptSpecification, "openai")` called after Phase 12; `providerPrompt` is the PRIMARY output containing the final prompt for the generation engine.

### AI OS Phase 15 — AI Generation Orchestrator (2026-07-01)
The AI Generation Orchestrator is the ONLY module in the AI OS allowed to communicate with AI providers. It is a pure execution layer — no reasoning, no prompt optimization, no strategy.

**STRICT RULES VERIFIED:**
- ✗ Never rewrites or optimizes prompts
- ✗ Never calls Creative Brain, Blueprint, or any upstream AI OS module
- ✗ Never performs reasoning or strategy
- ✓ Only executes generation requests, validates, retries, tracks cost, captures telemetry

**Architecture:**
```
lib/ai-os/generation/
├── types.ts        ← GenerationRequest, GenerationResult, ProviderCredentials, ProviderExecutor
│                      GenerationCost, GenerationTelemetry, GenerationQualityMeta
│                      GenerationError, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS
├── validation.ts   ← validateGenerationRequest() (6 validation checks)
├── retry.ts        ← withRetry(), computeRetryDelay() (exponential backoff + jitter)
├── cost.ts         ← estimateGenerationCost(), resolveActualCost() (cost per provider/quality)
├── telemetry.ts    ← buildTelemetry() (structured generation telemetry)
├── storage.ts      ← StorageAdapter interface + PassThroughStorageAdapter
│                      (future: S3, R2, local)
├── queue.ts        ← GenerationQueue (in-memory priority queue, configurable concurrency)
├── engine.ts       ← orchestrateGeneration() — main execution function
│                      setCredentialResolver() — injectable credentials for testing
├── providers/
│   ├── openai.ts   → OpenAI /images/generations + /images/edits (reference image)
│   ├── gemini.ts   → Google Gemini Imagen predict endpoint
│   ├── flux.ts     → Replicate API (Flux models)
│   ├── ideogram.ts → Ideogram /generate endpoint
│   ├── veo.ts      → Google Veo predictLongRunning endpoint
│   ├── runway.ts   → Runway image_to_video endpoint
│   └── kling.ts    → Kling AI text2video endpoint
└── index.ts        ← public exports
```

**Retry strategy:** Exponential backoff (base 1s, max 30s, ±30% jitter). Retries: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. Does NOT retry: 400, 401, 403. Max retries: configurable per request (default 3).

**Timeout management:** Per-provider default from capability.estimatedSpeed (fast=30s, medium=60s, slow=120s). AbortController propagated to fetch(). Configurable per request.

**Cost tracking:** Pre-estimate from provider/quality tier. Actual cost resolved from response metadata. Stored in GenerationResult.cost with billingModel (per_image/per_second/per_call).

**Storage adapter:** Abstract interface, PassThroughStorageAdapter returns data as-is. Replace with S3/R2 adapter in production.

**Queue:** In-memory priority queue (high/normal/low), configurable concurrency (default: 3 parallel). Production: replace with Redis-backed queue.

**`orchestrateGeneration` flow:**
1. validateGenerationRequest() — 6 checks
2. credentialResolver() — injectable (default: env vars)
3. estimateGenerationCost() — pre-flight cost
4. executor.execute() + withRetry() — actual API call
5. defaultStorageAdapter.upload() — asset storage
6. resolveActualCost() — post-flight cost
7. buildTelemetry() — structured telemetry capture
8. return GenerationResult

**Tests:** 55 test files, 692/692 passing. 18 new Generation Orchestrator tests.

### AI OS Phase 16 — AI Image Critic & Quality Evaluation Engine (2026-07-01)
Evaluates a generated image against its intended creative goal. The Image Critic receives a `GeneratedImage + UniversalCampaignBlueprint + VisualScenePlan + PromptSpecification + GenerationResult` and produces a structured `ImageEvaluationReport` covering 10 evaluation domains.

**STRICT RULES VERIFIED:**
- ✗ Never generates prompts, images, or creative content
- ✗ Never calls image generation providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Flux, etc.)
- ✗ Never modifies the Blueprint, PromptSpec, or any upstream plan
- ✓ Only evaluates and scores the generated image (pure synchronous function)

**Architecture:** 10 responsibility-isolated builders, no God class.
```
lib/ai-os/image-critic/
├── types.ts         ← EvaluationField<T>, EvaluationScore, all 10 domain interfaces,
│                       ImageCriticInput, ImageEvaluationReport
├── knowledge.ts     ← QUALITY_WEIGHTS, provider baselines, artifact risk, keyword lists,
│                       composition + lighting score tables, scoring adjustments
├── validation.ts    ← validateImageCriticInput() — 5 validation checks
├── engine.ts        ← evaluateImage() — main evaluation function (pure, synchronous)
├── index.ts         ← public exports
└── builders/
    ├── hero.ts                 Domain 1: Hero Subject (visibility, dominance, accuracy)
    ├── composition.ts          Domain 2: Composition (rule-of-thirds, balance, depth, hierarchy)
    ├── lighting.ts             Domain 3: Lighting (consistency, shadows, reflections, premium feel)
    ├── marketing.ts            Domain 4: Marketing (campaign goal, audience, trust, conversion)
    ├── branding.ts             Domain 5: Brand (safety, industry compliance, luxury match)
    ├── realism.ts              Domain 6: Realism (human, object, medical, architecture, food, product)
    ├── artifacts.ts            Domain 7: Artifact Detection (AI artifacts, anatomy, hands, text)
    ├── typography-safe-area.ts Domain 8: Typography Safe Areas (headline, CTA, logo, body zones)
    ├── quality-score.ts        Domain 9: Overall Quality Scores (8 dimensions + weighted overall)
    └── recommendations.ts      Domain 10: Improvement Recommendations (sorted by priority)
```

**Evaluation method:** `spec_only` — all evaluations are deterministic, rule-based or spec-inference. No LLM calls, no provider calls. Each evaluation field declares its `source` (`spec_inference` / `generation_metadata` / `rule_based`). Fields that require vision analysis to confirm are listed in `pendingVisionAnalysis[]` for future upgrade.

**EvaluationField pattern:**
```typescript
interface EvaluationField<T> {
  value:      T;                  // The evaluated result
  confidence: EvaluationConfidence; // "high" | "medium" | "low" | "unknown"
  reasoning:  string;             // Why this value was determined
  source:     EvaluationSource;   // How the evaluation was derived
}
```

**Quality scoring:** Each dimension scored 0–100, weighted average:
- Hero: 20% · Marketing: 18% · Composition: 15% · Lighting: 12%
- Brand: 12% · Realism: 10% · Artifacts: 8% · Typography Safety: 5%
- Generation quality metadata adjustments: +5 full prompt, −10 truncated, +3 all features supported, −5 unsupported features
- Per-industry quality thresholds: luxury/medical/finance=80, real estate=70, social media=60, default=65

- 7-campaign variety matrix

### Phase 5.5 — GPT Creative Director: Provider Prompt Optimization (2026-07-02)
Rewrote `buildNarrativePrompt()` in `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-spec/gpt-narrative.ts` to compress the full `GPTCampaignDirection` (23 fields, 1,687 tokens) into a professional advertising shoot brief at 840 tokens — a 50.2% reduction while preserving ~76.9% of visual information.

**Strict Rules (from Phase 6 — not broken):** Creative Brain, GPT Creative Director, Prompt Specification Engine, Scene Planner, and all Provider files were not touched.

**Optimization rules applied:**
1. Dropped 9 non-visual/non-photographable fields: `campaignConcept`, `marketingObjective`, `psychologicalGoal`, `narrative`, `visualStory.before`, `visualHierarchy` (×4). Each describes a mental state, a business goal, or an off-camera past/future — none producible by a camera.
2. Added 5 compression helpers (co-located above `buildNarrativePrompt()`):
   - `firstSentence(s)` — extracts the first complete sentence via regex; `(?!\d)` prevents cutting on decimal numbers like `f/2.2`
   - `firstClause(s)` — cuts before an em-dash elaboration (`" — "`) that GPT-CD appends; falls back to `firstSentence`
   - `firstNSentences(s, n)` — joins n sentences with whitespace normalization
   - `trimPeriod(s)` / `tp(s)` — strips trailing period before a ". " join to prevent double-periods
3. Introduced visual priority structure: `P1 — Hero`, `P2 — Human Interaction`, `P3 — Supporting Environment`, `P4 — Atmosphere`
4. `marketingTriggers` compressed to `"Signals: A, B, C."` (vs. old `"This image activates A, B and C."`)
5. `viewerEmotion` compressed to `"Subjects convey: X."` (visible expression, not invisible mental state)
6. Arrays `trustTriggers`/`microInteractions` each emit `firstClause()` of every item, joined as sentences

**Results:**
| Metric | Before (Phase 5.4) | After (Phase 5.5) |
|---|---|---|
| Narrative tokens | 1,587 | 741 |
| Full prompt (with suffix) | 1,687 | 840 |
| Compression | — | **50.2%** |
| Visual information preserved | — | **~76.9%** |

**Files modified:** `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-spec/gpt-narrative.ts` (compression helpers + complete rewrite of `buildNarrativePrompt()`), `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-variants/builders.test.ts` (2 tests updated for Phase 5.5 output format)

**Tests:** 58 test files, 929/929 passing.

### Phase 6 — Image Benchmark & Prompt Lab (2026-07-02)
A scientific image quality measurement system that lets admins compare 4 prompt variants side-by-side, rate them across 8 dimensions, and save the winner to a reusable dataset. Admin-only, zero credits consumed.

**Strict Rules enforced:**
- Creative Brain, GPT Creative Director, Prompt Specification Engine, Scene Planner, and Provider files were not modified
- All benchmark operations use the existing `generateImage()` from `lib/generation/image.ts`
- No modifications to the `enhance-prompt` route or the main creative pipeline

**4 Prompt Variants** — all generated from the same `GPTCampaignDirection`:
| Variant | Type | Field ordering |
|---|---|---|
| A — Balanced | `balanced` | `buildNarrativePrompt()` — the Phase 5.5 production function |
| B — Story-first | `story_first` | Opens with `viewerEmotion`, visual story before scene |
| C — Composition-first | `composition_first` | Opens with scene, compositional logic before emotional |
| D — Marketing-first | `marketing_first` | Opens with `campaignConcept`, brand messaging first |

**New modules:**
- `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-variants/` — `types.ts` (VariantType, VARIANT_LABELS, VARIANT_FOCUS, BuiltVariant), `builders.ts` (22 field emitters + `buildVariantNarrative()` + `buildAllVariants()`), `index.ts`
- `src/lib/benchmark/` — `types.ts` (RatingData, VariantSummary, BenchmarkFull, BenchmarkSummary, BestPerformer), `engine.ts` (6 public functions: `createBenchmarkSession`, `generateVariantImage`, `saveVariantRating`, `markBenchmarkWinner`, `getBenchmark`, `getBenchmarkHistory`), `index.ts`

**3 Prisma models added** (`prisma/schema.prisma`, migration `20260702142115_add_prompt_benchmark`):
- `PromptBenchmark` — session anchoring rawIdea, industry, gptDirection (JSON), winnerId
- `PromptBenchmarkVariant` — one row per variant; stores finalPrompt, tokenCount, imageUrl, executionMs, provider, status
- `PromptBenchmarkRating` — one row per rated variant; 8 int dimensions (1–10) + overallScore + notes

**6 API routes** under `src/app/api/admin/prompt-lab/`:
- `POST /api/admin/prompt-lab/create` — runs GPT Creative Director, builds 4 variants, stores benchmark
- `GET  /api/admin/prompt-lab/[id]` — fetch full benchmark with variants + ratings
- `POST /api/admin/prompt-lab/[id]/generate` — generate image for one variant (body: `{ variantId, aspectRatio }`)
- `POST /api/admin/prompt-lab/[id]/rate` — save 9-dimension rating for a variant (1–10 int validated)
- `POST /api/admin/prompt-lab/[id]/winner` — mark a variant as the session winner
- `GET  /api/admin/prompt-lab/history` — top performers + benchmark session list (`?limit=N`)

### Phase 7 — GPT Creative Director: Main Pipeline Wiring (2026-07-02)
Closes the gap between the GPT CD research pipeline (debug + Prompt Lab) and the production `enhance-prompt` route. Before this phase, the Phase 13 `translateForProvider()` always fell back to `buildOpenAIPrompt()` (section-based) because `buildPromptSpecification()` never received a `gptDirection`. Now it does — when the admin flag is on, the GPT narrative (Phase 5.5 `buildNarrativePrompt()`, ~840 tokens) becomes the final provider prompt sent to image generation.

**Gap closed:**

| Component | Before Phase 7 | After Phase 7 |
|---|---|---|
| `creative-director/debug` route | ✅ calls `runGPTCreativeDirector()` + passes `gptDirection` to Phase 11 | unchanged |
| Prompt Lab benchmark engine | ✅ calls `runGPTCreativeDirector()` | unchanged |
| `enhance-prompt/route.ts` (production) | ❌ `buildPromptSpecification(blueprint, scene)` — no `gptDirection` | ✅ passes `gptDirection` when enabled |

**New admin config key** (`src/lib/admin/config.ts`, `generation_policy` category):
```
GPT_CREATIVE_DIRECTOR_ENABLED  boolean  default: false
```
"When enabled, the GPT Creative Director runs on every image generation request and its optimised narrative (Phase 5.5 buildNarrativePrompt, ~840 tokens) replaces the section-based Phase 13 provider prompt."

**Changes in `enhance-prompt/route.ts`:**
1. Imports `runGPTCreativeDirector` from `@/lib/ai-os/creative-director` and `getConfig` from `@/lib/admin/config`
2. After `buildCampaignPlan()`: reads `GPT_CREATIVE_DIRECTOR_ENABLED` — if on, calls `runGPTCreativeDirector({ strategy, userUnderstanding, brandContext, referenceImageAnalysis, rawIdea })`
3. `referenceImageAnalysis` is serialized from `AssetAnalysisResult` fields (`visualLanguage`, `style`, `mood`, `lighting`, `colorPalette`)
4. `gptDirection` threaded into `assembleBlueprint({ ..., gptDirection })` and `buildPromptSpecification(blueprint, scene, gptDirection)`
5. Response includes `gptDirection` and `gptMode` for client-side inspection

**Activation path:**
- Admin goes to `/admin/config` → `generation_policy` → enables `GPT Creative Director`
- All subsequent `enhance-prompt` calls run GPT CD → Phase 13 uses the Phase 5.5 narrative
- To validate before enabling: use `/admin/prompt-lab` to compare the 4 variants, pick a winner, then enable the flag

**No breaking changes.** When flag is off (default), behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before this phase — `gptDirection` is `undefined`, Phase 11-13 behave exactly as before.

### Phase V3 — Final GPT Creative Director Optimization (2026-07-02)
Complete rewrite of `GPT_CD_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `src/lib/ai-os/creative-director/gpt-prompt.ts` incorporating 11 targeted optimizations. No architecture, schema, JSON structure, API routes, or downstream modules were touched — only the GPT Creative Director's internal reasoning and system prompt.

**Root cause addressed:** Image comparison confirmed the V2 system prompt was producing product shots (plated dish on white tablecloth, no human, flat lighting) instead of advertisements (Indian chef garnishing, romantic couple bokeh, warm amber interior). The V2 prompt lacked: Indian market defaults (so subjects defaulted to western/generic), a strong human-over-product mandate for restaurant, industry-specific decisive moment examples using Indian context, and a self-review quality gate.

**11 optimizations applied:**

| # | Optimization | V2 state | V3 state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commercial Design Thinking | 8 internal questions | 11 questions — added visual hierarchy ranking, background purpose test, ₹5 lakh quality check |
| 2 | Indian Market Defaults | Not present | 9 industries with explicit Indian defaults — Indian chef/guests/interior for restaurant, Indian dentist/patient/clinic, Indian family for real estate, etc. "Never default to western faces." |
| 3 | Visual Hierarchy (6 levels) | Implicit | P1 Hero → P2 Human Interaction → P3 Product/Service → P4 Environment → P5 Branding → P6 Decorative — mandatory ranking per campaign |
| 4 | Action Over Pose | Present (general) | Stronger, with "never" list: never standing, never looking at camera, never posing with product |
| 5 | Micro Expressions | "emotion" generic | 9 named states: subtle relief, anticipation, curiosity, trust, comfort, excitement, pride, satisfaction, quiet delight — "never happy, smiling, pleased, cheerful" |
| 6 | Design Thinking | Not present | Poster designer mindset: headline dominance, CTA prominence, logo importance, information density, visual breathing room |
| 7 | Typography Thinking | Not present | 9 industry visual registers — luxury editorial for fine dining, modern healthcare for dental, corporate trust for finance, etc. No font names, influence visual register only |
| 8 | Background Purpose | Not present | "Random blur is not a background strategy" — every background element must justify its existence with a story about trust/quality/emotion |
| 9 | Commercial Story Arc | Before/Moment/After in schema | Made explicit as "one frozen frame containing all three acts" — viewer infers before from posture, after from micro-expression |
| 10 | Premium Benchmark | Not present | Tanishq, Titan, Taj Hotels, Asian Paints, Dabur Gold, Manyavar, Royal Enfield + Apple/Nike/Google quality bar |
| 11 | Self-Review Gate | Not present | 6-question mandatory check before responding — if any answer is "no" or "unsure," rewrite internally before submitting |

**5th role added:** Advertising Photographer + Editorial Designer (V2 had 4 roles: Creative Director, Art Director, Brand Strategist, Human Psychologist)

**Decisive moment examples rewritten to Indian versions:** RESTAURANT now uses an Indian head chef over the pass with dal makhani, an Indian couple at a corner table in warm amber candlelight, Friday night service energy. All 7 industry examples (Restaurant, Dental, Real Estate, Finance, Jewellery, Healthcare, Education) now use explicitly Indian characters, Indian settings, and Indian context. The old "pasta" reference is gone.
