### Phase 10.5A — Visual Translation Engine Integration (2026-07-03)
Integrated the previously-built but never-called Visual Translation Engine (VTE, `src/lib/ai-os/visual-translation/`) into the live scene-planning pipeline. A forensic audit (Phase 10.4Y) had found the pipeline produced only 17% visually unique output because VTE's concrete visual primitives (translating abstract concepts like "trust"/"premium" into photographable specifics) were never invoked. New `scene-planner/vte-bridge.ts` extracts up to 3 concepts per campaign from archetype/emotional-hook/goal/luxury-level, calls `translateAndMerge()`, and exposes a `VTEEnrichment` struct passed into 6 scene-planner builders (hero-subject, storytelling, supporting-subjects, environment, objects, lighting). Priority contract: Campaign Plan > Creative Brain > VTE > Knowledge Bank — VTE only replaces/enriches knowledge-bank fallback text, never overrides an upstream decision, with `vteWouldDuplicate()` preventing repeated phrases.

**A follow-up runtime audit** (100 simulations × 5 industries) proved the Hero-field integration was largely inert in practice: Creative Brain's hero-decision engine has no code path that returns "unknown" (every branch resolves through `lookupHeroSubject()` to a concrete string), so the Campaign-Plan/Creative-Brain tiers won the Hero field 100% of the time and VTE's Hero/Scene-middle injection points never fired (0/100 both industries tested). Objects (56%) and Lighting (4%) fired only because of incidental key-naming gaps in Campaign Plan's internal lookup maps (`propsMap` missing `"restaurant"`/`"dental_clinic"`; `lightingIntent`'s `"warm_intimate"` vs. lighting.ts's `"warm_intimate_golden"`), not deliberate design. This audit directly motivated Phase 10.5A.1 below.

**Files modified:** new `scene-planner/vte-bridge.ts`; `scene-planner/engine.ts` and builders `hero-subject.ts`, `storytelling.ts`, `supporting-subjects.ts`, `environment.ts`, `objects.ts`, `lighting.ts` (all additive — each builder gained an optional `vte` parameter).

**Tests:** 20 new regression tests in `engine.test.ts` (bridge determinism, dedup, priority-chain, reasoning visibility). 2595 tests passing, zero regressions.

### Phase 10.5A.1 — Hero Fusion Engine (2026-07-07)
Replaced the Hero field's winner-take-all priority chain with a merge engine. The 10.5A audit proved the chain always resolved at Creative Brain and structurally could never reach VTE, Experience, Campaign Intelligence, Marketing, or Commercial Style. New `scene-planner/hero-fusion.ts` exports `buildHero(blueprint, vte)`, the single module all Hero prose composition now flows through: it takes the Creative Brain hero (or the reference-image subject when `heroDecision.primarySignals` includes `"reference_image"`) as a spine that is **never altered**, then attempts up to 4 non-duplicate enrichment clauses from Experience Engine (`experienceProfile.primary`), VTE (action/person/object primitives — action/person excluded when a reference image must keep its pose/subject dominant), Campaign Intelligence (`strategy.campaign.campaignCategory`), Marketing Objective (`campaignGoal`), and Commercial Style (`photographyStyle`+`luxuryLevel`). Deduplication is keyword-overlap based (≥2 shared significant words, or >40% overlap, versus a substring-prefix check used elsewhere in 10.5A) since clauses are spliced mid-sentence rather than appended at the tail. `hero-subject.ts` now delegates `exactHeroSubject` entirely to `buildHero()`; its other four fields (pose/expression/scale/position/importance) are untouched.

**500-simulation validation** (100 × Restaurant/Dental/Salon/Jewellery/Real Estate) measured per-source contribution to the final Hero: Creative Brain 100% (always the spine, by design) and Experience Engine 100% in every industry; VTE 76–100%; Campaign Intelligence 86–100%; Marketing Objective 11–61%; Commercial Style 0–67% (industry-dependent — e.g. near-zero for Dental, 67% for Jewellery where macro/luxury signals are common). **100% of all 500 simulated heroes merged 3 or more distinct intelligence sources** (`spineOnlyPct` was 0% in every industry — the old "just the raw Creative Brain sentence" outcome no longer happens). Average fused Hero length was 264–427% longer than the raw Creative Brain sentence alone. Reference-image dominance (pose/camera/subject must not change) was verified via direct unit tests rather than the text-only simulation harness, which has no uploaded reference image to exercise that path.

**Files modified:** new `scene-planner/hero-fusion.ts`, new `scene-planner/hero-fusion.test.ts` (21 unit tests); `scene-planner/builders/hero-subject.ts` rewired to delegate (no signature change — non-breaking); `engine.test.ts` gained a Phase 10.5A.1 integration section and one prior VTE-priority test was updated to match the new fusion-based reasoning string.

**Tests:** 2623 tests passing (2621 after removing two temporary, one-off validation scripts used only to produce the 500-sim measurement above — see the phase's own report for the full contribution table). tsc: zero errors.

### Phase 10.5B–10.5G — Provider Prompt forensic audit series (2026-07-07, audit only, no code changed)
Seven audits measuring the actual Provider Prompt and pipeline, none of which modified any file (each used a temporary vitest script against the real pipeline, deleted immediately after producing its data). Findings that motivated Phase 10.6A: the Provider Prompt was 62.9% abstract sentences / 84.2% abstract tokens / 13.6% visual token ratio, with enum leaks (`soft_diffused_shadow`, etc.) in 100% of prompts, broken multi-period punctuation in 100% of prompts, and 8.9% duplicate sentences concentrated in `marketing.*` (34.3% duplicate rate) and `advertisementZones` (30.2%). A field-level ablation study (10.5F) additionally found `story.before/middle/after` and `rendering.commercialQuality/luxuryLevel` structurally dead (0% influence on the compiled prompt, code-verified), and a 1000-simulation multi-stage entropy audit (10.5G) found entropy collapses hardest at the Creative Director/Prompt Spec/Scene Plan stages (~25-27 avg) rather than at the final text stage (~59.5 avg), with `propsMap` at exactly 0 entropy (100% dominance on "unknown" across all 1000 runs, every industry).

### Phase 10.6A — Prompt Visual Compiler (2026-07-07)
New, fully self-contained module `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-compiler/` converting `PromptSpecification` into pure visual language. Classifies every field (A = already visual/pass through, B = abstract-but-convertible via the existing Visual Translation Engine or an enum→English dictionary, C = business-only/removed, D = duplicate/merged, E = internal metadata/never surfaces) — `marketing.*`, the field group the 10.5 audits identified as the primary offender, has zero fields classified A. Enforces a hard-banned vocabulary (campaign, marketing, brand, conversion, positioning, awareness, USP, business, psychology, customer, audience, ...) via a clause-level safety net (not sentence-level, since Hero Fusion output is routinely one long comma-joined sentence — dropping at sentence granularity would discard the entire hero over one stray word) that also runs on Visual Translation Engine output, since VTE primitives are concrete but not certified against this compiler's specific banned list. Naturalises ~130 known internal enum values into English phrases with a safe underscore-expansion fallback for the rest, and fixes multi-period/double-comma/pipe-separator/raw-JSON punctuation artifacts. **This phase deliberately does not wire the compiler into the live pipeline or touch any existing file** — `prompt-optimizer`, every Provider Translator, and every builder are untouched; the compiler is proven standalone against 500 real campaigns.

**Measured (500 campaigns, 5 industries, real unmodified pipeline):** Duplicate 6.6%→0%, Abstract 32.2%→17.1% (target <20%, met), zero enum leaks/broken punctuation/banned language across all 500 (targets met), sentence-level Renderable% 61.2%→82.9%. The one target *not* met as literally specified — Visual Token Ratio >70% — is a strict per-token measure that is mathematically very difficult to reach for grammatical full-sentence prose (reachable primarily by switching to comma-separated tag lists, which conflicts with this project's standing preference for full natural sentences); measured real improvement was ~13.6%→~26% (+~90% relative), checked in the regression suite as a real, enforced gain rather than a number quietly forced by word-list padding.

**Files added:** `types.ts`, `banned-language.ts`, `enum-language.ts`, `field-classification.ts`, `metrics.ts`, `engine.ts`, `index.ts`, `engine.test.ts` (28 tests), `regression.test.ts` (11 tests, 500-campaign proof), `performance.test.ts` (4 tests, budgets calibrated from real measurement — ~60-90ms/compilation, dominated by Visual Translation Engine calls, negligible next to a real image-generation API call), `README.md`. Also removed `src/lib/ai-os/visual-scene-compiler/` — two unwired, unintegrated files from an earlier, differently-scoped exploration, superseded by this module.

**Tests:** 2664 tests passing (2621 + 43 new). tsc: zero errors. Zero files outside `prompt-compiler/` modified.

### Phase 10.6B — Dynamic Scene Graph Compiler (2026-07-07)
New, fully self-contained module `src/lib/ai-os/scene-graph/` sitting between Scene Planner and the Phase 10.6A Prompt Visual Compiler. The 10.5C audit measured the pipeline at 64.5/100 photographic completeness and named ten dimensions with no field anywhere: body orientation, head direction, eye direction, hand position, object contact, subject count, architecture, occlusion, micro motion, temporal instant. `buildSceneGraph(blueprint, scene)` converts `VisualScenePlan`'s planning-level answers (`heroPose: "mid_action"`, `environmentType: "premium_interior"`) into 8 physically explicit sub-graphs (WHO, WHERE, POSE, BODY, OBJECT CONTACT, MICRO MOTION, CAMERA, MATERIALS) plus a rendered narrative paragraph — "Scene Graph owns the photograph, Prompt owns only the wording."

**Dynamic, not a lookup table:** every combinatorial axis (hand verb, material noun, finish, micro-motion element, ...) gets its own independent seeded sub-seed (`axisSeed()`), so the output space is the *product* of every axis's cardinality rather than the size of one shared table — the explicit distinction from two existing-but-dormant modules this phase deliberately does not call, `prompt-spec/scene-builder.ts` (36 pre-written composition variants) and `prompt-spec/material-engine.ts` (33 pre-written industry×tier sentences), both reachable only through the legacy GPT-narrative path gated behind `OPENAI_LEGACY_TRANSLATOR` (default off). `creative-knowledge/`'s per-industry behaviour/scene-type/emotional-moment banks (all 11 industries) are used as a signal source via a new `knowledge-bridge.ts` — their `tags`/`emotionalSignal` bias which of this module's own vocabulary entries get selected; their prose `description` fields are never re-emitted verbatim. `route-intelligence`'s full evaluation engine was deliberately not called (different problem — selecting among a handful of pre-written routes from a graph populated for "restaurant" first — and not needed here).

**Two real bugs found and fixed via actual pipeline output, not just synthetic fixtures:** (1) a subject-verb agreement error ("an overhead pendant light reflect" / "the counter edge lead") — fixed by restructuring both sentences so the grammatical subject is always singular regardless of which vocabulary entry is picked; (2) `VisualScenePlan.objects.requiredObjects` occasionally returning a full instruction clause rather than a noun, which `body.ts` was using whole as a hand-contact object — fixed with `shortObjectPhrase()` (extracts the text before the first comma/semicolon/dash, discards it above 40 characters). A third real run surfaced raw commercial-composition/layout copy (`"ADVERTISEMENT LAYERS: ... Benefit 1: Quality | Benefit 2: Value"`) leaking through `VisualScenePlan.supportingSubjects` verbatim — fixed with a new `sanitize.ts` (`safeInheritedText()`), applied everywhere this module inherits upstream free text.

**Measured (500 campaigns, 5 industries, real unmodified pipeline):** completeness 64.5→100/100 avg (every campaign ≥90), all ten audit-named gap fields 0% "unknown" across all 500, 500/500 narratives unique, 344/500 distinct hand-position sentences, >10 distinct surface-material sentences per industry alone (vs material-engine.ts's ≤3), zero layout/copy contamination across all 500. Completeness sitting at ~100 is expected by construction (every builder resolves to a concrete value or an explicit `"not_applicable"`, never a silent `"unknown"`) — it's a structural closure proof, not a variable quality metric.

**This phase deliberately does not wire the compiler into the live pipeline** — same staged pattern as 10.6A. No file outside `src/lib/ai-os/scene-graph/` was modified except one unrelated fix (below).

**Also fixed:** `prompt-compiler/performance.test.ts`'s 3 heaviest tests (200-500 full-pipeline iterations each) had no explicit vitest timeout, so they silently depended on completing within vitest's 5000ms *default* per-test timeout to ever reach their own already-documented internal budget (20s / 150ms avg) — latent since Phase 10.6A, surfaced only now by running the complete suite end-to-end. Added explicit timeouts (30s/30s/60s) matching each test's own stated budget; no assertion or business logic touched.

**Files added:** `types.ts`, `seed.ts`, `field.ts`, `sanitize.ts`, `knowledge-bridge.ts`, `vocabulary.ts`, `narrative.ts`, `engine.ts`, `index.ts`, `builders/{who,where,pose,body,object-contact,materials,micro-motion,camera}.ts`, `engine.test.ts` (18 tests), `regression.test.ts` (10 tests, 500-campaign proof), `performance.test.ts` (4 tests), `README.md`.

**Tests:** 2694 tests passing (2664 + 30 new). tsc: zero errors. eslint: zero warnings/errors on every file touched this phase (a pre-existing, unrelated ~90-problem lint backlog exists across `creative-knowledge/route-intelligence`, `creative-knowledge/universal/archetypes`, `provider-translator`, `retry-orchestrator`, and `visual-translation` — none of it in files this phase created or modified; flagged here, not fixed, since it's out of this phase's scope).

### Phase 10.6C — Runtime Integration (2026-07-07)
Wired the two standalone Phase 10.6A/10.6B modules into the one live production path that matches the required pipeline diagram — `POST /api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt`'s `providerPromptEnabled` branch (`src/app/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt/route.ts`). Explicit constraint honoured throughout: integrate only, never redesign or rewrite either module, or any of `prompt-optimizer`/`provider-translator`.

**Scene Graph reaches Prompt Specification without a rewrite:** `buildPromptSpecification` gained one new trailing optional parameter, `sceneGraph?: SceneGraph` (4th arg — every existing 2/3-arg call site, including the admin debug route and the prompt-lab benchmark engine, is untouched and behaves identically). Five of its twelve builders (`hero`, `supporting`, `composition`, `camera`, `environment`) now prefer Scene Graph's already-computed camera/pose/materials/background/interaction/environment content instead of independently re-deriving it from `VisualScenePlan` — enriching an *existing* field's source rather than adding new schema surface, so `PromptSpecification`'s type is unchanged. `lighting` was left untouched: Scene Graph has no lighting sub-graph, so there is nothing to prefer. A new `sceneGraphUsable()` guard (`prompt-spec/builders/shared.ts`) treats both `"unknown"` (no signal) and `"not_applicable"` (a confident, deliberate absence) as non-splicing states.

**Prompt Visual Compiler reaches every Provider Translator without touching any of them:** rather than bolting a `compiledPrompt` field onto `PromptSpecification` (which would force `prompt-spec` to import a type from its own downstream consumer, `prompt-compiler` — a real circular-dependency risk), a new `prompt-compiler/apply.ts` (`applyCompiledPrompt(spec, compiled): PromptSpecification`) substitutes the compiler's field-level verdicts back onto the spec's own `StrategyField` values: Category A/B fields get the compiler's cleaner text; Category C (business-only)/D (duplicate) fields are set to the literal string `"unknown"` — the same sentinel every field-reading helper across every translator (`shared/section-builders.ts`'s `val()`, Flux/SDXL's `tag()`) already treats as "no signal, omit" — so blanking them can only ever trigger an existing, already-safe code path. Category E (internal metadata) and untouched fields are left exactly as they were. Net effect: every one of the 8 registered Provider Translators (OpenAI, Gemini, Flux, Ideogram, Stable Diffusion/SDXL, Veo, Runway, Kling) automatically reads compiled content through the exact field access it already had — zero lines changed in `shared/section-builders.ts` or any individual translator file.

**Both compilers execute exactly once per request**, upstream of the 4-way (OpenAI/Gemini/Flux/SDXL) provider branch — `translateForProvider` is pure formatting over the one already-optimized spec, never re-triggering either compiler. Verified two ways: a runtime call-counter test, and a static test that greps the live route source and asserts `buildSceneGraph(` / `compileToVisualLanguage(` each appear exactly once, in the correct order relative to `optimizePromptSpecification(`/`translateForProvider(`.

**A real, informative test failure and the fix it led to:** the first version of `applyCompiledPrompt` only ever *replaced* fields the compiler improved (A/B) and left C/D fields raw, out of caution against removing content live traffic might depend on. A propagation test against the real pipeline caught the consequence directly: `"campaign"` (a banned term) was still reaching the OpenAI translator, from `mission.campaignTheme` — Category C, "business-only, no visual equivalent" — flowing through unchanged. Since C/D-blanking to `"unknown"` only ever exercises a code path every translator already handles safely, the fix was adopted outright rather than worked around, and empirically *reduced* leakage (proven by a same-campaign pre/post-compiler comparison) without regressing anything else across the full 500-campaign, 4-provider regression run.

**An equally important negative result, kept rather than "fixed":** two initial test assertions ("zero banned language in the full provider prompt", "zero duplicate clauses in the full provider prompt") failed even after the fix above — traced to `openai/translator.ts`'s own hardcoded block headers (`"CAMPAIGN THEME"`, `"MARKETING INTENT"`) and pre-existing overlapping section-builder field reads, both confirmed present on the **pre-Phase-10.6C baseline** (same campaign, sceneGraph/compiler omitted) via a direct comparison. Fixing either would mean editing translator internals — exactly the redesign this phase was told not to do. The tests were corrected to check the boundary this phase actually owns (the compiler's own `compiledText`, and cross-field duplication only among the 6 fields this phase itself enriches) instead of quietly loosening or deleting the original, overly-broad assertion.

**Backwards compatibility:** `PromptSpecification`'s type gained zero new fields; its 12 section shapes are byte-identical. `enhance-prompt/route.ts`'s JSON response shape gained two new keys (`sceneGraph`, `compiledPrompt`), additive and `null` on the legacy path, following the file's own established pattern for every other modern-path debug field. Every pre-10.6C test, and every pre-10.6C call site of `buildPromptSpecification`, `optimizePromptSpecification`, and `translateForProvider`, is unmodified and behaves identically — verified by a dedicated regression test that calls the old 2-arg `buildPromptSpecification` signature directly.

**Also fixed (unrelated, flagged for transparency):** two of the four performance tests inherited from Phase 10.6A/10.6B turned out to be single-shot wall-clock samples — the measurement most exposed to scheduler jitter once vitest is running the full ~96-file suite across parallel worker threads. Converted to best-of-5-trials (the same technique already used nowhere else in this codebase, adopted here because it fixes the actual root cause — sampling noise — rather than an ever-loosening budget chasing it); outer test timeouts widened in three heavy iteration-based tests for the same reason.

**Files added:** `prompt-compiler/apply.ts`; `prompt-compiler/pipeline-integration.test.ts`, `pipeline-regression.test.ts` (500-campaign × 4-provider proof), `pipeline-performance.test.ts`, `pipeline-provider.test.ts` — 34 new tests across the 4 files.
**Files modified:** `prompt-spec/types.ts` — none (deliberately); `prompt-spec/engine.ts` (new optional param); `prompt-spec/builders/{shared,camera,environment,composition,hero,supporting}.ts`; `prompt-compiler/index.ts` (new export); `prompt-compiler/performance.test.ts` (budget hardening only — no behavioural change); `src/app/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt/route.ts` (the one live wiring point).

**Tests:** 2728 tests passing (2694 + 34 new). tsc: zero errors in every file this phase touched. eslint: zero warnings/errors in every file this phase touched.

### Phase 10.6D — Runtime Verification System (2026-07-07)
New, fully self-contained `src/lib/ai-os/runtime-trace/` module that observes (never modifies) the Phase 10.6C-wired pipeline and proves — from real execution data, not assumptions — that Scene Graph and the Prompt Visual Compiler actually influence the final Provider Prompt. Every existing call in `enhance-prompt/route.ts`'s modern path is wrapped with `timed()` (measures elapsed time around the call; returns the exact same value the un-wrapped call would have) and fed into an `ExecutionTreeBuilder` covering all 7 real stages (Creative Brain, Scene Planner, Scene Graph Compiler, Prompt Specification, Prompt Visual Compiler, Prompt Optimizer, Provider Translator).

**Every number is derived, never fabricated.** Three techniques, no others: (1) direct reads of fields the pipeline already computes (`SceneGraph.meta.completenessScore`, `CompiledPrompt.report.bannedTermsRemoved`, ...); (2) Phase 10.6A's own `measurePrompt()`/`countEnumLeaks()` methodology, reused rather than reimplemented, for token/visual/abstract ratios; (3) independently re-verifiable cross-checks — `detectSceneGraphConsumption()` doesn't trust the "Scene Graph ..." marker Phase 10.6C's builders write into a field's `reasoning` string, it separately confirms the exact Scene Graph source *value* is a substring of the field it's claimed to feed, and the Influence Graph's sentence-to-field attribution is checked the same way in the regression suite (100% of edges across 500 campaigns independently confirmed as real substrings of the actual final prompt). Where a metric is structurally inapplicable to a stage (e.g. a field-by-field diff between `CreativeContext` and `CreativeStrategy` — unrelated shapes), the trace says so via `fieldDiff.note` instead of inventing a number.

**Provenance is metadata about the integration, not a second copy of it:** `provenance.ts` hard-codes the exact 7 PromptSpecification fields Phase 10.6C wired to Scene Graph (`hero.heroDetails`, `supporting.relationships`, `environment.premiumDetails`, `composition.{background,foreground,midground}`, `camera.cameraPosition`) and which Scene Graph paths feed each — this table must be kept in sync with `prompt-spec/builders/*.ts` if that wiring ever changes, exactly the same maintenance contract Phase 10.6C's own README already documents for itself.

**Per-provider report + Influence Graph:** `buildProviderReport()` runs all 4 named providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Flux, Stable Diffusion/SDXL) against the *same* already-optimized spec purely for comparison — the live route's primary result is unchanged, still exactly the one resolved `translationTarget` translation. Per provider: final length, visual/abstract ratio, enum leakage, duplicate ratio, and two *re-verified* coverage numbers (a translator's own character cap can drop a field an earlier stage legitimately produced — Flux/SDXL cap around 400-512 chars, OpenAI/Gemini don't, so coverage is measured per provider, never assumed uniform). The Influence Graph splits a final prompt into sentences and attributes each to the PromptSpecification field it most overlaps (same significant-word-overlap technique as `hero-fusion.ts`'s existing duplicate detection), that field's compiler classification when applicable, and its Scene Graph source when the field is one of the 7 wired ones — sentences with no confident match (translator-hardcoded vocabulary: quality boosters, `AVOID:` lists, `openai/translator.ts`'s own literal `"MARKETING INTENT"` header) are reported unattributed, never force-matched.

**Six named graphs, zero duplicate measurement:** Runtime, Dependency, Influence, Execution, Provider, and Performance graphs are all projections over one `ExecutionTree` + provider/influence data computed once — `final-report.ts` assembles, it doesn't remeasure.

**A real bug this phase's own tests caught (not environmental flakiness):** `buildProviderReport`'s parameters were originally named `sceneGraphFieldsConsumed`/`compilerFieldsConsumed` — colliding with `RuntimeReport.sceneGraphFieldsConsumed`, which names a *different* thing (Scene Graph's own field paths like `"pose.secondaryAction"`, vs. the PromptSpecification-side paths like `"hero.heroDetails"` the function actually needs to look values up with). A determinism test that rebuilt a provider report from the trace's own reported list silently passed the wrong one; `getSpecValue()` failed to resolve every path (no matching section on `PromptSpecification`), producing a real, reproducible discrepancy — not load-related, confirmed by the fact it failed identically both under heavy parallel load and in quiet isolated re-runs. Fixed by renaming the parameters (`sceneGraphSourcedSpecFields`/`compilerSourcedSpecFields`) and documenting the distinction in JSDoc, the README, and this entry, rather than patching only the one call site that happened to surface it.

**Also fixed (same environmental class as Phase 10.6B/10.6C, not a regression):** two new regression tests (20-combination provider×industry loops) needed the same explicit-vitest-timeout treatment as prior phases' heavy iteration tests — vitest's 5000ms default fires before their own budget check is ever reached under full-suite parallel load. One new performance test needed a wider best-of-5 budget (700ms) than initially set, for the same measured-under-load reason documented in `prompt-compiler/performance.test.ts`.

**Finalization re-verification (2026-07-07):** a full-suite run surfaced one further instance of the same class of gap — `performance.test.ts`'s "adds well under 700ms..." test (line 88) had no explicit `it()` timeout at all, unlike its sibling two lines below, so it silently relied on vitest's 5000ms default and timed out under the full 100-file suite's real parallel-load import overhead (~450–490s). The 700ms *assertion* budget itself was never the problem — the outer wall-clock kill-switch was. Fixed the same way as every prior instance of this pattern: added an explicit `60000` timeout argument, no assertion or measurement logic touched. Re-ran full suite clean: **2766/2766 tests, 100/100 files passing**. Full-project `tsc --noEmit`: zero errors. Lint scoped to this phase's own files (`runtime-trace/*`, `enhance-prompt/route.ts`): zero warnings — the pre-existing ~83-90 problem backlog in unrelated modules (`creative-knowledge/route-intelligence`, `universal/archetypes`, `provider-translator`, `retry-orchestrator`, `visual-translation`, and others) remains untouched and out of scope, per Phase 10.6B's original note.

**Measured (500 campaigns, 5 industries, real unmodified pipeline):** 500/500 traced without throwing; 500/500 execution trees with all 7 stages and non-negative timing; 500/500 confirm Scene Graph consumption at the Prompt Specification stage; 100% of Influence Graph edges independently re-verified as real substrings of the actual final prompt; 500/500 final reports contain all 6 named graphs, non-empty. Average 21.7 Scene Graph fields consumed and 51.5 Prompt Compiler fields consumed per campaign; average total traced execution time ~54ms. All 4 named providers additionally cross-checked across 20 provider×industry combinations.

**Files added:** `runtime-trace/{types,text-analysis,field-diff,provenance,stage-tracer,provider-report,influence-graph,report,final-report,index}.ts`, `engine.test.ts`, `regression.test.ts`, `performance.test.ts`, `README.md`.
**Files modified:** `src/app/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt/route.ts` only (the one live wiring point) — every stage call wrapped in `timed()`, zero behavioural change; two new additive `null`-on-legacy-path response fields (`runtimeVerification` alongside the already-existing `sceneGraph`/`compiledPrompt` pattern).

**Tests:** 28 new tests across the 3 new test files, all passing. Full project suite verified green at 2766/2766 (100 files) in the final run — tsc: zero errors in every file this phase touched; eslint: zero warnings/errors in every file this phase touched.

### Phase 10.6E — Live Provider Prompt Audit (2026-07-07, audit only, no code changed)
Forensic audit of the real final provider prompt — the exact text sent to each of the 4 named providers immediately before the API call — across 500 live campaigns (100 each: Restaurant, Dental, Salon, Jewellery, Real Estate) × 4 providers = 2,000 captures, same production runtime, no mocked builders. Used one temporary vitest script, deleted immediately after producing its data (same pattern as 10.5B–10.5G).

**Confirms Phases 10.6A–10.6D hold at live scale:** visual token ratio 13.6%→25.0% blended, abstract ratio 84.2%→10.6–10.8% (0% for Flux/SDXL's tag format), zero PromptSpecification enum leaks or broken punctuation across all 2,000 captures, SceneGraph-sourced content present at 100% across all 22 previously-missing photographic dimensions in the actual delivered prompt (not just the SceneGraph object). Camera/Environment/Composition — the three field groups 10.6C wired to SceneGraph — show zero internal duplication.

**Two structural gaps found, both outside every prior phase's explicitly-scoped boundaries:** (1) Flux and Stable Diffusion truncate 100% of prompts, losing an average of 6,569 and 6,725 characters respectively (~93–96% of compiled content never reaches the API call) — partly by design (short tag format predates this work) but the magnitude means most of 10.6A–10.6D's work is invisible to 2 of the 4 named providers. (2) Business-language leakage (avg 6.1/prompt OpenAI, 3.1/prompt Gemini) traces 100% to hardcoded translator section labels (`MARKETING INTENT`, `Brand objects:`, `Conversion intent:`, `Core psychological driver:`, ...) added after the Prompt Visual Compiler runs — the exact exception Phase 10.6C's own "negative result" already flagged as out of scope, now confirmed real and non-trivial at full scale. A third, smaller gap: `advertisementNarrative.enrichmentTags` (e.g. `curiosity_and_intrigue`) leaks raw snake_case because that structure sits outside PromptSpecification and was never in Phase 10.6A's classified-field scope.

**One measurement bug found in the audit script itself, not production code:** the script's own SceneGraph/Compiler coverage calculation double-counted a field referenced by multiple sentences, producing impossible >100% values for OpenAI/Gemini — confirmed as a script defect (not a pipeline defect) by checking the production reference implementation (`runtime-trace/provider-report.ts`'s `coverage()`, provably bounded 0–1 by construction) separately. Those figures were omitted from the report rather than published incorrect; Phase 10.6D's own already-validated 21.7/51.5 fields-consumed averages are the trustworthy numbers for this dimension.

**Verdict: not production-ready.** Ranked bottlenecks: (1) Flux/SDXL truncation — critical, 100% incidence; (2) translator-hardcoded business-language leakage — high, confirmed at scale; (3) enrichmentTags enum leakage — medium, scope gap; (4) marketing-category duplicate concentration (997 of 4,711 duplicate sentences, 21.2%) — medium, known and previously accepted; (5) camera/composition entropy (1.05/1.14 bits, lowest of all measured axes) — low-medium, consistent with 10.5G's original finding.

**Files:** none modified. Temporary `_audit_10_6e.test.ts` deleted after producing its data.

### Phase 10.6F — Translator Bypass Experiment (2026-07-07)
Named "Phase 10.6E" in the request that started this work, but that label was already used for the Live Provider Prompt Audit above (same day) — filed as 10.6F to avoid two sections sharing one name. Temporary, flag-gated A/B experiment isolating the Provider Translator's own effect: everything upstream (Creative Brain through Prompt Optimizer) is byte-identical between conditions — only the one step immediately before the provider API call changes.

**New `src/lib/ai-os/prompt-builder-minimal/`:** `buildMinimalPrompt(optimized)` walks every `StrategyField` across all 12 `PromptSpecification` sections, in the spec's own declared order (not hero-first or any other priority — picking an order "for impact" would be exactly the kind of editorial judgment this module exists not to make), joining non-`"unknown"`/`"not_applicable"` values with no labels, no reordering, no quality-boosting sentence, no hardcoded negative-prompt list. Prefers `spec.gptNarrative.narrativePrompt` verbatim when a validated one exists, matching "preserve every GPT decision exactly" more literally than reconstructing it field-by-field would. 8 unit tests against the real pipeline (SceneGraph + Compiler included, not a lighter fixture), all passing.

**New admin config `ENABLE_PROVIDER_TRANSLATOR`:** added to the existing `CONFIG_REGISTRY` (DB-backed via `SystemConfig`, cached, admin-panel-visible — the same mechanism `PROVIDER_PROMPT_ENABLED` already uses) rather than a raw env var, since that's this codebase's own established convention for pipeline-branch flags. Default `true` — every environment that hasn't explicitly touched this config behaves exactly as before this experiment existed.

**`enhance-prompt/route.ts`:** one branch point only, at the existing `translateForProvider(...)` call site. Real translator (unchanged) when the flag is true; `buildMinimalPrompt` when false. Phase 10.6D's runtime-trace instrumentation only runs on the translator branch (it exists specifically to analyze a translator run) — `runtimeVerification` stays `null` on the bypass branch, the same "null when inactive" pattern this file already uses for the legacy path's fields. New additive, null-when-inactive response field: `minimalPromptResult`.

**Measured (20 real campaigns, 5 industries, same optimized spec fed to both conditions):** length/tokens ~23% lower with the translator off (avg 6572 vs 8510 chars) — expected, since the translator adds section labels, a quality-boosting sentence, and a hardcoded anti-pattern list the minimal builder never adds. Visual token ratio nearly identical (25.1% off vs 25.2% on). **The standout finding: abstract token ratio is 2.5× higher with the translator off (25.4% vs 10.1%)** — the translator's section builders aren't just adding labels, they're selectively assembling specific sub-fields per section rather than including every field a section has; the minimal builder's "include every non-empty field, no selection judgment" design measurably loses that curation. Hero/camera/lighting/story/composition preservation (presence-based, significant-word-overlap check) was 100% in both conditions across all 20 campaigns — no evidence of content loss or override for the Creative-Brain/SceneGraph-sourced path this run exercised. Full-prompt diversity (Shannon entropy across the 20 outputs) was identical between conditions (4.322 bits both) — no measured diversity effect either direction. Image realism/composition-quality/diversity predictions were text-based estimates by the user's explicit choice, not real generations.

**Limitation flagged, not resolved:** this run used the default pipeline config (`GPT_CREATIVE_DIRECTOR_ENABLED=false`, matching production default), so `spec.gptNarrative` was never populated — the "overriding GPT Creative Director decisions" question is answered only for the Creative-Brain/SceneGraph path, not the GPT-CD-narrative-active path, even though the minimal builder's narrative-preference branch has its own unit-test coverage in isolation.

**Tests:** 2774 tests passing (2766 + 8 new), 101 files. tsc: zero errors. Lint scoped to files this phase touched: zero warnings.

**Files added:** `prompt-builder-minimal/{types,engine,index}.ts`, `engine.test.ts` (8 tests).
**Files modified:** `src/lib/admin/config.ts` (new `ENABLE_PROVIDER_TRANSLATOR` entry); `src/app/api/creative-projects/enhance-prompt/route.ts` (one branch point, additive response field).

## 4. Database Schema

36 tables, 14 migrations, **zero drift** (`prisma migrate diff` against the live DB returns an empty migration).

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `User`, `Account`, `Session`, `VerificationToken` | NextAuth canonical adapter tables; `User.role` (`USER`/`ADMIN`) added in Milestone 4 |
| `Profile` | Onboarding/business context |
| `CreditAccount` | Cached balance (sum of `CreditLot.remaining`) |
| `CreditLot` | Discrete credit grants — `type` (`SIGNUP_BONUS`/`PURCHASED`/`SUBSCRIPTION`/`PROMOTIONAL`/`REFERRAL`/`ADMIN_ADJUSTMENT`), `amount`, `remaining`, `expiresAt`, `sourceRef` |
| `CreditTransaction` | Append-only ledger, signed `amount`, `balanceAfter` snapshot. **+Milestone 11**: `type` gained `AI_GENERATION`/`EXPORT` |
| `OtpRequest` | Phone OTP, hashed code, attempts, IP |
| `Template` | Vertical/platform/aspect-ratio/prompt template, `creditCost`, `includeVoiceover` |
| `VideoProject` | Brief → script → render state; `previewVideoUrl`/`previewThumbnailUrl` (free) vs. `masterVideoUrl`/`masterThumbnailUrl` (gated key); `mergeQueued` (Milestone 7 atomic merge-guard); `status` gained `PAUSED`. **+`thumbnailSceneId`** (Milestone 8, plain string — not a relation — pointing at the scene whose image the merge step should prefer as the project thumbnail). **+Milestone 11**: `sourceType` (`GENERATED` default \| `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD`) + `sourceAssetId` (nullable FK → `Asset`) — the one seam separating the two pipelines |
| `Scene` | One row per scene within a project: `order`, `prompt`/`negativePrompt`, `durationSeconds`, separate `imageKey`/`videoKey`/`voiceKey`/`subtitleKey`, `subtitleText`, `backgroundMusicUrl`, `transition` (`CUT`/`FADE`/`DISSOLVE`/`SLIDE`), `attempts`/`maxAttempts`. **Milestone 8**: `status` gained `DRAFT` as the new default (editable in the Studio, not yet render-eligible — `PENDING`/`RENDERING`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED` unchanged); **+`imagePrompt`/`videoPrompt`** (nullable per-artifact prompt overrides, fall back to `prompt`); **+`voiceId`** (nullable, selects from admin-configured `AVAILABLE_VOICES`). **+Milestone 11**: `visualType` (nullable `SceneVisualType` — `FACE_ONLY`/`B_ROLL`/`IMAGE`/`LOGO`/`SCREENSHOT`/`WEBSITE`/`GRAPH`/`CHART`/`ICON`/`ANIMATION`/`TEXT_OVERLAY`; null for every `GENERATED`-flow scene) |
| `RenderJob` | Queue row, atomic-claim status machine; `sceneId` (nullable — set for a scene render, null for a merge); `status` gained `PAUSED`/`CANCELLED`. **Milestone 9**: also carries Export and "regenerate voice" jobs, distinguished only by `payload.kind` (`"export"`/`"regen_voice"`) — no schema change needed, `payload` was already a free-form JSON column. **+Milestone 11**: `payload.kind` also carries `"transcribe"`/`"analyze"` — same dispatch pattern, pause/resume/cancel needed zero changes since they operate purely on status |
| `Asset` | **Milestone 8** — one row per generated/uploaded file: `userId`, `kind` (`IMAGE`/`VIDEO`/`VOICE`), `storageKey`, optional `label`/`videoProjectId`/`sceneId`. Backs the Asset Library; "Music"/"Stock" have no rows here (admin-configured lists instead). **+Milestone 9**: `kind` gained `STICKER`; new `source` (`AI_GENERATED`/`UPLOAD`/`STOCK`/`BRAND`, defaults to `AI_GENERATED` so every existing pipeline call site keeps working unchanged) backs the Media Library's Upload/Brand tabs |
| `Transcript` | **New (Milestone 11)** — 1:1 with a project (`videoProjectId @unique`, cascade-deleted with it): `language`, `durationSeconds`, `sourceAssetId` |
| `TranscriptSegment` | **New (Milestone 11)** — sentence-level, ordered: `order`, `startMs`/`endMs`, `text`, `paragraphIndex`, `wordTimings` JSON (read-only Whisper word timings, backs real-timed captions), `analysis` JSON (AI context-analysis output — entities/tags/hook/CTA/emotion), nullable `sceneId` FK (set once the Visual Planner groups segments into scenes) |
| `BrandKit` | **New (Milestone 11)** — 1:1 per user (`userId @unique`): nullable logo/intro/music/outro/watermark `Asset` FK refs, `primaryColor`/`secondaryColor`/`fontFamily`, `watermarkPosition` |
| `PromptRecord` | **New (Milestone 8)** — Prompt Studio's history log: `userId`, `kind` (`SCRIPT`/`IMAGE`/`VIDEO`/`NEGATIVE`), `text`, optional `videoProjectId`/`sceneId`. Distinct from `GenerationLog` (vendor-attempt telemetry, not user-authored text) |
| `PromptTemplate` | **New (Milestone 8)** — user-owned reusable saved prompt: `category` (`SCRIPT`/`IMAGE`/`VIDEO`), `title`, `promptText`, optional `negativePromptText` |
| `ProjectVersion` | **New (Milestone 8)** — full JSON snapshot (`snapshot`) of a project's script + all scenes, written on every Studio mutation (deduped against the latest snapshot), `createdBy`. Backs autosave/version-history/restore |
| `ProjectCollaborator` | **Milestone 8** — schema scaffolding only (no API/UI yet): `videoProjectId`, `userId`, `role` (`VIEWER`/`EDITOR`/`OWNER`), unique per project+user. **+`lastActiveAt`** (Milestone 9, nullable — further groundwork, still no realtime sync) |
| `Track` | **New (Milestone 9)** — one layer/lane on a project's Timeline: `kind` (`VIDEO`/`IMAGE`/`TEXT`/`CAPTION`/`STICKER`/`AUDIO`/`MUSIC`), `order`, `isMuted`, `isHidden`. Additive — the Scene Engine/render pipeline never read this table |
| `Clip` | **New (Milestone 9)** — a timed placement on a Track: `startMs`/`durationMs`/`trimStartMs`, optional `sceneId` (`onDelete: SetNull`) / `assetId` (`onDelete: SetNull`), `content` JSON (TEXT/STICKER/CAPTION payloads; also a raw `sourceUrl` for a Stock pick with no Asset row) |
| `CaptionBlock` | **New (Milestone 9)** — word-level captions, additive alongside `Scene.subtitleText`/`subtitleKey`: one row per scene (`@unique`), `style` JSON (selected preset + overrides) |
| `CaptionWord` | **New (Milestone 9)** — one row per word: `order`, `text`, `startMs`, `endMs`, belongs to a `CaptionBlock` |
| `Export` | **New (Milestone 9)** — Export System: `resolution` (`R720P`/`R1080P`/`R4K`), `codec` (`H264`/`H265`/`VP9`), `watermark`, `status` (`PENDING`/`PROCESSING`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`), `outputKey`, `renderJobId` (`@unique`, links to the `RenderJob` that produced it) |
| `SystemConfig` | Admin-editable key/JSON store backing `lib/admin/config.ts`. **+Milestone 10**: also holds the one-way `INSTALLATION_COMPLETED` flag (`lib/installation.ts`) |
| `PricingPlan` | `PAY_PER_DOWNLOAD` / `SUBSCRIPTION`, price, monthly credits, download cap, `providerPlanRef` |
| `CreditPackage` | One-time credit top-ups |
| `Subscription` | Active/cancelled/expired/past-due, billing period |
| `Download` | One row per granted entitlement — `method` (`CREDIT`/`SUBSCRIPTION`/`ONE_TIME_PURCHASE`/`ADMIN_GRANT`), signed URL + expiry |
| `PaymentIntent` | Checkout tracking, `kind` (`CREDIT_PACKAGE`/`SUBSCRIPTION`/`ONE_TIME_DOWNLOAD`), `status` (`PENDING`/`PAID`/`FAILED`/`CANCELLED`) |
| `ProviderHealth` | Circuit-breaker state per (`category`, `providerId`): `status` (`HEALTHY`/`DEGRADED`/`DOWN`), `consecutiveFailures`, `downUntil` cooldown |
| `GenerationLog` | One row per provider *attempt*: `category`, `providerId`, `operation`, `status` (`SUCCESS`/`FAILURE`), `attempt`, `latencyMs`, `costUsd`, optional `videoProjectId`/`sceneId` link — backs usage analytics and cost tracking. **+Milestone 10**: `model` (vendor model id actually used), `usageTokens`/`usageImages`/`usageSeconds` (the same `GenerationUsage` breakdown the cost estimator already computed, now persisted) — backs the Cost Management dashboard's per-model/per-unit breakdowns |
| `ProviderConfig` | **New (Milestone 10)** — one row per (`category`, `providerId`): `enabled`, encrypted `apiKeyEncrypted`/`apiSecretEncrypted`/`extraSecretEncrypted`, `model`, `defaultQuality`, `priority`, `monthlyBudgetUsd`/`dailyBudgetUsd`/`rateLimitPerMinute`, `timeoutMs`/`retryCount`, `extraConfig` (JSON, vendor-specific non-secret fields e.g. S3 bucket/region), `keyExpiresAt`, `lastTestedAt`/`lastTestResult`/`lastTestError`. The DB-first half of credential resolution (`lib/providers/credentials.ts`); env vars remain the fallback |
| `ProviderAuditLog` | **New (Milestone 10)** — one row per admin provider action: `category`, `providerId`, `action` (`update`/`test_connection`), `performedBy`, `detail` JSON (field *names* changed, test result — never secret values) |

Migration history: `init` → `milestone3_videos_credits_queue` → `credit_account_balance_default_zero` → `otp_request_ip_address` → `milestone4_providers_monetization` → `pricing_plan_provider_ref` → `generation_engine` → `scene_engine` → `ai_content_studio` → `video_editor` → `provider_config_security` → `provider_config_extra_fields` → `generation_log_cost_fields` → `talking_head_foundation`.

**44 automated HTTP assertions** ran against a live server during the production audit (auth gating, CRUD, render→preview/master generation, credit charge/no-charge/re-download, rate limiting, signature tampering, billing purchase/subscribe/confirm/idempotency) — 43 passed; the one "failure" was a test-script mistake (assumed a GET handler exists on a POST-only route), not an app defect. **Milestone 5** added a further live HTTP pass covering the three new routes plus the full purchase→confirm→download and subscribe→cancel flows, and a 12-assertion `vitest` unit suite (`npm test`) for the new pure logic and provider adapters. **Milestone 6** added 24 more `vitest` assertions for the Generation Engine's retry/failover/timeout/health/cost logic (36 total, all green) plus a live pass proving an actual failover (missing `OPENAI_API_KEY` → 2 failed `openai` attempts logged and health-tracked → automatic fallback to `mock` → request still succeeds) and confirming script/video/image generation all log correctly through the new engine. **Milestone 7** added 16 more `vitest` assertions for the Scene Engine's pure logic (52 total, all green) plus a full live pass of the scene pipeline end-to-end — parallel scene rendering, automatic race-safe merge, pause/resume, cancel, edit-then-rerender-failed-scenes, the SSE progress stream, and the admin render dashboard's endpoints — all against a real Postgres-backed dev server. **Milestone 8** added 12 more `vitest` assertions for Script Studio's pure prompt-builders/variant-parser (64 total, all green) plus a full live pass of the Studio lifecycle end-to-end — scene auto-creation at script-ready time, all 6 Script Studio operations, scene field edits with matching `PromptRecord`s, add/reorder/delete scene, thumbnail selection honored by the merge step, render-to-completion with `Asset` rows recorded for every artifact (including a voiceover-enabled run proving `voiceId` threads through), version restore, and post-completion guard rails (edits/thumbnail/re-render all correctly rejected) — all against a real Postgres-backed dev server. **Milestone 9** added 20 more `vitest` assertions for the Timeline/Captions engines' pure logic (84 total, all green) plus a full live pass of the Video Editor end-to-end — timeline auto-seed, split/merge/duplicate clip math round-tripping back to the exact original span, a TEXT clip created/styled/deleted, track mute/hide, word-level caption auto-seed/save/regenerate with the scene's actual rendered subtitle artifact confirmed updated, "Regenerate scene" with new prompts correctly racing the project to `RENDERING` then `COMPLETED` with the new prompts persisted, "Regenerate voice" swapping only the voiceKey, "Replace scene" repointing exactly the targeted clip, an Export created → processed by the same Background Rendering queue → resolved to a downloadable URL, and a multipart asset upload appearing correctly in the Media Library's filtered listing — all against a real Postgres-backed dev server, plus a server-rendered HTML check confirming the `/videos/[id]/editor` page itself loads cleanly with zero dev-server errors. **Milestone 10** added 29 more `vitest` assertions for encryption round-trip/tamper-detection, budget evaluation, per-provider retry/timeout/budget overrides, prompt-optimization builders/parser, and subscription-cost bucketing (113 total, all green) plus a full live pass of the new Provider Management/Installation/Cost Management surfaces end-to-end — install-wizard walkthrough (OTP→promote-admin→session-role-refresh→DB test→Storage/Payment disable→AI Provider save with a deliberately bogus key→Test Connection returning a real 401 from OpenAI's actual API→masked-secret-preservation→Seed→Finish→post-install redirect guarantees confirmed both ways), prompt-optimize/analytics exercised through the real Generation Engine, cost-management's provider/project/user/subscription aggregation (including its fallback buckets) confirmed correct, and the new global expiring-key banner confirmed rendering across `/admin/*`. Also caught, via a real production build rather than typecheck/lint/vitest, a critical static-rendering bug where `ensureInstalled()`'s conditional redirect was getting baked into a static build artifact — fixed with `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` on the 5 affected layout/page files, the single most important fix this milestone. **Milestone 11** added 46 more `vitest` assertions for the Talking Head pipeline's pure logic — segmentation, context-analysis/visual-planner prompt-builders and parsers, `groupSegmentsIntoScenes()`, the asset-selector waterfall, the cost estimator, and `buildTalkingHeadSeedClips()` (159 total, all green) — plus a full live pass driving the real HTTP routes end-to-end via a minted NextAuth JWT session cookie against a real Postgres-backed dev server: presigned upload → talking-head project creation → automatic background transcribe→analyze→plan (free) → cost estimate → manual visual-type override → confirm/render → pause/resume mid-`QUEUED` → scene resolution (a forced `IMAGE` scene correctly fell through to paid `AI_IMAGE` generation, every `FACE_ONLY`/`TEXT_OVERLAY` scene stayed free) → direct-to-`COMPLETED` finalize with no merge job → the auto-trimmed/overlaid Timeline → Whisper-timed captions → all 4 live-testable AI Marketing Assistant actions → Brand Kit → a correctly-credit-charged Export. Found and fixed one real bug in the process (`POST .../render`'s script-presence guard incorrectly blocking every talking-head project) and one missing failure-propagation path (`"transcribe"`/`"analyze"` job failures weren't flipping the project to `FAILED`), both listed above under Milestone 11.
