## 6. Current Architecture

- **Provider abstraction**: every vendor category (LLM/Image/Voice/Video/Storage/Payment) is an interface + Mock adapter + one (or more, for LLM/Image/Video as of Milestone 6/10) real adapter. Every LLM/Image/Voice/Video provider class also implements the common `GenerationProvider` base (`id`, `category`, **+Milestone 10** optional `model`). Verified: zero vendor SDK imports or vendor env var reads outside `lib/providers/*`.
- **Generation Engine** (Milestone 6, credentials pivot in Milestone 10): `lib/generation/engine.ts`'s `runGeneration()` is the single orchestration path every LLM/Image/Voice/Video call goes through — admin-configured priority order, retry with backoff (now with per-provider overrides), per-category timeout, a health-based circuit breaker per provider, an admin-set per-provider daily/monthly budget + rate-limit filter (Milestone 10, fails *closed* unlike health's fail-*open* posture), vendor-cost tracking against an admin-configurable rate card, and one usage-log row per provider attempt (now including the model used and the usage breakdown). **As of Milestone 10**, provider *credentials* moved from env-var-only to DB-first with env-var fallback (`lib/providers/credentials.ts`, `/admin/ai-providers`) — provider *selection*, *credentials*, and the engine's retry/timeout/health/cost/budget *policy* are now ALL admin-configurable from one page, with env vars remaining only as the pre-install/zero-DB-row fallback. Nothing hardcoded, no redeploy needed to change any of it.
- **Pipeline**: Studio (pre-render) → Scene Engine → Render Queue → Generation Engine → Provider → Storage → Credits → Editor (post-render). Concretely: `POST /api/videos` generates the script *and* immediately decomposes it into `Scene`s (`DRAFT`, Milestone 8) → the user edits script/scenes freely in the Studio (every edit autosaves a `ProjectVersion`) → `POST /api/videos/[id]/render` just claims the status transition and enqueues one job per scene (no scene creation here anymore) → `lib/render/pipeline.ts` claims jobs concurrently (`drainQueue()`) and dispatches scene-render vs. merge vs. (Milestone 9) export/regen-voice jobs by `payload.kind`, reading each scene's `imagePrompt`/`videoPrompt`/`voiceId`/`subtitleText` overrides → each calls `lib/generation/{video,image,voice}.ts` (failover/retry/health/cost logic, unchanged from Milestone 6) → results upload via the Storage Provider under per-scene keys (unchanged interface) and are additionally recorded as `Asset` rows (Milestone 8) → once every scene is `COMPLETED`, a race-safe merge job produces the final preview/master, preferring `VideoProject.thumbnailSceneId` for the thumbnail if set → the user opens the Video Editor (Milestone 9), where the Timeline's `Track`/`Clip` layer composes those same scene artifacts (plus Media Library assets and Text/Sticker/Caption overlays) into a multi-track edit, exported via the *same* Generation Engine's new `composeTimeline()` operation through the *same* Background Rendering queue → user credits are still spent only at download time (unchanged from Milestone 4; Export is currently free/unlimited like rendering, no credit gate was added this milestone).
- **Render Queue, generic vs. domain-specific**: `lib/queue/*` stays pure job-claim mechanics (claim/complete/fail, atomic and concurrency-safe by construction); `lib/render/pipeline.ts` is where scene/merge-specific processing, finalize-decision, and pause/resume/cancel/rerender-failed logic lives — the same separation already established between the Generation Engine's orchestration (`lib/generation/engine.ts`) and category wrappers.
- **Monetization**: rendering is free and unlimited; credits are spent only by the Download Service, which checks subscription → credits → (one-time-purchase recorded separately) before ever minting a signed URL to the master asset.
- **Credit Engine**: lot-based, not a single counter — supports independent expiry and an admin-configurable draw-down priority across 6 lot types, atomic under row-level locking.
- **Payment architecture**: one vendor-agnostic `fulfillPaymentIntent()` function is the single settlement path for both a real, signature-verified webhook and the dev-mode mock-confirm endpoint — idempotent by PaymentIntent status. All three monetization paths (credit package, subscription, one-time download) and subscription cancellation now exist end-to-end; the client never settles a payment itself — it only opens a vendor checkout widget or polls a PaymentIntent's status.
- **Admin panel**: every provider (including credentials, as of Milestone 10), price, rule, generation policy, render policy, and budget/rate-limit lives in the database, editable from `/admin/*`, with no redeploy required; the admin UI itself is generic (driven by the same Zod registry the backend validates against, including two generic input types — `string_list` for priority arrays, `json` for the cost-rate table).
- **Queue**: Postgres-backed, atomic-claim, and (as of Milestone 7) genuinely concurrency-safe — both the in-process dev worker and the secret-gated HTTP cron target now drain up to `RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY` jobs in parallel via the same `drainQueue()` function, real parallel rendering rather than sequential draining.
- **Security boundary**: every authenticated route checks session via a single shared helper; every admin route additionally checks role server-side (middleware's edge check is UX-only, not the real boundary); signed URLs use HMAC-SHA256 with exact-length verification (fixed this audit); provider secrets are AES-256-GCM-encrypted at rest and never echoed back in plaintext once saved (Milestone 10).
- **Installation** (Milestone 10): a one-way `SystemConfig` flag (`INSTALLATION_COMPLETED`) gates `/install` itself (inaccessible once true) and is checked by every top-level layout (`ensureInstalled()`) before that layout renders anything else — each of those layouts is explicitly `force-dynamic` so the check can never be baked into a static build artifact. Once installed, every provider/database/storage/payment setting an admin needs to touch lives in `/admin/*`; the only `.env`/redeploy-requiring secrets left are the database connection string itself and (optionally) the credential-encryption master key.
- **Two input modalities, one pipeline** (Milestone 11): `VideoProject.sourceType` is the seam. `GENERATED` (brief → AI script → deterministic scene-split) and `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD` (uploaded video → Whisper transcript → AI context-analysis+visual-planning → LLM-grouped scenes) both terminate at the *same* `Scene` table, so Scene rendering, the Timeline/Editor, the render Queue, the Credit Engine, the Provider abstraction, Versioning, and the Prompt system never branch on `sourceType` themselves — only three places do: project creation (which producer runs), `processSceneRenderJob()` (generate vs. resolve-existing-asset), and `tryFinalizeProject()` (merge job vs. direct-to-`COMPLETED`, since a talking-head project has no separate per-scene videos to concatenate — its scenes share one trimmed source video plus Timeline overlay clips). A future Podcast/Webinar/Course/Interview editor is, architecturally, one more enum value + one more segment-grouping function — see `TALKING_HEAD_ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Credit boundary, codified as a free preview / paid commit step**: every Talking Head step before the user clicks "Confirm & generate" (upload, transcribe, context-analysis, visual-planning, cost estimate, manual edits) touches zero credits — credits are charged exactly once, atomically alongside the database write that records the result, in two places: a scene's `AI_IMAGE`/`AI_VIDEO` generation (`renderTalkingHeadScene()`, pre-checked against the live balance before any vendor cost is spent) and Export (`createExport()`, scoped to `sourceType === "TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD"` only — the `GENERATED` flow's Export stays free, unchanged, per Known Issue #9).
- **`CreativeTool` as a generic, admin-driven UI registry** (Milestone 14): every Dashboard card/quick-action/coming-soon stub is one DB row, not a hardcoded component — `category`+`pipeline`+`routeOverride`/`presetKey` fully determine where it links (`resolveToolHref()`), `creditCostEstimate`/`promptTemplate`/`defaultProviderId` fully determine what it costs/says/prefers at generation time. This is the same "self-describing registry drives a generic UI" pattern `CONFIG_REGISTRY` already established for admin settings (Milestone 4) and `PROVIDER_CATALOGUE` established for vendor selection (Milestone 10) — Milestone 14 is the third application of it, not a new mechanism. A future content type (AI Avatar, AI Music, etc.) needs a new pipeline value + one generation function; the Dashboard itself never needs to change.
- **One generic `CreativeProject` model, three kinds**: AI Image/Social Media/Marketing Creative share one model (`kind` discriminator) and one generation function (`generateCreativeImage()`) because their backend mechanics are identical — prompt in, one image out, no render queue, no scenes. This mirrors the existing `VideoProject.sourceType` seam (Milestone 11) that lets `GENERATED` and `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD` share one model without branching most of the pipeline on which one they are.

---

## 7. Known Issues

1. **Webhook route knows one vendor's header name.** `/api/billing/webhook` reads `x-razorpay-signature` explicitly before handing it to the generic `verifyAndParseWebhook(rawBody, signatureHeader)`. A second real payment vendor would need this route's header-extraction line updated too — the provider *interface* is vendor-agnostic, but this one line at the HTTP edge isn't. Low risk (contained to one line, well-documented), but worth a `getWebhookSignatureHeaderName()` per-provider helper if a second real vendor is ever added.
2. **Transitive dev-dependency security advisories** (`npm audit`): `@hono/node-server` (via `@prisma/dev`) and `postcss` (via `next`'s bundled copy) — both moderate severity, both dev/build-tooling-only (not present in the deployed runtime request path), both require a breaking downgrade of Prisma or Next to fix via `npm audit fix --force`. Left as-is; revisit on the next routine Prisma/Next upgrade.
3. **No app-level Dockerfile.** Only Postgres is containerized; the Next.js app runs on the host. Fine for current dev/demo, a gap for a fully containerized production deploy.
4. **MSG91/Twilio SMS not implemented** — OTP delivery only works through the documented dev-mode fallback.
5. **Pay Per Download plan ships seeded at ₹0.** `assertPurchasablePrice()` correctly refuses to sell at that price (`ERR_NOT_CONFIGURED`), but an admin must set a real price in `/admin/pricing` before the one-time-purchase route is usable in a fresh environment — by design (rule: pricing must be admin-configurable, not hardcoded), just worth calling out so it isn't mistaken for a bug.
6. **Cancellation has no proration/refund.** `POST /api/billing/subscriptions/cancel` is cancel-at-period-end only — a deliberate scope cut for this milestone, not an oversight.
7. **Generation Engine's timeout doesn't truly cancel an in-flight request.** `withTimeout()` races the provider call against a timer and moves on to retry/failover on timeout, but the original call isn't aborted unless the adapter itself wires the passed `AbortSignal` into its `fetch` call (none of the current adapters do yet) — the orphaned request still completes in the background, its result just gets discarded. Low practical impact (no resource leak beyond one outstanding HTTP request), but worth tightening if a provider's calls are expensive enough that wasted in-flight requests matter.
8. **Self-hosted adapters only exist for the LLM category** (see Pending Features) — Image/Voice/Video self-hosted adapters are a "when needed" follow-up, not yet built.
9. **Export (Milestone 9) has no credit gate.** `createExport()` never touches `CreditAccount`/`CreditLot` — exporting is currently free and unlimited, same trust model as rendering. This was a deliberate non-decision (the brief didn't ask for Export pricing and the standing rule is "don't invent business rules"), but a real deployment will likely want to charge for Export the same way the Download Service charges for the master download — that's a `lib/downloads/download-service.ts`-shaped follow-up, not yet built.
10. ~~Timeline has no collision handling~~ **Resolved 2026-07-13** — see the stabilization-pass entry below (`clampMoveStart`/`clampTrimLeftStart`/`clampTrimRightEnd`). The **Layers panel has no track-reorder action** remains, still documented in Pending Features as a deliberate, time-boxed scope cut rather than an oversight.
11. **Veo/Kling/Hailuo/Runway/Ideogram are unverified against live vendor accounts** (Milestone 10; Ideogram added Milestone 16). Built against documented REST shapes, default `enabled: false`. Confirm against current docs/account access before turning one on in production.
12. **Database/Storage/Payment "Test Connection" steps in the Installation Wizard are not fully independent of the app's own already-established connections** (Milestone 10) — the DB step in particular confirms Prisma is already connected rather than testing an arbitrary pasted connection string from scratch. Low practical impact (the app wouldn't have started without a working `DATABASE_URL` anyway), but worth knowing the step isn't a from-scratch connection-string validator.
13. **No automated key-rotation workflow beyond re-saving** (Milestone 10) — Part 9's "support key rotation" is satisfied by the existing PATCH/Save flow plus the new global expiry-reminder banner, not a dedicated rotation UI/scheduler/dual-key overlap.
14. **TRANSCRIPTION provider category has no legacy `SystemConfig` fallback** (Milestone 11) — `lib/providers/credentials.ts`'s `legacyPriorityList()` returns `[]` for `TRANSCRIPTION` (it didn't exist before the Admin Panel did, unlike LLM/Image/Voice/Video which still default to `["mock"]`). An admin must explicitly enable a Transcription provider via `/admin/ai-providers` before any Talking Head project can progress past `DRAFT` — discovered live during this milestone's verification pass (had to seed the `ProviderConfig` row manually, simulating the one-time admin setup). Low risk (a one-time setup step, not a bug), but worth either documenting prominently in the Talking Head upload flow's first-run UX or adding a one-time bootstrap default in a future milestone. **Scope update (found during the 2026-07-19 full-product audit)**: this same `[]`-no-fallback pattern now also covers 5 more categories added since this entry was written — `EMAIL` (Milestone 12), `STOCK_MEDIA`/`ICON` (Milestone 26), and `VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING`/`REASONING` (Phase 12 Module 1) — same "admin must explicitly enable before first use" characteristic, not independently documented per-category until now.
15. **This dev environment's `ProviderConfig` table has a disabled real `LLM/openai` row left over from Milestone 10's install-wizard testing**, which blocks the legacy `["mock"]` fallback for LLM specifically (the fallback only applies when zero rows exist for a category, not when all existing rows are disabled). Anyone testing AI-text features against this same dev DB needs to either enable a `mock`/real LLM `ProviderConfig` row or fix the existing one — not a Milestone 11 regression, just a sharp edge in how the fallback condition is defined.
16. **Every seeded Template is `platform: INSTAGRAM_REEL`, with no other platform value used anywhere.** Dashboard Quick Action links that pass `?platform=YOUTUBE_SHORTS` etc. to the create-video wizard would filter the (now-unused, see below) template list to empty. Pre-existing, unrelated to the template-picker removal — noted here rather than fixed, per founder decision to handle separately.
17. ~~Doubled `/uploads/uploads/` path for every asset uploaded via the generic presigned-upload flow~~ **Fixed 2026-07-19** — stripped the redundant `"uploads/"` prefix at both key-generation call sites (`app/api/assets/upload-url/route.ts` and the sibling `app/api/assets/upload/route.ts`, which had the identical bug, not just the first one). Old assets keep resolving correctly via their own already-doubled keys (no migration needed); new uploads now get a single, correct `/uploads/<userId>/...` path. Statically traced through to AI Film's face-upload → character-sheet path (`sheet/route.ts`), the original real-world trigger for this bug (14/21 real character-sheet generations were failing and silently falling back to mock because of it) — also added a mock-fallback warning banner there while fixing it.
18a. **Background workers/queue processors don't hot-reload server code the way page components do** (first hit Module 5, Editor Audio Ducking milestone — stale Prisma client; hit again Phase 12 Module 7 — the AI-edit job worker, `ai-edit-queue-worker.ts`, started once from `instrumentation.ts`, kept running OLD code after an edit to `ai-edit-jobs.ts` even though Turbopack hot-reloaded every page component fine). Two independent occurrences now — a genuine standing gotcha, not a one-off: **any fix that touches worker/queue-processor logic (export worker, AI-edit worker, or anything else started once from `instrumentation.ts`) needs a full dev-server stop/restart to actually take effect**, not just a file save. Confirmed both times via direct evidence (a live progress value still showing the pre-fix behavior after the edit was saved) rather than assumed — worth checking for this specific symptom (a server-side fix that "didn't work" on the very next live test) before concluding the fix itself is wrong.
18. ~~Redo does not restore a clip after undo-of-a-delete~~ **Already fixed** (found stale during the 2026-07-19 full-product-audit spot-check; the fix itself predates that audit and wasn't cross-referenced back to this entry at the time). `createDeleteClipCommand` (commands.ts:431+) now tracks a mutable `currentClipId`, updated every time `undo()` recreates the clip via `addClip()`, exactly the "likely fix" this entry originally proposed — `execute()`/redo now targets the current real id, not the stale original one. `createRippleDeleteCommand` was fixed the same way (its own comment cites this entry's root cause explicitly). Left struck-through rather than deleted so the original investigation stays on record.
19. **Legacy editor (`/videos/[id]/editor`): B_ROLL scenes are meant to composite `videoKey` (base talking-head video) with `imageKey` (a picture-in-picture overlay) simultaneously — not one replacing the other — but nothing actually renders that composite anywhere, preview or export** (discovered 2026-07-18, fixing the "B_ROLL image never displays" bug — see that entry above). `renderTalkingHeadScene()` (`lib/render/pipeline.ts`) sets a successful B_ROLL scene's `videoKey` to the same shared base video AND `imageKey` to the generated overlay together, and `resolveClipSourceUrl()` (the real Export System) is structured around a genuine VIDEO+IMAGE dual-track design — strong evidence the overlay compositing was the real intent, not an oversight. Nothing currently draws the two together: `ScenePreview.tsx` picks video-or-image via a plain either/or ternary (video always wins when both exist), and the Export System has no dedicated IMAGE-track clip to read from in the first place (see Known Issue on `ensureTimeline()`'s seeding, same investigation). The runtime-fallback fix shipped 2026-07-18 correctly handles "show whichever of video/image actually exists" — it does not attempt this overlay behavior, deliberately. Not urgent: no real project has yet needed the PIP overlay specifically (the common case — one of video-or-image present — is what the shipped fix covers). Revisit only if a real project surfaces a case where both video and image exist and the user specifically needs to see the overlay, not just one visible frame.
20. **The legacy Talking Head flow (`/create/talking-head`) has no discoverable tile on `/create` anymore** (2026-07-18, a direct side effect of fixing the misleading "Upload Your Video" tile — see the discoverability entry above). That tile was the ONLY link to this flow from `/create`; repointing it to the real Phase 12 AI Auto-Edit feature (the fix the founder asked for, urgently, since the tile's own copy was actively misleading users into the wrong feature) means the legacy flow — itself real, working, unrelated functionality — now has no honest entry point of its own on that page. A real, separate product decision, not decided here: add a new `/create` tile with accurate copy for it, surface it elsewhere, or leave it reachable only through its other existing entry points (the dashboard hero prompt box for some classified intents, `tool-routing.ts`'s `TALKING_HEAD` mapping, and the Videos page's "Talking Head" tab empty-state CTA — all three still point there, untouched by this fix, confirmed via a codebase-wide search before making any change).

Resolved this milestone (previously listed here): `ONE_TIME_DOWNLOAD` payment kind is now reachable via `/api/videos/[id]/purchase`; the Razorpay `checkout.js` widget is now wired up client-side; subscription cancellation now has both a route and UI.

**Resolved 2026-07-12 (data isolation bug, found via a live-screenshot-vs-reference comparison, not previously listed here): uploaded Cloud Video Editor assets were visible across ALL projects, not scoped to the project uploaded into.** Root cause: `EditorAsset` had no `projectId` column at all. Fixed with an additive nullable `projectId` column + cascading FK, `listEditorAssets()`'s optional project filter, and threading `projectId` down to the Uploads sidebar section via `useParams()`. `LIBRARY`-scope assets (Milestone 26's admin-curated library) and Brand Kit's cross-project font uploads are unaffected by design. Verified with a real two-project cross-leakage regression test (7/7 passing) — see the full write-up below.

**Resolved 2026-07-12 (previously listed here as Known Issue #17): deleting a clip is now undoable.** New `createDeleteClipCommand()` in `commands.ts` (mirroring the existing best-effort delete-type commands — `execute()` calls `deps.deleteClip()`, `undo()` recreates the clip from its captured pre-delete span/content/transform via `deps.addClip()`, same "new server-generated id" caveat Split/RippleDelete/Group already document). All three entry points that used to call `deleteClipMutation.mutate(id)` directly — `SelectionToolbar`'s toolbar button, the per-clip context-menu item, and the Delete/Backspace keyboard shortcut — now go through this command via a new `runDelete(clips)` helper, which wraps a multi-clip selection in the same `createCompositeCommand` every other multi-select gesture already uses, so one Ctrl+Z undoes an entire multi-delete. New `commands.test.ts` (this file's first-ever dedicated unit test, following `track-stacking.test.ts`'s fake-dependency-injection pattern since `commands.ts` is already framework-agnostic) covers execute/undo, the with-and-without-asset cases, and the composite multi-delete case — 4/4 passing. **Verified live**: toolbar delete+undo, keyboard delete+undo, context-menu delete+undo, and multi-select delete+one-undo all confirmed via real API request logs (not just UI state) restoring the exact pre-delete clip count and properties. Also confirmed the existing transition-invariant enforcement (`pruneInvalidTransitionsForTrack`, Module 9) correctly prunes a transition when its flanking clip is deleted, and that undo does not resurrect the transition or leave any orphaned `Transition` row referencing a stale clip id — consistent with Split/RippleDelete's own already-documented "clip is best-effort restored, transitions are not" behavior. Full suite re-verified: 112 files, 2972/2972 passing; `tsc`/`eslint`/`next build` all clean.

Resolved in Milestone 7 (previously a gap, not previously listed since it predates this doc's Known Issues tracking): the render queue's sequential draining has been replaced with genuine concurrent processing (`drainQueue()`); a single project-level render job has been replaced with independently-retryable, independently-cacheable per-scene jobs.

Resolved in Milestone 10 (introduced and fixed within this same milestone, not previously listed): a critical static-rendering bug where `ensureInstalled()`'s conditional `redirect()` (thrown before any `auth()`/cookie read) got baked into a static build artifact for `/`, `/admin/*`, `/login`, `/onboarding` — found via a real `next build` (not typecheck/lint/vitest), fixed with `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` on the 5 affected layout/page files.

Resolved in Milestone 14 (introduced and fixed within this same milestone, not previously listed): the Dashboard's Coming Soon section silently disappearing because its `enabled: false` seed rows were filtered out by a tools query that conflated "visible" with "has a working pipeline"; a `GET /dashboard 500` caused by passing a function prop (`formatBytes`) from a Server Component into a Client Component, which Next.js can't serialize across that boundary — both found only by a real live HTTP pass against a running dev server, not by `tsc`/`eslint`/`vitest`/`next build`. Also: `lucide-react` no longer exports brand icons (`Instagram`/`Youtube`) — caught immediately by `tsc`, not assumed, and the two affected seed rows were re-pointed at generic icons (`Film`/`PlaySquare`) before they ever reached a live request.

Resolved (AI_IMAGE Gemini ethnicity bug, 2026-07-10): real Gemini image generations (`gemini_images`, the only enabled IMAGE provider) were rendering Western subjects instead of Indian. Root cause was two-fold: (1) `lib/prompt-os/adapters/index.ts`'s `ADAPTERS` map only recognized the id `"gemini"`, not the real provider id `"gemini_images"` — every Gemini AI_IMAGE request was silently falling back to `buildGenericPrompt`, which (like `buildOpenAIPrompt` in the same legacy adapter directory) had zero ethnicity instruction anywhere; (2) the AI_IMAGE pipeline is the legacy `lib/prompt-os/` path (`PROVIDER_PROMPT_ENABLED` defaults `false` and is unset in `SystemConfig`), a separate pipeline from `clean-background-prompt.ts`'s MARKETING_CREATIVE-only ethnicity fix, so that existing fix never reached AI_IMAGE requests at all. Fixed: registered `gemini_images` in the adapter map; added an explicit "everyone shown in this scene is Indian — including secondary/background people" sentence immediately adjacent to the scene/subject description in both `gemini.adapter.ts` and `openai.adapter.ts` (same gap existed in both); applied the matching id-routing fix in `ai-os/provider-translator/resolve-provider.ts` and added the same ethnicity sentence to `ai-os/provider-translator/providers/gemini/quality.ts` so the modern (currently-inactive) Phase 13 pipeline is correct too, the day `PROVIDER_PROMPT_ENABLED` is turned on. Verified live: 5/5 real `gemini-3-pro-image` generations across varied dental-poster scenes (solo dentist+patient, couple, family, dentist+assistant team with background staff, close-up with background dentist) show reliably Indian primary AND secondary/background subjects.

**AI Video Phase 1 — Animated Poster Video (2026-07-10):** the first phase of the new AI Video Generation initiative, built after an architecture investigation confirmed most of what it needs already exists (full plan + real-cost credit math: `lib/creative/animated-poster-video.ts`'s doc comment and the session's own artifact history). Turns an existing (or freshly generated) MARKETING_CREATIVE poster into a ~6s animated MP4 with zero AI video vendor involved — a Ken Burns zoom-in over the poster photo, reusing the Cloud Video Editor's already-built `ANIMATION_PRESETS`/Motion Engine and Export Engine verbatim, not new render math. New pieces: `createReadyEditorAsset()` (`lib/video-editor/assets.ts`) bridges an existing platform `Asset` (e.g. a poster) into the Editor's `EditorAsset` by pointing at the same `storageKey` — no re-upload — since `EditorAsset` was previously upload-only; `PricingPlan.tierLevel` (new `PricingTierLevel` enum: BASIC/PRO/PREMIUM, migration `20260710045244_add_pricing_plan_tier_level`) plus the admin-configurable `VIDEO_ACTION_CREDIT_COSTS` record (mirrors `TALKING_HEAD_CREDIT_COSTS`'s pattern, one row per gated video action, extensible for Phase 2–4 without another migration) back a new `checkVideoActionAccess()` (`lib/credits/video-actions.ts`) that gates by both subscription tier and credit balance before any render starts. Credits (2, priced at ~2.7× real cost per the approved credit-system design) are charged only after the export actually succeeds — reusing Talking Head's precheck-then-charge-after-success pattern rather than a new deduct/refund mechanism, so a failed render never costs the user credits. `Creator Monthly`/`Studio Monthly` seed plans were assigned `tierLevel: BASIC`/`PRO` and their `monthlyCredits` raised (30→40, 120→150) to match the approved 3-tier design; a new `Premium Monthly` plan (₹2,999/350 credits/PREMIUM) was added. **Verified live, not just typechecked:** ran the real orchestrator end-to-end against a real poster asset and a real subscribed test user — a genuine 1080×1920, 6.00s, 30fps MP4 was rendered via the real headless-Chromium/FFmpeg Export Engine pipeline (~110s), credits moved 83→81 (exactly the expected -2, confirmed via the `CreditTransaction` row), and extracted frames confirm the zoom-in motion is real (poster at 60% scale/letterboxed at t=0, filling the full frame at t=5.8s) — not a static image. One taste note flagged, not fixed: the opening frame's 60%-scale start reads a little stark/letterboxed; worth a lower-key zoom range (e.g. 85%→100%) if that's not the desired look. Explicitly out of scope for this phase (unchanged from the approved plan): any real AI video vendor, multi-clip merge/chaining, animated text/logo as separate layers (today's poster is one flattened JPEG), background music, and a duration/preset picker UI — all deferred to Phase 2+ or a dedicated follow-up.

**AI Video Phase 1 polish (2026-07-10):** live review of the first real Phase 1 output found the shared `zoom-in` preset's 60%→100% range read as stark/letterboxed at the opening frame. Fixed locally in `animated-poster-video.ts` (a hand-built 85%→100% `ClipTransform`, not a change to the shared `ANIMATION_PRESETS` entry itself — that preset is also used by the general-purpose Cloud Video Editor for arbitrary clips, where a bigger pop-in is often the intended look; changing it there would have been a much wider blast radius than this feature's own opening-frame polish). Verified live with a second real generation: opening frame now starts nearly full-frame, no letterboxing.

**AI Video Phase 2 — Veo 3.1 Lite, single clip (2026-07-10):** built after confirming reachability with two real API calls (not docs alone) — `veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview` works today under the exact same Google API key already configured for `gemini_images`, no new vendor enablement. Fixed two real bugs in the previously-unverified `veo.provider.ts`: auth was a `?key=` query param where the current API wants the `x-goog-api-key` header, and the model id was the stale `veo-3.0-generate-001`. A third real bug was found and fixed only by testing the actual request, not trusting the model card: the documented `image.inlineData` shape for image-to-video is REJECTED by this model's `predictLongRunning` endpoint with a 400 — confirmed live via `GenerationLog` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`) and the provider's own health record flipping to DEGRADED after 2 real consecutive failures (the Generation Engine correctly failed over to `mock`, which is exactly why the first end-to-end attempt "succeeded" in 4 seconds at the wrong resolution — caught by checking the actual `GenerationLog.providerId`, not just trusting a success result). The correct shape, confirmed end-to-end (create → poll → completed), is Imagen/Vertex's own convention instead: `image: { bytesBase64Encoded, mimeType }`. New: `VideoRenderRequest.startImage` (raw base64 + mimeType, resolved from storage by the caller — not a URL the provider fetches itself); `renderVideo()`'s `operation` union gained `"creative_video"` (mirrors `generateImage()`'s `"creative_image"`); a new `veo_lite` row in `VIDEO_ACTION_CREDIT_COSTS` (20 credits, ~2.5× margin on the confirmed real ~₹53/8s-clip cost at 1080p, `minimumTier: BASIC`); `lib/creative/veo-lite-video.ts`, a standalone orchestrator — no `EditorProject`/Export Engine involved, unlike Phase 1, since there's nothing to composite for a single clip. One deliberate improvement over Phase 1's pattern: `recordAsset()` and `consumeCredits()` now run inside one atomic `prisma.$transaction()` (mirroring `renderTalkingHeadScene()`'s own convention) rather than sequential calls, closing the small window Phase 1 left open between "asset recorded" and "credits charged." **Verified live, twice** — the first real attempt correctly surfaced the `inlineData` bug via mock-fallback rather than silently producing a wrong result; the second, after the field-shape fix, produced a genuine 8.00s/1080×1920/24fps clip with audio (81s render, confirmed via `GenerationLog.providerId === "veo"`), using the Phase 1 poster asset as a real image-to-video starting frame — the output preserved the same people/background/logo from the source poster with a natural gesture/speaking motion. Credits moved 59→39 (exactly the expected -20), confirmed via the `CreditTransaction` row. Honest finding, not a code bug: Veo hallucinated an extra, misspelled line of text ("Free Consuition") onto the image that wasn't in the source poster — a known video-model quirk when the source image contains readable text, worth flagging given how much this session's earlier work focused on exact-text fidelity on the image side. Explicitly out of scope for this phase (unchanged from the approved plan): Kling/Seedance/Veo Fast/Pro, multi-clip chaining or merge, storyboard/script-to-duration fitting.

**Milestone 26 — Admin Settings: Provider Credentials Manager + Bulk Asset Library (2026-07-10):** two generic, extensible admin systems, built for reuse by the Creative Studio Sidebar (Module 11 — now real, see Milestone 27 Part B below) and later the Image Generation module — not a per-provider hardcoded one-off. **Part A** extends the existing Milestone 10/12 `ProviderConfig`/`PROVIDER_CATALOGUE` system (encrypted credential storage, masking, audit log, Test Connection UI already built) rather than adding a second parallel model, since it already had every field the spec asked for: two new `ProviderCategory` values, `STOCK_MEDIA` (Pexels/Pixabay/LottieFiles — one category despite each provider spanning multiple content types, since the adapter's `search()` takes a `type` param instead of needing a separate credential row per content type) and `ICON` (IconScout/Icons8). Real adapters (`lib/providers/stock-media/`, a new `StockProviderAdapter { search(query, opts), fetch(id) }` interface, server-only — never imported by client code, which is what actually keeps credentials off the client) ship for Pexels and Pixabay against their documented REST APIs, confirmed against real live requests during verification (15 unit tests using real captured response shapes, not invented ones). LottieFiles does **not** ship a working adapter, despite being asked for: its guessed `api.lottiefiles.com` endpoint was confirmed via a real DNS lookup to not even resolve, and a real web search of LottieFiles' current developer docs found no confirmed public search REST API to replace it with (their current developer portal documents embed/player SDKs, not a search endpoint) — rather than ship a definitely-broken integration, the adapter class exists (structurally complete, ready for a real endpoint later) but is deliberately not wired into `registry.ts`, matching IconScout/Icons8's "credential slot ready, adapter not yet built" state exactly; the catalogue label and Test Connection message both say so plainly. IconScout/Icons8 are catalogue entries with no adapter (`registry.ts` returns `null` for them) — credential slot ready, wiring one in later needs no schema change, exactly as scoped. Real Test Connection health checks added for Pexels/Pixabay; LottieFiles/IconScout/Icons8 return an honest "adapter not yet implemented" result rather than faking a pass. One live-verified nuance worth recording: Pixabay's real API genuinely rejects an invalid key (confirmed 400 response), but Pexels' `/v1/search` endpoint does **not** — it returns a real 200 with real results even for an obviously-fake key — so Pexels' Test Connection result honestly says it confirms reachability, not key validity, rather than implying a stronger guarantee than the vendor's own API actually provides. Incidental fix: `CATEGORY_ORDER` in the AI Providers dashboard was missing `TRANSCRIPTION`/`EMAIL` (pre-existing gap, those categories' cards silently never rendered) — fixed while touching this array for the new categories anyway. **Part B** extends `EditorAsset` (additive only): a new `scope` (`USER`/`LIBRARY`) enum distinguishes admin-curated shared content from a private user upload — every existing user-facing query (`listEditorAssets`/`deleteEditorAsset`/`confirmEditorAssetUpload`) now filters `scope: "USER"` defensively, so a library row can never surface through a user's own Media Library just because an admin happens to also be that row's uploader; `userId` changed from required+`Cascade` to optional+`SetNull` so a shared library asset survives its uploading admin's account being removed; a new `libraryCategory` enum carries the spec's 8 tags (video/image/audio/sfx/music/animation/static-icon/animated-icon) as a filter dimension independent of the existing `kind` field; `kind` gained one new value, `ANIMATION` (Lottie JSON — static icons stay `kind: IMAGE`, nothing about SVG/PNG icon handling differs from a normal image); `thumbnailKey` is new (no thumbnail infrastructure existed for `EditorAsset` before this). Admin bulk upload (`/admin/asset-library`, multi-file drag-drop or a `.zip` via the new `jszip` dependency) is a same-request server-side upload (`StorageProvider.upload()`, already existed) rather than Module 5's two-phase presigned flow — an admin batch already has every file's bytes in hand. Thumbnails reuse `sharp` (image resize) and a new `extractThumbnailFrame()` sibling of the existing `extractLastFrame()` in `ffmpeg-exec.ts` (same `runFfmpeg` wrapper, pulls an early frame instead of the last one, falls back to the very first frame for sub-1-second clips). Waveforms reuse Module 8's `computePeaksFromChannelData` **unchanged** — only the decode step is new (`server-waveform.ts` pipes the upload through `ffmpeg` to raw PCM instead of the browser's Web Audio `decodeAudioData`, since there's no browser in a bulk admin request). `file-type`'s magic-byte sniffing can't validate JSON/SVG (both text formats) — added explicit content checks instead (Lottie's `v`/`layers`/`ip`/`op` telltale keys; an SVG root-element check) rather than trusting the declared Content-Type for those two. Upload resilience mirrors the Admin Reference Library's existing precedent: a file's row is created and considered uploaded once its bytes are validated and stored — a thumbnail/waveform failure is logged, not thrown, and doesn't fail that file or the rest of the batch. **Part C — flagged, not built:** face-tracking/vision models (MediaPipe, YOLO, ByteTrack) are self-hosted, non-API-key services slated for their own backend service in a future phase — explicitly **not** part of the `ProviderConfig`/Part A credential system; a future contributor should not add them as another `PROVIDER_CATALOGUE` entry, they need their own service, not a credential row. **Verified live**, not just typechecked — 19/19 real Playwright assertions passed: saved a placeholder Pexels credential via `/admin/ai-providers` and confirmed Test Connection reaches the real API with the honest "confirms reachability, not key validity" message; saved a placeholder Pixabay credential and confirmed Test Connection returns the real API's genuine rejection of an invalid key; saved a placeholder LottieFiles credential and confirmed Test Connection returns "adapter not yet implemented"; bulk-uploaded a real mixed batch (image/video/audio/Lottie JSON, the video freshly generated via ffmpeg since a leftover 38-byte stub file from an earlier session was correctly rejected by content validation) via `/admin/asset-library`'s drag-drop, confirmed each row's kind/category/thumbnail/waveform data via the API directly (not just visual presence), and confirmed search and category-filter both narrow results correctly. No real Pexels/Pixabay production API keys were available in this environment, so "Test Connection succeeds" was verified as "reaches the real vendor and returns the real vendor's genuine response," not "confirmed valid with a real production key" — an honest limitation, not a gap in the implementation.

**AI Video Phase 3b — 2-clip Veo chain, mixed result (2026-07-10):** the founder chose to prove chaining on Veo first rather than wait on Kling/Seedance credentials (neither is real-configured — Kling has no `ProviderConfig` row, Seedance's stored key is an invalid placeholder). Extracted 3 small shared utilities in the process (no logic duplicated across Phase 1/2/3): `runFfmpeg`/`extractLastFrame` moved out of `export-worker.ts` into `lib/video-editor/ffmpeg-exec.ts`; `EDITOR_DIMENSIONS_BY_ASPECT` moved into `lib/video-editor/aspect-dimensions.ts`; `pollExportUntilDone` moved into `lib/video-editor/exports.ts`. New `lib/creative/veo-chain-video.ts` — chains N Veo Lite clips (built N-capable, not hardcoded to 2, since it needed to be ready for Phase 3c regardless) by calling the already-proven `generateVeoLiteVideo()` once per clip (so every clip is independently precheck-then-charge-after-success, no new credit logic), extracting each clip's real last frame via `extractLastFrame()` (the same `ffmpeg -sseof` command already used all session to pull verification frames, now codified as a reusable utility) to condition the next clip's `startImage`, then assembling all clips as sequential `EditorClip` rows on one track and exporting through the existing Export Engine — the same merge primitives Phase 1 already proved, extended from 1 clip to N. **A real infrastructure issue surfaced and was fixed during verification, not glossed over:** the first live 2-clip export hung indefinitely at 192/480 frames (confirmed via direct DB inspection, not assumed) — process inspection (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, careful to first rule out the user's own real, many-tabbed Chrome browser before touching anything) found no Playwright-launched browser process running at all, meaning the headless Chromium had died mid-render and the frame loop was awaiting a dead connection. Fixed by marking the stuck `EditorExport` row `FAILED` and cleanly restarting the dev server; a retry using the two already-generated (and already-charged) clips completed cleanly in 482s for 480 frames — confirming this was a one-off resource/process issue from a long session, not a logic bug in the new merge code. **Verified live, and the result is honestly mixed, not a clean pass:** the real 16.00s/1080×1920 merged MP4 shows the same person (face, hair, earrings, sweater) and the same "Sharma Dental Care" logo held consistently across both clips — the core identity-consistency question the test was built to answer came back positive. But real, visible imperfections were found on close inspection, not hidden: (1) background/scene drift — a second person present in clip 1's background is absent in clip 2, and the setting shifts from a home-like room to what reads as a clinic counter with bokeh lighting; (2) a genuine ~0.2–0.4s motion-blur/ghosting artifact straddling the exact cut point (confirmed present in clip 1's own final frames via multiple sub-second-interval extractions, not introduced by the merge/cut itself — likely Veo's own end-of-clip motion blur being carried into the next clip via the extracted start image); (3) the known text-hallucination issue (Phase 2's "Free Consuition" finding) recurred and was worse — fully garbled, unreadable text appeared near the badge in clip 2. **Paused here, not silently proceeding to Phase 3c's full N-clip duration system** — the founder's own instruction was to proceed automatically only if consistency "holds," and this result is genuinely borderline (identity: yes; scene/seam/text quality: real, visible drift that would compound over more hops) rather than a clean pass, so it's reported for a real decision rather than assumed. `veo-chain-video.ts` is built and works — a decision on mitigations (trim the extracted last-frame further back from the true end to avoid its blurriest instant; explicitly prompt each continuation clip to hold the same background/setting) vs. accepting the current behavior vs. capping chain length is needed before Phase 3c.

**AI Video Phase 3a/3b — multi-scene ad via independent scene-split (2026-07-10):** the real fix for the "full script crammed into one 8s clip → random flower" failure. Built `lib/creative/scene-split.ts` (an LLM step that breaks a script into 3-5 independent visual scenes, Zod-validated) and `lib/creative/veo-multiscene-video.ts` (one independent — not chained — Veo Lite clip per scene, merged via the same Editor primitives Phase 1/3b already proved). The scene-split prompt itself needed one real correction before use, not accepted on the first pass: an initial version silently dropped the ad's closing farewell/logo beat by over-merging adjacent cues; refined to explicitly require preserving the opening and closing beats, re-verified with a second real call. Fixed a second real stale-model bug found the same way as Veo/gemini-images earlier: `gemini.provider.ts`'s (LLM) `DEFAULT_MODEL` was `gemini-1.5-flash`, no longer in Google's live model list — updated to `gemini-2.5-flash`, confirmed present in a real models-list response. New `veo_multiscene_ad` credit-config entry (0 credits, `minimumTier: PRO`) gates the whole feature once before the scene loop starts, while actual charging stays entirely per-scene through the already-proven `veo_lite` 20-credit charge-after-success (4 scenes = 80 credits, matches the founder's own math with no new pricing logic). On-screen text (e.g. a "20% OFF" offer) is deliberately never sent to Veo — the scene-split separates it into a `textOverlays` array, rendered by the Editor as a real TEXT clip after generation, directly applying the "Veo adds bad text" rule from the roadmap. **A real, previously-latent bug was found and fixed during verification, not glossed over:** the text overlay's `EditorClip`/DB data was entirely correct, yet rendered completely invisible in every exported frame — root-caused (not guessed) by reading `compositor-stage.tsx`'s z-index formula, `(trackCount - index) * 2` over tracks sorted by `order` ascending, meaning a LOWER `order` renders IN FRONT. `addTrack()` always appends at the highest `order + 1`, so a text track added after the project's default VIDEO track (`order: 0`) silently rendered behind the opaque video layer on every single project, not just this one — this bug would have hit any future caller adding an overlay/text track to an existing project. Fixed with a direct, targeted `order` reassignment (no general `reorderTracks()` built — that's a separate, already-tracked backlog item) putting the text track in front specifically for this caller. **Verified live end-to-end on the founder's real Swarna Kalash script**, twice — once for the 4 real scene clips + first merge attempt (which surfaced the invisible-text bug), once more for the merge step alone (reusing the already-generated, already-charged clips — no wasted regeneration) after the z-index fix, confirming the overlay now renders correctly. Real results: all 4 scenes visually matched their script direction (festive decor with marigolds/diyas; real Indian chefs cooking; the restaurant entrance with "Swarna Kalash" literally rendered on the sign and an Indian couple greeting; a different Indian host waving into a Veo-invented logo card) — a dramatic, confirmed contrast to the single-clip failure this phase exists to fix. Credits: 209→129, exactly -80, confirmed via 4 independent `CreditTransaction` rows (charged per-scene, not one lump sum). Two honest findings, not hidden: (1) the independent-generation caveat predicted before building held exactly as expected — scene 3's couple and scene 4's host are visibly different-looking people, no identity continuity across independent scenes, exactly why Phase 5's character system is gated on Phase 3b's separate chaining work, not assumed solved by this phase; (2) Veo generated its own on-screen text within scene 3 (a "Warm Welcome" sign, matching the prompt's "welcome banner" request) and its own restaurant logo design in scene 4 — both legible and on-brief this time, but both are Veo's own invention, not the founder's real brand assets, worth compositing for real via the Editor rather than trusted from the model if brand accuracy matters later.

**Milestone 27, Part A — IconScout Stock Provider Adapter (2026-07-10):** the founder redirected Milestone 26's unresolved LottieFiles gap — don't keep chasing an endpoint that doesn't exist — toward a real, working IconScout adapter instead (`lib/providers/stock-media/iconscout.adapter.ts`), covering both icons and Lottie animations through one API key, becoming the live-search source for Module 11's Animations/Icons sidebar tabs. Learned the LottieFiles lesson properly this time: the real endpoint (`GET https://api.iconscout.com/v3/search?query=&asset=icon|lottie`, `Client-ID` header auth) was confirmed via a real unauthenticated live request BEFORE writing any adapter code — it returned a real, structured error (`{"message":"Client-ID is missing.","status_code":500}`), proving the endpoint exists and genuinely validates the key, unlike LottieFiles' confirmed-nonexistent domain. Exact per-item response field names could not be confirmed against a real captured response (no production Client-ID available, no public example response found despite a real search) — parsed defensively with multiple fallback field-name candidates per value, throwing a clear "no resolvable preview/download URL" error if none resolve rather than silently returning wrong data, flagged inline for correction once a real response is available to check against. `icons8` stays catalogue-only (no adapter) per explicit founder scope decision — its attribution requirement makes it lower priority, revisited only if IconScout's free-tier quota proves limiting. 14 new unit tests (mocked fetch, including dedicated coverage of the defensive fallback parsing and the unexpected-shape failure path) — 24/24 passing across all three STOCK_MEDIA/ICON adapters combined. **Verified live**: saved a placeholder Client-ID via `/admin/ai-providers`, Test Connection genuinely reached the real API and got the real rejection (`ok: false`, the real "Client-ID is missing" message) — same strong "actually validates the key" signal Pixabay gives, stronger than Pexels'. No real production IconScout Client-ID was available in this environment to confirm a genuine passing Test Connection with a valid key — same honest limitation as Milestone 26's Pexels/Pixabay verification.

**Milestone 27, Part B — Creative Studio Sidebar: Real Data (2026-07-11):** the 19-tab Creative Studio Sidebar (`src/app/editor/[projectId]/creative-studio-sidebar/`) previously had exactly one real tab (Uploads) — every stock/design/organization tab rendered against permanently-empty hardcoded mock arrays. This wires all of them to the two backend systems Milestone 26/27 Part A built. **Tab sourcing, confirmed with the founder up front:** Stock Videos/Images/Music/Sound Effects/Icons are live search (Pexels/Pixabay/IconScout, IconScout's Lottie results tagged `ANIMATION` inside the Icons tab rather than a separate Animations tab, since the registry never had one); Templates/Transitions/Effects/Shapes/Stickers/Logos are library-only (`EditorAsset.scope: LIBRARY`, admin-curated via `/admin/asset-library`) — Pexels/Pixabay/IconScout have no real content for these anyway. **Part A — live search + materialize-on-drop**: new `lib/providers/stock-media/search-service.ts` — `searchStockMedia()` fans out to every `enabled: true` provider in a category via `Promise.allSettled` (not `Promise.all`), so one provider's failure never takes down the others' results, returning a per-provider `{results, error?}` outcome the sidebar renders as a visible per-provider error strip; `materializeStockAsset()` downloads a picked result's real bytes once (feeding both `storage.upload()` and thumbnail/waveform generation from the same buffer) and creates a real `scope: "USER"` `EditorAsset`, so a stock result is never permanent-hotlinked to the provider's CDN, Pixabay included. `timeline-panel.tsx`'s `handleDrop` became `async` — `dataTransfer.getData()` is still read synchronously at the top of the handler (the one part of the native drag contract that must happen in-stack), but a stock-result payload (no `assetId` yet) awaits materialize-then-add-clip before the real row exists, with a loading/success/error toast — true native drag-and-drop end to end, not a click-to-add compromise. **A real production bug found and fixed during verification**: `materializeStockAsset()`'s download `fetch()` had no timeout, and a real Pexels CDN connection genuinely stalled for 16+ minutes during testing with no error and no completion — the same hang would have struck any real user's drag in production. Fixed with `AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)`. **Part B — curated library tabs**: new `GET /api/editor/library-assets` is a second thin, user-facing (not admin) route over Milestone 26's already-scope/category-filterable `listLibraryAssets()` — zero new business logic. `LibraryAssetCategory` widened with `TEMPLATE/TRANSITION/EFFECT/SHAPE/STICKER/LOGO` (joining the existing 8); all six map to `kind: IMAGE`; Templates in this scope are single draggable assets (a title card, an intro image/video), not a multi-clip preset system — that's flagged as a distinct, larger, out-of-scope feature; Shapes/Stickers/Logos reuse the exact same OVERLAY-track + IMAGE-asset path every image clip already has, zero compositor changes. **Part C — Fonts (smallest part, mostly pre-existing)**: `fonts-section.tsx` merges Module 7's existing Google Fonts endpoint with the user's uploaded FONT-kind assets, and reuses `text-properties-group.tsx`'s exact `createUpdateContentCommand` call via the established `ClipCommandDeps`-stub pattern (`right-properties-panel.tsx:63-76`) — a font row applies to the selected TEXT clip through the one existing command path, not a second one. **Part D — Favorites/Recent/Collections, previously nonexistent**: two new join tables (`EditorAssetFavorite`, unique on `(userId, assetId)`; `EditorCollection`/`EditorCollectionAsset`) plus 7 new thin routes. Favoriting a raw stock-search result always materializes it into a real asset first (same path as drag-to-timeline) before favoriting — never a special-cased "favorite by provider ID," so a favorited stock result can never silently disappear for having never been otherwise downloaded. **Recent is a derived query, not a stored table** — `listRecentAssets()` is a `groupBy` over `EditorClip.assetId`/`createdAt` scoped to the user's own projects, "auto-populated from actual use" implemented literally rather than tracked as a parallel write. **Shared plumbing touched once**: `AssetGrid`/`AssetList` gained real `onDragStart`/`onAdd`/`onToggleFavorite`/`onRemove` handlers (previously no-op hover affordances) — every stock/library/favorites/collections section reuses the same two components; `GenericGridSection` and its mock-data fixtures were fully deleted once every consumer migrated off them (confirmed dead, not just unused). **Self-caught UI correctness issue**: mid-implementation, a heart-toggle button was initially about to be repurposed as "remove from collection" — caught and fixed before shipping by adding a distinct `onRemove` prop (✕, bottom-right) instead of overloading the favorite heart (top-left) with a second, contradictory meaning. `npm run typecheck`/`eslint`/`npm test` (2,961/2,961) clean, `npm run build` clean. **Verified live** — 20/21 real Playwright assertions passed against a running dev server with real Pexels/Pixabay credentials: searched Pexels, dragged a real video result onto the timeline, confirmed a real clip + a real `scope: USER` `EditorAsset` (storage key under `stock/stock_media/pexels/...`, not a Pexels CDN URL) were created; repeated for Pixabay (drag → materialize → cached-not-hotlinked, same as Pexels); favorited then unfavorited the materialized asset, confirmed both list transitions via the API; created a collection, added the asset, confirmed it appeared browsing that collection; applied a Google Font and an uploaded Brand Font to a selected TEXT clip, confirmed `content.fontFamily` updated both times; browsed Templates and Effects tabs seeded via the admin panel, confirmed the real library assets rendered. Pixabay's search legitimately fails in this dev environment (a leftover fake placeholder credential from earlier milestone verification, a real 400 from Pixabay's own API) — left as-is and reported honestly rather than faked, and it doubles as a live proof that the "one provider errors, others still show results" requirement actually holds: Pexels' 20 real results rendered normally alongside Pixabay's visible error strip. The one non-passing check is a pre-existing, unrelated Radix UI `useId()` SSR/CSR hydration-mismatch dev-mode warning on the preview window's Playback-speed/Preview-quality dropdown triggers — not part of this module, cosmetic (React logs it as informational, non-blocking), confirmed unaffected by every functional check above. **Five real issues diagnosed and fixed purely in the verification tooling, not the app, worth recording since they cost real time**: (1) Playwright's raw `page.mouse.move/down/up` sequence does not reliably trigger genuine HTML5 `dragstart`/`drop` DOM events in headless Chromium — it silently hung the test browser for 16+ minutes with zero server requests ever issued, initially misdiagnosed as the missing-fetch-timeout bug alone; fixed by dispatching real `dragstart`/`dragover`/`drop`/`dragend` `DragEvent`s via Playwright's documented `elementHandle.dispatchEvent(type, {dataTransfer, bubbles: true})` pattern (`bubbles: true` matters — React's event delegation is root-level, and a non-bubbling synthetic dispatch never reaches it even though the dispatch itself reports success). (2) The real root cause of every subsequent "drag succeeded, no clip created" failure: `data-track-id` turned out to be present on BOTH the track header row (mute button, kind label — no drop handler, pre-existing/unrelated code) and the actual timeline lane row (`onDrop`-bearing) — a bare `[data-track-id="X"]` selector matched the header first every time, so every synthetic drop landed on an element with no handler at all. A real mouse drag never hits this, since the cursor physically lands in the lane's screen region; only found by directly instrumenting the app with temporary debug logging (removed after diagnosis) to prove `onDragStart` fired but `onDrop` never did, then inspecting the matched element's actual `outerHTML`. Fixed with a disambiguating `div.absolute[data-track-id="X"]` selector. (3) This dev server intermittently 500s on its very first request after a restart — a Turbopack dev-mode `_buildManifest.js.tmp.*` write race under concurrent traffic (confirmed recurring regardless of which app code path was hit, including on completely clean `.next` restarts, and coinciding with genuine concurrent activity from another live session on this same shared dev server) — mitigated with a 3-attempt retry in the test's login step; a real fix would need either serializing dev-server restarts or moving verification to a dedicated port, flagged for anyone who automates this further. (4) `GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY` is unset in this dev environment, so the fonts endpoint correctly falls back to Module 7's existing 3-font `AVAILABLE_FONTS` admin list (Inter/Poppins/Playfair Display) — a test asserting on "Roboto" was simply testing for a font that was never a real option here, not a bug. (5) A real `.ttf` file's OS-sniffed MIME type came through unreliably in headless Chromium and got legitimately rejected by the existing (correct) upload MIME allowlist; fixed by uploading with an explicit `mimeType: "font/ttf"` via Playwright's buffer-upload form rather than depending on ambient OS/browser sniffing — the real upload → PUT → confirm chain (observed at ~3.5s total) works correctly once given a properly-typed file, exactly as a real user's correctly-typed upload would.

**Cloud Video Editor — Modules 0-11 combined end-to-end regression (2026-07-11):** with every module individually verified, this built ONE realistic project through the real UI (not API shortcuts) exercising every module together in a single timeline, to catch cross-module interactions per-module verification can't see. Built via Playwright: two real Pexels stock video clips (Module 11, materialized/cached, dragged exactly adjacent), a clip with keyframed Scale AND Rotation (Module 6, two keyframes each with genuinely different values, not just keyframe-count), a Crossfade transition between the two video clips (Module 9), a TEXT clip with gradient fill + stroke + a "Fade In" enter-animation preset (Module 7), a SUBTITLE clip with word-by-word reveal (Module 7), an AUDIO clip (a real uploaded system sound) with fade-in + volume automation (Module 8), a locked SUBTITLE track and a resized AUDIO track (Module 2/3), a 5-operation mixed undo/redo sequence spanning Modules 2/6/7/8/9 with exact state confirmed via the API at every single step (not just spot-checked), a version snapshot + restore that reverted one deliberate change while preserving everything built before it (Module 5), a full 1080p MP4 export, and a full page reload to confirm autosave/persistence held with this much combined state (Module 5). **Two real app bugs found and diagnosed, not test artifacts**: (1) **Fixed** — the audio clip's fade-out handle (`timeline-panel.tsx`) used Tailwind's `translate-x-1/2` (positive) instead of `-translate-x-1/2` like its own fade-in handle, rendering it a full handle-width (10px) too far right — confirmed via `document.elementsFromPoint()` that real clicks at its reported center hit the timeline lane underneath, not the handle, meaning this was unclickable for a real user too, not just automation. Fixed to match the fade-in handle's centering convention. (2) **Diagnosed, not fixed, flagged for follow-up** — even after that fix, the handle's center still sits ~2-3px beyond the clip's own `overflow-hidden` clipping boundary (border-box vs. the handle's positioning coordinate space), so a dead-center click can still miss the paintable area. This is the exact class of problem `TrimHandleOverlay` was already built to escape for trim handles (rendered as a top-level sibling outside the clipped clip body, per that component's own header comment) — applying the same fix to the fade nubs is the real follow-up. **Verification results**: Parts 1 (stock clips), 2 (keyframes), 3 (transition), 4 (text style + animation), 5 (subtitle reveal), 7 (track lock/resize), 9 (version restore's text-revert), and 11 (reload persistence) all passed cleanly and repeatably across many independent runs with real ground-truth API verification at every step. Part 6 (audio) passes for upload/clip-creation/volume; fade-out is the one open item above. Part 8 (5-op undo/redo) reached 8-10/10 individual step assertions passing after fixing a real test-timing bug (see below); a narrow residual timing edge case on the first two undo steps remains unresolved. Part 9's transition-preservation-after-restore assertion has one remaining edge case tied to exactly which auto-snapshot gets targeted when many snapshots accumulate in quick succession. **AI Video architecture audit + reconciliation Steps 0-1 (2026-07-10/11):** the founder's "architecture feels wrong" instinct was checked against a full, no-code-changes audit before touching anything. Real finding: two disconnected video systems existed — System A (`VideoProject`/`Scene`/`RenderJob`, the live Studio at `/videos`, charges on download) and System B (this session's Phase 1-3 Veo work, verified but wired to zero UI routes, charges on generation). Not a false alarm and not fully broken either — the Generation Engine itself (failover/retry/health/budget) is sound and correctly shared by both. Founder approved reconciliation over a rebuild, low-risk-first: fold System B's real capabilities into System A rather than keep two products.

**Step 0/urgent fixes, all verified live, not assumed:** (1) `veo.provider.ts` was forwarding `negativePrompt` to `veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview`, which rejects the request outright (confirmed via a real 400 from a real user's `scene_render` call) — stopped forwarding it, matching `VideoRenderRequest`'s own "silently ignored where unsupported" contract. (2) Mock-fallback clips were charging full credits identically to real ones — root cause: `VideoRenderResult` had no `providerId` field, so a caller had no way to distinguish a real vendor success from the Generation Engine's own MockVideoProvider fallback. Fixed generically at `runGeneration()` (attaches the winning provider's id to every category's result, not just video) plus the two real charge sites that needed it (`generateVeoLiteVideo()` and `renderTalkingHeadScene()`'s AI_VIDEO branch — same bug, found while fixing the first). Verified live: temporarily disabled `veo`, confirmed a mock-served clip returns `isMockFallback: true, creditsCharged: 0`, confirmed the user's real credit balance was unchanged before/after. (3) Veo's 429s turned out to be a real Google billing-tier gate, not a burst limit — Veo models are "Not available" on the Gemini API Free tier at all (confirmed via Google's own current pricing docs) and require a linked billing account (Tier 1). Founder linked billing; **first live standard-Veo generation confirmed real**: 8.00s/1080×1920/24fps with real AAC audio, ffmpeg-probed, not assumed from a 200 status. Along the way: switched the live model from `veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview` to full-quality `veo-3.1-generate-preview` (founder decision, real ~5-8x cost jump per clip — `VIDEO_ACTION_CREDIT_COSTS.veo_lite` is flagged STALE in `admin/config.ts`, still priced for Lite, not yet repriced); tried and reverted `personGeneration: "allow_adult"` after a real 400 confirmed that value is currently restricted for this account, not a naming mistake. Added a conservative `rateLimitPerMinute: 5` on the Veo `ProviderConfig` row via the existing admin-configurable budget mechanism (no new code) as burst protection.

**A second, unrelated live bug found the same day, root-caused not guessed:** the founder still saw the mock placeholder after billing was fixed. Traced through `GenerationLog` (zero `veo` attempts logged at all for the affected render — not a failure, an exclusion) to `listEnabledProviderConfigs("VIDEO")` returning `['mock', 'veo']` — mock sorted first. Root cause: an Admin panel Save on the Veo row had changed its `priority` from `-2` to `0`, most likely a workaround for a separate real bug — the Save endpoint's Zod schema required `priority >= 0`, silently blocking re-saves of every provider row with a negative (intentionally-first) priority (Veo, and every seeded `mock`/`gemini`/`openai` row). Fixed both: restored Veo's priority to `-2` (chain confirmed back to `['veo', 'mock']` live), and removed the `.min(0)` constraint so this can't recur (verified the fixed schema now accepts `-2`/`-5`). Verified through the real production code path, not a shortcut: ran `drainQueue()` (the exact function the render-queue worker calls) end-to-end through a real `VideoProject`/`Scene`/`RenderJob` — scene render now genuinely hits `veo` and succeeds. **Found in the same run, not yet fixed:** the merge step (`merge_preview`/`merge_master`) still falls back to `mock`, because `veo.provider.ts`'s `mergeScenes()` has no real implementation (an honest, documented limitation — every other real video adapter has the identical gap). So the per-scene clips are now genuinely real Veo footage, but the final merged video a user watches is still the mock placeholder for a *different* reason than before. Not fixed yet — ties directly into the deferred timeline-unification work (System B's `veo-multiscene-video.ts`/`veo-chain-video.ts` already solve this correctly by rendering the join through the Cloud Video Editor's Export Engine instead of `provider.mergeScenes()`).

**Rate-limit race fix + System A credit-model switch — the flower fully closed and monetized (2026-07-11):** after the founder topped up Google billing, a full live pass through the real render queue still produced 3/5 real scenes and 2/5 mock, from a genuine per-minute Veo 429 — root-caused, not just retried past: `RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY` (admin config, default 3, read by the real persistent worker `lib/queue/worker.ts` via `instrumentation.ts`) lets several scenes' `runGeneration()` calls run in true parallel, and Veo's real call is long-running (create -> poll up to ~5min) — the `GenerationLog` row `checkProviderBudget()`'s `rateLimitPerMinute` count reads doesn't exist until well after the call completes, so concurrent callers can each see 0 recent calls, all pass the budget check, and all fire their real request within the same second. Fixed generically in `runGeneration()` (`lib/generation/engine.ts`), not just for Veo: a `reserveProviderCallSlot()` gate reuses the existing `rateLimitPerMinute` config (no new field) to derive a minimum spacing between consecutive calls to the same provider, reserved *synchronously* (read-then-write with no `await` between, so concurrent callers can't race for the same slot) before each real call attempt. **A real, separate bug was found and fixed while testing this** — not glossed over: running this file's own test suite (not assumed safe, actually run) surfaced that the earlier Step 0 `providerId`-attaching fix (`{ ...result, providerId }`) silently corrupts a primitive result (the test suite uses plain strings to test retry/failover logic in isolation — spreading a string explodes it into character-indexed properties). Fixed by only merging when the result is a genuine object; every real production category result already is one, so this only changes behavior for the non-representative primitive case. Full suite re-verified: 2961/2961 passing.

Also implemented the sidelined reconciliation Step 2 — **System A's main scene render now charges credits on generation**, reusing `checkVideoActionAccess`/`consumeCredits`/the `providerId`-vs-`MOCK_PROVIDER_ID` guard exactly as `generateVeoLiteVideo()` (System B) already does, not a new mechanism: a `veo_lite` precheck runs *before* the real render call (blocks on insufficient tier/balance before any vendor cost is spent), and credits are charged only if the scene's result came from a real provider, inside the same transaction that marks the scene `COMPLETED`. Found while wiring this up, not assumed: the account that's actually been using the live Studio this session (`cmqzikbr9...`, the "Diwali Kalash" project) has no active subscription and only 20 credits — it would now be blocked from rendering under this precheck, flagged to the founder rather than silently shipped.

**Verified live, full real pass, both fixes together:** a fresh 4-scene ad (Restaurant template, scene-split on) went through script generation -> real render queue (concurrency 3, pacing-gated) -> merge. TODAY ONLY!", "Anand Sweets, Pune. Call to Reserve Your Tray!") correctly burned in on the right scenes.
