**Cloud Video Editor: TEXT/SUBTITLE-behind-VIDEO z-index bug fixed at its general root cause, plus the residual fade-out handle clipping and an undo/redo timing question resolved (2026-07-11).** The combined Module 0-11 regression pass above had surfaced a core-workflow blocker: any TEXT/SUBTITLE track added to a project already containing VIDEO rendered invisible, both live and in real exports. Traced before touching any code: `compositor-stage.tsx`'s `baseZ = (trackCount - index) * 2` z-index formula and `timeline-panel.tsx`'s own track-panel listing sort are the *same* array (tracks ascending by `order`) — a lower `order` is already both the topmost row in the panel and the topmost layer in the composite, consistent with each other. The formula was never the bug. The actual defect was in `addTrack()` (`lib/video-editor/tracks.ts`): every new track was assigned `order = last.order + 1`, unconditionally appending at the bottom of both the panel and the composite — backwards from what any editor user expects when adding an overlay onto existing video. Fixed generically: `addTrack()` now prepends (`edge.order - 1`, reading the current lowest `order`) for every track kind except AUDIO, which keeps appending since it has no compositor-visual-stacking role. This replaced, rather than added to, two now-redundant narrow one-off workarounds (`lib/creative/veo-multiscene-video.ts`, `lib/scenes/merge-via-editor.ts`) that had each manually reassigned a text track's order after calling `addTrack()` — both removed along with their now-unused `prisma` imports. New `lib/video-editor/track-stacking.ts` extracts the pure z-index math (`computeTrackZIndex`/`computeTrackZIndexByOrder`) out of `compositor-stage.tsx` so it's independently unit-testable, following this codebase's established DB-bound-service/pure-logic-extraction split; `track-stacking.test.ts` (7 tests) directly encodes the reported bug scenario (a TEXT track added after VIDEO must land above it) plus SUBTITLE-after-TEXT, OVERLAY, a second VIDEO track, the AUDIO exemption, and exact alignment with `createProject()`'s real VIDEO(0)+AUDIO(1) seeding.

**Audio fade-out handle's residual 2-3px overflow-clipping (flagged, not yet fixed, in the prior regression entry) also fixed**, using the same interaction-overlay-extraction principle as `TrimHandleOverlay`'s own Bug #3 fix: each fade nub is a 10px circle centered exactly on the clip edge (`-translate-x-1/2`), so ~5px of it is meant to overhang past the clip's own bounds — but the clip's root div is `overflow-hidden` (needed to clip the waveform/label), which was clipping that overhang down to 2-3px of hit-testable/visible handle. Unlike the trim handles, this didn't need a full lift to a lane-level top-level sibling (no cross-clip stacking-context contention here, since clips on the same track never overlap) — `ClipBlock` now returns the fade handles as a plain sibling `<div>` alongside `clipBody`, positioned with the identical `left`/`width`/`top-1 bottom-1` basis but without the clipping container, still owned by the same `startFadeDrag` closure. Verified live: `document.elementsFromPoint()` at the clip's exact right edge now resolves the fade-out nub as the topmost element (previously buried/unreachable there), and a real pointer-drag on it successfully moved `fadeOutMs` from 0 to 667.

**Undo #1/#2 timing question — investigated with reproducible evidence, concluded a test-script artifact, not an app bug.** Built three progressively-refined Playwright diagnostics against the live regression project. The first "clean" attempt (`undo-diag2`) itself turned out to be flawed: a fixed 1000ms "ensure unlocked" setup wait let a slow PATCH land *after* the next operation's own PATCH had already succeeded, corrupting the observed state. Rebuilt with zero fixed waits and full poll-to-confirmation after every single interaction (`undo-diag3`); the clean run showed both undo steps landing exactly as expected (lock toggle then volume change, undone in reverse order, each fully settled before the next assertion). Conclusion: the anomaly seen in the full regression pass was very likely the already-documented flaky transition-popover interaction (a UI action that sometimes doesn't register a real command) shifting expected-state indices by one — a test-script artifact, not a defect in the undo/redo mechanism itself.

**Re-verified after all fixes**: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errors, only pre-existing unrelated warnings), and `vitest run` (111 test files, 2968/2968 passing) all clean; `next build` clean. Because the fix only changes `addTrack()`'s behavior for *newly created* tracks, the existing regression project's TEXT/SUBTITLE tracks (created before the fix, in the old bottom-appending order) were not retroactively corrected — there is no track-reorder feature in this app yet (a gap already called out in Known Issue #10), so re-verification deleted and recreated those two tracks through the real `POST /tracks` API (exercising the actual fixed `addTrack()` code path, not a DB shortcut) with their original clip content restored. Confirmed via the DB that the new tracks landed at `order -1`/`-2`, both above `VIDEO`'s `order 0`. Re-ran a real export (39.5s/1280×720/30fps, ffprobed) and extracted frames at 6s and 7s: both the styled "New Text" (gradient/stroke) and "Subtitle text" clips are now clearly visible over the video in the actual rendered output — the exact symptom the original regression pass caught, now confirmed resolved end-to-end, live and in export.

**AI Film — generation-free structure built end-to-end (2026-07-12), deliberately built while the real Veo/Gemini daily quota was exhausted (see Phase 3b's chained-consistency test) so the founder can test real generation himself the moment it resets, rather than losing a day of build time waiting.** Extends `VideoProject`/`Scene` rather than a parallel model, per the reconciliation lesson already learned twice this week: a `FILM` `VideoProjectSourceType`, a new `FilmCharacter` model (`slotIndex`, up to 2 AI variation Asset ids, optional face-upload side/front Asset ids, `characterSheet` Json, a `FilmCharacterStatus` progression `PENDING → VARIATIONS_READY/FACE_UPLOADED → SELECTED → SHEET_READY`), and a nullable `Scene.filmCharacterId` — storyboard scenes are ordinary `Scene` rows and reuse the entire existing render/merge/credit pipeline, not a second one (migration `20260711181323_add_film_character_and_source_type`). All 6 of the founder's screens now exist as real pages wired to real routes: **Input** (`/create/film` → `POST /api/videos/film`, no generation, just creates the project + character slots); **Character** (AI variations via a real `generateImage()` call per character, a real presigned face-upload path reusing the exact pattern `create/talking-head/page.tsx` already established, and a select action); **Character Sheet** (a real vision-LLM call — `generateScript()` with `imageUrl` + `responseFormat: "json"` — describing the chosen photo into a structured sheet); **Storyboard** (a real LLM scene-planner, `film-storyboard.ts`, mirroring `scene-split.ts`'s proven system-prompt/Zod-validation shape, producing 10-15s scenes each tagged with which character slot appears in it); **Merge** (reuses `mergeScenesViaEditor()` completely unchanged, since final assembly has no dependency on how each scene's clip gets made). All of these are real, callable, credit/tier-gated (`checkVideoActionAccess("film")`, 0 credits/PREMIUM tier — a structural placeholder gate, same pattern `veo_multiscene_ad` already established, real pricing to follow once a real per-clip cost is known) — built but **deliberately not triggered by me**, per the founder's explicit instruction not to spend real generation calls himself. **The one deliberate exception, an honest structural stub, not a shortcut:** `POST /api/videos/film/[id]/scenes/[sceneId]/generate` (the per-scene video generation step) does its real ownership/tier/credit checks and then returns a clear 501 explaining that the character-consistency method is still unresolved — Phase 3b's chained test only has 2 real Variant-A (last-frame-chaining) hops and zero Variant-B (reference-anchoring) data, nowhere near enough to wire a real method without guessing. The Scenes screen's "Generate scene" button surfaces that same explanation rather than silently doing nothing. **Verified live** (the generation-free parts only, nothing that would spend a real API call): logged in via the dev-admin bypass, created a real film project through `POST /api/videos/film` (confirmed 2 `FilmCharacter` rows created, `PENDING` status), loaded `/videos/[id]/film` and confirmed the flow hub's state machine correctly resolves to the Character screen from real DB state, confirmed `/create/film`'s Input screen renders correctly, and confirmed the storyboard/merge routes correctly reject with honest 400s when called before their preconditions are met (characters not yet sheet-ready; no storyboard yet) — proving the guard rails work without ever reaching a provider call. Test project deleted after verification. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint --max-warnings=0` (scoped to every new/touched file), and a clean `next build --turbopack` (after clearing a stale `.next` cache unrelated to this work) all passed.

**What's left is exactly one piece: per-scene generation, gated entirely on Phase 3b's character-consistency question (4a).** Every other part of AI Film — schema, all 6 screens, all other routes, credit gates, merge — is built and would need no further structural work once 4a has an answer. See Section 9's "Later — AI Film" for the founder's step-by-step for tomorrow's test and exactly how its result plugs into finishing this one stub.

**AI Film — character sheet's design locked: photo is the identity anchor, text is supplementary (2026-07-12).** Founder correction on the same day the generation-free structure shipped: text alone can't hold a character consistent (the model re-invents the face each scene) — the character's own stored photo is what actually does that, and it was already sitting unused on `FilmCharacter` (`selectedVariationAssetId`/`faceUploadFrontAssetId`). Confirmed all 3 of the founder's real test characters resolve to genuine, loadable images first (`status: READY`, fetched real bytes over HTTP, not assumed from the DB row alone). Extracted `resolveFilmCharacterReferenceAssetId()` into `lib/film/types.ts` — deliberately a dependency-free file (no `prisma`) since the Character Sheet screen (a Client Component) needed the same face-upload-wins-over-AI-variation priority the sheet-generation route already had inline, and the two must never drift onto different photos for the same character. Two real changes: (1) the **Character Sheet screen** now shows a large, navy-bordered "Identity anchor" photo per character with the vision-LLM's text sheet explicitly labeled "Details (supplementary)" underneath — replacing the old 56px thumbnail sitting equally-weighted beside the text; (2) **`scenes/[id]/generate/route.ts`** (the per-scene generation stub) now does real, live-proven resolution: for any scene with a linked character, it walks `scene.filmCharacterId → FilmCharacter → resolveFilmCharacterReferenceAssetId() → a real Asset row`, the exact same resolution `generateVeoLiteVideo()` already uses for `startImageAssetId` — confirmed via a real HTTP round-trip against a synthetic scene, returning `{ conditioningAssetId, conditioningMethod: "reference_image_anchoring" }` in the 501 body. A b-roll scene with no linked character correctly reports it would stay text-only. **The stub is still a stub — no video provider is called, per-scene generation is still not triggered.** Only the data path (photo → scene) is wired and proven; the consistency METHOD is now decided (reference-image anchoring, i.e. Phase 3b's "Variant B" — every scene of a character conditions on that character's OWN stored photo, not the previous scene's last frame the way chaining/"Variant A" does), but whether it actually holds identity across a real multi-scene film is exactly what the founder's own test tomorrow answers — see Section 9's "Later — AI Film" for the updated tomorrow-plan, which now directly tests this exact method rather than an abstract A-vs-B choice. `tsc`/`eslint` clean; verified live via real HTTP against both a character-linked scene and a b-roll scene, cleaned up after.

**Known Issues #17** (below): the doubled `/uploads/uploads/` URL bug surfaced while confirming character photos are loadable — noted there, not fixed (harmless today, out of scope for this fix, touches a shared route).

**Cloud Video Editor: CapCut-Desktop visual-fidelity pass (2026-07-12) — styling/layout only, zero functional changes, verified live.** The founder attached a CapCut Desktop reference screenshot and asked for the editor's every panel (top bar, left icon rail, media/asset library, preview window, right properties panel, bottom toolbars, timeline) to be visually restyled to match its spacing/density/icon-style — explicitly not a feature pass, with an explicit instruction to stop and ask rather than guess wherever matching the reference would require real functional additions. Three scope-defining questions were resolved with the founder before any code changed: (1) keep this app's own orange accent (`--color-accent-orange`) everywhere rather than adopting CapCut's teal — spacing/density/icon-style only, not hue; (2) the right panel's existing clip-properties groups (Transform/Crop/Blend/Text/Audio) get restyled, but the reference screenshot's "Project/Details tabs + Smart Suggestions + Global Edits" content is a different, currently-nonexistent AI feature and stays out of scope; (3) clip thumbnails get tiled from each clip's real asset thumbnail rather than skipped — this turned out to require a small additive read-path extension (see below), approved as in-scope once that tradeoff was made explicit.

New editor-scoped design tokens added to `globals.css`'s `@theme` block (Tailwind v4 CSS-first theming, no separate `tailwind.config`): `--color-editor-line`/`-surface-1`/`-surface-2` (replacing ~50+ scattered `border-white/10`/`bg-white/5`/`bg-white/10` one-off utility classes across every editor file with three centrally-tunable values), `--text-micro`/`--text-nano` (replacing ad hoc `text-[11px]`/`text-[10px]`), and 9 `--color-track-*` tokens (video/audio/subtitle/text/overlay/effects/voice/music/sfx) pulled out of `timeline-panel.tsx`'s previously-hardcoded `TRACK_COLORS`/`AUDIO_SUBTYPE_COLOR` maps — hue-per-track-kind differentiation is preserved exactly as before, just centrally tunable and muted toward a more cohesive palette. Every editor file's hardcoded chrome classes were migrated to these tokens (bulk-verified via a repo-wide `grep` sweep at the end, confirmed zero stragglers remain inside `src/app/editor/[projectId]/**`). The shared `Button` component (`components/ui/button.tsx`) was deliberately left untouched — the editor is dark via hardcoded utilities, not the app's `.dark` class system, so a new dark-tuned variant wouldn't engage automatically there anyway, and editing the shared component would risk the light marketing/dashboard UI that also consumes it, for no benefit over the already-established per-call-site override convention every editor file already uses.

Per-panel changes: **top bar** restructured to a 3-column grid (back-link + autosave-status on the left, truly centered project name, Undo/Redo/History/Export grouped on the right) — no fabricated "Share" button, since that's not a real feature here. **Left rail** gained a visible icon-above-label under every tab (previously tooltip-only), matching the reference's density. **Media/library panels** moved from a 2-column to 3-column grid with a real duration badge overlaid on every thumbnail — including a parity fix for the Uploads tab's own card component, which had never had a duration badge at all despite every other grid card having one; now reads `asset.durationSeconds`, already-available data, no new query. **Preview window** playback bar reskinned (icon spacing, a divider before the speed/quality/fullscreen cluster); crop-handle and motion-path drag math left untouched. **Right panel** groups/sliders/toggles retoned; command-dispatch logic (`commit`/`liveUpdate`/`commitSingle`) untouched. **Bottom toolbars** gained a `ZoomOut` icon (previously only `ZoomIn`) framing the zoom slider, matching the reference's icon-pair convention. **Timeline**: `PlayheadLine` recolored from `bg-error` (red) to a neutral white line with a small top marker cap — red is reserved for destructive actions and orange is the one interactive accent, so neither should double as "current playback position"; `ClipBlock`'s per-kind background now reads the new `--color-track-*` tokens.

**Clip-thumbnail tiling (the one part of this pass that touches a server query, not just classNames)**: `AssetView` (`src/app/editor/types.ts`) and its backing `EditorAssetView` (`src/lib/video-editor/assets.ts`) gained a `thumbnailUrl: string | null` field, surfacing the already-existing `EditorAsset.thumbnailKey` column through `listEditorAssets()` and its 3 other read-path siblings (`listFavorites()`, `listCollectionAssets()`, `listRecentAssets()` — all updated identically for type consistency). Zero new thumbnail-generation logic, zero migration. `ClipBlock` now renders a tiled (`background-repeat: repeat-x`) background layer behind non-audio clip labels when `asset.thumbnailUrl` is set. **Known, documented gap, not a bug**: `thumbnailKey` is only ever populated by the Admin Asset Library and stock-media materialization paths (`thumbnails.ts`'s two call sites) — a plain "Upload media" clip (most real user clips) still shows no thumbnail, since wiring generation into the upload-confirm flow was explicitly scoped out rather than silently expanding this pass.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errors, same 84 pre-existing unrelated warnings), and `vitest run` (111 files, 2968/2968) all stayed clean after every phase, not just a final pass. `next build` clean (dev server stopped first — running `next dev`/`next build` concurrently against the same `.next` output corrupted it once earlier this session; documented so it doesn't recur). A live Playwright interaction pass covered drag-move, drag-trim, track-header resize, Add Track, split, duplicate, delete, undo, group, and ungroup against the existing regression project. **Three apparent failures in the first pass, all confirmed as test-script artifacts, not regressions, using the same poll-to-confirmation discipline established earlier this session**: (1) fixed-`waitForTimeout` waits were too short/racy for several mutations — fixed by polling the API for the expected state change instead, after which drag-move/split/duplicate immediately passed; (2) a drag-trim attempt failed because `TrimHandleOverlay`'s hit-target (a deliberate prior architectural choice — see that component's own Bug #3 header comment) only mounts once the clip is hovered/selected, which the test hadn't done before attempting the drag — passed once the script hovered first; (3) a track-resize attempt failed because the target track had scrolled below the test's fixed viewport height, not because of any real hit-testing problem — passed once verified against a track guaranteed on-screen. **One genuine, pre-existing bug incidentally discovered while isolating a real "undo doesn't restore a deleted clip" failure** (confirmed with request logging: the DELETE succeeds, but the Undo button is disabled immediately afterward): `SelectionToolbar`'s and the per-clip context-menu's `onDelete` handlers (`timeline-panel.tsx`) call `deleteClipMutation.mutate(id)` directly, bypassing the `runCommand()`/Command-pattern path every other mutation (move/trim/duplicate/split/group) goes through — so deleting a clip is the one operation in this editor that was never undoable, before this session's changes and unrelated to them (confirmed by inspecting the handler's unmodified logic). **Not fixed here** — a real functional bug fix is out of scope for a styling-only pass per the founder's own explicit instruction — reported instead; see Known Issues.

**Timeline: trim-lag on keyframed clips fixed, zoom made real, ruler ticks made zoom-adaptive (2026-07-12) — three bugs reported together after live use, investigated before any fix per the founder's own instruction.**

*Issue 1 — trim lag on keyframed clips, root-caused and fixed.* Confirmed live (real multi-step Playwright drags, not a single down-move-up) that the lag reproduces ONLY on a clip with an expanded keyframe lane, never on a plain clip — so this was a genuinely new bug, not a resurfacing of the earlier trim-width "Bug #1" (that fix, confirmed still intact: a plain clip's width tracked the live drag smoothly, step for step). Root cause: `ClipKeyframeTrack` (`keyframe-track.tsx`) computes its own `left`/`width` purely from React props (`clip.startMs`/`durationMs`), and never participated in `ClipBlock`'s rAF-driven live-drag visual (`applyVisual()`/`onUp()`, which write directly to the clip's own DOM node via a ref, deliberately bypassing React state for per-frame performance — see that code's own header comment). So during a drag, the clip body resized smoothly while its keyframe lane stayed frozen at the pre-drag size for the entire gesture, only snapping to the correct size once the trim committed and the server round-trip's refetch landed — exactly the "lag hota hai fir trim hota hai" (feels delayed, then eventually trims) sensation reported. Fixed with the same registry pattern `clipElRegistry` already uses for group-mate clips during a move: a new `keyframeTrackElRegistry` (`timeline-panel.tsx`), `ClipKeyframeTrack` registers its own root div by clip id, and `ClipBlock`'s drag handlers now write the identical live `transform`/`width` to it too, for all three drag modes (move, resize-left, resize-right) and both the live-drag and commit/revert paths. **Verified live**: keyframe-track width now moves in exact lockstep with the clip's own width on every drag step (previously frozen the whole time).

*Issue 2 — trim precision, confirmed a display limitation, not a real constraint (no code change needed beyond Issue 3's fix).* Read every trim code path (`pxToMs`, `snapTrimEdge`, `snapMoveStart` in `timeline-engine.ts`) — all already continuous millisecond math, no whole-second rounding or snap-to-grid anywhere. The perceived "only reachable at whole-second marks" came from two things, both resolved by Issue 3's ruler fix: the ruler previously showed literally only whole-second ticks at every zoom level (no finer visual reference to aim at when zoomed in), and the admin-configurable snap threshold (`EDITOR_SNAP_THRESHOLD_PX`, default 8px) converts to a much wider millisecond window at low zoom (e.g. 800ms at the old minimum), making trims feel snappy toward round numbers.

*Issue 3 — zoom, two distinct real bugs found (the slider itself was not broken).* (1) The ZoomIn/ZoomOut icons in `bottom-status-bar.tsx` were plain `<svg>` elements with no `<button>` wrapper or click handler at all — purely decorative framing around the slider. Confirmed live that dragging the slider genuinely did change `pxPerSecond` (clip width scaled 1200px→6000px), but clicking the icons — the first thing most users try for a discrete zoom step — did nothing, which is almost certainly what read as "zoom doesn't work." Fixed: both are now real buttons using the exact same `ZOOM_STEP` (1.25×) multiplier as the Timeline's own existing `+`/`-` keyboard shortcuts (now exported from `timeline-panel.tsx` instead of a second hardcoded constant). (2) The ruler's tick rendering was hard-coded to exactly one tick per whole second regardless of `pxPerSecond` — real zooming just spread the same whole-second ticks further apart or closer together, never showing finer or coarser granularity. Fixed with two new pure functions in `timeline-engine.ts` (mirroring the file's existing pure-math convention, unit-tested — 8 new tests): `pickTickIntervalMs(pxPerSecond)` picks the smallest "nice" interval (50ms…30min) whose on-screen spacing clears a 60px minimum, and `formatTickLabel(ms, intervalMs)` formats it appropriately (decimal seconds for sub-second intervals, `Ns` for whole seconds — unchanged from before — `M:SS` for minute-scale). `MAX_PX_PER_SECOND` raised from 300 to 600 (`store.tsx`) so max zoom actually reaches a 100ms tick interval (a real "frame-accurate" range at 30fps — 33ms/frame — rather than bottoming out at 200ms). **Verified live**: ruler shows `0.0s/0.1s/0.2s…` at max zoom and `0s/10s/20s…` at min zoom; zoom buttons confirmed to move `pxPerSecond` across its full range.

**Verification (all three)**: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` (0 errors, same 84 pre-existing warnings), `vitest run` (112 files, 2980/2980, +8 new tests) all clean; `next build` clean (dev server stopped first). Live Playwright pass: 9/9 checks passing (zoom buttons, adaptive ruler ticks at both extremes, keyframe-track lockstep tracking during a real multi-step drag).

**Issue 4 — smart track creation on drag: built (2026-07-12), after the founder resolved the IMAGE-kind ambiguity by SOURCE CATEGORY rather than a heuristic.** Decision: images from Stock search/Uploads default to VIDEO (primary content); images from the curated Library's decorative categories (Shapes/Stickers/Logos/Icons) default to OVERLAY — checked from the asset's actual source at drop time, not guessed.

New pure resolver `resolveDropTrackKind()` (`lib/video-editor/drop-track-resolution.ts`, 7 unit tests) implements the full routing table: TEXT→TEXT, VIDEO→VIDEO, AUDIO→AUDIO (one track kind regardless of Voice/Music/SFX, per Module 8's existing subtype-tag convention — never three separate kinds), IMAGE→OVERLAY when `libraryCategory` is one of `SHAPE`/`STICKER`/`LOGO`/`STATIC_ICON`/`ANIMATED_ICON` else VIDEO, everything else (FONT, ANIMATION with no matching category) → `null`, meaning "don't guess, no-op" — the same conservative default a drop outside any valid track already had. Getting `libraryCategory` to this resolver required threading it through the drag payload: `DraggableAssetPayload` (`creative-studio-sidebar/types.ts`) gained a `libraryCategory?: string` field, `library-grid-section.tsx`'s `toGridItem()` now forwards `asset.category` into it, and both `asset-grid.tsx`/`asset-list.tsx`'s `onDragStart` handlers now include it in the payload they set.

New command `createAddTrackAndClipCommand` (`commands.ts`) — creating a track then a clip on it is genuinely two sequentially-dependent server creates (the clip's `trackId` doesn't exist until the track create resolves), which neither `createDeleteClipCommand`'s pattern nor `createCompositeCommand` (runs independent siblings, not a dependent pair) could express alone, so this is its own command: `execute()` awaits `addTrack()` then `addClip()` with the real new track id; best-effort `undo()` removes the clip then the track, same "new server-generated id" caveat every other create-type command in this file already documents. Needed a new `AddTrackAndClipDeps` (extends `ClipCommandDeps` with `addTrack`/`removeTrack`) since neither existing deps object exposed track creation — `timeline-panel.tsx` builds it once as `addTrackAndClipDeps`, reusing the already-instantiated `addTrack`/`removeTrack` mutations. 4 new unit tests (`commands.test.ts`) cover execute ordering, `audioSubtype` passthrough, undo, and a safe no-op when undo is called before execute.

Wiring in `timeline-panel.tsx`: `handleDrop()` (the existing per-track-row handler) now calls `e.stopPropagation()` so a drop landing on an existing track never also reaches the new fallback; a new `handleEmptySpaceDrop()` is attached to the scroller (`data-timeline-scroll`)'s own `onDrop`, catching anything that didn't land on a track row — including the entirety of a zero-track project, since the scroller's own box always has real screen area regardless of track count. It resolves the target kind, and only if no unlocked track of that kind already exists does it construct and run the new command — an existing suitable track is always reused via the plain `addClipMutation` (unchanged, not command-wrapped, matching how a direct per-track drop already behaves) rather than creating a duplicate. TEXT is special-cased to skip asset resolution entirely (content-only clip, `{text: "New Text", fontSize: 48, color: "#FFFFFF"}`, mirroring `TrackHeader`'s own "+" add-clip default) since TEXT clips have no backing asset by design. A shared `resolveDroppedAsset()` helper (materializes a stock result if needed) was extracted out of the original `handleDrop` so both handlers use the identical materialize-then-resolve logic rather than duplicating it.

**Verified live** against a genuinely empty (zero-track) project, via synthetic `DragEvent`s carrying real payloads (dispatched directly at the scroller, since several of these sources — a draggable TEXT preset, a real curated-library sticker — aren't fully wired UI yet independent of this fix; this exercises the actual changed code path with realistic data either way): dropping a TEXT payload auto-created a TEXT track with a real text-content clip; a VIDEO asset auto-created a VIDEO track referencing that asset; a sticker-library IMAGE (`libraryCategory: "STICKER"`) auto-created an OVERLAY track, not VIDEO; an AUDIO asset auto-created an AUDIO track; a plain-source IMAGE (no libraryCategory) correctly routed to VIDEO and **reused** the already-existing VIDEO track rather than creating a duplicate, landing a second clip on it. Undo confirmed end-to-end: 4 sequential undos (via the real Undo button, waiting for it to re-enable between each — a rapid raw-keyboard-shortcut loop intermittently dropped one of the 4 Ctrl+Z presses in testing, a Playwright/Chromium synthetic-event timing artifact unrelated to the app, not reproducible via real button clicks) cleanly removed all four auto-created tracks in reverse order, each with its clip. 113 test files / 2991 tests passing (2980 + 11 new); `tsc`/`eslint`/`next build` all clean.

**Cloud Video Editor: live-screenshot-vs-CapCut-reference gap pass — 6 issues investigated, 5 fixed, 1 confirmed not a regression (2026-07-12).** The founder compared a live screenshot of the editor against the CapCut Desktop reference and reported 6 items; each was investigated for root cause before any fix, per standing instruction.

*Issue 1 (HIGH SEVERITY, data isolation) — uploaded assets were visible across ALL projects, not scoped to the project they were uploaded into.* Root cause confirmed by direct schema inspection before writing any fix: `EditorAsset` had `userId`/`scope` but **no `projectId` column at all** — a genuine missing-schema-field bug, not a query filter that existed but was skipped. Fixed with an additive migration (`20260712121327_add_editor_asset_project_scoping`): nullable `EditorAsset.projectId` (`onDelete: Cascade` from `EditorProject`) — nullable both because `LIBRARY`-scope rows never have one and because every pre-existing `USER`-scope row has no recoverable project affiliation, so historical uploads are deliberately left unassigned (they simply stop appearing in any project's Uploads tab going forward, rather than continuing to leak into every project as before) instead of being guessed/backfilled. `listEditorAssets()` gained an optional 4th `projectId` param, added to its `where` clause only when present; the GET `/api/editor/assets` route reads `?projectId=` from the query string; the upload-URL route stamps the new column at creation time, with a `getOwnedProject()` ownership check when a `projectId` is supplied. **A second, previously-unknown bug was found while investigating**: `projectId` was already being silently dropped between `editor-workspace.tsx` (where it's available) and `<CreativeStudioSidebar />` (rendered with zero props by design, per Module 11's `SidebarSectionDef` contract) — so a schema-only fix would have been insufficient regardless; `uploads-section.tsx` now reads `projectId` via `useParams()` (the same established zero-props pattern `use-quick-add.ts`/`fonts-section.tsx` already use) rather than widening that contract. **Correctly distinguished from Milestone 26/Module 11's `LIBRARY`-scope assets** (admin-curated, intentionally global) — left completely untouched; also confirmed via a repo-wide `grep` for `scope: "USER"` that `listEditorAssets` is the only user-scope list query in the codebase, so there is no separate "Bulk Asset Library" instance of this bug elsewhere — the founder's phrasing conflated Milestone 26's admin-facing terminology with the general concept of the user's own library. One design correction caught by `tsc`, not the founder: `projectId` was initially made *required* end-to-end, which broke Brand Kit's own font-upload flow (`useUploadEditorAssetMutation()` with no project context — a brand font is intentionally cross-project) — fixed by making it optional everywhere in the chain instead, since only the plain "Upload media" flow needs project-scoping. **Verified with a real two-project, real-file-upload, real-browser regression test** (mandatory per the founder's own instruction, not just an API check): created two real projects, uploaded a real video into project A via the actual UI, confirmed it does NOT appear in project B's Uploads tab and vice versa, confirmed zero asset-id overlap between the two projects' lists — 7/7 checks passing.

*Issue 2 — media-library thumbnail fallback regression.* Confirmed real: `uploads-section.tsx`'s `AssetThumb` was rendering a flat grey box with the same Film/AudioLines/Type icon for every card of a given kind, not the agreed "solid color block keyed by track/clip type" fallback. Fixed by reusing the exact `--color-track-*` design tokens the Timeline's own clips already use (`globals.css`'s `@theme` block, from the earlier visual-fidelity pass) — VIDEO→`track-video`, AUDIO→`track-audio`, FONT→`track-text`, ANIMATION→`track-overlay` — so a card and a clip of the same kind now read as the same "kind of thing" at a glance, matching the earlier thumbnail decision instead of a generic icon.

*Issue 3 — Timeline toolbar row (split/duplicate/delete/marker) not rendering with nothing selected.* Confirmed: the row itself always rendered, but the entire action-button cluster was conditionally absent from the DOM when nothing was selected (not merely disabled) — only "+ Add Track" showed. Fixed by restructuring `SelectionToolbar` so every button always renders, each with its own `disabled` logic based on selection-state preconditions — matching the reference convention (icons visible-but-greyed when empty, enabled when a clip is selected) instead of hide-when-empty. A real Marker button was added (reuses the already-working `addMarkerMutation`); Crop/Rotate were deliberately **not** added despite being named in the report, since neither has a corresponding discrete existing action in this app today — adding non-functional buttons would violate the standing no-fake-UI rule.

*Issue 4 — zoom control disconnected at the page's bottom-right corner.* Confirmed and fixed: removed the zoom slider/buttons from `bottom-status-bar.tsx` (which now only shows read-only resolution/duration) and added a new `TimelineZoomControl` directly into the Timeline's own toolbar row (same row as split/delete/marker), matching the reference's integrated placement.

*Issue 5 — preview player resolution/quality-switch control (Module 3) reachability check.* Confirmed **not a real regression** — the Preview Quality button was already present in the code with no hiding logic; live Playwright confirmed its bounding box places it fully on-screen between the Speed and Fullscreen controls. No code change made.

*Issue 6 — right panel empty state restyle.* Restyled only, per the founder's explicit no-new-content boundary: replaced the bare `<p>Select a clip…</p>` with the app's existing shared `EmptyState` component (icon + title + description, centered), the same pattern already used elsewhere in the Creative Studio sidebar — no new panel/tab/AI-suggestion content added.

**Cloud Video Editor: stabilization pass — trim/stacking/audio/UI re-verified from scratch after user reports they still saw problems live (2026-07-13).** The founder reported that several previously-reported-fixed issues (trim lag, clips stacking, audio silence) still appeared to be happening in their own live session, and asked for every claim to be re-proven with real recorded evidence rather than trusted from a prior summary. Investigated as four fresh items, no prior fix assumed to hold.

*Environment first: a full clean restart, then a real, consequential discovery.* Found and killed a stray `next build --turbopack` process running concurrently with the dev server (the exact `dev`+`build`-collision hazard this file already documents), plus several duplicate `npm run dev` trees and a week-old orphaned `prisma studio` process — all cleared. Mid-investigation, `next.config.ts`/`tsconfig.json` changed out from under a running test and triggered a live dev-server restart, plus an orphaned process from a completely different session ID turned up — confirmed with the founder to be their own second window actively working on the same project (not a rogue process), so the approach shifted to coordinating with the live server rather than repeatedly restarting over it.

*Issue 1 — trim delay/glitch, re-verified across all 4 requested scenarios, confirmed already working.* Built four real scenarios (plain clip, a clip with real 2-keyframe Scale animation, two exactly-adjacent clips, two adjacent clips with a real Crossfade transition) and drove each trim via genuine slow multi-step mouse drags with a Playwright video recording, sampling the clip's live DOM width at every step (not just before/after) to catch a lag a screenshot pair would miss. All four tracked the mouse in real-time lockstep and committed correctly. One real, separate finding surfaced along the way (not the reported lag, but directly relevant to Issue 2 below): at an *exactly*-touching clip boundary, `handleLaneHover`'s nearest-edge distance check is a true tie, which a strict `<` comparison always resolves to the earlier clip's edge — the later clip's own edge handle is unreachable by hover at that one exact pixel-range. Low-impact (the boundary is still trimmable from the other clip's side) and not touched — a real, separate follow-up, not this session's reported bug.

*Issue 2 — "ek ke upar ek clip aa jata hai" (clips end up stacked), confirmed as a real, reproducible bug and fixed.* Root cause, confirmed by reading every code path before writing a fix: this Timeline never had same-track collision handling at all — a documented, deliberate scope cut from Milestone 24/25 (Known Issues' own "Timeline has no collision handling" entry), not a regression. `updateClip()`/`addClip()` (server) and `applyVisual()`/`onUp()` (client live-drag + commit) had zero overlap checks anywhere; `snapMoveStart`/`snapTrimEdge` only *snap* within a small threshold, they never *clamp*. Confirmed live and reproducible with a single, ordinary gesture: dragging a new clip from the sidebar and dropping it on top of an existing one created a genuine server-side overlapping row and rendered as garbled, overlapping clip blocks (screenshot evidence). Fixed with three new pure functions (`clampMoveStart`/`clampTrimLeftStart`/`clampTrimRightEnd`, `timeline-engine.ts`, 14 new unit tests) — a clip's move/trim/drop always stops at a neighbor's edge instead of continuing through it, the same "block, don't reject" convention mainstream NLEs use. `clampMoveStart` specifically needed a monotonic-sweep design (commit to one escape direction from the nearest blocker, then only ever push further in that same direction) after an initial per-step "nearest side" re-decision was found, via its own unit test, to oscillate forever between two back-to-back neighbors. Wired into every same-track mutation site: `ClipBlock`'s `applyVisual`/`onUp` (move, resize-left, resize-right) and `TimelinePanel`'s `handleDrop`/`handleEmptySpaceDrop`, via a new shared module-level `clipsOnTrackExcluding()` helper (two separate component scopes needed the same neighbor list). **A second, real bug was found while verifying the fix against a transition scenario**: the clamp initially also fought a clip's own active-transition partner — a transition deliberately ripple-shifts its incoming clip earlier to open a real crossfade overlap window (Module 9), and the blanket clamp didn't know that overlap was intentional, forcing the clip back down to the partner's edge and breaking the transition's own invariant (which then correctly, but confusingly, auto-pruned it). Fixed by threading a new `transitionPartnerIds` prop into `ClipBlock` (computed once per clip from the existing `transitions` array) and excluding those ids from the neighbor list the clamp uses — snapping to a transition partner's edge is still allowed, only the hard overlap-block is skipped. **Verified live, twice**: a real sidebar-drag-onto-existing-clip repro that used to create a same-position overlap now lands the new clip cleanly at the neighbor's true end, confirmed via server data (zero overlapping pairs) and a clean side-by-side screenshot; a real trim-into-a-transition-boundary repro now correctly grows to the actual dragged position (was previously wrongly force-shrunk to 1500ms) with the transition's pre-existing, documented "remove don't auto-resize" behavior still intact and unrelated to this fix.

*Issue 3 — audio not playing, root-caused as a real, high-impact upload-truncation bug, not an audio-code bug at all.* Built a real project with an uploaded audio clip and a video clip carrying its own embedded audio (confirmed via `ffprobe`: real h264+aac streams) and pressed the real Play button (satisfying the browser's autoplay-gesture requirement, same as `resumeSharedAudioContext()`'s own design). The uploaded audio clip played correctly; the video clip's own audio did not — `video.paused` stayed `true` even though its `currentTime` appeared to advance (an illusion caused by the editor's own playhead-sync code explicitly setting `currentTime` every frame, unrelated to real playback). Direct event instrumentation caught the real cause immediately: `MediaError` code 4, `"PipelineStatus::DEMUXER_ERROR_COULD_NOT_OPEN: FFmpegDemuxer: open context failed"` — Chromium could not open the file at all. Investigated the file itself before assuming a code bug: `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg -f null -` both decoded it cleanly (not corrupt), but its `moov` atom sat at the very end of the file, after a 12.7MB `mdat` — a browser-hostile "non-faststart" layout. Rather than trust a single synthetic fixture, cross-checked against the founder's own real account data: the real, actually-uploaded-by-the-founder video (`lizzat_papad_final_111.mp4`, via the real "Upload media" flow) was found on disk in **5 copies, 4 of which were truncated to exactly 10,485,760 bytes (10 MiB)** — the 5th, uploaded most recently, was the real, full 168.4 MB file. Root cause confirmed in `next.config.ts`'s own `experimental` block: Next.js's middleware layer has a default `middlewareClientMaxBodySize` of 10MB that silently buffers-and-truncates any request body above it — the presigned-upload PUT (`/api/assets/mock-upload`) passes through this middleware like every other request, so any upload over 10MB was being cut off mid-file with no error surfaced anywhere. **This was found already fixed in-flight by a concurrent second session working the same codebase** (`experimental: { middlewareClientMaxBodySize: "2gb" }`, confirmed via `tsc` that the correctly-named property for this Next.js version is `middlewareClientMaxBodySize`, not the newer-docs `proxyClientMaxBodySize` name, which doesn't typecheck against the installed version) — independently re-verified rather than trusted: re-uploaded the real 168.4MB file through the actual UI and confirmed the stored copy matches byte-for-byte (176,548,117 bytes, not truncated), then confirmed the same real video now plays with genuine, progressing audio (`readyState: 4`, real `play`/`playing` events, `currentTime` advancing at real-time rate) where the truncated copy had thrown a hard demuxer error. **Also verified the export side explicitly asked for**: rendered a real export (MP4, 720p, mixing the real video-with-audio clip and the uploaded audio clip) through the actual export queue, then ran `ffprobe`+`ffmpeg -af volumedetect` on the output — a real AAC stereo stream, `mean_volume: -12.6dB`/`max_volume: -0.5dB` (genuinely audible content, not silence). No code change was needed from this session for Issue 3 — the fix was already correctly in place; this entry documents the independent root-cause and re-verification.

*Issue 4 — UI vs. the CapCut reference, freshly compared with a populated multi-track timeline.* Built a real project spanning VIDEO (two clips + a Crossfade transition), TEXT, OVERLAY, and AUDIO (with a real waveform) tracks and took a fresh full-editor screenshot for a direct side-by-side against the reference image. Confirmed still-present structural differences, several already deliberate scope decisions from the earlier visual-fidelity pass (not re-litigated here) and some genuinely still open: (1) CapCut's media-category tabs (Media/Audio/Text/Stickers/…) run horizontally across the top of the left panel with a second-level sub-nav (Import/Media/Subprojects/Yours/Spaces/Library) inside it; this app's tabs are a single vertical icon rail — a real structural layout difference, not just density. (2) CapCut's timeline clips show real tiled video-frame thumbnails; this app's plain-upload clips still show the flat color-block fallback (Issue 2 from the earlier session's own fix) since thumbnail generation was never wired into the plain-upload path — a known, already-documented gap, re-confirmed still open. (3) CapCut's timeline toolbar carries roughly 15 tool icons (crop/rotate/effects-wand/PiP/audio-mix/mic-record/…) against this app's 7 — a deliberate no-fake-UI decision from the earlier pass (buttons only for actions that actually exist), reconfirmed intentional, not an oversight. (4) Track rows read taller in the reference (room for visible thumbnail imagery); this app's rows are more compact. None of these were addressed in this pass — closing (1) and (2) are real, scoped follow-up work (a navigation-architecture change and an upload-time thumbnail pipeline respectively), not a "make it solid" stabilization fix, and were flagged rather than silently built.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean (one unrelated pre-existing error surfaced briefly in `next.config.ts` mid-session from the concurrent second session's own in-progress edit — confirmed not caused by this work and resolved by the time of the final check); `eslint` — 0 errors, same 84 pre-existing warnings; `vitest run` — 113 files, **3005/3005** passing (+14 new: `clampMoveStart`/`clampTrimLeftStart`/`clampTrimRightEnd`). `next build` clean (0 errors, all routes including `/editor/[projectId]` at 105kB). Every finding in this entry is backed by a real Playwright recording/screenshot and, where relevant, real `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` output — not inferred from code alone.

**Cloud Video Editor — Part A: upload-integrity safeguard, tooltip fix, toolbar grouping (2026-07-13).** A follow-up to the stabilization pass above: the upload-truncation bug's fix (`middlewareClientMaxBodySize: "2gb"`) closes the specific hole that was found, but doesn't stop a *different* future limit (a different middleware setting, a reverse proxy in front of a real deployment, anything) from silently truncating an upload again with zero error anywhere — asked for explicitly as "the real fix for the class of bug, not just this instance of it."

*Upload path audit.* Every file-upload route in the app was inventoried: the editor's presigned flow (`/api/editor/assets/upload-url` + `mock-upload` + `confirm-upload`), the generic Media Library's identical two-phase flow (`/api/assets/upload-url` + `confirm-upload`, also backing Talking Head/Brand asset uploads), and three direct-multipart routes (`/api/assets/upload`, Admin Bulk Asset Library, Admin Reference Library) that parse `req.formData()` in one request rather than a separate PUT. All of them run through `src/middleware.ts`'s matcher (which covers virtually every request), so the global `middlewareClientMaxBodySize` fix genuinely covers all of them — confirmed both by reading the actual code path (middleware buffers up to the configured cap regardless of which handler eventually runs) and empirically, by PUTting a real 13.1MB video straight at the generic (non-editor) `/api/assets/upload` route and confirming the stored file matched byte-for-byte, not just the editor's own route.

*The actual class-fix: `StorageProvider.getObjectSize()`.* New method on the `StorageProvider` interface — a cheap metadata-only read (`fs.stat` for `MockStorageProvider`, `HeadObjectCommand` for `S3StorageProvider`), never a full `download()`. Both `confirmEditorAssetUpload()` (`lib/video-editor/assets.ts`) and `confirmAssetUpload()` (`lib/assets/service.ts`, the generic flow) now compare the object's real stored byte count against `fileSizeBytes` — already captured from the client at upload-url time, already persisted on the asset row, previously never checked again — before ever marking an asset READY. A mismatch throws a new, distinct `UploadIntegrityError` (kept separate from `InvalidStateError` so the route can return a real `409 ERR_UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` instead of a misleading 404); the editor's `EditorAsset` (which already has a `FAILED` status) is explicitly marked FAILED, while the generic `Asset` model (no `FAILED` status in its enum, and adding one wasn't needed to satisfy "never silently succeeds") simply stays at `PENDING_UPLOAD` and throws — the asset never reaches READY either way. `editorApi()`'s existing fetch wrapper already calls `toast.error()` on any non-success response, so the new error surfaces to the user automatically — no additional frontend wiring needed. **Verified live with a deliberate mismatch** (declared 5,000,000 bytes, actually PUT 1,234), independent of the now-fixed 10MB config so the test stays valid regardless of that setting: both the editor and generic confirm-upload routes correctly returned `409 ERR_UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE`, the editor asset's real final status was confirmed `FAILED` (never `READY`) via a follow-up query, and a correctly-sized upload in the same run still completed normally (no false positives).

*Tooltip positioning bug, fixed.* `ClipKeyframeTrack`'s empty state (`keyframe-track.tsx`) — "No animated properties — use the stopwatch icons in Properties to animate one." — was a permanently-rendered `<div>` sized to the clip's full rendered width with no real tooltip behavior, reading as an unstyled black bar sitting directly under (and, at typical clip widths, visually merging with) the selected clip. Replaced with the same real Radix `Tooltip`/`TooltipTrigger`/`TooltipContent` primitive the sidebar rail's own icon tooltips already use (`rail.tsx` — the app's `TooltipProvider` already wraps the whole app at the root layout, so no new provider was needed): a compact `Clock` icon + short label sits in the row at its normal height, and the full explanatory sentence only appears in a real floating tooltip on hover. Confirmed live: the row no longer dominates the strip, and hovering shows a properly-positioned, properly-styled tooltip anchored to the icon.

*Timeline toolbar grouping.* Added two more visual divider hairlines (matching the one that already separated the marker button) so the existing action buttons read as four logical clusters instead of one undifferentiated row: split/duplicate/ripple-delete (single-clip editing) | group/ungroup (structural) | delete (destructive) | marker. No new buttons — purely grouping what already exists.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean (0 errors in every changed file); `eslint` — 0 errors, same 84 pre-existing unrelated warnings; `vitest run` — 113 files, 3005/3005 passing (unchanged — these are service/API-layer changes verified live per this codebase's established DB-bound-service convention, not new pure-logic extraction). `next build` clean, dev server cleanly restarted after. Live Playwright evidence for all three fixes: the deliberate-mismatch integrity test (both flows, 409 + FAILED status + unaffected-good-upload sanity check), a cropped screenshot of the real floating tooltip on hover, and a cropped screenshot of the toolbar showing all four icon clusters visually separated by dividers.

**Cloud Video Editor — Part B Step 1: real Timeline filmstrip generation, extraction+storage only (2026-07-13).** The Timeline's clip blocks show no real frame preview today — a flat color rectangle + text label, or (for admin-library/stock assets only) a single tiled static frame (the 2026-07-12 visual-fidelity pass's `thumbnailUrl`). Asked for a genuine multi-frame filmstrip, scoped explicitly into sub-steps with a stop-and-confirm gate after extraction+caching, before any canvas-rendering UI work.

*Investigated existing infrastructure before writing anything new*, per the standing rule: `extractThumbnailFrame()`/`generateVideoThumbnail()` (`ffmpeg-exec.ts`/`thumbnails.ts`) already pull one frame at 1s in, resize via `sharp`, and are wired into exactly two call sites (`asset-library.ts`'s admin upload, `search-service.ts`'s stock materialize) — never plain "Upload media" uploads. `EditorAsset.thumbnailKey` is a single scalar column; no existing schema concept for multiple frames per asset.

*Schema*: additive migration (`20260713084737_add_editor_asset_filmstrip`) adds `EditorAsset.filmstripKey`/`filmstripFrameCount` (both nullable) — a single sprite-sheet image + its tile count, not N separate storage objects or a child table. One file, one client fetch, trivially sliceable once the tile size is known.

*New shared module* `lib/video-editor/filmstrip.ts` — zero fs/ffmpeg/DB imports (same "pure logic in its own importable-from-anywhere file" split `timeline-engine.ts` already established), so the eventual client-side canvas renderer can import the exact same constants the server generator uses instead of duplicating them: `FILMSTRIP_TILE_WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (80×80, fixed — every tile is `cover`-cropped to this regardless of the source video's own aspect ratio, so `tileWidth = spriteWidth / frameCount` always holds with nothing extra to store) and `computeFilmstripFrameCount(durationSeconds)` (denser for longer source videos — one frame per ~2s — clamped to [8, 40] so a 5s clip still gets a real strip and a 30-minute one doesn't generate hundreds of tiles for one asset; this fixed per-asset pool is generated once and cached, not recomputed per render or per zoom level — zoom-responsive density is a Part B Step 3 client-rendering concern against this same cached pool, not an extraction-time one).

*Extraction*: `extractFilmstripFrames()` (`ffmpeg-exec.ts`) — one ffmpeg invocation per asset (`-vf fps=<frameCount/durationSeconds> -frames:v <frameCount>`), not `frameCount` separate `-ss` seeks; `generateVideoFilmstrip()` (`thumbnails.ts`) resizes each raw frame to the fixed tile size via `sharp` (`fit: "cover"`) and composites them side-by-side into one horizontal JPEG via `sharp({create:...}).composite([...])`.

*Wiring*: `confirmEditorAssetUpload()` (`assets.ts`) — VIDEO-kind only, best-effort (same non-throwing try/catch precedent the two existing thumbnail call sites already use: failure never blocks the upload, just leaves `filmstripKey` null, same fallback ClipBlock already has for a missing `thumbnailKey`). Deliberately relies on Part A's integrity check having already run first in the same function — the bytes downloaded for filmstrip generation are guaranteed genuine, not silently truncated. `EditorAssetView`/`AssetView` (both server and client type) gained `filmstripUrl`/`filmstripFrameCount`; every read site projecting the old `thumbnailUrl` field (`listEditorAssets`, `listFavorites`, `listCollectionAssets`, `listRecentAssets`, confirm-upload's own response) updated identically for type consistency — `tsc` caught all three view-mapping sites that needed it.

**Verified live, not just code-complete, exactly as asked**: uploaded a real flower-timelapse video through the actual "Upload media" UI button (not an API shortcut, not the admin library) into a fresh project, polled until READY, and confirmed via the real API response: `filmstripFrameCount: 8` (matching `computeFilmstripFrameCount(5.055s)` exactly) and a real `filmstripUrl`. Downloaded the actual generated sprite file from disk — 640×80px, exactly 8 tiles × 80px as designed (confirmed via `sharp().metadata()`) — and visually inspected it: all 8 tiles show genuinely different frames, with the flower bud visibly, progressively opening from fully closed (tile 1) to fully bloomed (tile 8) — definitive proof of real, correctly-ordered, per-timestamp extraction, not a duplicated or corrupt strip. `thumbnailUrl` correctly stayed `null` for this same asset (that gap is separate, untouched by this fix, and still open).

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` — 0 errors, same 84 pre-existing warnings; `vitest run` — 113 files, 3005/3005 passing (one unrelated `ai-os/prompt-compiler/engine.test.ts` flake seen in the full-suite run, confirmed pre-existing/order-dependent by re-running that file alone — 28/28 passed in isolation, nothing in this change touches prompt-compiler). `next build` — the Turbopack flag hit the same pre-existing dev+build `.next`-collision flakiness this file already documents (confirmed unrelated by running a plain `next build` without `--turbopack`, which succeeded cleanly with 0 errors including a normal `/editor/[projectId]` bundle); dev server cleanly restarted after. **Explicitly not yet built**: any Timeline UI change — `ClipBlock` still renders the old single-tiled `thumbnailUrl` background (or the flat color block) exactly as before; this step was extraction+storage only, canvas rendering is next.

**Cloud Video Editor — Part B Step 2: canvas-based filmstrip rendering, wired into `ClipBlock` (2026-07-13).** Step 1 generated and cached real per-video sprite sheets but never rendered them; this step draws them.

*New pure function* `computeVisibleFilmstripFrameIndices(frameCount, assetDurationMs, trimStartMs, durationMs, maxVisibleFrames?)` in `filmstrip.ts` (9 new unit tests) — treats sprite frame `i` as representing source time `i * (assetDurationMs / frameCount)` (the sprite has no per-frame timestamps stored, only a count, so this is a deliberate approximation) and returns which cached frames fall within a clip's trimmed visible window, with ±one-frame-interval padding on each edge so a boundary doesn't cut off the visually-nearest frame, and always at least one index even for a trim window narrower than one frame's interval. The optional `maxVisibleFrames` parameter (unused by this step, thinning evenly rather than truncating from one end when passed) exists specifically so Step 3's zoom-density work builds on this same function instead of a parallel one.

*Rendering*: `ClipBlock` (`timeline-panel.tsx`) gained a `filmstripCanvasRef` + a `useEffect` mirroring the existing waveform canvas's own structure exactly (redraws on commit/trim/resize, not during a live drag — drags mutate the DOM directly via `applyVisual()` everywhere else in this file too) — loads the sprite via a new module-level `loadFilmstripImage()` cache (keyed by URL, so the same asset's sprite is decoded once regardless of how many clips/re-renders reference it), then `drawImage()`s each visible frame's source-rect from the sprite onto equal-width destination slots spanning the clip's current rendered width — real `<canvas>`, never per-frame DOM `<img>` elements, exactly as scoped (a wide, heavily-zoomed clip would otherwise mean dozens of image nodes). Falls back to the old single-tile `thumbnailUrl` background (still used by admin-library/stock assets, which don't have a filmstrip yet — Step 1 only wired generation into the plain-upload confirm-upload path) when no filmstrip exists, then to the flat color block — a real three-tier fallback, nothing regresses for assets this pass didn't touch.

**Verified live, not just code-complete**: dragged a real uploaded video onto the Timeline via genuine HTML5 drag-and-drop (not an API shortcut) and confirmed via direct pixel inspection that the resulting `<canvas>` is 100% painted (11,817/11,817 non-transparent pixels), then visually confirmed the rendered strip shows the real, correctly-ordered bud→bloom sequence matching Step 1's own sprite. **Trim-awareness specifically verified**, not assumed from the code alone: built two clips referencing the same asset in one project — one spanning the full 5.055s (showing all 8 frames, bud through full bloom) and one trimmed to only the last 1.555s (`trimStartMs: 3500`) — and confirmed the trimmed clip's rendered strip shows only 3 tiles, every one already well into bloom, never showing the closed-bud frames the full clip displays elsewhere in the same screenshot session. One honest, expected limitation surfaced and left for Step 3: at extreme zoom (a 5s clip stretched to ~1800px wide), the fixed 8-frame cached pool gets visibly upscaled/blurred rather than showing more distinct frames — exactly the motivation for Step 3's zoom-responsive density (the `maxVisibleFrames` parameter already built in Step 2 above exists for this), not a bug in this step.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` — 0 errors, same 84 pre-existing warnings; `vitest run` — 114 files, 3014/3014 passing (+9 new `computeVisibleFilmstripFrameIndices` tests; the previous entry's `prompt-compiler` flake did not recur). `next build` clean (dev server stopped first this time, avoiding the same collision the prior entry hit; `/editor/[projectId]` at 106kB); dev server cleanly restarted after.

**Cloud Video Editor — premium design-token foundation (2026-07-13).** Requested explicitly as prep work — "get it right here rather than scattering values later" — with a hard stop-and-confirm gate before the one genuinely risky part: swapping the accent color.

*Investigated scope before touching anything.* The existing `--color-editor-line`/`-surface-1`/`-surface-2` tokens (2026-07-12 visual-fidelity pass) already centralize the editor's hairlines/tinted fills; `--color-accent-orange` (the requested swap target) turned out to be a single **global** token used in 53 places app-wide — only 22 of them in the editor, the other 31 in marketing/dashboard/admin. Flagged this to the founder before writing any code (as explicitly instructed): editor-scoped swap (a new token, orange untouched everywhere else) vs. sitewide replacement vs. don't swap yet. **Confirmed: editor-scoped only.**

*Colors.* `--color-editor-line`/`-surface-1`/`-surface-2` keep their existing names (40+ call sites already reference them) but moved from translucent-white alpha overlays to solid hex values matching the requested palette (`#272c36`/`#1b1e26`/`#20293a`) — this cascades automatically with zero component-file changes for anything already using them. Two genuinely new tokens fill gaps that didn't exist before: `--color-editor-bg` (`#0b0b0d`) and `--color-editor-panel` (`#14161c`) — the editor's root shell previously borrowed the Dashboard's own `--color-surface-0` (a *different*, unrelated dark-UI consumer per that token's own comment), and every `<aside>`/toolbar/timeline-panel sat directly on the page background with no fill of its own. Applied `bg-editor-bg` to the root layout and preview-window wrapper (replacing `bg-surface-0`), `bg-editor-panel` to every structural chrome container that had none (top toolbar, left sidebar, right properties panel, bottom status bar, Timeline's own root, the Export sheet). `--color-editor-accent` (`#5b7cfa`) and `--color-editor-danger` (`#ff4d4f`) are new, editor-only tokens — every editor-internal `accent-orange`/`text-error`/`bg-error` usage (38 occurrences across 14 files) was repointed to them via literal class-name replacement, not a token-definition change, since these editor files were previously referencing the *sitewide* orange/error tokens directly, not an editor-scoped alias. **Verified the scope boundary held, not just assumed**: read `--color-accent-orange`'s live computed value on a non-editor (admin) page after the swap — still exactly `rgb(249, 115, 22)` (`#f97316`), completely unchanged; `--color-editor-accent` resolves to the new blue-violet only where an editor file's class actually references it.

*Typography.* Confirmed Inter was already loaded app-wide via `next/font` (`lib/fonts.ts`) — nothing to add. Added a 4-step editor-scoped scale (`--text-editor-heading` 20px/600, `--text-editor-panel-title` 16px/600, `--text-editor-body` 14px/400, `--text-editor-caption` 12px/500) under new names rather than reusing the sitewide `--text-heading-*`/`--text-body-*`/`--text-caption` tokens — those are tuned for the light marketing/dashboard theme (different weights, e.g. sitewide caption is 400 not the requested 500) and reusing the exact names would have silently reskinned every non-editor consumer of them, not just the editor. Searched for genuinely ad hoc sizing first (`text-[Npx]`/`text-xs`/etc.) — found exactly one, a 9px keyframe-row label below even the existing `--text-nano` floor, deliberately left alone rather than forced up into a scale that doesn't fit it. Applied the new scale to its two clearest matches: the top bar's project name (`text-editor-heading`, replacing a borrowed 14px/600 `text-label-md`) and both panel-title elements (`PanelHeader`'s shared title + the right panel's own "Properties" heading, `text-editor-panel-title`, same borrow-fix).

*Spacing/radius/shadow.* `--radius-editor-card` (18px), `--radius-editor-button` (14px), `--shadow-editor-card`, and `--spacing-editor-button-height` (44px — Tailwind v4 height utilities read off the `--spacing` namespace, not a `--height-*` one, so this is where a named 44px token actually has to live to generate a usable `h-editor-button-height` class) all defined as editor-scoped tokens, same reasoning as typography (the sitewide `--radius-*`/`--shadow-*` tokens are shared by the light-theme shadcn Button primitive). Applied card radius+shadow to the Export panel's history-row card (a real list-item-sized card, not one of the tiny asset-grid thumbnail tiles, which stayed at their existing size to avoid a disproportionate 18px radius on a ~100px tile) and button radius to the Export button. **Deliberately did not apply the 44px button-height token to existing small toolbar/icon buttons** — the top bar itself is only 48px tall, so a 44px button would leave almost no vertical margin, a real layout conflict flagged in-code rather than silently forced through; the token is defined and ready for whenever a genuinely visual pass gives the relevant toolbars room for it.

**One honest, disclosed gap**: the Export panel's own "Start Export" button still shows the sitewide orange/primary color — it uses the shared shadcn `Button` component's default variant (no editor-token override), and per this codebase's own established precedent (2026-07-12 visual-fidelity pass), the shared Button component is deliberately never touched to avoid risking the light marketing/dashboard UI. Every other accent-colored element in the editor (selected-clip ring, range-input thumbs, track solo/lock icons, keyframe diamonds, transition badges, playhead-adjacent markers, sidebar active states) does show the new blue-violet — confirmed live across a real selected clip and its full Transform/Crop/Blend panel.

**Bug caught by the build, not by review**: the first version of two new CSS comments contained a literal `--radius-*`/`--text-heading-*` pattern — CSS's `*/` comment-closer sequence appeared mid-comment (`heading-*/--text-body`), prematurely terminating the comment block and breaking every rule after it. Turbopack's dev-server hot-reload caught it immediately (`CssSyntaxError` in the browser overlay); fixed by rephrasing both comments to avoid the literal `*/` adjacency, then independently re-validated the whole file by parsing it directly through `postcss.parse()` before restarting.

**Verified live**: a real project with a real uploaded+selected clip, screenshotted at full-editor scale and cropped into the requested representative panels — top bar (new heading size + panel background + rounded Export button), a selected clip (blue-violet ring, replacing the old orange), and the Properties panel (new panel-title size, panel background, blue-violet range-slider thumbs throughout Transform/Crop/Blend). No console/page errors during the whole pass.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` clean (0 errors, same 84 pre-existing warnings; globals.css itself isn't eslint-scoped, expected); `vitest run` — 114 files, 3014/3014 passing (a pure-CSS/JSX-className pass needed no new tests); `next build` clean (dev server stopped first to avoid the documented collision; `/editor/[projectId]` unchanged in size); dev server cleanly restarted and re-verified live afterward.

The Cloud Video Editor's own equivalent gap (`/editor/[projectId]`, `lib/video-editor/tracks.ts`'s `EditorTrack`) is now resolved — see the dated changelog entry above for the real drag-to-reorder + cross-track clip drag build.

## 9. AI Video & Film Roadmap (Master Plan)

The founder's authoritative phase order for the AI Video/Film initiative — kept here so it persists across sessions and is never re-litigated or re-investigated. Update this section, don't duplicate it, as phases complete.

### THE VIDEO CORE FLOW IS COMPLETE AND LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-07-11)

Script → scene-split → real Veo Lite scenes → vendor-independent merge → text overlays → charge-on-generation credits, no "pick a template" step, no flower. This is the real, working, monetized path a user experiences today through the live Studio (System A, `/videos`). Confirmed with a real 4-scene run: 4/4 scenes real Veo, a real 32.00s/1080×1920/30fps merged video (ffprobed), both text overlays correctly burned in, exactly `-80` credits charged (4×20, one `CreditTransaction` per real scene), balance 189→109.

**The full "flower" root-cause chain — five independent bugs, each found by tracing the actual failure, not guessed, each now fixed. Do not re-investigate any of these:**

1. **Quota/billing** — Veo is not available on the Gemini API Free tier at all (confirmed via Google's own pricing docs); required linking a billing account. Separately, standard Veo's ~5-8x per-second cost drained the account's prepaid balance during verification — reverted the live default back to Veo Lite (`veo.provider.ts`'s `DEFAULT_MODEL`, and the live `ProviderConfig.model` row) to fit the ₹300-500 target budget; standard Veo kept reachable via an explicit model override for a possible future Premium tier (`VIDEO_ACTION_CREDIT_COSTS.veo_standard`, 100 credits, priced but not wired to any caller).
2. **Provider priority ordering** — an Admin panel Save on the Veo `ProviderConfig` row changed its `priority` from `-2` to `0` (working around a separate, now-fixed Zod bug that rejected negative priorities), which silently sorted `mock` ahead of `veo` in the failover chain — every real generation resolved to the mock placeholder without veo ever being attempted. Fixed: priority restored to `-2`; the Admin Save schema's `priority: z.number().int().min(0)` relaxed to allow negatives (matching the DB column and the "negative = try first" convention every seeded provider already used).
3. **Merge-to-vendor** — `processMergeJob()` called `provider.mergeScenes()` through the Generation Engine; Veo/Kling/Seedance all throw "no generic scene-merge capability" (an honest, documented limitation), so even with real per-scene clips the FINAL merged video always fell back to mock. Fixed: new `lib/scenes/merge-via-editor.ts` assembles the real scene clips as `EditorClip`s and renders the join through the Cloud Video Editor's Export Engine (real headless-browser-compositor + ffmpeg, the same vendor-independent path AI Video Phase 3's `veo-multiscene-video.ts` already proved) — this step now involves zero AI vendors and cannot hit this failure mode again.
4. **Rate-limit race under concurrency** — `RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY` (default 3, the real persistent worker `lib/queue/worker.ts`) lets several scenes' Veo calls fire in true parallel; since Veo's call is long-running (create → poll for minutes), the `GenerationLog` row the rate-limit count-check reads doesn't exist yet when concurrent callers check it, so multiple calls land within the same second regardless of `rateLimitPerMinute`. Fixed generically in `runGeneration()` (`lib/generation/engine.ts`, benefits every category, not just video): a synchronous per-provider slot-reservation gate derived from the existing `rateLimitPerMinute` config, reserved before any `await` so concurrent callers can't race for the same slot.
5. **Credit model** — System A charged nothing at generation time (Milestone 4's original "rendering is free, only download costs credits" design, which made sense before real vendor cost was in play). Fixed: `processSceneRenderJob()` now calls `checkVideoActionAccess("veo_lite")` before rendering (blocks insufficient tier/balance before any vendor cost is spent) and charges 20 credits only when the result's `providerId !== "mock"` — reusing the same precheck/charge/mock-guard pattern System B's `generateVeoLiteVideo()` already proved, not a new mechanism.

Two bugs found incidentally while fixing the above, both also fixed: the Admin Save schema also silently required `keyExpiresAt` in full-ISO-datetime form when the form only ever sends a bare date (found while diagnosing #2, not yet hit in practice — no row currently has this field set, left as a known sharp edge, not fixed since it wasn't blocking anything); and the earlier `providerId`-attaching fix (`{ ...result, providerId }`) silently corrupted primitive results, caught by actually running `engine.test.ts` (not assumed safe) while verifying fix #4 — fixed by only merging onto genuine objects.

### Reconciliation — still open

The founder-approved plan to fold System B's real capabilities into System A rather than keep two disconnected products (System A = the live Studio; System B = this session's standalone `lib/creative/*.ts` orchestrators, still wired to zero UI routes). Steps 1 (scene-split into System A) and 2 (credit-model switch) are done, above. Remaining, in the founder's original approved order, none started yet:

3. **Start-image into System A's scene render** — `VideoRenderRequest.startImage` already exists on the shared interface; System A's scene render just never populates it. Wiring it in (a per-scene "starting image" field, settable from the Scene Editor) is mostly connecting an existing wire, not new capability.
4. **Animated Poster as a quick-create shortcut into System A** — fold `generateAnimatedPosterVideo()` (System B, Phase 1) into a VideoProject pre-seeded with one scene whose visual is an existing poster Asset. Not done — `generateAnimatedPosterVideo()` is still the only way to get this feature, still unreachable from any UI.

Explicitly NOT to be defaulted on — Phase 3b's chaining test was a mixed result (identity held; real background drift, a seam-adjacent motion-blur artifact, and text hallucination were also found), never resolved to a clean pass.

**Timeline unification (Cloud Editor vs. legacy Studio timeline) — still deferred as its own separately-scoped investigation**, per the original decision, with one nuance: the merge fix (item 3 above) already routes System A's merge step through the Cloud Editor's Export Engine, so the two systems are no longer fully separate at the rendering layer — but System A's own native `Track`/`Clip`/`Export` model (Milestone 9, `processExportJob()`/`composeTimeline()`) is untouched and has the identical "vendor can't composite" gap `mergeScenes()` had, just not yet hit in practice. Not investigated or scoped this session.

**B4 (2026-07-22) — Talking Head's parallel pipeline retired at the discovery/nav layer, NOT a data-model unification.** A real-DB audit before touching anything found the actual risk surface was tiny: 24 `TALKING_HEAD_UPLOAD` projects total, 20 with zero `Track`/`Clip` rows (never left pre-render), 3 `COMPLETED` with real rendered output, and exactly 1 `FAILED` project with genuine in-progress editable state (4 tracks/6 clips). - `generateVeoLiteVideo()` — still actively used internally by `veo-multiscene-video.ts`/`veo-chain-video.ts`. Cannot delete without breaking those. Also now genuinely duplicated (not identical, but the same precheck/charge/mock-guard shape) by `processSceneRenderJob()`'s own new inline logic in `pipeline.ts` — a real, small "no dup logic" gap introduced by today's credit-model fix, not yet consolidated, worth a look whenever this area is touched again.
