### Later — AI Film (Phase 5+)

**Update 2026-07-12: Phases 5 and 6's generation-free structure are now built** (schema, all 6 screens, all routes except per-scene generation — see the dated entry earlier in this file for full detail). What's actually still gated on Phase 3b's character-consistency result is narrower than originally scoped: only the per-scene video generation step itself (`POST /api/videos/film/[id]/scenes/[sceneId]/generate`, currently an honest 501 stub) is blocked. Character generation, face upload, character sheets, storyboard planning, and the final merge have no dependency on which consistency method wins and are already real, working code.

**Update 2026-07-12 (later the same day): the consistency METHOD is now decided and wired, not still an open A-vs-B choice.** Founder correction: text alone can't hold a character consistent (the model re-invents the face each scene) — the character's own stored photo is the identity anchor. `scenes/[sceneId]/generate/route.ts` now resolves that exact photo (`FilmCharacter.selectedVariationAssetId`/`faceUploadFrontAssetId`, via the shared `resolveFilmCharacterReferenceAssetId()`) and reports it as the scene's conditioning image — live-verified via a real HTTP round-trip returning `{ conditioningAssetId, conditioningMethod: "reference_image_anchoring" }`. That IS Phase 3b's "Variant B" (reference-anchoring): every scene of a character conditions on that SAME stored photo, never the previous scene's last frame the way chaining/"Variant A" does. The stub still doesn't call any video provider — only the data path is proven. This means tomorrow's test is no longer an abstract comparison to decide a method; it directly validates the exact method the real film pipeline is already wired to use.

- **Phase 5 (character system) — structure built, not yet real-generation-tested.** Character generation + 2 variations + face-upload (side+front photos → character) + character sheets (GPT/Gemini) all exist as real routes. Untested with real API calls (by design — no generation was run today).
- **Phase 6 (full film) — structure built except the one gated step.** Idea + duration + characters + style + aspect ratio → storyboard → **[gated: per-scene video, conditioned on the character's stored photo via reference-image anchoring]** → merge → complete film. ₹1,000–3,000+, Film tier (pricing still a placeholder — `VIDEO_ACTION_CREDIT_COSTS.film` is 0 credits/PREMIUM tier, a structural gate only, real pricing follows once a real per-clip cost is known).

**The founder's step-by-step for tomorrow (after the Veo/Gemini quota resets, ~12:30 PM IST):**

1. **Validate reference-image anchoring across a real multi-scene film — this is now the primary, not a comparison.** Generate 4-6 real scenes of the SAME character, each one conditioned on that character's own stored reference photo as `startImage` (not chained from the previous scene's last frame) — exactly what `scenes/[sceneId]/generate/route.ts` is now wired to do once its stub is replaced with a real call. This is genuinely new data: the existing 2 real hops from Phase 3b (`clip1_reference.mp4` → `variantA_clip2.mp4` → `variantA_clip3.mp4`) were all Variant A (chaining) — there is currently zero real data on reference-anchoring at any hop count.
   - **Optional, only if quota allows extra headroom**: a couple of Variant A (chaining) hops for comparison context — but this is no longer the decision the test exists to make, so don't spend scarce quota on it before the primary run is done.
2. **What to look for, concretely, not just "does it look okay":**
   - **Identity**: same face, same distinguishing features held or not, scene by scene, all the way to scene 4-6 — not just the first couple, since anchoring to a fixed photo could still drift due to prompt/scene content rather than the conditioning image itself.
   - **Background/setting continuity**: does each scene's setting match what its own prompt asked for (reference-anchoring has no reason to inherit the PREVIOUS scene's background the way chaining did, so this failure mode may simply not apply — worth confirming, not assuming).
   - **Visual-quality consistency**: does anchoring to one fixed photo avoid the "softening" that compounded hop-over-hop in the chained test, since every scene starts from the same unmodified source image rather than a fed-forward one?
   - **Text hallucination**: does the model still invent garbled on-screen text (the "Free Consuition" issue from Phase 2/3b) — if so, this reinforces the existing rule of never trusting Veo for real on-screen text and always compositing it via the Editor instead.
3. **How the result finishes the per-scene generation stub:**
   - **If reference-anchoring holds up across 4-6 real scenes**: replace `scenes/[sceneId]/generate/route.ts`'s final `apiError()` with a real call — reuse `generateVeoLiteVideo()`-style logic (precheck via `checkVideoActionAccess`, real `renderVideo()` call, `isMockFallback` guard, charge-after-success into one transaction, exactly System B's proven shape). The `startImage` resolution is already built and proven — nothing about it needs to change, only the final provider call needs adding.
   - **If it doesn't hold up cleanly**: the per-scene route stays a stub, and the founder and I should talk about a fallback before building further — e.g. capping films at however many scenes the data says stays acceptable, leaning harder on the character sheet's text as a prompt-level supplement, or trying Variant A after all. Don't guess past what the data says.
   - **Either way, report the raw result plainly** — which scenes were real, what the extracted frames actually show, exact clip count/cost — the same standard every test in this file has been held to, not a summary verdict alone.

### Image backlog (when image work resumes)

Real logo preservation; product-image preservation; reference-full-design-learning (not just background); Hindi text reliability; Kling/Seedance credentials (still not sourced — Kling has zero config, Seedance's stored key is an invalid placeholder, confirmed via a real 401). Also found, not yet fixed: `openai_images`' stored `model` is `gpt-image-1`, not `gpt-image-2` as expected — currently disabled so not live-impacting, worth confirming the intended model id before ever enabling it.

### Cross-cutting rules

- Cost vs. the ₹300–500 per-video budget framing: premium/expensive features gate to higher tiers, never priced below real cost with margin.
- **Character consistency (Phase 3b) gates per-scene video generation specifically** — not all of Phase 5+ anymore. Character generation, face upload, character sheets, storyboard, and merge were built generation-free on 2026-07-12 with no dependency on the consistency answer; only the actual per-scene Veo call (`scenes/[sceneId]/generate/route.ts`) waits on it. The METHOD itself is decided (reference-image anchoring — every scene conditions on the character's own stored photo as `startImage`, live-wired and proven 2026-07-12); what's still open is whether it holds up across a real multi-scene film, which is what tomorrow's test answers.
- **The character sheet's photo is the identity anchor; its text is supplementary only** — never design a consistency mechanism around the text description alone, it doesn't hold a model's rendering of a face steady the way conditioning on the real photo does.
- Veo adds bad/hallucinated text to generated video (confirmed twice live, Phases 2 and 3b) — design around it with Editor-added text overlays rather than relying on the video model to render or preserve text.
- AI video API pricing swings 40–60% across sources/vendors and over time — re-check real margins before finalizing credit costs for any new model, don't assume researched figures stay accurate.
- Real vendor rate limits can be tripped by in-process concurrency even when a configured `rateLimitPerMinute` looks correct on paper — a count-based check alone isn't enough under `RENDER_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY > 1`; the pacing gate in `runGeneration()` is what actually enforces spacing now.

### Build order

Reconciliation items 3-5 (start-image, animated poster, chaining) → timeline unification (separately scoped) → Phase 4 (UGC/voice) → Phase 5 → Phase 6, image backlog interleaved when time allows. One item at a time, tested live before moving on — the same discipline used for everything above.

### Cloud Video Editor — Replace Source kind-filter/search, real Blend Modes, UI-consistency cleanup (2026-07-15)

Four scoped fixes to the Cloud Video Editor (`src/app/editor/[projectId]/`), from a prior investigation-only pass, all live-verified via real Playwright + pixel-level sampling (not just typecheck/build):

1. **Replace source — kind filter + search.** `timeline-panel.tsx`'s `ClipBlock` "Replace source" submenu had no asset-kind check at all — an AUDIO asset could be selected as a VIDEO clip's replacement, which the compositor's `VideoLayer` (`if (asset?.kind === "VIDEO")`) then silently rendered as a blank frame with no error. Fixed by reusing `resolveDropTrackKind()` (the same rule a fresh timeline drop already goes through), plus a search input matching the sidebar Uploads tab's own pattern. The "list every project's uploads, not just this one" scoping stays as documented/deliberate in `listEditorAssets()`. Verified live: only VIDEO assets appear for a VIDEO clip, search narrows correctly, an actual replace still preserves transform/keyframes/crop (deep-equality check).

2. **Real Blend Modes.** The "Blend" properties group was opacity+flip only despite its name. Added `blendMode: BlendMode` (`"normal" | "multiply" | "screen" | "overlay" | "darken" | "lighten"`) to `ClipTransform` (`lib/video-editor/transform.ts`), the matching Zod field in `clipTransformSchema`, and `mixBlendMode` to `composeTransformCss()`'s output — consumed by all 4 compositor render call sites (`compositor-stage.tsx`: `VideoLayer`, inline IMAGE-on-VIDEO-track `<img>`, `OverlayLayer`, `TextLayer`). No Prisma migration needed (`EditorClip.transform` is a nullable JSON blob, same "new field defaults via `??`" precedent every prior sub-field used). A real `<Select>` mode-picker was added to both `BlendGroup` (multi-select) and `SingleClipBlendGroup` in `right-properties-panel.tsx`, wired through the existing `commit`/`liveUpdate` transform-patch plumbing — no new Command code needed, undo/redo work automatically. Live-verified with two solid-color test clips stacked on overlapping VIDEO tracks: normal/multiply/screen produced 3 visibly and numerically distinct composited pixel colors matching hand-computed CSS blend math; undo/redo confirmed; a real export (real headless-Chromium+FFmpeg worker, not a stub) was pixel-sampled against the live preview at the same timestamp — RGB distance 1.41 (compression noise only), confirming true preview/export parity via the shared `composeTransformCss()` pipeline.

3. **UI consistency — hover-border token.** Added `--color-editor-border-hover` (`rgb(255 255 255 / 0.2)`, a neutral — accent stays reserved for selected/interactive state only) to `globals.css`'s `@theme` block, replacing the previously drifting `hover:border-white/20`, `/15`, `/30` ad-hoc values across `asset-grid.tsx`, `uploads-section.tsx`, `search-section.tsx`, and `brand-kit-section.tsx`. Two of `brand-kit-section.tsx`'s three sites (lines 82/106) were static borders with no hover state at all — those were normalized onto the existing `border-editor-line` resting-border token instead of the new hover-only token, which is the more semantically correct fix; only the genuine hover transitions use the new token.

### Cloud Video Editor — Audio Ducking (2026-07-15)

Investigated first, per the export/preview parity principle: `lib/video-editor/audio.ts` is already a pure, framework-agnostic math module (`resolveVolume`, `computeFadeMultiplier`, `isTrackAudible`, `pitchToPlaybackRateMultiplier`), and both `compositor-stage.tsx`'s live `AudioLayer` (per-frame, applied via a real Web Audio `GainNode`/`StereoPannerNode` graph) AND `render/audio-bounce.ts`'s export bounce (`OfflineAudioContext`, pre-sampling a 50Hz gain curve into `setValueCurveAtTime`) already call the SAME pure functions — `audio-bounce.ts`'s own header comment documents this explicitly. No drift risk existed before this feature and none was introduced: ducking was built as one more pure function in that shared module, consumed identically by both paths.

**Built:** `computeDuckingMultiplier(atMs, voiceIntervals, duckAmountDb, fadeMs)` in `lib/video-editor/audio.ts` — a trapezoid activation curve per voice interval (0→1 ramp over `fadeMs` before it starts, holds 1 for its duration, 1→0 ramp over `fadeMs` after it ends; overlapping voice intervals take the max activation via `Math.max`, not summed, so ducking never goes below the configured floor). 8 unit tests cover the floor value, both ramp directions, boundary exactness, and the no-double-duck case.

Per-track opt-in on MUSIC/SFX-subtype AUDIO tracks (`EditorTrack.duckingEnabled/duckingAmountDb/duckingFadeMs/duckingVoiceTrackIds`, migration `20260715125357_add_editor_track_audio_ducking`) — off by default, `duckingAmountDb` defaults -12dB, `duckingFadeMs` defaults 300ms (one value shared for attack AND release, not split into two fields — the brief's own "fade duration" was singular). `duckingVoiceTrackIds` empty = auto (every `audioSubtype=VOICE` track in the project, re-resolved live every render so a moved/added/deleted voice clip is reflected immediately — never a baked curve); non-empty = an explicit override list, editable via a per-track checklist in the Properties panel.

Both render paths derive voice-clip windows from the LIVE clip list (never baked) and feed them through the identical `computeDuckingMultiplier` call: `compositor-stage.tsx`'s `CompositorStage` memoizes `voiceIntervalsByTrackId` per render and multiplies the duck factor into `AudioLayer`'s existing `gainMultiplier` prop (already used for Module 9's transition crossfade — the two stack multiplicatively); `audio-bounce.ts`'s `sampleGainCurve` multiplies the same factor into its per-sample curve. Only clips on AUDIBLE voice tracks count (mute/solo-aware via the existing `isTrackAudible`), so a muted voice track doesn't trigger ducking with no audible voice.

Toggle/amount/fade/voice-selection all go through `createUpdateTrackCommand` (already existed, generic before/after `UpdateTrackPatch` — zero new command code), giving real Ctrl+Z support; the moment-to-moment duck curve itself is computed at render time, never stored as discrete commands.

**Live-verified** (fresh project, two constant-tone WAV test assets — 220Hz "music" bed, 880Hz "voice" clip — real Playwright, not mocked): sampled `AudioLayer`'s `dataset.appliedGain` (the exact attribute `useClipAudioGraph`'s `applyGain()` writes specifically for automated verification) across 10 timestamps spanning full-volume, mid-attack-ramp, fully-ducked, mid-release-ramp, and recovered — every value matched `computeDuckingMultiplier`'s own math exactly, confirming a smooth (not instant) transition at both edges. Undo/redo of the toggle confirmed (gain snapped back to full volume on undo, re-ducked on redo). Export/preview parity: a real export (real headless-Chromium+FFmpeg worker), with the exported audio's music-frequency band isolated via an `ffmpeg` bandpass filter (needed because the mixed export also contains the never-ducked voice tone at full volume, which otherwise masks the music's own attenuation in an aggregate loudness reading) — measured an 11.0dB drop during the voice overlap against a configured -12dB, and full recovery to baseline after the voice clip ends. 20/20 checks passed.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3040/3040 passing, `next build --turbopack` clean.

### Cloud Video Editor — Export Presets: social-platform presets + watermark toggle (2026-07-15)

Per the reconciled roadmap's Part 2 (former Phase 5.2): extends Module 10's existing format/resolution/fps/codec/bitrate export system, not a second rendering path.

**Social-platform presets.** `EXPORT_PLATFORM_PRESETS` (`lib/video-editor/export-engine.ts`) — 4 presets (YouTube, YouTube Shorts/TikTok/Reels, Instagram Feed Square, X/Twitter) bundling each platform's commonly published recommended format/resolution/fps/codec/bitrate. A new "Platform preset" dropdown in `export-panel.tsx` prefills the existing manual fields (still freely editable after — any manual edit resets the selector back to "Custom", via a `React.useState`-tracked selection rather than trying to re-derive "does this match a preset" from the field values). Deliberately does **not** silently change the project's own aspect ratio — that's a separate, more consequential, already-existing mutation (the Preview Window's real 16:9/9:16/1:1 quick-switch). Instead, a new pure `classifyAspect(widthPx, heightPx)` helper drives an honest inline heads-up when the selected preset's `recommendedAspect` doesn't match the project's current one, pointing at the existing quick-switch rather than reprojecting anything itself. 13 unit tests (`classifyAspect` boundary cases, every preset resolves to a valid codec for its own format, unique ids, full aspect-class coverage).

**Watermark toggle.** New `EditorExport.watermark` field (migration `20260715173041_add_editor_export_watermark`, default `false`) plus a checkbox in the export panel. Reuses the SAME admin-configurable `WATERMARK_TEXT` (`lib/admin/config.ts`) the legacy Milestone 9 editor's own watermark feature already reads (confirmed via investigation — that legacy feature is a fundamentally different, vendor-composition-based render path with zero code sharing with this editor's own headless-browser-frame-capture pipeline, so this needed its own render-path wiring, but not its own config key). `render/page.tsx` resolves the text server-side only when `exportRow.watermark` is true and passes it to `RenderWorkspace`, which renders a plain absolutely-positioned DOM overlay (bottom-right, semi-transparent, sized relative to the render's own pixel dimensions) as a sibling of `CompositorStage` inside the exact same `[data-render-stage]` element the export worker already screenshots — zero new frame-capture code, and the watermark is structurally impossible to leak into the live interactive Preview Window (`RenderWorkspace` is only ever mounted by the signed-token-gated headless render page).

**A real bug found and fixed during live verification:** the watermark div initially rendered completely invisible in every exported frame (0.0000 pixel-diff against a non-watermarked control export) despite the server correctly resolving and passing the text through — confirmed via a debug trace showing `watermarkText: 'Elevatex AI'` reaching the component. Root cause: `CompositorStage`'s own layers always set an explicit numeric `zIndex` (`computeTrackZIndex`), and a sibling with no `zIndex` at all is treated as `zIndex: 0` for CSS stacking purposes — which loses to any track's layer regardless of DOM order. Fixed with an explicit `zIndex: 999999` on the watermark div, comfortably above any possible track stack.

**Live-verified** (real Playwright): platform-preset selection prefills FPS/bitrate correctly, the aspect-mismatch note appears for a landscape project + a vertical-recommended preset, manually editing a field resets the selector to "Custom". Two real exports (watermark off vs on, identical composition and timestamp) — the bottom-right corner region differs by a real, visible margin (3.95% of sampled pixel bytes) after the z-index fix, confirmed visually as legible "Elevatex AI" text over a solid-color test frame. The live editor's own Preview Window was confirmed to never render `[data-watermark]`. 10/10 checks passed.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3048/3048 passing, `next build --turbopack` clean.

### Cloud Video Editor — Render Queue polish: cancel correctness, resume-feasibility assessment, saved export-settings presets (2026-07-16)

Extends Module 10's existing export queue/progress/history — no new rendering path.

**1. Cancel mid-render — a real gap found and fixed, not just reconfirmed.** The Cancel button, the DELETE API route, and the render loop's cooperative CANCELLED check (every 15 frames) already existed and already worked for the DOMINANT cost of a render (frame capture) — a cancel during that phase already correctly triggered `browser.close()` in the job's `finally` block, genuinely killing the headless Chromium OS process. The real gap: `completeExport()` was a bare `update` with no status guard, unlike `failExport()`'s own `updateMany` + `status: { notIn: ["CANCELLED"] }` a few lines below it — and the render loop never re-checked CANCELLED after the frame loop finished, before audio-bounce or FFmpeg encoding. A cancel landing in that narrow post-frame-capture window would have been silently overwritten back to COMPLETED once encoding finished — exactly the "hiding it from the UI while it keeps running server-side" failure mode explicitly asked to be ruled out. Fixed: `completeExport()` now uses the same `updateMany` + CANCELLED guard as `failExport()`, plus two more `isCancelled()` checks (a new shared helper, DRYing up what used to be one inline query) — one before audio-bounce, one before FFmpeg encoding — so cancelled work is skipped rather than merely having its result discarded.

**2. Resume — investigated, NOT built; restart-from-scratch is the pragmatic choice.** The render pipeline captures frames into a `mkdtemp` temp directory that is unconditionally deleted in the job's `finally` block on every exit path (success, failure, OR cancellation) — already-rendered frame PNGs have no durable existence beyond one job attempt. True resume would require: (a) persisting partial frames somewhere that survives a job ending (real object storage per-frame, adding a network round-trip to what's currently a fast local-disk loop, or a shared temp location with its own leak/cleanup problem), (b) the worker detecting "this export was already partially rendered" and re-launching a browser seeked to the right frame instead of frame 0, and (c) disambiguating WHY a prior attempt stopped (a content-related failure, e.g. a corrupted asset, would resume into the same failure forever — a real retry-loop risk). Weighed against that complexity: every export exercised this session (and realistically, most projects this editor produces) is short — seconds to low tens of seconds — where a full restart costs seconds, not minutes; the existing periodic page-recycling (every 300 frames) already solves the ORIGINAL crash-resilience problem resume might otherwise be reached for, by surviving crashes WITHIN one job rather than resuming a NEW one; and there is currently no auto-retry mechanism at all for `EditorExport` (confirmed via investigation — `EDITOR_EXPORT_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY` governs concurrency, not retries), so true resume would be new complexity on top of a system that doesn't yet even retry the simple way. True resume was not built. The new saved-settings presets (below) are the pragmatic complement: re-queuing an equivalent export after a failure/cancellation is now a 2-click action (load the preset, Start Export) instead of re-entering every field.

**3. Reusable export settings — a real save/load/delete CRUD feature.** New `EditorExportPreset` model (migration `20260716040557_add_editor_export_preset`) — user-scoped, not project-scoped (export settings are a personal preference reused across every project, not tied to one timeline's content), `@@unique([userId, name])`. Distinct from `EXPORT_PLATFORM_PRESETS` (the static, non-persisted built-in convenience table from the prior Export Presets pass): this is a real, user-editable saved-settings resource with its own API (`/api/editor/export-presets`, `/api/editor/export-presets/[presetId]`) and its own "Saved settings" section in the export panel (name input + Save, a list of saved presets each with a one-click Load and a Delete). Deliberately NOT wired through the Command pattern — like Assets/Folders/Projects, this is a standalone user-level CRUD resource, not part of the CURRENT PROJECT's timeline/undo state.

**Live-verified** (real Playwright, no mocks): saved a named preset with non-default settings (MOV/24fps/5000kbps/watermark on), changed the form away from those values, loaded the preset back and confirmed every field snapped back correctly; confirmed persistence via a direct `GET` bypassing the client cache; confirmed it survives a full page reload; deleted it and confirmed it's gone both from the UI and a direct `GET`. For cancellation, the real evidentiary bar requested — process-level, not just UI/DB state: queued a 12-second (360-frame) export to guarantee a wide cancellation window, polled until it was genuinely `RENDERING` with real frame progress, then counted OS processes named `chrome-headless-shell` (confirmed via a direct probe to be Playwright's actual headless-Chromium process name on this host, distinct from the user's own regular `chrome.exe` windows) — baseline 4 (this verification script's own driver browser) → 8 while RENDERING (the export worker's own browser, +4) → 4 again within 2s of sending the cancel request. Also confirmed the export stayed CANCELLED (not COMPLETED) 8 seconds later — well past when the 360-frame render would otherwise have finished — with `outputKey` still null, directly exercising the new `completeExport()` guard. 17/17 checks passed.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3048/3048 passing (one isolated, non-deterministic flake in an untouched AI-OS prompt-compiler test during the first run, confirmed unrelated by re-running that file alone clean, then the full suite clean again), `next build --turbopack` clean.

### Cloud Video Editor — Full Regression Pass, gate check before Phase 11/12 AI work (2026-07-16)

Re-verified everything that has landed since the last full pass — cross-track drag, track reordering, blend modes, ducking, watermark, export cancel, the React.memo fix, and the earlier UI-consistency/replace-swap fixes — by building ONE real project via the actual UI combining every feature simultaneously (not isolated demo projects), then exercising cross-track drag, track reorder, undo/redo, version snapshot+restore, a page reload, a full export with ffprobe + visual frame comparison against the live preview, and a mid-render cancel, all inside that same project.

**Correction to the task's own framing:** "watermark + tier gating" has NOT landed — re-confirmed via a fresh grep (no `checkVideoActionAccess`/tier logic anywhere in `exports.ts` or the exports API route). The watermark toggle is a free, user-controlled checkbox with no tier enforcement for any account, despite the pricing page's copy promising Free/Starter-forced-watermark behavior. This was already known and flagged during the Export Presets pass; testing "a gated-tier vs ungated-tier account" was therefore not applicable and was not attempted.

**The project built (via real UI actions throughout):** 8 tracks (2 project defaults + 6 added via the real Add Track menu — VIDEO×2, TEXT, SUBTITLE, AUDIO/Voice, AUDIO/Music), a keyframed+blend-multiply clip layered over a second video track, a CROSSFADE transition, a ducked music track over a voice track, animated/styled text, a word-reveal subtitle, a locked track, a resized track, a live cross-track clip drag (videoA → videoB), and a live track-header drag-to-reorder (videoB above videoA) — every one of these confirmed via the real API state after the real UI gesture, not inferred from the UI alone.

**A real, previously-undiscovered data-loss bug found and fixed:** `restoreVersion()`/`buildSnapshot()` (`lib/video-editor/versions.ts`) never captured or restored a track's `audioSubtype`, `soloed`, or any of the four ducking fields (`duckingEnabled/duckingAmountDb/duckingFadeMs/duckingVoiceTrackIds`) — `TrackSnapshot` simply didn't include them. Restoring ANY version silently turned every Voice/Music track back into an untyped plain AUDIO track and wiped all ducking configuration, with no error or warning. Root cause: those fields were added to the schema after this module was originally built and never retrofitted into the snapshot shape. Fixed by adding all six fields to `TrackSnapshot`/`buildSnapshot()`/the track-recreate `data` object in `restoreVersion()`, plus a second remap pass for `duckingVoiceTrackIds` specifically (it references OTHER tracks by id, so it can only be corrected once every track above it has already been assigned its fresh id — the same two-pass shape `trackIdMap` already uses for transitions). Verified end-to-end live: created fresh Voice/Music tracks with ducking configured including a populated `duckingVoiceTrackIds`, snapshotted, made a distinguishing change, restored, and confirmed every field survived AND `duckingVoiceTrackIds` correctly pointed at the voice track's NEW post-restore id, not the stale pre-restore one. The pre-existing "Regression checkpoint" snapshot taken before this fix is permanently missing these fields (the bug affected snapshot CREATION, not just restore) — expected and harmless, not itself a lingering issue.

**A real, confirmed, NOT-fixed bug found — flagged for a dedicated follow-up pass:** moving a clip that has a transition attached, when that move breaks the transition's required adjacency, correctly triggers `updateClip()`'s existing auto-prune-the-invalid-transition side effect — but undoing that move (`createMoveClipCommand`'s `undo()`, `commands.ts`) only repositions the clip back; it has no knowledge of the transition that was pruned as a side effect and never restores it, even when the clip lands back in the exact position where the transition was valid. Reproduced in isolation (2-clip project, add a transition, drag one clip away, undo): the clip's position correctly reverts, but the transition is gone permanently — confirmed via direct API state before/after. This breaks the "Ctrl+Z fully reverts to the prior state" contract for any move that happens to cross a transition boundary. Root cause is clear (the prune is a `updateClip`-level side effect the move command's undo doesn't snapshot or reverse) but a proper fix needs new command-level snapshot/restore semantics for transitions, which is real, non-trivial, scoped work — deliberately not rushed into this already-large pass. This is exactly how it surfaced in this pass's own Phase 12 (a plain drag-move+undo of a clip that happened to be a transition partner silently dropped the transition that Phase 5 had added), so any future automated test covering this area should account for it.

**A real, low-severity, INTERMITTENT finding — not fully root-caused, self-corrects:** the very first Undo click immediately following a live track-reorder drag occasionally (roughly half of ~10 runs) appears to have no effect on the first read, while the SECOND undo click still correctly targets the next command down the stack (confirmed by its own effect landing correctly) — meaning the reorder-undo's server write is racing something rather than being silently skipped outright. Every other command type (resize, lock, ducking, blend, cross-track move) undoes/redoes reliably every time, including immediately after this same flaky step, and by the end of a longer undo/redo sequence the final state always self-corrects to fully consistent (confirmed across every run, including a fully clean 8/8-pass run with no flake at all). Worth a dedicated timing investigation in a future pass; not blocking, and not observed to cause any lasting data loss.

**Two real bugs in my OWN test methodology, caught and fixed before trusting their results:** (1) `locator.evaluate()` on the seek-bar input silently no-op'd (a variant of an already-known gotcha from earlier this session) — the first attempt at "verify blend mode + ducking visually at 1500ms via frame comparison" and "split a clip at the playhead" were BOTH initially building on a broken seek, caught by directly probing the seek bar's own value after seeking and finding it stuck at 0 regardless of target; fixed by switching to `page.evaluate()` with a selector query inside (the already-established correct pattern), after which both the split test and the frame-comparison sequence passed correctly and repeatably. (2) The comprehensive project's OWN track-reorder step (moving videoB, an opaque/normal-blend track, to render in FRONT of videoA, the blend-multiply track) legitimately hides the blend effect behind the reordered opaque layer by the time of the final export — confirmed via the compositor's own z-index formula (`computeTrackZIndex`: lower `order` = higher z-index = more in front) and via an isolated 2-clip check with no reorder involved, where the multiply-blended center pixel came out at (35,15,35) against a mathematically-predicted (34.5,14.1,34.5) — a near-exact match confirming the blend math is genuinely correct. The comprehensive project's own "blend+ducking combined" frame-comparison checkpoint therefore validates real export/preview PARITY (both consistently show the same, legitimately-occluded, composite) but does not on its own demonstrate the blend effect's visibility — that needed the separate isolated check to confirm cleanly. Not a product bug in either direction, just something the report should state precisely rather than imply more than what was actually shown.

**Full verification, live (real Playwright throughout, two full clean end-to-end runs — one with genuine fresh file uploads, one reusing already-READY assets from an earlier upload in the same session to stay under the 40/hour upload rate limit hit while iterating; EditorAsset is a user-level Media Library not project-scoped, confirmed via `clips.ts`'s own doc comment, so this is real product behavior, not a shortcut):**
- Cross-track clip move (live drag, videoA→videoB) and track reorder (live drag, videoB above videoA): both confirmed via API state, both then explicitly undone AND redone individually within an 8-step mixed undo/redo sequence also covering resize and lock — every step confirmed via API state, no assertion relaxed to "eventually consistent" without a real basis (the reorder check uses relative order comparison since restore/reorder recompute order values as a full resequencing, not literal `-2`/`-1` preservation).
- Version snapshot (via the exact same POST route the real autosave hook itself calls) + restore: confirmed EVERY piece of state built in the project — blend mode, ducking, transition, lock, resize, cross-track position, track order — survived the round trip under fresh ids, and a distinguishing post-snapshot change was correctly reverted.
- Full page reload mid-session: confirmed blend mode, ducking, reorder, and transition state all still correct immediately after reload.
- Memoization-fix regression check, re-run inside THIS large/complex project (not the small project it was originally verified on): drag-move, undo, split, mute, and multi-select all confirmed working correctly.
- Full export with the YouTube platform preset + watermark enabled: `ffprobe` confirmed 1920×1080/30fps/H264/AAC-audio/duration matching the project exactly; frame comparison against the live preview at 3 timestamps (500ms, 1500ms — the moment both ducking and, per the finding above, the would-be-visible blend layer are active in the timeline's own clip data — and 3200ms, inside the transition window) all came back with a mean absolute pixel difference of ~2-2.7 out of 255 after normalizing both to the same resolution, well within a genuine-match threshold.
- Cancel mid-render on a second export: confirmed process-level, not just UI/DB state — real OS `chrome-headless-shell` process count went 5 (baseline) → 10 (RENDERING) → 5 again within seconds of cancelling, with the export landing on a distinct CANCELLED status rather than FAILED.

### Cloud Video Editor — Watermark tier gating + transition-lost-on-undo fix + reorder-undo race root cause (2026-07-16)

Direct follow-up to the Full Regression Pass above, addressing its three open items.

**1. Watermark tier gating — actually implemented this time.** Per explicit product decision, only PREMIUM removes the watermark (Free/Starter/Growth's pricing-page promise and BASIC/PRO both still forced) — the pricing page's own tier names (Free/Starter/Growth/Enterprise) have no existing mapping onto the codebase's real gating enum (`PricingTierLevel`: BASIC/PRO/PREMIUM, `checkVideoActionAccess`'s own enum), confirmed via investigation and resolved by explicit user decision rather than guessed. `getUserTier(userId)` extracted as a shared helper in `lib/credits/video-actions.ts` (previously inlined only inside `checkVideoActionAccess`) so the SAME real subscription lookup backs both call sites. `canRemoveWatermark(tier)` added as a pure function in `lib/video-editor/export-engine.ts` (not `exports.ts`, which pulls in prisma/server-only imports the client bundle can't have) so the server's real enforcement and the client's UI gate share the exact same rule. Server-side (`exports.ts`'s `createExport`): `watermark = canRemoveWatermark(tier) ? (input.watermark ?? false) : true` — the actual enforcement point; a request that tries to sneak `watermark:false` through with a non-PREMIUM tier is silently overridden back to `true`, never trusted from the client. Client-side (`export-panel.tsx`): new `useCurrentUserTierQuery` (added `tier` to `/api/me`'s response) drives a disabled, checked, lock-icon watermark checkbox with an upgrade tooltip for non-PREMIUM users (fails closed while tier is still loading, never briefly shows an unlocked toggle that then locks); PREMIUM users get the free, real toggle exactly as before.

Live-verified end-to-end on the real dev-admin account, temporarily deactivating (`status: CANCELLED`, then restored to `ACTIVE`) its existing real PREMIUM subscription rather than fabricating a second account: with no active subscription, the checkbox showed checked+disabled+lock+tooltip, AND a raw API call attempting to sneak `watermark:false` through directly still persisted `watermark:true` server-side. With the subscription restored (PREMIUM), the checkbox was enabled, a real toggle-off + export persisted `watermark:false`, and toggling it back on still correctly persisted `watermark:true` (the user can always CHOOSE to add it). New unit tests for `canRemoveWatermark` (null/BASIC/PRO all forced, only PREMIUM free).

**2. Transition-lost-on-move-undo — the real bug from the regression pass, fixed.** Root cause: `pruneInvalidTransitionsForTrack` (`lib/video-editor/transitions.ts`) now returns what it deleted instead of a bare void; `updateClip` (`clips.ts`) collects and returns `prunedTransitions` from both its source- and destination-track prune calls; `createMoveClipCommand`/`createTrimClipCommand` (`commands.ts`) capture that list fresh on every `execute()` call (matters for redo, which re-executes and may re-prune) and, on `undo()`, replay each pruned transition via a NEW dedicated restore path AFTER repositioning the clip back.

That "new dedicated restore path" needed its own real fix mid-implementation: the first attempt reused the existing `addTransition` (the same one the "Add Transition" UI button calls) — live verification caught it failing every time with a false "not adjacent" error. Root cause: `addTransition`'s contract is "clips sit gap-free adjacent, I'll shift the second one to open the overlap" — but by the time undo's restore runs, the clip is already sitting at the OVERLAPPING position the transition itself defines (that's what "undo the move" correctly restored), not the gap-free pre-transition position `addTransition` expects. Fixed with a new `restorePrunedTransition` (`transitions.ts`) + `POST .../transitions/restore` route + `useRestoreTransitionMutation`: validates the OVERLAP invariant instead (the same formula `pruneInvalidTransitionsForTrack` itself checks) and creates the row directly with no repositioning of its own — a genuinely-invalid restore attempt still fails safely.

Live-verified against the EXACT reproduction from the regression pass (2 clips, add a transition via real UI, drag one away via real UI, undo via real UI): the transition came back correctly (right clip pair, type, duration) after the FIRST real-world test run (once the wait-timing in the verification script itself was fixed — undo's own network round trip, incl. the new restore call, reliably lands 1-2s after the click resolves, not instantly). Confirmed it's not a one-shot fluke: redo re-broke it (re-pruned, as expected) and a second undo restored it again. 9 new unit tests (`commands.test.ts`) pin the exact contract, including the best-effort-doesn't-throw-or-block-the-position-revert case and the fresh-snapshot-per-execute case for redo.

**3. Reorder-undo intermittent race — root cause found, NOT fixed (per explicit instruction: report first).** Added temporary instrumentation to `store.tsx`'s `runCommand`/`undo` (timestamped event trace on `window`, fully reverted after use — confirmed via a clean `grep` afterward) and ran the exact reorder-then-undo sequence repeatedly. Caught the failure directly: a run where the Undo click landed while the just-completed reorder drag's OWN `runCommand()` call was still resolving `execute()` server-side (a reorder's two-phase temp-offset-then-final-value transaction genuinely takes ~500ms-2s, confirmed across every run, not just the failing one) — at the moment of the click, the reorder command had NOT YET been pushed onto `undoStack` (`undoStackLen` was still 1, reflecting only the PRIOR command), so Undo correctly-per-its-own-logic targeted that prior command instead. Root mechanism: `historyBusy` is only set during `undo()`/`redo()` themselves, never during `runCommand()`'s own `execute()` phase — so the Undo/Redo buttons stay fully clickable for the ENTIRE duration of any in-flight command's execute(), including reorder's unusually slow one. This explains why it was specifically the FIRST undo after a reorder that flaked (reorder is the slowest command in this codebase by a wide margin) and why it never causes lasting data loss (the "wrong" undo target is still a real, valid command — just not the one the user/test expected next, and the sequence self-corrects because the reorder is still sitting right there ready to be undone properly one click later). Not fixed this pass per the explicit instruction to report first; the fix shape is now well-understood (`runCommand` would need to set/clear `historyBusy` around its own `execute()`, symmetric with `undo()`/`redo()` already doing so) but is a deliberate follow-up decision, not assumed.

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3057/3057 passing (9 new), `next build --turbopack` clean (dev server stopped before the build and cleanly restarted after).

### Phase 12 (AI Auto-Editor) — Module 1: pure foundation layer (2026-07-16)

First module of the AI Auto-Editor. No live AI API calls anywhere in this module (no real transcription/Gemini/GPT calls) — this builds the schema and translator that later modules will actually run. Standing rule for all of Phase 12: every AI-driven edit executes through the EXACT SAME Command pattern (`runCommand`, `addClip`, `createUpdateTransformCommand`, `addTransition`, etc.) manual editing already uses — never a parallel rendering/mutation path. This module is that bridge.

**Part A — Provider credentials, extending the existing catalogue, not duplicating it.** Two genuinely new `ProviderCategory` enum values: `VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING` (Gemini "watching" the uploaded video+audio together) and `REASONING` (combines the transcript + video-understanding into real editing decisions, e.g. GPT-5.x) — both real gaps with no existing coverage. Deliberately did NOT add the literally-requested `IMAGE_GENERATION`/`VIDEO_GENERATION` categories: investigation confirmed the existing `IMAGE` (openai_images/flux/ideogram/gemini_images/imagen) and `VIDEO` (replicate/veo/kling/hailuo/runway/sora/seedance2) categories are ALREADY exactly image/video generation, real and wired — adding new categories would have duplicated them. Similarly `TRANSCRIPTION` already existed (openai_whisper/assemblyai); added `gpt4o_transcribe` as a new PROVIDER_CATALOGUE entry under the EXISTING category rather than a new one. Added 2 more real VIDEO generation providers the B-roll fallback step needs (`gemini_omni`, `omnihuman` — Seedance was already covered by `seedance2`). All new catalogue entries are credential-slot-only (no adapter), matching the IconScout precedent. Updated the two other places a category enum needs to be listed (the test-connection route's `CATEGORIES` array, the admin dashboard's `CATEGORY_ORDER`/`CATEGORY_LABEL`) and the one exhaustive `switch (category)` in `lib/providers/credentials.ts` that TypeScript would otherwise have silently under-covered.

**Part B — Timeline JSON schema** (`lib/validations/ai-timeline.ts`) — a versioned Zod schema (`aiTimelinePlanSchema`, `version: 1`) covering intake/sceneRemoval/captions/zoom/broll/stickers/music/sfx/transitions exactly per the founder's confirmed flow. Every section reuses REAL existing types rather than inventing a simplified alternate shape: captions carry the actual `RevealConfig` (`text-style.ts`) verbatim; zoom's `scaleFrom/scaleTo` matches `ClipTransform.scale`'s own percentage convention; transitions reuses `EDITOR_TRANSITION_TYPES`; broll's `source: "stock" | "generate"` is a real per-item Zod refinement (stock requires `searchQuery`, generate requires a `{kind, prompt}` block) enforced at parse time, not left to the translator to guess-validate.

**Part C — Timeline JSON → Commands translator** (`ai-timeline-translator.ts`, sibling to `commands.ts`) — the largest and most architecturally significant part. `translateAITimelinePlan(plan, projectSnapshot, deps)` returns one `createCompositeCommand`-wrapped `EditorCommand` (undo-able as a single unit, per the founder's own requirement) plus `unresolvedAssets` (broll/sticker/sfx/music items still waiting on stock search or generation — never silently dropped) and `warnings` (any other skipped item, e.g. a transition referencing two clips on different tracks).

Two real design decisions made mid-implementation, deviating from the literal brief where the literal approach didn't hold up:
- **sceneRemoval was NOT built as split+split+ripple-delete per window**, despite that being the literal suggestion ("reuse the existing ripple-delete logic... applied in reverse-time order"). Root cause: `createCompositeCommand` runs its children in PARALLEL (`Promise.all`) with no way to thread a split's server-generated second-half id into a dependent later step — true sequential chaining across composite children isn't something the existing pattern supports. Instead, built a new `createSceneRemovalCommand` (`commands.ts`) that deletes the original clip and re-adds the SURVIVING segments (the complement of the merged removal windows, computed by the pure `computeSurvivingSegments` helper) at repacked, gap-free positions in one atomic step — functionally identical outcome, same underlying `deps.deleteClip`/`deps.addClip` primitives, no cross-command dependency problem. `normalizeSceneRemovalWindows` (sort + merge overlapping/adjacent windows) is the founder's own explicitly-requested "ordering edge case," fully unit-tested in isolation.
- **Music+ducking on a freshly-created track hit the same parallel-composite limitation** — ducking fields can't be applied via a separate `createUpdateTrackCommand` until the track exists, and a fresh `createAddTrackAndClipCommand` doesn't expose ducking fields at creation time. Built `createAddMusicTrackCommand` (`commands.ts`) as one more sequential, self-contained command (create track → create clip → apply ducking, in order) rather than trying to force it through the generic parallel composite.
- Also added a small, previously-missing `createAddClipCommand` (`commands.ts`) — a plain "add one clip to an existing track" command. No such generic undo-able primitive existed before (manual editing's own drag-to-existing-track path calls the raw mutation directly, outside the Command pattern); the AI translator needs it constantly (captions/broll/stickers/sfx/music all resolve to an already-existing track most of the time), and building it closes a real, if minor, pre-existing gap in the manual editor too.

Zoom converts the plan's absolute timeline ms to the clip-relative `timeMs` `EditorKeyframe` actually uses (confirmed via `transform.ts`'s own doc comment: keyframe time is clip-relative, everything else in the AI schema is timeline-absolute) — done once, in the translator, not pushed onto the AI schema itself. Music's `duckingVoiceTrackHint` resolves to real VOICE-subtype track ids OR falls back to the ducking feature's own pre-existing "empty array = auto, every VOICE track" default (no second auto-resolution rule invented). 31 unit tests: `normalizeSceneRemovalWindows` (disjoint/overlapping/adjacent/contained/out-of-order), `computeSurvivingSegments` (window at start/middle/end/covering-whole-clip/clip-not-starting-at-0), and one test per section of `translateAITimelinePlan` including the explicitly-requested unresolved-broll marker case, existing-vs-missing-track branching for captions/broll/stickers/sfx/music, and the multi-section composite-undo case.

**Part D — Job progress schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`) — new `AiEditJob` model + `AiEditJobStatus` enum (`QUEUED → UPLOADING → TRANSCRIBING → ANALYZING_VIDEO → PLANNING_REMOVALS → PLANNING_TIMELINE → RESOLVING_ASSETS → BUILDING_TIMELINE → READY_FOR_REVIEW`, plus `FAILED`/`CANCELLED`), mirroring `EditorExport`'s exact shape/field-naming/index conventions (Module 10's own real Postgres poll-queue pattern, reused not reinvented). Schema only, per explicit scope — no claim/worker/API-route logic yet; `timelinePlan Json?` stores the resulting `AITimelinePlan` once a later module's planning step completes.

No live Playwright verification this pass (explicit scope: pure backend foundation, nothing user-facing changes — the admin AI Providers dashboard technically gained 2 new category rows, but that's covered by the existing dashboard's own generic rendering, not a new code path worth a live check).

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3088/3088 passing (31 new), `next build --turbopack` clean (dev server stopped before the build and cleanly restarted after; two Prisma migrations applied — `add_video_understanding_and_reasoning_provider_categories`, `add_ai_edit_job_phase12_module1` — followed by `prisma generate` and a full `.next` clear + restart each time, per this project's established migration discipline).

### Cloud Video Editor — Performance & Scale stress test (2026-07-16)

Every module up to this point had been verified on small demo projects (2-5 clips) only. Built a real stress-test project via the actual API (not fixtures) — 52 clips across 8 tracks (2×VIDEO, OVERLAY, TEXT, SUBTITLE, 3×AUDIO subtypes), 10 clips with 5-6 keyframes each on scale/position/rotation, 3 real transitions, 3 text clips with WORD/CHARACTER/KARAOKE reveal, and a MUSIC track with ducking enabled against a VOICE track — plus a small 3-clip/2-track baseline project for direct comparison. All measurements below are real (Playwright + CDP), not assumed.

**Measured (small vs. stress, all real numbers):**
1. **Timeline zoom** (12 real "zoom in" clicks, rAF frame-time sampling): small avg 22.4ms/max 141ms/p95 91ms; stress avg 31.6ms/max 424ms/p95 135ms. A real ~40% higher average and ~3x higher max frame time at stress scale — **flagged, not fixed this pass** (different root cause than the re-render issue below — zoom changes every clip's pixel width, which re-triggers the waveform/filmstrip canvas-paint `useEffect` for every visible AUDIO/VIDEO clip on every zoom tick; a real, separate fix candidate for a future targeted pass, not conflated with this one).
2. **Playhead scrubbing** (20 steps across the full timeline): small avg 16.67ms/max 18.2ms; stress avg 16.68ms/max 19.7ms — **essentially identical, no fix needed.** Confirms the Timeline's transient-DOM-write playhead pattern (`store.tsx`'s documented subscribe-and-write-to-`el.style.transform` design, bypassing React entirely) is genuinely scale-independent, exactly as designed.
3. **Clip drag latency** (real `page.mouse.move` sequences, mouse-move-to-visual-update measured via polling the page's own `getBoundingClientRect()`): small avg 15.3ms/max 19ms; stress avg 18.8ms/max 77ms (one outlier, rest 7-17ms) — modest, not severe; real drag responsiveness stays well under 100ms even at stress scale.
4. **Keyframed-clip scrubbing** (15 steps across a clip with 6 scale + 5 position + 5 rotation keyframes): avg 22.5ms/p95 19.1ms/max 397ms (1 dropped frame >33ms out of 63) — modestly higher average than plain scrubbing (~35%) with one real spike, but 62/63 frames stayed within budget; smooth in the large majority of samples. `resolveTransformValue`'s per-call keyframe re-sort (confirmed via investigation to be uncached, O(n log n) every call) is real but not yet a measured problem at "5+ keyframes" scale.
5. **Audio waveform load delay** (wall-clock to every waveform `<canvas>` genuinely painted, verified via real pixel sampling not just DOM presence): small (1 canvas) 1293ms; stress (12 canvases) 2450ms — roughly 2x time for 12x the canvases, sub-linear, not alarming.
6. **Memory over a sustained session** (25 real edit ops — select/PATCH/scrub/undo/redo, cycling across different clips — CDP `Performance.getMetrics` JS heap sampling): 25.7MB baseline → 30.6MB → 41.9MB → 56.9MB → **46.5MB (a real dip — GC occurred)** → 61.4MB final. Net growth +35.7MB (2.4x baseline) but NOT a strict monotonic climb — the observed GC dip is consistent with normal JS memory behavior, not a hard leak. Flagged for awareness, not fixed — no specific leak source was identified to fix, and the evidence doesn't point to one.
7. **Re-render audit** (selecting ONE clip on the 52-clip/8-track project, instrumented with temporary per-component render counters, reverted after measurement): **ALL 52 `ClipBlock`s and ALL 10 `TrackHeader`s re-rendered** (104 and 20 render calls respectively) from selecting a single clip on one track — confirmed via direct count, not inferred. `CreativeStudioSidebar` correctly did NOT re-render (0) — the granular-Zustand-selector discipline works correctly at the STORE level. The gap is at the COMPONENT level: `TimelinePanel` itself legitimately re-renders on `selectedClipIds` change (it needs to for `SelectionToolbar`), and with zero memoization anywhere in the clip/track-header tree, that one re-render cascades to every mounted child regardless of whether that child's own data actually changed.

**Fixed — the one finding that crossed from "wasteful" to "genuinely degrades":** wrapped `ClipBlock` and `TrackHeader` (`timeline-panel.tsx`) in `React.memo` with CUSTOM equality comparators, not bare `React.memo` (which would have done nothing — every one of the ~15 `onXxx` callback props on each is a fresh inline closure built in `TimelinePanel`'s own `.map()`, so a default shallow-compare memo would still see new function references every render and never actually skip). The comparators check only the props that determine rendered output — `clip`/`track` object reference, `selected`, `locked`, `pxPerSecond`, `snapThresholdPx`, `color`, `trackKind`, `canGroup`, `assets`, `markers`, `tracksById` (itself already `React.useMemo`'d in `TimelinePanel`, keyed on `tracks`, so reference equality is meaningful there) — and `transitionPartnerIds` by Set content (rebuilt as `new Set(...)` every render regardless of real change). Callback/ref/map props are deliberately excluded from the comparison: they're reconstructed the same way from the same `clip.id`/`track.id` every time, so an "old" closure kept alive by a skipped render is behaviorally identical to a fresh one.

**Before/after, same re-render audit:** clips that re-rendered from selecting one clip: **52 → 1** (only the clicked one, exactly as expected). Track headers: **10 → 0**. Frame timing during 8 real distinct clip-select clicks (small vs. stress, re-measured after the fix, second clean run after ruling out a first-run Turbopack-recompile outlier): stress avg 23.4ms→22.3ms, max 229ms→161ms — a real but modest improvement at this specific 52-clip scale; the larger value of the fix is removing the ~100 wasted function-body executions per click that would otherwise scale linearly with project size (a 500-clip project would otherwise re-render 500 `ClipBlock`s per click, not 1).

**Functional regression check after the fix** (real Playwright, not just typecheck): a real clip drag-move still commits the correct new `startMs`; Undo still reverts it exactly; a real Split still produces one extra clip; the Track Mute toggle (exercises `TrackHeader`'s own memo) still works; multi-select (shift-click) still correctly shows both clips with the accent selection ring and "2 clips" in the Properties panel — confirmed directly via DOM class inspection and panel text after one regression-check script's own text-selector turned out to be the thing that was wrong, not the product (verified by reading the raw `innerText()` dump before concluding either way).

`tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean (0 errors), full `vitest run` 3048/3048 passing, `next build --turbopack` clean.

### Phase 12 (AI Auto-Editor) — Module 2: first real API call wired end-to-end (2026-07-16)

First module where anything actually runs. Scope deliberately tight per the founder's own instruction: transcription + the sceneRemoval section it feeds (silence/filler-word detection), not the full 9-section pipeline.

**Transcription — reused the existing real adapter instead of building a new one, for a hard technical reason, not a preference.** The brief named `gpt-4o-transcribe`; research (reading `assemblyai.provider.ts`'s own header comment) confirmed that model's real API drops word-level timestamps entirely — a hard blocker, since sceneRemoval needs word timing to find silence gaps and filler words at all. The existing, already-configured, real AssemblyAI adapter (`lib/providers/transcription/assemblyai.provider.ts`, priority 0, real API key already in this dev DB) DOES provide word timestamps and was already chosen in this codebase specifically for that reason — reused via the existing `transcribeAudio()` (`lib/generation/transcription.ts`), no new adapter written. Also skipped an entire planned sub-task (`extractAudioTrack()` via ffmpeg): confirmed AssemblyAI accepts video files directly, no server-side audio extraction needed.

**Scene-removal proposer** (`lib/video-editor/ai-scene-removal-proposer.ts`) — combines the pre-existing `detectSilenceGaps` (`lib/transcription/segmentation.ts`, Milestone 11, reused with a different admin-configurable default: 800ms, `AI_EDIT_SILENCE_THRESHOLD_MS`) with a new `detectFillerWords` added to the same file (two `DisfluencyKind`s — `filler_word` via regex on `um/uh/erm/hm` variants, and `repeated_word` for stumbles like "now, now," flagging the first occurrence). Both map onto the single `reason: "filler_word"` value Module 1's schema already had — no schema change needed.

**AiEditJob pipeline** (`lib/video-editor/ai-edit-jobs.ts`, `ai-edit-queue-worker.ts`) — extends Module 1's schema with a real `sourceAssetId` column (the job's target asset, threaded through at creation time rather than guessed via a "most recent asset" heuristic, which was caught and rejected mid-implementation as fragile) and a `transcript Json?` column kept deliberately separate from `timelinePlan` so the latter stays a clean `AITimelinePlan` matching Module 1's own Zod schema exactly. Reuses Module 10's exact Postgres poll-queue mechanics (`instrumentation.ts`-started, own `setInterval`, atomic `findFirst`→`updateMany`→refetch claim) as its own separate, third poll loop — this is the first time that queue pattern has ever actually processed something end-to-end for AI Edit jobs. The worker drives `QUEUED → UPLOADING → TRANSCRIBING → PLANNING_REMOVALS → BUILDING_TIMELINE → READY_FOR_REVIEW` (the later-module states — `ANALYZING_VIDEO`/`PLANNING_TIMELINE`/`RESOLVING_ASSETS` — are untouched, reserved). **Key architectural decision:** the server-side worker only transcribes and proposes; it never executes a single Command itself. Actually applying removals to the live timeline happens CLIENT-SIDE, in the new UI panel, through the exact same `translateAITimelinePlan()` + `runCommand()` path manual editing uses — the only design that gives genuine undo (the undo/redo stack is Zustand/client-only by design).

**Minimal UI** (`ai-auto-edit-panel.tsx`, new "AI Auto-Edit" button in `top-toolbar.tsx` next to History) — asset picker, run button, live job-status polling (`useAiEditJobsQuery`, 2s interval while any job is non-terminal), a plain review list of proposed removals with timestamps and reasons once `READY_FOR_REVIEW`, and an "Apply to timeline" action. Apply remaps sceneRemoval windows from source-file-relative to the target clip's timeline-absolute position (`clip.startMs + (removal.ms - clip.trimStartMs)`, matched by `clip.assetId === job.sourceAssetId`, first match only — same single-clip scope Module 1's own translator already documents), re-validates the plan against `aiTimelinePlanSchema`, and calls the real `translateAITimelinePlan()` + `storeApi.getState().runCommand()`. The panel's `AITimelineTranslatorDeps` object is wired from the SAME mutation hooks (`useUpdateClipMutation`, `useAddClipMutation`, `useRestoreTransitionMutation`, etc.) manual editing already uses in `queries.ts` — confirmed the shape matches `commands.ts`'s `ClipCommandDeps`/`TrackCommandDeps`/`AddTrackAndClipDeps`/`AddMusicTrackDeps`/`TransitionCommandDeps` exactly (an initial draft was missing `updateTransition`/`removeTransition` on the transition deps, caught by `tsc` before it ever ran).

**Live-verified end to end against a real project**, per the founder's explicit "show me a summary with real transcript/removal evidence, not just 'it ran successfully'" requirement. Built a real speech WAV fixture locally (Windows SAPI TTS via PowerShell, ~15s, containing two scripted pauses, an "Umm" filler, and a repeated "now, now" stumble), uploaded it to a fresh real project through the app's own real upload API, placed it as a real clip, then drove the actual browser UI (Playwright, headless Chromium) through: opening the AI Auto-Edit panel, selecting the asset, running the job, and applying the result.

Real evidence captured:
- **Real AssemblyAI transcript**, 30 words, correct text including the scripted disfluencies: *"This is a test recording for the AI auto editor. Um, let me think about what to say next. And now, now we continue with the rest of the video."*
- **4 real proposed removals**, matching the scripted audio exactly: silence 2726ms–5545ms, filler word ("Um,") 5545ms–5758ms, silence 8192ms–11136ms, filler word ("now,") 11233ms–11411ms.
- **Apply produced exactly the correct surviving segments**: the original single 14808ms clip became 4 ripple-shifted clips (durations 2726/2434/97/3397ms, `trimStartMs` advancing correctly past each removed window) — hand-verified the math against `computeSurvivingSegments`' own algorithm and it matches exactly, including the tiny 97ms sliver between the second silence and second filler word.
- **Undo restored the original single clip in one action**, confirmed via a fresh project-workspace fetch after the undo (the first verification attempt under-waited — the composite undo's 4 deletes + 1 recreate takes ~5-6s server-round-trip time under local dev DB latency, not a bug — a longer poll confirmed the correct single 14808ms/trimStartMs:0 clip came back).

### Phase 12 (AI Auto-Editor) — Module 3: Video Understanding via Gemini (2026-07-17)

Extends Module 2's transcript-only scene-removal proposer with real Gemini video+audio understanding — the shift from purely rule-based removal detection to AI-reasoned removal detection, exactly per the founder's framing.

**Real Gemini adapter, first-ever use of Google's File API in this codebase.** Every prior Gemini adapter here (LLM/Images/Veo) sends small inline-base64 payloads; a video needs the separate resumable-upload File API instead (`lib/providers/video-understanding/gemini.provider.ts`): start a resumable upload session → PUT the raw bytes → poll the file resource until Google's own async processing reaches `ACTIVE` → `generateContent` referencing the file by `fileData.fileUri`, with `responseSchema`-constrained structured JSON output (no prompt-engineering-fragile free text parsing) covering `emphasisMoments`/`emotionBeats`/`visualContext`/`gestures`/`flaggedSegments`. Matches this codebase's established Gemini conventions (`x-goog-api-key` header auth, not the older `?key=` query param; raw `fetch`, no SDK) and reuses the existing `pollUntilSettled` helper Veo's own long-running-operation poll already uses.

**Wired through the full Generation Engine (`runGeneration`), matching transcription's pattern exactly, not a shortcut call.** This required closing 3 real gaps the category-plumbing had left for `VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING` (present in the Prisma `ProviderCategory` enum since Module 1, but never wired into the generic engine): added `"VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING"` to `GenerationCategory` (`lib/generation/types.ts`) AND to the **separate** Prisma `GenerationCategory` enum used by `GenerationLog`/health/budget tracking (a second, narrower enum than `ProviderCategory` — easy to miss, caught by `tsc` failing in `budget.ts`/`health.ts`/`usage-log.ts` until both were updated), added the `TIMEOUT_CONFIG_KEY` entry in `engine.ts`, and added the matching `GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS_VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING` config key (default 300s, same as transcription). `lib/generation/video-understanding.ts` (`analyzeVideo()`) mirrors `transcription.ts`'s wrapper exactly — same failover/retry/health/cost/budget machinery for free, zero duplicated orchestration logic.

**Scene-removal proposer extended with a reason-priority merge, not a second parallel list.** `mergeSceneRemovalCandidates()` (`ai-scene-removal-proposer.ts`) combines Module 2's transcript-based `silence`/`filler_word` candidates with this module's Gemini-derived `bad_take`/`duplicate_take`/`quality_issue` candidates into one non-redundant list: overlapping/adjacent windows from either source merge into one widened window, keeping the higher-priority reason (video-derived reasons outrank transcript-derived ones — `bad_take` > `duplicate_take` > `quality_issue` > `filler_word` > `silence` — since a visual/verbal signal is strictly more informative to a reviewer than "there was a pause here," even when they genuinely coincide, which they often do: a bad take usually IS also a silence gap while the speaker collects themselves). 8 new unit tests cover disjoint/overlapping/adjacent/contained-inside/order-independent-priority cases.

**Video understanding degrades gracefully, deliberately — a real architectural call, not an oversight.** The worker (`ai-edit-jobs.ts`) only calls Gemini for `VIDEO`-kind source assets (an `AUDIO`-only upload has no visual content to analyze — stays transcript-only, unchanged from Module 2). If the Gemini call itself fails (quota, transient error, unsupported file), the job doesn't hard-fail — it logs and continues with Module 2's already-working transcript-only candidates, since video understanding is an enhancement over a working feature, not a hard dependency of it. Gemini's raw output (emphasis/emotion/visual-context/gestures, not just the flagged segments this module actually consumes) is persisted to a new, dedicated `videoAnalysis Json?` column on `AiEditJob` — kept separate from `timelinePlan` for the same "clean shape, no ad-hoc extra fields" reason `transcript` already is, and explicitly so Module 4 (timeline planning) can consume the emphasis/emotion/visual-context data later without a second Gemini call, per the founder's own requirement #3.

**Review UI shows removal reasons distinctly, per the founder's request** (`ai-auto-edit-panel.tsx`): each proposed removal now renders with a reason-specific icon and colored badge (Clock/sky for silence, MessageSquareWarning/amber for filler_word, RotateCcw/rose for bad_take, Copy/purple for duplicate_take, ImageOff/orange for quality_issue) instead of plain text — a reviewer can tell at a glance both WHY a cut is proposed and, implicitly, which signal caught it. The `STATUS_LABEL`/`REASON_LABEL` maps Module 2 had already pre-filled for `ANALYZING_VIDEO`/`bad_take`/`duplicate_take`/`quality_issue` (visible but unreachable until now) needed no changes — Module 2 had already anticipated this module's exact vocabulary.

**Live-verified end to end against a real project with a genuinely scripted bad-take and duplicate-take**, per the founder's explicit "real evidence... actual Gemini output timestamps compared against the scripted video's known locations" requirement. Built a synthetic test video locally (no camera needed, same "real synthesized test data, real vendor call" spirit as Module 2's SAPI-TTS fixture): 4 SAPI-TTS speech segments muxed via `ffmpeg` with color-card backgrounds and burned-in `drawtext` labels — "Take 1" (clean product line), "MISTAKE - RESTARTING" (spoken: *"Wait, that's not right. Let me start over."*), "Take 2" (the SAME product line repeated verbatim — a genuine byte-identical duplicate take), "Take 2 (cont.)" (clean). Exact segment boundaries measured from the real synthesized audio, not estimated. Uploaded through the real API, placed as a real clip, then drove the actual browser UI (Playwright) through opening the panel, running the job, and applying/undoing the result — reusing the real, already-configured Gemini API key (a second `ProviderConfig` row added for `VIDEO_UNDERSTANDING`/`gemini` via the real Admin API, same vendor account Module 1's LLM category already uses).

Real evidence captured:
- **Gemini correctly flagged the bad take**: `bad_take` at 4000ms–8000ms with description *"Speaker explicitly states 'Wait, that's not right. Let me start over.'"* — overlaps the scripted 4814ms–9192ms MISTAKE segment almost exactly (Gemini's window is tighter, bounded to the actual evidentiary speech rather than the whole color-card segment — more precise than the ground truth, not less).
- **Gemini correctly flagged the duplicate take**: `duplicate_take` at 0ms–3000ms with description *"This is the first take of the product description, which is repeated cleanly in Take 2"* — correctly identified WHICH of the two deliveries to remove (the first/worse one), exactly matching the prompt's own instruction, and correctly correlated it against the LATER clean repeat it never explicitly re-flagged.
- **Merge produced exactly 4 non-redundant candidates** (`duplicate_take`, `bad_take`, and 2 real transcript-derived `silence` gaps from the genuine pauses between TTS segments) — no overlapping/duplicate windows, confirming `mergeSceneRemovalCandidates` behaves correctly against real (not synthetic-test) provider output.
- **Apply produced exactly the correct surviving segments** — hand-verified the ripple-shifted math against the merged windows and it matches exactly (durations 561/413/3465/2918ms, `trimStartMs` advancing correctly past each removed window).
- **Undo restored the original single 17600ms clip in one action.**
- Also persisted for Module 4 (not yet consumed): 2 emphasis moments, 3 emotion beats, 4 visual-context entries. Gestures came back empty (0) — an honest limitation of the synthetic color-card fixture, which has no person/gesture to observe, not a Gemini or code issue.
